Soleniods how many garages store them in a lead lined box in case they are fried by emp pulses Oh and what make video camera(SPECIAL EFFECT PANNING SHOT PAH!) works when nothing else electrical does the one that pays you the most in advertising mate thats who Look I could go on and on with pointless input for 90 odd minutes Had and accident in the last six months wanna claim yep I want 90 mins of my life back from you Spielberg!!!

title: Just Plain Stupid
review:
Spielberg used to have it.Cruise never did. He's been playing the same character since The OUTSIDERS. Proof of this is in the way his character in WOTW leaves his dockworker job all smiles and practically skipping. (Then, in a moment of extreme mood swings, he becomes angry dad and throws a baseball through a window.) As for Spielberg, he proves he's still the master, all right. The master of filming actors as they look off camera at events we the viewer apparently are not worthy of. These scenes must take up at least 50% of this awful film's running time. Roland Emmerich and M. Night Shamalayan (two horrible filmmakers in their own rights) do a better job of ripping of Spielberg than Spielberg does.

Enter Tim Robins, convenient backstory supplier and resident weirdo. Like Cruise's unexplainable shift in character at the film's opening, Robins goes from gun toting wardog to whimpering coward with no strong answer as to why.

I realize this is an alien film yet I can only suspend my disbelief so far and that car surviving the plane wreck is just asking way too much. It's as bad as shots of people waiting for the opening ground to reach their feet before moving out of the way, just so the director can get some use out of his dolly. WOTW is packed with continuity problems and just plain ridiculous circumstances, such as Cruise scolding his son about not bringing food, while they are in someone's kitchen. Does mindless summer fare have to be so, well, mindless? This movie is a flat-out insult to any intelligent film-goer. I'd rather see the straight to video, C. Thomas Howell version. At least that one should be good for a laugh. I was too angry at this WOTW to find anything amusing about it.

title: What a stinker!!!
review: This movie had so much potential. But they spent all the budget on special effects and no money on an actual story. I can't believe Spielberg could have made such a stinker. His stock certainly will take a nose-dive after this one. What little "story" there was made little sense and was full of holes. The ending was just plain stupid. The visuals were stunning but there was little to back them up. It's kind of like someone took 10 still photos of various stuff and then strung them together and called it a movie. And the movie industry wonders why people are flocking to the theaters this year. Movies require style AND substance. Heck, sometimes you can even get by with just substance and no style. But style by itself will never work.

title: Don't believe the hype....
review: In all honesty, I was completely disappointed by this film. It was hyped up to the maximum, and I guess this is what made me decide to see it. I wanted to know what all the fuss was about, and in my opinion, it didn't deserve it. In any other circumstances, I probably would've given this film a four, at a stretch it would get a five. But this deeply disappointed, and totally failed to be what the makers claimed it would be. Tom Cruise wasn't what he was built up to be in this remake, and I would have to say that the only saving grace is the inclusion of Dakota Fanning, who is definitely going to be big in the future. I'm in no way saying that Cruise was terrible, but I guess the hype ruined everything, because you expect so much from the movie, and it just fails to deliver. I won't be recommending this film at all.

title: This is one of the worst movies I've seen in my life!
review: Saw War of the Worlds last night- can't BELIEVE it's a Stephen Spielberg flick- truly one of the worst movies I've ever seen. Save your money and rent it on DVD in a few months at the most, but don't waste your time or money seeing it in the theater.least you'll only be out a few bucks that way. The characters were not likable, the story had way too many holes to be believable- there was no way to suspend disbelief! I am in shock at how bad this film was. The only 2 "kudos" I can give is that a few of the special effects are cool and Dakotah Fanning is a great actress, although her character was unsympathetically annoying.

title: What a terrible film
review:
The problems with this movie have nothing to do with the time period or the strays away from the book. It comes from the HUGE plot holes in the film.

  • If an EMP takes out everything electronic, how does that one guy manage to film the tripod coming out of the ground on his DIGITAL VIDEO CAMERA?! (granted, we can just call this an oversight, but really, come on Steve) - The biggest and worst plot hole comes from the end. Boston is a large metropolitan city, and the tripods were there. So how come Roy's ex-wife and her family are all looking like they just got done having tea? The tripods lay waste to all of metropolitan New York in a matter of hours, why is Boston special? Their street is perfectly fine, they are all dressed nice, WTF?!! The last scene of the movie would have played out a lot better if it had been placed in a smaller city, one that the tripod's probably wouldn't have bothered with so quickly.


I thought that the special effects were great, but if you're going to do a movie on tripods, do a better story (The Day the Tripods Came, The White Mountains, etc.), or just think about this before you throw millions of dollars into a disappointing film

title: Eyes Wide Shut (and should stay that way)
review: This is a more personal view of the classic movie. It focuses on the effects of the "war" on a single family. Unfortunately, it isn't clear why we should particularly care for this family other than the father is the same arrogant character that Cruise plays in most of his films and Dakota Fanning can appear wide-eyed and scared when she's not yelling at her father or acting wise beyond her years. Just as in E.T., Spielberg has the teenage boy rebel and disobey his parent. It was irritating in E.T., but here, it just makes one not really care whether he lives or dies. As a sci-fi film, it fails. As a study of a family in crisis, it fails more miserably. Don't waste your money on this one. It's not even worth a rental.

title: Best fx-worst script
review:
The first 45 min. are fantastic. The last hour-plus will leave you disappointed...and that's an understatement.

Great fx-best cg to date. But, fx do not a movie make.

At the end of the press screening I attended, nobody applauded. Lots of groans (above my own).

Just like Mr. & Mrs. Smith, this has a great premise. Spielberg and Cruise drop the ball.

Yes, I read the book. Heard the radio play. Blah, blah. I know it's a remake (of sorts). But even this has tons of plot holes. My "suspension of disbelief" wasn't suspended. Sorry.

As much as I really wanted to like this movie, I just couldn't.

Bottom line: if you MUST see it, rent it.

title: Don't Even Compare it to the Book
review:
First, I will say that there were only three major things that were actually taken from the book.

1. The fact that the alien's machines were tripods and had tentacles 2. There was a scene in which the main character is in a basement 3. The demise of the aliens.

Other than that, it's pretty much just another alien flick squashed on top of a 'single parent getting to know his kids' subplot.

What made H.G. Wells' book so fantastic was that it moved with the subtlety of an M. Night Shyamalan film. There wasn't a lot of fight scenes, or running through the streets. After the initial attack with the 'heat ray' the rest of the book basically revolves around the main character walking through horrific desolation and having all his preconceptions about the 'modern-ness' of the Victorian World dashed to pieces. It was moving, it made you think. Plus my favorite scene in the book doesn't even translate into a modern retelling. It involves the main character in a horse drawn carriage traveling down a road in the rain. One of the tripods steps out of the shadows and into the road in front of the guy, terrifying the horse so much that it falls and breaks its neck and leaving our hero to stare up at the thing, illuminated by flashes of lightning. It's an incredibly described scene and really illustrates how unprepared and arrogant Wells felt the Victorians were.

Now onto the movie...in modern times...and not in England...for some reason. Oh right, the reason was to have Tom Cruise in it. Gotcha.

The aliens aren't shocking and neither is their technology because the world at that point is the world that has been exposed to Issac Asimov, Star Wars, Alien etc. They have nuclear weapons and modern tanks. Wells' 'heat ray' isn't a shocking thing in this context.

The directing is well done, but the story is such a departure from, well, the story that it really doesn't work if you've ever read the book.

Certain unnecessary plot points such as the tripods already being under the surface for a long while before the events of the movie and the red fungus/lichen stuff that spreads everywhere feel really forced.

The narration, drawn right from the book, seems so out of place as the world it was criticizing isn't even being depicted.

I will say that the acting was good and engaging, but the mushy sub plot really detracts from the flow of the story.

title: As usual, the original movie rules, the remake is totally lame
review:
Two words: Lameous Maximus. While the invading aliens have developed technology capable of destroying earth and disabling nearly all of mans technology, the complex inner-workings of the common camcorder elude even the most brilliant alien scientists.

Why should the aliens use their latest greatest alien technology to attack earth when they can bury million year old technology in the earth and dig it up when they get to our planet. This is sort of like the US air force leaving their F-16's and stealth fighters at home when they fight abroad so they can dig up some old biplanes that have been buried for one hundred years.

Insignificant Technical Note: Man didn't inhabit the earth a million years ago when they buried the machines. But, maybe the aliens didn't want to attack the crocodiles and alligators so they decided to wait?

Oh NO here come the aliens they are destroying the city. I can: 1. Leave the city and hide in the country? Nope too obvious. 2. Go underground and hide in the city? Nope the subways can be dangerous. 3. Board a large well lighted ship that is loaded with people and surrounded by alien tripods of death. YES!

Oh NO here come the aliens they are destroying the army. However, I know that even though our latest missile technology bounces off their tripods like BB's, I can destroy the aliens and their indestructible tripods of death with nothing but my bare hands.

Now, the best part of the movie, when the kid refuses to listen to Tom Cruise and charges into the oncoming tripods of death, a cheer comes from the audience and cry of: Death to the IDIOT! The crowd was fed-up with the lame humans and had begun rooting for the aliens.

title: Suing for false advertising
review: If it were possible to sue for false advertising, this film would have a class action suit in record time. I've read WoW and have seen films on it. THis was not one of them! If you like movies about dysfunctional families and screaming kids, then this is made for you. No one seems to be acting in anyway to try and survive. When trouble pops up, the reasoning in almost every scene is to go to the most likely place to attack attention, places that have a lot of people together. THis is only a movie about a cliché separated family, son hates father, daughter is wise but taken to bouts of hysteria, and a father whose only attributes is the inability to make any decision on his own: see it, dozens of times. If you want to see War of the Worlds, do not go to this; WoW is a very minor character that can barely be seen by the overly large ego of Tom Cruise.

title: Makes INDEPENDENCE DAY look like the Fourth of July.
review:
My Take: A terrifying and exciting version of the classic H.G. Wells tale. Possibly the best version.

(This is an extension of the review I wrote in April 2007)

Unlike his "Close Encounters of the Third Kind" and "E.T.: The Extra-Terrestrial", Spielberg's adaptation of H.G. Wells WAR OF THE WORLDS doesn't give a peaceful message of aliens being friendly to earth's beings. The aliens here are, to all those familiar with Wells' story (And most thankfully, most are), hostile and couldn't think of any other reasons to land here on Earth, but to destroy it. While WAR OF THE WORLDS might be geared as entertainment, bringing Spielberg back in his days with JAWS and JURASSIC PARK. But upon mastering his skills as a more serious filmmaker in SCHINDLER'S LIST and SAVING PRIVATE RYAN, he makes WAR OF THE WORLDS a much darker experience, making it more effective and more frightening. Spielberg shares Wells' vision in a tale of an invasion on earth by emotionless aliens. This is thrill-master Spielberg at his best.

The camera focuses mainly on Ray Ferrier (Tom Cruise) and his family, who are forced to leave their home, and run for their lives after an gigantic tripod emerges from the soil and destroy everything in its path. The films plot, thankfully, didn't burst into an all-out war that pits man and aliens in the ultimate war. Like what Tim Robbins' character says, "This is not a war when there's a war between man and maggots... This is an extermination." That's some of the elements that actually elevate this from other alien invasion films. "Independence Day" or "Mars Attacks!" per say.

From the first frame to the last, I think it was a wonderful film. The flaws are there, but in favor mind-blowing entertainment and sheer terror, I won't hold them against the film. The special effects on the tripod machines are impressive, not because the CGI is top-notch, but that because how effectively ominous they are. These tripods join the shark from JAWS and the Raptors from JURASSIC PARK as yet another perfect killing machine as only Spielberg could create. If this is not the best adaptation of Wells' classic tale, it's definitely the most frightening. WAR OF THE WORLDS is terrific entertainment.

Rating: ***** out of 5.

title: The aliens die due to the Earth's bacteria! How original!
review: All the special effects in the world can't justify keeping with H.G. Wells' original ending. I find it insulting that Spielberg would try to impress moviegoers with 21st Century techno-fluff minus an original ending. Think "The Natural" wherein the novel ended with a strikeout and the movies ended with a homerun. It is okay for a movie to change a novel's ending. I read H.G.'s story in Junior High; I didn't need to spend good money to see the same ending augmented by computer enhancements. I'm sure my own laptop could generate the same effects and save me the ticket price. Also Cruise seems to be going through the motions as "Ray"...I'm not convinced that his character really cares about mankind or Dakota Fanning. "Ray" just wants to save his own a**.

title: Loved it!
review:
I never thought a movie could compare to Sin City. War of the Worlds was a close second. Even though Tom Cruise is a weirdo, he does have talent. He played a great part in this movie and I loved watching him grow as a father in this movie.

Although I question some aspects of this movie, it still kept me on the edge of my seat. After the tripods come out of the ground, they make this machine like sound that was rather creepy if I do say so myself. Every time they made that sound, I knew something bad was going to happen and had to grab my friend's hand to not freak out. I was on the edge of my seat the whole time.

I was really impressed with the aliens in the movie. They were not all fake looking, yet were still freaky. Steven Spielberg didn't ruin the movie by making them huge and mean. They acted like they would on a weird and different planet.

I have to say that of all the movies I have seen, this is by far one of the best when it comes to special effects. Even though this movie is about the destruction of the earth by huge tripods, they weren't that fake looking. It was just a really believable movie. The acting was surprising well and I was all around impressed. I didn't like the book, but the movie was more than I expected. Go see it and make your own decision.

title: See it for the effects...
review:
The only honest reason I can give this a 6 is due to the spectacular effects!

Bad Things: The script was simply... there, and as for the acting. If this doesn't ruin Cruise's career, just remember, neither did Cocktail. Of the two "child stars," the boy had better quit his career now before he gets a lifetime of Razzies, the girl I've been told has acted well in the past, which only tells me she was probably told over and over to "look scared, no, more scared, even more, SCARED, overacted scared... there, that's it!" I hate to razz upon Spielberg, but this time it had to be done.

Good Things: The effects and devastation! The Tripods were a beautiful combination of the book and Lovecraft. The aliens themselves? Watch ID4, and hunch 'em over a bit and lengthen. I would've preferred a design novel-based, and would rather have the old version's man-in-a-suit aliens, but I suppose I can settle with these.

So, go see it for the effects, without acting expectations... and you just may enjoy!

title: Wonderful movie, mediocre ending
review:
Seriously? Why do so many of you hate this movie? I even read a post asking if anyone WASN'T going to see it just because it was Spielberg. Come on, give me a break. The man has made an amazing array of films over the years that have shaped Hollywood just as much as Star Wars re-defined cinema in the late 70's. If anything, Spielberg deserves our respect. I just can't accept the fact that someone out there doesn't like Spielberg.

Two, none of the reviews on the first page of the War of the Worlds page have a positive review of the movie. I completely disagree.

The film was brilliant. Brilliantly shot, brilliantly acted, and finally, finally, finally, a brilliant use of special effects.

The only part I dislike is the ending, where Tom and all his family survive. That was dumb.

To all you out there who aren't cynical asses w/ little pricks, go see the film. You'll love it. I don't recommend it for kids. Because they'll react the exact same way Dakota Fanning does in the beginning of the film where she covers her mouth and yells a muffled, "oh...god..." See it.

title: An Unexpected Disappointment
review: If ever there was a trailer that wrongly convinced you of what a movie was really like, this would take the cake. Watching the previews for this movie I was excited to see a Sic-Fi Drama that perhaps was similar to "Independence Day" but I was horribly disappointed. Steven Spielberg's confusing attempt to make this suspenseful thriller a comedy has dismally failed. I was too mad to laugh at any of the comedic or incredibly corny scenes that surrounded what could have been great entertainment. The best part of the movie was the beginning scenes which showed the relationship between Ray Ferrier (played by Tom Cruise) and his two children Robbie Ferrier and Rachel Ferrier (played by Justin Chatwin and Dakota Fanning). Best actor goes to Fanning's wonderful performance and great screaming abilities. Her huge eyes and some talent for comedy helped me out with a few chuckles during this long, drawn-out, incredibly corny movie. Probably the lowest part of the movie was when Cruise says goodbye to his son (who is not yet old enough to drive) who demands to see the army fight these creatures because 'He Must'. They had me rolling my eyes and looking down at my watch as the camera scanned down on Cruise gripping the last of his son's body as Chatwin crawls up the hill to massive explosions. As I walk out of the movie theater, the only thing that comes to mind is, "I could have been doing... anything!" Don't waste your money and don't waste your time on this feeble attempt for a big budget movie.

title: The movie OK, but not no classic.
review:
Right, I just saw this movie and must say the special effects were fantastic, something Spielberg never fails on!! But the story line was WEAK and whats the point in having strong special effects if your story lines weak??? (Kinda defeats the purpose). To start off, we have the stereotypical "rebellious" teenage son that never listens to his father and then we have the "Look at me I want to overact to get good reviews" Dakota Fanning, that screamed at any given opportunity, which more than annoyed me. Even though I believe the novel is excellent, the movie lacked in areas and also anyone reading: (independence day IS BETTER in my opinion).

The empty streets of Boston was very erm, weird since the houses were all intact and it seemed like the aliens must have passed over that city. (pretty dumb as the aliens were meant to have destroyed the world and did a good job wherever Cruise and his children went). Then there is the mom who was wearing her best apron with her hair in a bun like she was about to cook the Sunday roast other than just been attacked by vicious tripod aliens. (HOW UNREAL)And another thing that completely annoyed the **** out of me!!, How the heck did the son survive??? I mean the tripods completely destroyed the grassy area with a fire ball but somehow he made it to Boston even though everything and everyone around him died. (And I'm not just talking about normal civilians, I'm talking about the military in their armours and tanks, they all died, but the son in his leather jacket and denim, survived!!, like WTF??) To be honest, Spielberg never fails on excitement (The special effects) but just like A.I, the story line could have done better.

Let us go back to the days of Jaws.....

title: War of the Goonies. No serious spoilers, except the movie!
review:
War of the Worlds, 2005 No spoilers to speak of I have seen the complete film in the USA. It doesn't matter how or where. This is my opinion on this film and is just one person's opinion. Paramount deserved better. I hope we see another version of War of the Worlds by a fiscally responsible director who will allow the money to be seen in the production rather than the payroll.

Not scary.

Mr. Spielberg is quick to call George Pal a corny producer. I understand that desperate people do and say desperate things. I can tell you, I believe this film will be pretty much "history" after about the first 20 days in release. Mr. Pal's version, which Paramount released in 1953 and continues to be a respected, if flawed, classic fifty years later. I can't imagine this new and limited effort will be held with respect in 5 years, much less 50 years.

Let me look at a few points..

Corn.. I consider the Martians playing with the bicycle as corny.

Spielberg criticized Pal's version. Yet, did you notice five full segments were copied From Pal's film rather than Spielberg coming up with something better than what he ridicules as corny.

Promotion  Does anyone beside me wonder about those "faux-chat" rooms that open, are full of sales crap and strangely closed before any "real people" have an opportunity to feedback. Didn't Columbia / Sony get in trouble with the Justice Department for doing this kind of thing? Direct to video! I wonder about films made in the "ready for TV format" rather than in scope. If the picture were to be truly impressive, it would need to have a big screen, not a small flat image that's ready for TV. I know the excuse that small pictures make the image more claustrophobic and other b.s. Fact is, if you only plan to fill the image with 60% of the image of a scope picture, you save some big bucks on special effects.

What climax? None of us felt there was one.

Martian rip-off. The Martian, to me, seemed to be a dead ringer for one used in Independence Day a few years ago. Different size, different color, but what do you think? The little kid.. I don't know if little kids belong in this movie or not. She was certainly the best actor. I suppose she will attract children to a movie many adults will consider inappropriate for children.

Tom Cruse. Time to retire. Did you see him on David Letterman? The effects are the better part of the movie thanks to ILM. Cruse didn't know what ILM was! Maybe he's on too much medication.

Music  Good.

Effects  So much rain, fox, smoke, darkness and Jump Cuts, I found it hard to see what was special. Makes me feel Bert Gordon was involved with this film. For the limited time LucasFilm had to do the effects for Spealburg, well done for no original concept.

Anything new? Not really. **spoiler?**We've seen most of it before. The train was something new, but came across like the flaming cows in MARS ATTACKS. Even under the guise of might, it didn't work very well. But it was a very good idea. Most of this film is a direct rip off from others.

Wrap it up!. I have come to the conclusion the biggest problem with this film is getting a green light in November and having the film "in the can" in May. There was time pressure to get things done that could not be done "properly" on a short schedule.

You can have 500 or 5000 effects shots, sure. But this is the first time in years I can remember seeing razor edges on traveling mats. Perhaps this should have been held up for Christmas to allow the film to be anchored properly.

Good to see Ann Robinson and Gene Barry fora few seconds.

My hope is George Lucas will do this film properly for Paramount. Great book. Pal's version is a true classic. This version will give people the squirts. Needs to be done again by someone who can do it with a little integrity for HG Welles and Paramount.

title: Rent the 1953 British version instead
review:
When one chooses to remake a film one must make one of two choices. One can either expand on the original or go in an entirely different direction. This big budget summer bust does neither. With uneven special effects and bad editing, Steven Spielberg presents some of the sloppiest story telling of his career. (remember Indiana Jones and the Temple of Doom) Worse yet, Tom Cruise reverts back to the arrogant character he made famous in the 80s and early 90s. He does little to show us the maturity he displayed in such films as COLLATERAL or his other Spielberg collaboration, MINORITY REPORT. The are some genuinely tense moments that will put you on the edge of your seat, but for your hard earned money I'd wait for second run or video/DVD. Better yet take your hard earned money and spend it on BATMAN BEGINS. Now that's a good movie.

Sincerely, Marc Richardson

title: Try to look at this movie in a different light
review:
"It's a Spielberg so it's got to be good" is an easy statement to make but a little more difficult to substantiate. Take the first half-hour of War of the Worlds. All the impressive stuff you see there you have seen elsewhere: bombardment from whatever source above, hideous things disgorging from below, devastating mayhem in a concrete jungle, horrendous carnage in the same concrete jungle, and more. Yet, this first half hour demonstrates convincingly that Spielberg does it better, not so much with anything that you can conveniently point to, but as a sum total of everything he has done. These include the photography, particularly the play of colour and light, the sound (and alternating silence to increase tension), the angle of the shots, the movements and timing of them, just to mention a few. Every shot is brilliantly conceived, meticulously executed and painstaking edited into the traumatic, shattering virtual reality experienced by the audience in that first hour marking beginning of the alien invasion.

WOTW does not go out of its way to be preachy on morals of humanity or to be a testament to family sentiments, although there is a bit of both. That the tripod machines have been buried for millions of years underground has been repeatedly mentioned, to signify something that is left to the audience's interpretation. The relationship of delinquent father Ray Ferrier (Tom Cruise) with son Robbie and daughter Rachel is somewhat standard fare.

Nor does the movie attempt to be entertaining in the normal sense. For example, there is very little humour, the only noticeable crack at a laugh being where they take temporary refuge in Ferrier's ex-wife's house, when all the "food" that Robbie had scooped up in the rush constitutes ketchup and an assortment of sauces.

What Spielberg seems to want to do with the movie is to create a realistic world of horror and despair depicted in H.G. Well's story. He does it through the eyes of a trio of father, daughter and son, and later only father and daughter. There is a noticeable absence of any macro picture, as seen in "Day after tomorrow" or some similar movies. The problem with the standard approach of giving you a few shots in different major cities around the globe is that it often comes across as so very artificial and formulaic. Focusing only on the protagonists actually makes the experience more realistic for the audience.

One particular technique he has used very successfully is to employ a rather abrupt shot, the meaning of which is puzzling for one second, but then starts to sink in. One example is Ferrier emerging after a night's hiding in the basement. We see a part of the living room of the house, as the camera pens to showing what looks like a huge fan. This turns out to be the remnant of the jet engine of a crushed plane, as the camera reveals that the "living room" we see is just what is left of the collapsed house, which is in the middle of something that look like the remains (if any) of a V-2 bombardment. Just brilliant. Another example is where close to the end, we see one of the terrifying tripod machines sitting on top of a industrial building, and it took us a second to catch on the fact that the machine is in some kind of a trouble, the turning point of the entire story.

Tom Cruise has made a reasonably good attempt to take on a new persona, this one verging on an anti-hero. It will do him good to make more attempts in this direction (but obviously not in MI 3 scheduled for 2006)  just see how well Kevin Costner has done in "The upside of anger". Dakota Fanning is not challenged as much as in "Hide and seek", playing here a child living in an essentially normal environment with her mother and model stepfather. With the character being quite normal herself, albeit with a bit of claustrophobia, Fanning did get a chance to scream her head off portraying all kinds of fear and horror. Justin Chatwin playing Robbie is not that well known. Miranda Otto who has been so wonderful in LOTR has miserably little to do here as the estranged wife. Tim Robbins does get to do some acting as one of those eccentric characters.

title: WAR of the WORLDS - A World Where E.T. is Transformed into Darth Vader
review:
...........................................................from Pasto,Colombia...Via: L.A. CA., CALI, COLOMBIA....and ORLANDO, FL

WARNING: May contain a few SPOILERS!

In a perfect world, any film directed by Steven Spielberg and starring Tom Cruise and Dakota Fanning (Man on Fire, Taken, I Am Sam), would be a marvel. But, alas!...As we all know, live in a perfect world, we do not! The sad reality is this: War of the Worlds is, undoubtedly, a visual stunner...and absolutely NOTHING else.

Unfortunately, we live in a world where the young filmmaker who gave the world cinematic master-works as JAWS, Indiana Jones (along with George Lucas), ET, The Color Purple and Schindler's List, has become a film- industry magnate (co-owner of Dreamworks studio) and where the principal goal is not making great movies, but making great money! Unfortunately, we live in a world where the "Seventh Art" has been relinquished to nerdy CGI techs. That WAR abounds in visually high-impact, jaw-dropping, disturbing and Uber-unsettling scenes, which, at times, may even border on the artistic, is undeniable. But WAR is soulless cinema. It has more of the feel and look of a large- scale, passive video game, where there is no real character development, because everything is completely subordinated to the frenetic and incessant visuals.

It is possible, or perhaps likely, that most video game-lovers will adore this film. Also, if you fancy the release of adrenaline akin to that you get during most theme park rides, WAR just might turn out to be one of your favorites! But this type of activity almost always leaves an unpleasant aftertaste, as does this film.

Barely 10 minutes in, WAR is already busy depicting the arrival, or rather the emergence, in this case, of alien invaders. From the moment of their rise to the surface, the "aliens" are relentless in their campaign of extermination of the human race.

Rachel (Dakota Fanning) appears throughout the entire movie screaming, crying and whining, incessantly, to the point of becoming utterly unbearable. Tom Cruise (Rachel's father) makes a superhuman effort to save his role from disaster, andalmost succeeds! But the dialog is so forced, so contrived and its characters so superficial, so two-dimensional, it ends up being one big 'Mission Impossible' for Mr. Cruise! There is a small respite from the on-screen images of genocide, some half an hour before its abrupt and unceremonious "FIN"When survivalist, Tim Robbins' (Mystic River, The Shawshank Redemption) character, offers his home as shelter to little Rachel and her dad. But the scene does not really fit all that well into the film. It's as if Spielberg and his inner circle made the decision to put some scene, or other, there, and simply failed to find anything better.

Then, in the blink of an eye, all the aliens just up and die, and, in the most surreal, Deus Ex Machina, of ways....they ALL lived happily ever after!!!!! .The only thing missing was: "The END", plastered all over the screen.....50's style! As video games are ubiquitous in today's society, WAR, will surely have its audience, but I would really think twice before watching this sterile vision of a dark, creepy and soulless world with anyone under age 10! Be that as it may, for what it's worth

4*.......ENJOY / DISFRUTELA!?!?!?!?

Any comments, questions, observations, in English o en ESPAÑOL, are most welcome!........................................

title: Fails to live up to expectations.
review: What a huge disappointment. It seems that the bigger the advertising budget, the worse the movie! The ending was appalling and a total let down. Tom Cruise is wooden and unsympathetic. I didn't care whether he lived or died. Dakota Fanning overacts her little heart out, which is a shame as she is normally great. With such a woefully thin plot, the special effects were just not good enough to carry this film. About the only thing I did like was the sound effect that let the viewer know that an alien tripod was nearby (similar effect to a pending shark attack in 'Jaws'). I think Steven Spielberg made this one by numbers, as his usual creativity was sadly lacking. Worth a look when the DVD has been discounted, otherwise don't waste your money.

title: An Insult to HG Wells
review:
This film is a massive disappointment and an insult to HG Wells. Clichéd characters such as the divorced dad who's a jerk but turns out to be a hero in the end, clichéd action scenes such as Cruise and the grenade and a clichéd Hollywood ending. Cruise as usual just plays himself as that's all he's capable of and he's a mediocre to average actor at best and Dakota Fanning and Justin Chatwin are just plain annoying. The film has some good scenes such as when the tripod first appears and the tripods and special effects themselves are good as to be expected from ILM, but on the whole this film just smacks of a missed opportunity.

I'm usually a fan of John Williams scores but this one is nothing special at all and I also also thought the terrorism references were in very poor taste and the reasons for Spielberg and Koepp including them are very questionable.

Above all this film should have been set in Victorian England just like the book. That would have set it apart from all the other aliens invade the USA films.

Why also can't Spielberg work with proper actors for a change instead of big stars who can't act particularly well. Cruise who seems to be more interested in promoting himself instead of the film or War of the worlds, should have been the last choice for a film like this, which is supposedly based on a classic story and I really think Spielberg is way past his best.

title: Snore Of The Worlds!
review:
In 1953, some wise folks got together and made a very good visual re-telling of an H.G. Wells novel. Fast-forward 52 years, and some too-smart-for-their-own-good folks got together to ravage the long-cold grave of H.G. Wells and make... uh ... money! The only excuses for Spielberg making a movie this crap-tacular are:

1) He had 100 million dollars burning a hole in his pocket... and

2) He had just purchased a new kitchen knife and wanted to test it by editing a new film... and

3) Tom Cruise was already drunk in the living room helping to brainstorm a new project

Will the film make money? Of course, it's by Spielberg. Will the ladies love it? Of course, it has Tom Cruise in it. Will anyone be able to explain the half-baked premise, the myriad unbelievable inconsistencies, the lack of likable characters, or why highly-intelligent aliens would wait thousands of years to overthrow our world when they could have had it centuries ago for a string of beads? Of course, that's what fans are for.

I was originally going to give the movie a 2 star rating, but I had to give kudos to Spielberg and Cruise for brainwashing me into watching another of their duets after witnessing The Mi-snore-ity Report.

title: Aliens are Stupid; Humans are Stupider
review:
I wasn't dead set on seeing WotW, but I found myself with time on my hands, and the reviews have been pretty good. Now that I've seen it, I have to wonder why.

Some reviews I've read make the point that this wasn't overly reliant on special effects. If it wasn't absolutely reliant on special effects, I don't know what movie ever has been. Certainly the acting can't be said to carry the movie. Tom Cruise turns in the most wooden performance since Pinocchio wished he could be a real boy. Reviews have heaped praise on the performance of Dakota Fanning as Cruise's daughter. but I thought she laid it on awfully thick, to the point that I kept thinking of Jon Lovitz' old SNL character, Master Thespian ("I'm acting!"). She was most convincing when she was screaming. Justin Chatwin, who played Cruise's son, was nondescript. The strongest performance in the film comes from Tim Robbins, who has a short and unnecessary role that wasn't in the original story. He seems to have been added by the writers to inject some tension into what would otherwise have been a long stretch of characters trying to hide quietly in a basement.

The acting wasn't enrapturing. How was the storyline? Ridiculous. Wells would surely have refused to attach his name to it. His classic has been subverted by Spielberg, Friedman, and Koepp. Under their heavy thumbs, the story of man's struggle for survival and the power of nature has turned into yet another hackneyed "father goes through travails to win the affections of his estranged kids" story. Instead of being truly alien invaders, the villains of this film have been here all along, more or less. At least their battle machines have been, buried by the thousands beneath the ground since before there were people at all. This was one of several attempts to adapt Wells' story to a world beset by terrorism; the enemy is among us, be paranoid, blah blah blah. Such a theme gets good box office, but it doesn't necessarily make for a good story. It didn't work in this case.

The rewrite, in fact, necessarily pokes Wells' story full of holes, and these show up as ridiculously illogical plot points throughout. The worst one of all goes right to the heart of the story as it is. The aliens are killed off by exposure to earthly microbes. If their machines have been lurking underground for millennia, how could they not have known about disease? The point is made at the beginning of the film that the aliens have been watching us throughout our evolution, waiting for the opportunity to strike. How did they miss the plague, chicken pox, the flu? How did such stupid aliens manage to build spaceships? In one scene, they are shown reacting to a bicycle wheel as if they've never seen a wheel before. When the aliens are shown, they seem to have nothing more than animal intelligence. Their ships are intelligent, but the aliens themselves aren't all that bright. Was it smart to bury the spaceships and wait around while mankind started investigating the earth? What are the odds that nobody ever noticed the presence of millions of alien spacecraft just a couple of thousand feet under the ground? You'd think somebody would have picked up on them. I suppose Spielberg could have been making the point that aliens are stupid and humans even stupider. Those of us who paid to see this film may be the stupidest humans of all.

Perhaps the most ludicrous example of bad writing comes toward the end of the movie. We see a sizable group of humans held in a cage Every so often, a tube comes down and takes one away to be processed for the aliens nefarious purposes (I won't give away what that is, but think "Turf Builder"). Inevitably, Tom Cruise is sucked into the tube... and at this moment, someone thinks of holding onto him. The cage is filled with people, the attack has been going on for a week at this point, but only at this point does someone think of doing this. Only when Tom Cruise is sucked into the tube do they hit upon the most basic plan thinkable to save a victim.

All this being said, the special effects and action sequences were excellent. They carry the day here, to the point that there is barely any dialog in the last half hour. That may not have been unintentional. Cruise is at his best when we can't hear what he's saying, and we are largely spared his voice for a large part of the film.

War of the Worlds is run of the mill at best, and downright bad at its worst, and anyone who can say with a straight face that it isn't completely dependent on CGI effects and explosions to distract us from what is nothing more than another bland action blockbuster must have seen a different film than I did. The 1953 Byron Haskin production is much better than this latest flaccid attempt from Spielberg. The new version is a movie very much in the vein of predecessors such as Independence Day and Men in Black II. If it weren't for the blinding flashes, there'd be nothing to watch.

title: A lousy re-enactment of H.G.Wells classics
review:
Going to this movie I was not really expecting miracles, but I did not think that Spilberg would fall so low. I was not expecting Cruise to be at the pinnacle of acting art, but I was not expecting his performance to be so stiff either.

There is very little by way of a story in a movie. Putting H.G.W. into modern-day USA has been a Big Mistake (TM). Trying to make this look like "any common Amrican can be a hero" thing is a disaster. The whole "conflict of generations" thing between Cruise and his son is so-o-o-o out of place, space, time and off-topic that any sensible editor would have done the good thing cutting out entirely.

And the little bravado 'Yes, we won!' where no victory was achieved by man? Pathetic...

title: Could have been so much better!!!
review:
So very disappointing! With all of Tom Cruise's crazy antics these past few weeks I put all of my faith in Steven Spielberg. What was the point? Where was the substance? This movie was nothing but "run, scream, hide" over and over again. Plus, I love how those in Boston they were trying to reach were perfectly fine while the city lay in ruins. Nothing happened to them. I mean come on...their clothes looked like they just came from the dry cleaners while everyone else looked like hell. Such a disappointment. Oh, and why did the heads of the aliens look exactly the aliens from Independence Day?

This movie is almost as bad as A.I. for Mr. Spielberg. When the lights came up I heard a few applause but many disapproving comments. No doubt this movie will make a lot of money but I hope to see better in the future from Mr. Spielberg.

title: A War of Worlds
review:
I went. I saw. I cried.

If you have yet to see Mssr. S's War of the Worlds, do so. But not if you're expecting to re-visit the world of HG Wells.

Prior to viewing this, try to get your hands on the '53 version. Then read the book. Then see this latest venture. You'll detect a slight difference and may lapse into spectacular disappointment.

Mr. S's venture does little to shed new light on the Wells original. Though aided by incredible CGI, this director's storytelling skills have been lost beneath the weight of delivering summer simplicity and box office returns to a Hollywood that must now kneel before its bank balance. What should have been an incredible piece of sf film has become yet another piece of Hollyweird drivel.

While I enjoyed the popcorn and the fun of another science fiction spectacular, Stephen's other efforts in this genre including CLOSE ENCOUNTERS and ET shine much brighter than this latest attempt.

It would have helped him greatly if he had bothered to read the book. Based on what I saw, neither the director nor screenwriters seemed to have found it fitting to do so.

title: Woe Of The Worlds
review:
I'd confidently say that this is the worst film Steven Spielberg's ever made. Right from the panoramic opening shot of those New York docks the viewer is forced to distance them-self from both the action, and more importantly for this film, the characters. To quickly compare the openings other random Spielberg films, E.T.'s first scene is shot from very low angles, which helps the audience understand the whole story from a child's point of view, the opening of Saving Private Ryan is another classic attention grabbing opening sequence were the audience is virtually thrown in with the soldiers that are landing, achieved by shaky point of view shots, slow motion and an inescapable aural invasion that really grabs you by the senses.... Then this. From the beginning we are forced back in our chairs watching a pretty unlikeable character, well, do pretty much nothing for just under a couple of hours. When i say, 'do nothing', i don't mean that there isn't any action in the film, rather i mean that he's exactly the same character at the start of the film than he is at the end of it. None of the events of the film seem to change him. There's one scene that sticks out in my mind as being particularly rubbish, that being the one were Ray Ferris (Cruise) lets his son run off to be blown up. That scene could have been the best in the film, a total turning point that could have made it, well, good. Instead we get a Cruise not seeming that bothered about his own flesh and blood getting pulverised, an appropriate response in my view would have been to break down and beg him to stay, and because of their (badly portrayed) past he goes anyway... just an idea... And then i was thinking about the scene in The Last Crusade (Spielberg again) where Henry Jones thinks he's lost Indi. 'There's so much i never told him', we can tell he's gutted that he thinks he's lost his son. Then when he indi clambers back up to the top of the mountain, he grabs him and says 'i thought i'd lost you boy' Not here. When the ridiculous end comes around and the son bounds up to Ferris in the final scene Cruise might as well give him a jovial punch on the arm and say 'all right. what's up'. The fact that the son needlessly survives bewilders me entirely. Cruise is awful in it. But i'd blame spielberg for A casting him and B letting him get away with such lazy acting. the character demanded the same venomous, spiteful idiot that he Cruise portrayed in Rain Man. It also needed that character arc when we think by the end of the film that he's actually all right guy that can actually see things from other people's perspectives... but as i said at the start of this rant, he, as a character, goes nowhere. Even when he does get the chance to be resilient, it seems more by chance than any kind of Determination that he manages to blow up one of the tripods. Then there's Dakota Fanning. OK, she is really good in the film. Her acting is fantastic anyway, well above the standard of most of her adult peers. So when she's given a pretty mediocre character like this to play she really shines. The only bits where there's any real tension is the bits when she's in danger. The most nerve recking being the one when she's trapped in the car which is under mob siege. And that bit doesn't even involve Aliens. Again though, by the end her character just kind of disappears without changing. When the aliens come into the house near the end and all the actions in the basement of Tim Robbins house, i felt it was a very cheap and far less tense/exciting slap in the face to Shyamalan's 'Signs' movie. And then when i thought about it, it was exactly as if they'd taken the scene from Jurassic Park where the kids are hiding from the Raptors in the kitchen and making it really really really devoid of tension. I don't even see the point in mentioning what becomes of the aliens. The whole film is about that family, and i don't think i've ever seen such boring three characters committed to cinema. Just me? I just really can't believe that was a Steven Spielberg film... i even think the terminal's good. I'd like to think that maybe, like stephen king does or something, he got a ghost director to fill in for him. Looks more like Renny Harlin to me. Oh Well. I guess an argument for the film is that it tries to mirror our own fears about terrorism or apocalypse...but it's just so... dull.

Would have got 2/10, but a couple of very good moments and Dakota Fanning claw it to 4/10 for me. And i'm trying to be generous.

title: FAKE CGI + No Empathy = DUD
review: The plot had no cohesion making it difficult for many in the audience to get caught up in the film. That's a big surprise because if you don't empathize with the lead character, what's the point of a disaster film? I had hoped that this would be better. I found myself trying hard to like the film but failing miserably. Despite the number of effects, they were very ho-hum as well. Sad to say that War of the Worlds was a huge misfire. I was SO looking forward to this film and was just severely disappointed by this unsatisfying and incredibly shallow movie. Also, this movie just wouldn't end and I wanted it to so badlyalways the sign of a good movie right? I'd have to say that you'll want to skip this one.

title: A belly full of spices; but a meal totally devoid of nourishment!
review:
I suppose the best way to characterize my feelings about this technical exercise in special effects is to cite a very perceptive remark made by Frank Lloyd Wright many years ago when asked for an assessment of American television. His response was that television was "chewing gum for the eyes!" So, to paraphrase that great visionary let me say that Spielberg's "War Of The Worlds" is chewing gum for the brain - nothing more!

Hollywood now has an astonishing arsenal of special effects devices which are put to good use in this pathetic excuse for serious cinema. I am old enough to remember seeing the 1953 edition of this "invasion from Mars" story as a young boy. This film just doesn't measure up after you realize that it is little more than a catalog for what the special effects guys can do. Impressive though they may be, my brain can still do better!

The subplot of how this catastrophe helps bring a dysfunctional father back into the lives of his children consists largely of closeups of facial expressions of the actors. As a matter of fact, I had the feeling when leaving the theater afterward, that working on this turkey might explain Tom Cruise's recent bizarre behavior and comments about psychiatry and health issues. Could it be that working on this film has triggered his own bizarre behavior on topics about which he knows nothing; or should we just lay the blame on the brain-rot that comes from buying into bizarre pseudo-religions?

I can't remember any dialog, any music, substantial plot development, or virtually anything else except the chewing gum special effects overkill that took up two hours of my time.

In closing let me say that this product may just possibly win an Oscar for special effects making it appear historically much more important than it is. Yet, most of the great unwashed masses of people searching for sensual stimulation will rave about how "great" this film is. But then, they also think today's commercialized screaming is acceptable as musical art too!

title: Disappointing Mr. Spielberg.
review: I am an avid movie-goer but have been more disappointed by movies in these last two years than I have been for my ten odd 'movie-going' years before that. I have come to realise that movies dependent on heavy advertising and promotion are so for a reason: they need it to sell tickets. Armed with this knowledge I have managed to avoid the torture and anguish of sitting through much off the garbage-disguised-as-movies spewed out by Hollywood of late. Unfortunately, I did not think that the above rule of advertising applied to Steven Spielberg movies...I was wrong!! The following adjectives come to mind when I think of this movie: void, anti-climactic, vacant. It occurred to me as I left the theatre that Spielberg settles for nothing less than 'the best': protagonist, Tom Cruise, one of the best child actresses in Hollywood, Dakota Fanning, the greatest narrator of all time, Morgan Freeman and not least of all cutting-edge special effects. No complaints, but could there be a reason for this? Is it possible that, unlike some of the other great directors of Hollywood, Spielberg has no confidence in his abilities; so much so in fact that he needs 'the best' to distract us from what a movie is all about, the plot. The movie started out great...after the first five minutes I was excited for what was to come but then nothing did! As time went on I began to feel anxious as nothing (other than explosions and mass destruction) had happened and the end had to be near. I thought to myself "another one (director) bites the dust". The abruptness with which the movie ended seemed to me evidence of the fact that the film crew themselves were embarrassed by their own work and simply wanted, no, needed, this multi-million-dollar ordeal to end. The movie lacked any substance and quite frankly I wish Spielberg would fail miserably with it so that he might put a little more thought into his next project. Unfortunately I am certain that the propaganda alone will ensure that it is a success at the box office.

title: (Despite a few holes) this was one FANTASTIC "WAR" (minor spoilers ahead)
review:
I was skeptical going into this, like many of you, I am sure. The Cruise/Holmes angle...the Spielberg losing his touch angle (at least with his last two films 'Catch Me' and 'Terminal'.) So imagine my surprise when this turned out to be THE blockbuster summer movie bonanza I had been waiting for. Spielberg is back....and oh is he ever with a vengeance. This is most definitely not the auteur Spielberg at his Saving Private Ryan Schindler's List best, but this is rock 'em sock 'em give-it-to-them-and-leave-them-breathless Spielberg who made us s*** ourselves at the thought of going near the water or the thought of EVER visiting a Costa Rican island with a codgerly old man who keeps talking about mosquitoes and petrified amber.

Let's get the obvious out of the way first. Yes, you've heard correct. The special effects are seamless and AMAZING. I am blown away at how effortless his team (with the help of ILM) make this stuff look. It will truly blow you away. The scenes with the bridges and tunnels and ferries (oh my!) will leave you feeling as if you just went through this ordeal yourself. Spielberg often has a knack for doing this with action flicks. Providing you with a sense that you are right there with the protagonist (or in this case protagonists.) The camera work is almost hap-hazard, if you will, shooting from P.O.V. angles that aren't always associated with your basic summer action flare.

That being said, the most surprising thing to me was the way I actually did sort of care about these characters. I had read reviews (critical) saying that the movie was a spectacle of effects (IOW, amazing to look at, but not much depth.) I have to say, I could not disagree more. Tom Cruise (playing against type somewhat) was not the "know-it-all Scientology guru" who has (in recent months) become more famous for his views on anti-depressants and Katie Holmes-tonsil hockey than his actual acting skills. His character was incredibly flawed, unskilled, a lackey, a loser, if you will. We see him with his kids (who obviously couldn't care less if they were with dear old Dad or watching paint dry), and we see that he hasn't the first clue how to care for them. He is more like a big kid himself, someone who has never been forced to grow up. Until now. Without giving anything away, I will just say that the scene where Tom Cruise's character Ray comes back from his initial encounter with the tripod machines is INTENSELY REAL. Both my friend and I commented that it was 10 of the most intense and unnerving minutes of the film. The reactions of Ray and his kids plays out realistically (frantically grabbing batteries and peanut butter?) while not knowing what to do or say. Dakota Fanning (Ray's daughter Rachel) will BLOW you away. Much like Haley Joel Osment in The Sixth Sense, this just might be mainstream bravura Oscar-caliber.

It's not to say that this film is flawless. There are certainly several loopholes (how did the guy with camera have the only working electronic device in NJ exactly?) However, it makes for a pretty fun popcorn ride. I hate to really give anything away, for those of you who have not read the book or are unfamiliar with the plot, however, the film sticks pretty close to it. It's just nice to see it in the hands of someone like Spielberg, so that we can see a truly great action/adventure director return to form, and not leave the theater disappointed.

4.5 out of 5 stars.

title: War of the Worlds: A War of Inept Film-making
review:
This film is just another in a long line of failed blockbusters, only this time, it's headed by the biggest and some say best director of our time. While that may be true, his films since Schindler's List have been in stark contrast with the films he directed before that film. Even Jurassic Park from the same year was an amazing piece of action and adventure directing from a man who basically invented the summer blockbuster. But since his very personal film in Schindler, the man has changed. He has become "The Beard," and I don't really like where he's headed.

Spoiler Warning!

This movie is a mindfuck of blasé film-making. I could go into lengthy paragraph after lengthy paragraph on the matter, but let's get to the heart of the matter instead. The big problems include:

1) The humans are never able to mount an offensive against the aliens, essentially rendering the entire film a chase movie until blind luck finds its way to the human side. 2) Dakota Fanning screams throughout the entire film. In fact, if I didn't know better, I'd say she was the definite lovechild of Spielberg and Kate Capshaw, as she pretty much acts like Capshaw's character in Temple of Doom. 3) The music blows -- a lackluster performance from John Williams all around (and it's not often you can say that about the man.) 4) This film attempts to be a drama/horror film, something that Spielberg is much less adept at than, say, adventure. This film could've been a great adventure film, but Spielberg really went the Signs route here (except it's much much more boring and banal.) 5) The aliens are lame and they aren't scary at all. What kind of retro nonsense is that Tripod design, anyway? 6) There are literally three lines of humorous material. And since the action/adventure isn't there, this one is a total snooze because of it. Oh, and the line about the terrorists from Fanning is groan-inducing. 7) Kaminski, the cinematographer, really needs to get out in the sun a bit more. His blue motif is wearing thin for me these days and it's really bogging down Spielberg as a director in my opinion as well (this is the guy who Spielberg has used ever since Schindler's List, and it shows. Spielberg used to bounce back and forth between many cinematographers because he wanted his own vision moreso than someone else's. But Kaminski has changed that and it's a shame to see the majority of Spielberg's films these days feel so cold and heartless.) 8) The action pieces are crappy at best. 9) The decision to stay with just Cruise for the entire film doesn't work at all. Whereas in Signs, at least the characters were semi-interesting, but we don't have that here. Cruise, his daughter, and his son are paper-thin in terms of character development. 10) The biggest problem lies in #1, and the result is a very lackluster ending. The aliens don't get beat by humans, but rather by a derivative plot device. Then Spielberg tries to turn on the tears, and the result is uncharacteristically flat and empty.

This is Spielberg's worst movie since The Lost World. And it feels very much the same in terms of shoddy character development, lame plot, and poor characterization. Just like I asked when I reviewed that film, where is the wonder and excitement from earlier in Spielberg's career? I'm very disappointed in the direction that Spielberg is taking his film-making these days, and frankly, I'm starting to look forward to other directors' projects (like King Kong by Peter Jackson, for example) much moreso than his at this point. I grew up with the kind and wonderful aliens of Close Encounters of the 3rd Kind and E.T. and now I'm given a very jaded opposition to those films in War of the Worlds. At least A.I. made me think. This film doesn't even allow me to turn on my brain.

I'm sorry you've become so disenchanted with your films and the world itself, but there's no reason to take it out on the rest of us, Steven.

Sincerely, An Old Fan

P.S. Independence Day blew your film away by miles, sir.

title: Swann's Way
review:
Spielberg is usually smarter than this, because this was doomed from the very beginning. Forget that nowadays if Cruise is in the thing, it has to be stretched from something whole to a platform for his posturing.

But quite apart from that there were already two excellent achievements for this. First we had the book, which has excellent energy: mechanical beasts as languid swans among us. Consummate language of inevitability.

Then we had Orson Welles on Wells; the radio drama that blurred the definition of sight. Yes, this is about sight and always has been. The 1953 version acknowledged this and took out all the religious stuff and replaced it with things whose sight is lethal. And what things those eyes were! Designed on Mars to emulate beaux art wrapping of what in the fifties was considered the ultimate in high tech vision: the three dots of color TeeVee. The saucers in this case were floating on legs of electricity and exterminated gracefully.

Sure, it was essentially a chase movie, but a chase of an eye following poor souls. What could be more cinematic? On the heels of this our genius in Hollywood decides to take the same material and scrub all the cinematic value out of it. Sure, he could have approached it with the same intelligence as "Close Encounters," which was a French New Wave film about the creative discovery of imagination. It was essentially a movie about movies.

Perhaps he didn't know. Perhaps he just didn't have time: this was pushed up two years ahead of schedule. Perhaps he just didn't care, since all his efforts at intelligent and meaningful film-making just blend into his more mundane commercial successes.

But he does know how to stage a scene that manages motion: the orchestrated motion of camera, foreground and often opposing motion in the background. He doesn't do well in three dimensions and you can see every static storyboard along the way. But when he's good at vision, he's good.

Plus. Plus this gives the opportunity of the extra motion of the swans, which is how Wells described the ships.

But no dance here, no cinematic composition. And no languid ships. These are a cross between the monsters of "Wild Wild West" and "Star Wars." At least those were apt. These ships clunk and grind. They destroy and collect. Their eyes and weapons are different from each other. Instead of being otherworldly, they seem distinctly human, as if they were designed by Lex Luthor.

Okay, so the story changes focus from being about invaders to being about Tom and kids. Even Mel Gibson in his basement was more engaging, and that's pretty damning.

One final insult. This starts the same as the 1953 movie, with a narrator giving background. With Wells always in our minds, who is selected? Morgan Freeman. You may even like his avuncular, low key acting-as-appearance. But as he who introduces doom? No.

Ted's Evaluation: 1 of 3 -- You can find something better to do with this part of your life.

title: A mind-blowing yet chilling experience
review:
Quite possibly the best film i have seen in a long time. Possibly Spielbergs best so far. Choosing to focus on the small family figures is far more emotional and personal that focusing on the "players" so to speak i.e. the president and hero's". The first film since "vertigo" in which the protagonist spends the entire film running from the danger. Cruise plays a part in this unlike hes previous roles. He is in fact an complete B*****d, a bad father and a natural coward, but the movies portrayal of his change in character to protect his children is far better than watching even the special effects which wow for all the right reasons - they loom in the background but are never the focus of the cameras attention. The brilliant use of sound (this is one that NEEDS to be seen in the cinema) is chilling at its worst. It gives the film the constantly oppressive feel it has.

however i was surprised to see the film with such a low rating. 15 would have been far more appropriate. I'm not suggesting 12 year olds are too young to see it, but bringing in younger children would definitely be disturbing for them. i left the cinema at midnight mildly disturbed by some of the material the film brought up (read genocide, blatant murder for the need to survive, paedophilia and others which would be spoilers.

This is definitely not a reason to miss out though. A brilliant film, the years must see so far as well as batman begins

title: Nothing Special
review:
Spielberg once again fails to make a spectacular movie, and I'm beginning to wonder why he's considered to be among the greatest directors of all time.

It's not that this film is bad, it's just that it's not good, if that makes any sense. The storyline is average, and the special effects are good, but since when have effects been what makes a movie good?

We've got the typical depiction of an average guy as an action hero. The chances of surviving one attack from the alien tripods is slim to none, yet Ray (Tom Cruise) survives five attacks, two encounters with their tentacle-things, and a close encounter with at least three aliens, manages to single handedly take out a tripod, AND MAKES IT OUT WITHOUT A SCRATCH ON HIM! Well he had had some scratches, but you know what I mean.

There are plot holes everywhere, and one of the most disappointing endings I have ever seen. I'm not talking about the classic "bacteria kills aliens" ending; I've always loved that. About half way through the film, the son abandons his father and sister, even after they spent so much time building up his character to be a good guy. The military is attacking the aliens and he's like "I need to see this!" and, at least during the scene, the both he and Tom are overacting to the point of dread. Anyway, Tom leaves him and as soon as he does, the entire ridge Robbie (the son) was on explodes and becomes engulfed in flames. This all takes place around Connecticut. At the end of the movie, Tom arrives with his daughter in Boston at his ex-wife's parent's house. Everyone walks out, with a nice cameo by Gene Barry and Ann Robinson as the parents. Tom's character is watching, the from behind everyone, comes Robbie. BULL! Not only was there no way Robbie could have survived, but the fact that he still managed to beat his dad and sister to Boston is simply impossible. This scene ruined the feel of the movie for me, and I know I'm not the only one out there.

Another problem I have is it's extremely predictable. Then again, what isn't anymore?

All in all, this is just a special effects show with an average plot. As far as invasion movies go, I'd have to say Independence Day was better. War of the Worlds took itself too seriously and spent far too much time trying to develop a story, while Independence Day accepted the fact that it wasn't a story and spent more time being entertaining.

title: Anti-climax to the max...
review:
When I get excited about seeing a particular movie it quite often turns out to be a disappointment. This certainly rings true for "War Of The Worlds (2005)". The tension builds.. and builds. The special effects are excellent. The acting ranges from good (Tom Cruise) to phenomenal (Dakota Fanning). The movie picks up the pace from the get-go. It's a roller coaster ride right up until the time when you start to think: "so... where is this all leading to..."? That's when things totally fall apart. There is no story to speak of. When the credits rolled I was left wondering "why did I pay 9 euros and 2 hours of my life watching "this"? It's not a pretty sight folks. The idea of aliens invading earth has so much potential. It could have been a classic. It could have been a trilogy. It could have been a thriller/feel good/action/horror movie all rolled into one. It's a actually... a dud. The final 10 minutes are so anti-climax, it's not even funny. It might be true to the book (haven't read it) but it certainly doesn't work for me personally in the cinema.

It's not as bad as "Any Given Sunday" though...

title: It stinks. It really does.
review:
For you effects lovers who don't care about much else, stop reading and see a matinée. For the rest of you that think effects should be subservient to worthwhile plot and well-crafted editing, read on. (I'll be as brief as IMDb allows).

As others have said, the first 45 minutes or so of this flick are worthwhile. Good tension-building and good action. It's a steady and painful decline from there until, after a couple of unintentionally funny military lines, your jaw drops in utter horror at how ridiculously Spielberg finished the film.

WotW gets 3 stars from me because the first 45 minutes were a 7 the ensuing 1'15" a 1. Please don't support this kind of substandard entertainment by paying full box office price as I foolishly did. I should have surmised that the advertising onslaught was a desperate attempt to rack up as much 1st week cash as possible before the word got out about how bad this film is.

title: Disappointing
review: Like the child I was in 1954 when I first saw War of the Worlds at my local theater, I awaited with great excitement the return of the movie that most affected my childhood. I had previously seen a UFO and seriously believed that an invasion could happen. That movie scared me so badly I couldn't sleep for days without frequently looking out my bedroom window expecting to see the tripods! I instead this time fall asleep counting the flaws in this movie. I expected this time around, after 51 years, really creative ways to scare the hell out of us. I wondered how Spielberg was going to recreate that fear that he surely felt (since we are about the same age) when he first saw it. It may have been scarier if I was still 7 years old, but to an adult an Alien it was not. More credible ways on how the aliens got here, in light of all the UFO lore available to us now, could have been used- like gigantic triangle shaped mother ships releasing tripod shaped battle tanks. The original movie had them arriving as projectiles from Mars. For its day the original tripod craft were much more frightening than Spielberg's. Compare the original 1953 version to this movie, and corny acting aside, see if you think Spielberg made a significant improvement. I think not.

title: Edge of your seat - Spielberg at his best!
review:
Look first things first..this is a remake of the 1953 War of the Worlds movie starring Gene Barry. A classic movie and the special effects for it's time were quite good.

Having said that, this new War of the Worlds is not your Daddy's War of the Worlds. Sure in our age of movie magic, special effects have to be better...but WOW!! I don't think I'll be able to watch this on DVD with my surround system because my neighbors will surely lose their picture off their walls because the sound was incredible.

The movie starts off with some character development and that shows poorly for Mr. Cruise. With his recent negativity in the news lately, it only makes you dislike him even more but that's good acting and scripting too! He's just not a good father and doesn't seem to want to try to be either.

His children are with him only because it's probably in the divorce agreement. They really don't know him and he surely doesn't know them, but he's about to spend some quality time with them soon enough! Once the strange storms start up around the world....all hell breaks loose. I don't want to give much away here but again if you know anything about movies and the original, there is a martian invasion. But did they just come down now or have they been here for years? That's the question. Once they are here however, Tom Cruise realizes that now, more than ever..he needs to be a father...a hero..and mainly to his children. That won't be easy but you'll have to see how he does for yourself.

Cruise was very convincing in his role but Dakota Fanning as usual, stole the show. This young lady is going to be a phenomenal star (as if she isn't already). She has out shined such veteran stars as Denzel Washington, Robert De Niro and Sean Penn. Watch for a best actress nomination for this young star!

I loved this movie and though the ending was a bit abrupt, there really wasn't much more Spielberg could have done with it. As far as remakes go however, this is one of the best you'll ever see! Check it out and prove me wrong! Enjoy! Sam

title: Should've won the 3 Oscars it was nominated for!
review: I kind of remember seeing in the theater, that was fun! Visually striking and masterful sound extravaganza. War of the Worlds is highly under appreciated, thought provoking and very engaging. Tom Cruise did great, I'm blown away this film even got hate really doesn't deserve it. Steven Spielberg is a legendary filmmaker and always will be no matter what he's artist with great vision.

title: absurd with a disgusting aftertaste
review:
Nicely shot movie. I just don't understand how aliens who can travel through space and who had all the time in the world to research our world didn't think of microbes. That's just absurd.
Another thing that was expected but still left a bad test on my mouth is the revelation at the end that Robbie is alive and well with his family. I mean come on. He is one of the most disgusting, crazy and selfish characters I have ever seen in movies. The guy deserved to be killed.

title: Very Disappointing
review: Should have been better than Independence Day (I.D. hereafter) but was not even as good. Better acting than I.D. but not as entertaining. The problem is when Spielberg tries to mix powerful acting with hardcore action - it just wasn't convincing. Most of the focus was on one families' struggle where as I feel most people in the cinema would have preferred more focus on the action (as in I.D.). There was a really long, boring section mid-way through the film where Cruise and his daughter get stuck in a basement or something - nothing really happens in this part. Special effects are good of course as one would expect - Aliens somewhat reminiscent of those in I.D. as well, maybe they're the same ones!

title: To sum up, the movie sucks!
review:
I saw the trailer at the cinema and thought: Finally a trailer that doesn't show the best part of the movie!

However after seeing the movie I must say, that the marketing really people did their best at the trailer. They simply didn't have anything amazing to show!

To sum up, the movie sucks! If you liked "The Day After Tomorrow" and/or "Signs", you might like this one, otherwise just skip it. I know it has Tom Cruise and was directed by Steven Spielberg, but don't let it fool you, I isn't not a bit as good as Minority Report.

Save your money!

title: Not worth a $8 movie ticket
review:
This is a standard run-of-the-mill alien movie. There's no real point to the movie and then it just ends. My wife and I were both not impressed.

The young girl, Dakota Fanning, is excellent once again. Although her character spends the entire 2 hours crying and being scared, it's still an impressive amount of acting.

Rent the movie if you really want to see it. You won't have missed much. I think Steven Spielberg just needs to quit doing alien movies by now. Between this and Artificial Intelligence, he should hopefully get the point.

title: Independence Day is better
review: War of the Worlds was not realistic enough to keep me interested. Obviously, the movie is meant to be fiction, but the least they could've done is stayed realistic within the fiction world they created in the movie. There are too many coincidental things happening to the family in this movie. I enjoy a good fantasy movie any day, but I just couldn't believe that things would've happened the way they did in this movie and it ruined my ability to enjoy the movie and enter the fiction world it created. In Independence Day, at least the President's wife dies and the plot is realistic within a world being attacked by aliens. When War of the Worlds ended, I was surprised it was over and was left feeling confused and disappointed. If you want to see a good alien movie, this is not the one to see. Tom Cruise and Dakota Fanning are great, but the movie itself is really not worth watching. War of the Worlds would be a box office bomb and no one would give it a second look if the names Steven Spielberg and Tom Cruise weren't associated with it.

review:
OK let me get this straight..These aliens planned this for a millions of years and in couple of days they get wiped out.. come ON be more realistic..
