title: The main storyline deals with a girl trying to find her mommy.
review: At the beginning of the movie, it was okay but then it went downhill. Before the aliens came the movie was about this family and then the aliens came and they looked liked giant cameras with wires sticking out on a tripod. then they amazingly got a car that actually worked when no other car worked which was unrealistic. The girl was obnoxious, she would not shut up and only wanted her mommy, she was okay at the beginning before the aliens came because she was not a screaming idiot. as soon as they got to the moms house she was not there and the next day there was a plane crash and they did not hear it or feel it which is could not happen and then the rest of the movie was focused on the girl getting to her mommy(what a bore). I've watched other movies directed by Steven Speilburg and he made the aliens act like the dinosaurs in Jurassic park which was more realistic than this crap because the dinosaurs had a reason called instincts, aliens are supposed to be smarter than us considering they built those suits and would have a reason to exterminate us and would have done there research and find that bacteria could kill them. other unrealistic things about this movie is that Robbie wants to all of a sudden join the army twice even though he never mentions it before in the movie.When Robbie joined the military he survived a massive explosion which no one could have survived, another thing that could not happen is that when one guy got sucked into the machine from the big metal basket no one care but when the main character got in everyone tried to get him out but did'not care about the other guy, other scenes like these happen in the movie which make some people ask themselves that watch the movie why were those people the only ones that lived through everything and the military.The ending was happy and it showed the girl running to her mommy which was what the movie was based on and they show Robbie miraculously still alive and surprisingly once they get to Boston all the aliens die at once which if there was that many aliens it would take years for them all to die off. don't spend your money on this junk, go see batman begins or Charlie and the chocolate factory.

title: Terrible movie
review: The special effects were few and repetitive. It was the same alien spider machines over and over. We did get to see the alien critters for a few seconds, but it was too little. There were too many close ups. Seeing a close up of a peanut butter sandwich, for instance, doesn't do much for me. There were too many dark, murky scenes. Maybe this is supposed to have something to do with fear. I though it had to do with minimal sets. In short, it was the least movie playing for the most money. Too much of the time Cruise and his kids were screaming at each other, or just screaming. It's as though the kids were completely unawares of the situation, and could only scream or fight Cruise at every turn. That doesn't say much for kids. To me, this movie had no socially redeeming value. Is it then pornography? *********SPOILERS**************** The inclusion of the potential pedophile and his murder by Cruise was gratuitous and unnecessary.

title: Shyamalan syndrome
review:
This movie suffers from what might be called Shyamalan syndrome after the creator of Signs (with Mel Gibson and Joaquin Phoenix), although the problem may well have originated with Wells' original version (I haven't read it).

The problem is this: a species of aliens with infinitely superior technology, capable of crossing light-years and possessing weapons of mass destruction that brings the Earth to it's knees are suddenly killed off by a trivial factor. I think the term for this is deus-ex-machina, or god from the machine, where in plays the plot complications would be seemingly hopelessly complicated and some guy playing a god would get lowered down from a crane, point his finger around and tidy everything up. Given the inability of the writers to make a convincing resolution to the complex problems they created, they instead wave a magic wand and *poof* problems solved.

So in Signs, the technologically advanced (albeit slow moving) aliens take over the world but fail to notice that water, which covers 2/3 of the planet, is highly toxic to them. All one needs is a Louisville slugger and a few cleverly-placed glasses of water to defeat the advanced race. In War of the Worlds, they pretty much have the planet toasting like a marshmallow over the barbecue after watching the planet for a million years or so, and then are killed by microorganisms.

Folks, even us humans would be smart enough to look into the microorganism situation if we went to another planet. Maybe send a few probes to check things out, etc. Even a Star Trek expendable-guy-in-the-red-shirt to act like a canary in a coal-mine. Nope, these interstellar travelers just cavalierly marched in, obliviously incinerating things left and right. They probably even left the gas caps unscrewed on the tripods, flicking cigarette ashes out the window while they drove.

The movie was *okay*, the special effects amazing, the 9/11 references disturbing, but the ending was just crap. "Oh yeah, some germs killed them..." I thought Independence Day solution with with the computer virus was a lot more believable. Okay so we have to believe that the aliens to open email attachments, but at least it was creative, even poetic.

title: A weak adaptation of a great story
review:
Have seen this film twice now and I feel it gets worse with each viewing. War of the Worlds is my favourite piece of modern fiction and this film turns what is an exciting and thought provoking book into a simple, populist drama. The characters are very weak, especially Tom Cruise's son who appears to act in a most bizarre and fake fashion. His kids are foul. Tim Robbins is wasted and merges three characters from the book into a simple loopy and shell shocked survivor. The lovely Thunderchild sequence with the steamer trying to escape is slashed into another 'ooooh' moment with the capsized ship. The action is poor, the artilleryman and his soldiers being replaced with a half-hearted army attack on the hill.

With one of the greatest director's in history, a good cast and limitless money this film is nowhere near what it should have been. In my opinion Signs was better at the drama and suspense of alien invasion, Independence Day was better for a depiction of the fall of mankind.

The Good: There are a few good points. First, the photography and landscapes were at times lovely. The tripod effects were good from a distance, not that great up close. Dakota Fanning was good, not amazing but good

The Bad: All of the characters were pretty grim The Boston end sequence Over the top 'action' and 'shocks' at the expense of story and characterization Morgan Freeman as the narrator. After Richard Burton we have been spoilt Relocation to 'anytown' USA and modern times

title: Slow movie with Unbearably bratty kids
review:
I saw the trailer on Oprah, and it looked really good. Too bad I went to see the movie because the best parts were in that trailer.

To be fair, the movie begins well -- nice set up of the characters, interesting, suspenseful beginning. Then it gets old really, really fast.

What also caught me by surprise was how unbelievably bratty and maddening the kids were. If there were a theme to the movie, it would be that parents' love is unconditional. I would have left them in a hurry (and I don't feel bad about saying that -- someone wrote the characters with very little redeeming qualities except for the fact that they are someone's kids). The little girl is beautiful -- except when she's covered in ash -- then she looks ghostly and is eerily frightening, like she was taken out of a horror movie & misplaced in this one. She is a good actress, though, and when she let out her high pitched girlie scream (several times in the movie), I really wanted to commit physical violence -- and I'm known for my gentle nature, no joke. Same with her brother -- over-teen-aged kid who wants to "join the action" -- never mind that the action is a many-legged, bloodsucking space alien -- does he have a brain??? I wanted to leave several times during the movie; and I wanted to throttle the kid characters several more times. I only made it through because I was writing this blurb in my head. Thank goodness I went to the matinée and didn't pay full price. If you saw the trailer, you saw enough.

title: $30 million to run around screaming?
review:
Alright. Let's see if I can get this straight.

In every other movie where our species/planet is threatened, one can usually the human protagonist to figure out exactly what to do to save our sorry skins. I find it hard to believe that so many people thoroughly enjoyed this movie where the human protagonists run around screaming for an hour and a half and, finally, 10 minutes from the end, the bad guys just start dying with no help from us. Don't know how much Cruise got paid for this job but I'm sure he got paid lots to do nothing! Now I read the book years ago and so knew how the book ended - I kinda expected that they'd edit the ending a bit to make it a bit more interesting.

My reaction when I left the movie theatre? "Meh."

title: This movie REALLY sucked.
review:
There is not cohesive plot. Tom Cruise's character is a moron with no redemption value at all as a human being. The teenage son is annoying as hell, e.g., he "must see" what's going on behind the hill with the army battling the aliens. Idiot kid! Death is happening behind the hills, if you had any common sense you flee the other way. Dakota Fanning manage to pierce both my ear drums with her incessant screaming.

Really annoy plot holes: A plane crashes over them and levels everything in the neighborhood...yet their convenient get-away mini van doesn't have a scratch on it... not only that, the random crash leaves a nice clear path for them to drive away. Additionally, some how the aliens were so wise as to bury their mega-death tripod killing machines in all the urban centers. How the hell did they know where the cities would be built on? REFUND PLEASE!

title: They have arrived and there's nothing we can do to stop them.
review:
Warning, since I'm not quite sure what I'm going to type, this may contain a spoiler.

I just got back from seeing War of the Worlds and I must say, I was very impressed. I had heard about the original radio broadcast and had a vague idea of the plot, but I really had no idea what to expect from the movie. After being disappointed in a few recent Tom Cruise films (The Last Samurai, Minority Report to name a couple), I was not expecting much from him. However much like Collateral, I was pleasantly surprised in this film.

The plot of the movie itself now seems unoriginal (although when War of the Worlds was first published, I'm sure it seemed much more original), but it was an entertaining film. It managed to be suspenseful even though the outcome of the movie was foreseeable from the very beginning.

However, as much as I enjoyed the film, I have three complaints. My first two are just small complaints, but complaints none the less. At the beginning of the film when the "lightning storm" hits New York around Ray's (Tom Cruise) house, all the electrical devices stop working. However, one man continues to film the machine, and his camera still works. This continuity error stuck out like a sore thumb and was quite distracting from the going ons in the film. My second complaint is another "convenient mistake" in the film. When Ray, Robbie and Rachel arrive at their mother's place and hide in the basement, a plane crashes and destroys almost the entire house and everything around it. However, the van (which was parked right in front of the house) was completely undamaged despite all the damage around it.

My third complaint is about the plot itself. The end of the movie was very weak. It didn't sum up anything and nothing was really solved. It was almost as if Steven Spielberg decided "Ok, I'm out of ideas. Screw it, let's just end the movie." However, despite these complaints, War of the Worlds was an awesome movie and is right up there with Batman Begins as my favourite movie of the year. I give it 9/10.

title: Worth the wait (until it comes out on DVD) or maybe TV.
review: For starters, not funny, not scary, not technically accurate, bordering on boring. I think there was one funny line in the entire script and I already forgot what it was. Not one scary moment in the movie. Some really unbelievable technical goofs: the camcorder; how come Tom Cruise is the only person in the US that guessed that everyones starter solenoid is defective. Why does the ferry work perfectly and every other mechanical device on the east coast fail to work. How come the military vehicles work fine but everyone else's vehicle is dead? The list goes on and on. One would also hope for at least on or two twists in the plot. Went with 5 people and got five thumbs down.......

title: awesome up until the end
review: SPOILER WARNING This was turning into one of the best sci-fi/action movies ever up until the utterly ridiculous Hollywood ending. How is the entire world decimated by the aliens, but a pregnant lady and her old parents have just been chilling in their house while the world is destroyed? They all were spit shine clean and look like they were ready for a nice family outing to the park or something. And don't even get me started on how in hell the kid made it out of that huge fireball explosion. On top of that, why didn't grandma and grandpa let him take a shower and put on some newly washed clothes like they obviously had been doing? Spielberg should know better than to put this at the end of what could have been a sci-fi classic.

title: War of the Worlds - A Disappointment
review:
Steven Spielberg has unfortunately missed the mark with a film that can best be described as hollow. The outstanding special effects and Spielberg's unequaled attention to camera angles and imagery cannot be saved by a screen play lacking in character and plot development.

Dakota Fleming gives the best performance in the film as Tom Cruise's daughter. Her character at least shows depth and feeling. Even Tom Cruise's acting ability doesn't provide any depth to his character as he can't rescue a flat screen play.

The special effects allow snippets of brilliance but there is nothing to unite them together into a story. The only characters that are of any depth in the plot are Cruise and his two kids. Other than the edge caused by his being a divorced dad seeing his kids on the weekend and their anger towards their dad, there is no further character development. The movie would have benefited greatly from other characters being introduced and developed beyond their shear terror in reaction to the invasion.

To make matters worse, the ending of the movie falls flat and appears as if it is nothing more than an afterthought. Some set up would have been nice.

If asked to go see this movie, you might consider doing something more important ... like washing your hair!

title: Shame on Spielberg
review: I rented this movie because my local video store sent me a 99 cent coupon and I knew that was all it was worth. I was right. Spielberg should be ashame that he attached his name to this junk. The screenwriter should be drawn and quartered, tarred and feathered and then burned at the stake. Too harsh, well we laughed through the first hour as stupid people stood around while others were being disintegrate. Then we cringed ourselves as Dakota Fanning just kept screaming. Then we just wanted to shut them all up. At the end we sat in disbelief when a character thought dead shows up miraculously. What major ridiculous junk.

title: Worse ever
review:
A rating of "awful" is fair for this movie. I have never seen such a bad movie, even comparing to the cheesy sci fi's from the 1950's. The main problem with this movie is how offensive the cast are and the lack of plot. The plot is not the same as H.G. Well's book, not even close.

Tom is not too bad, other then his character is unreal, disjointed, and acts as a complete supplicant to his offspring. The little girl is the typical sick representation of a brat that Spielberg seems to be obsessed with. A mouthy brat girl who always observes important events first, out smarts all adults, and asks questions well above her age group. There is something deeply wrong with Spielberg. The brat son was essentially the same. All three primary characters, and the freak in the farm cellar, were not related to anything real, they were non-human characters. I've seen Japanese Anime with much more believable characters.

The only reason I can conjure that motivated these people to make this trash movie is some kind of agenda to make Americans stupid and empower children over their dumb and impotent parents. Now that theory is the only good sci fi in this flick.

title: Ladies and Gentlemen, we've brought back the alien invasion movie!
review: No matter how corny or comedic the old alien invasion movies may seem, or how many times they have you left in stitches towards the end, there is nothing funny about Steven Spielberg's version of the H. G. Wells novel. This movie is by all intents and purposes, perfect. I have never before been so terrified during a movie, and it's not even in the horror genre. This adaptation of a classic novel just proves that Steven Spielberg still has what it takes to entertain today's de-sensitized audience by combining a tragic and disastrous plot, equally mind-numbing visual effects, terrifying sound effects, and a cast that effortlessly pulled off the momentous task of conveying a truly catastrophic storyline. There was a constant fear and panic upon every face of the actors. This movie truly brought out the worst in humanity in the face of such utter loss of hope and fright. I loved how you had the sense of panic right along with the characters as if it was utterly impossible to get away from the machines. You had a feeling of "they're gonna GET you!" the entire movie. And when the aliens began dying off, it was such a great move to have the tripods walking around in erratic circles, as if the machines themselves had become infected. I was deeply impressed by this one that I saw it in the theater at least 5 times and now own it on DVD. It's definitely one of the movies that I'll continue to watch over and over, with the same foreboding chill running up my spine when the machines first emerge from the ground. This is a serious movie for all those parodies and cheesy alien flicks that make you giggle. This insanely realistic alien invasion (if there is such a thing) is a perfect 10 in my book! :)

title: Best Movie I've Ever Seen!!!
review: Those who say this movie is "horrible", I don't think they were paying attention to the movie. This is "Definitely" Tom Cruises best performance!!! The Tripods were Absolutely Chilling and frightening to see. I felt like I was actually experiencing the things in the movie. I have a feeling that the events that happened in this movie will happen someday in the far/near future!!! Those who are into Sci-Fi films should definitely see this thrilling movie. You should see this movie while it's still in the theater, because the bigger and louder the film is the better it is!!! Again to the people who seen and disliked the movie, I suggest you go see it again, and pay attention this time.

title: This didn't seem like a Spielberg movie....
review:
....in that it was too crap. OK, first off the special effects were amazing. BUt I always thought Spielberg had movies with good stories that brought something original to the party. WOTW seemed like it could have been done by any action movie director - Michael Bay maybe :-S

OK not much time but things that got to me:

1) If the aliens coveted our planet for a million years, why didn't they just take over before humans existed? Even cavemen could have been exterminated with a pointy stick. 2) How come Tom Cruise ALWAYS seemed to be the prime target for the tripods etc? Out of all the thousands of people crowding the streets...BUt despite this he always managed to avoid their superior technology and weapons. 3)On that note, if it was "an extermination" why not bomb us or gas us or release a selective plague upon us? Instead, the MASSSIVE tripods weapon of choice was laser weapons to take humans out one at a time?!?!!? 4) Also, with their superior technology how come they had no infrared, x-ray etc sensors. All that stuff is common on our own war machines. It would make it a lot less simple to "hide behind a mirror". 5) OK, why WAS Tom Cruises car the ONLY one working. He was lucky?....Hmmm, more story please. 6) The aliens used human blood to fertilise their red weed? This sounds too B-grade to be expanded upon...Sufice to say, with all the species to choose from on earth, are we REALLY the best candidate for fertiliser from an economic point of view?. Ahem - think about The Matrix on his point too... 7) OK, I know people are dumb, but how many of you guys would have stood around while that first tripod emerged? Especially when, like Tom Cruise, every crack in the ground and falling object seemed to have his name all over it?

OK that's all can think of on my short lunch break. My final words are: Average for an action movie - crap for a Spielberg movie.

title: disappointing
review:
I was disappointed in War of the Worlds. I must admit that I am not a fan of science fiction in the first place, but at the very least, I did expect to be able to follow a story line and be subjected to a bit of real suspense. However, there was no real story...just "hide and stay out of their way". There was no suspense...just a lot of grimaces and wide-eyed looks from Tom Cruise and screams from Dakota Fannning. I never once was convinced by the acting that they were going to be 'taken'. (no suspense) Throughout the movie I wondered about the children's mother and family...but not a hint about them until the end...and even then, no explanations. (including that would have at least have made a 'story' out of the script) And not a word about the son's activity/adventure after he left his dad and sister...weak!! So, as I said...NO story! The aliens were sad as well...no "personality", just plodding and zapping. And what was the deal with spewing blood? It made no sense..again, no explanation or reason for it.

In summary, the alien/machines appear..a crowd gathers..everyone screams and runs (lots of running crowds!!)..some get zapped..Tom survives...repeat, repeat, repeat, repeat. The statement at the end was the best part of the whole movie!

title: PLOT SPOILERS? there's no plot to spoil.......
review:
First of all, I'll get the plot spoilers out of the way. Tom Cruise has an inconsequential job as a dock worker in new york, and two kids, and a ex wife situation. Then, while he's looking after them for the weekend, aliens come down from the sky "through the lightning" into the ground, into their mass killing metal tripod machines, which were "buried there all along". Before you know it, said machines are "everywhere", of course we only see the ones wreaking havoc in America, cos thats the only place that matters.

More havoc, violence, raygun zapping/vaporising of white middle class American humans ensues, with cruise doing the honorable thing and running away from them. Then, more of that. Then, bit more. Then, they get his daughter, and cruise suddenly turns commando and personally impregnates a couple of hand grenades up the tripod's bum and they all die.

Then, get this. The voice over at the end explains how they were all doomed from the start, because of their inability to resist our germs and viruses that we have on this planet, and thats what killed them after all.

Us and them both. If we continue to tolerate this sort of parasitic mindless twaddle in cinemas any longer, we shall surely perish. It is painful. It is insulting. It is pathetic. It is offensive. It is willfully ignorant. It is cheap.

Why go to the cinema to see rivers of blood, hundreds of bodies mowed down vacantly, and utter chaos and destruction? Why not go to Iraq, or Rwanda, or Afghanistan, or Darfur, and see it first hand. America produced and directed all four of them by the way.

Of course, it could never happen here, cos we are America, and only evil aliens that have "been planning this for years" could possibly make us refugees. Hence the validity of this film? Er, no.

Some films make you think, while you're watching them, about 5, 10, 20 things even. War of the worlds did not have sufficient plot or character to give cause to think about anything, once, at all ever.

The only thing i realized whilst watching, is that the kind of learned helplessness that sedated audiences viewing it are reinforcing is an invaluable tool for the Hollywood-military- governmental agenda; hence we are being programmed that war is normal, and don't try and stop it, just comply, fight, and die.

By the way, if it was the bugs that killed the aliens, then how the heck did they manage to build and bury their tripods underground all those years ago. This film explains nothing, gives nothing, offers nothing, inspires nothing. Please don't see it.

title: pure claptrap
review: disastrous, pretentious, exploitative, and over-hyped to the extreme, it is easy to see why Hollywood's box office receipts are down when this load of claptrap is billed as the best movie of the summer. spielberg must have pulled in a lot of IOUs from the critics to save this one from the horrid reviews it deserves. derivative in every significant way and pointless in every way, the movie ends with the kind of ra-ra silliness that would have been appropriate to a 1950s horror flick like the Blob. A poor effort from everyone involved. Should be ashamed of themselves. People in our audience were literally laughing and booing at the ending. even for sentimental spielberg, this takes the cake. avoid at all cost. worse than AI even, and that was hard to beat. such a disappointment given the promise of Minority Report.

title: Enjoyable, but not "Earth shattering".
review:
Keep in mind that I watch movies totally for enjoyment and rate them on that basis only. I'll leave the technical discussions to those with more knowledge in that area.

Things I liked about this movie: 1) Cool effects. The Martians were awesome. The destruction of humans, buildings & such was great and seamless. No hokey effects here! 2) Acting was believable---could have been better tho.

Things I did not like about this movie: 1) Annoying sub-plot with Cruise & his family. That stuff doesn't belong in a sci-fi movie. (They did that crap in Starwars II also and it sucked.) If Cruise wants to play the daddy role, then find another movie to do it in. 2) Could have used more visuals of the Martians and more intensity when the humans' weaponry is being destroyed---you know, like tanks flying up in the air and exploding, planes crashing into stuff when they're beamed, etc. 3) Somehow it needed a little more explanation. You don't know where the Martians came from unless you've either read the novel or seen the original movie. And you have to guess at the atrocities they were using the humans for (of course if it's just for drinking the blood, then you've got another vampire movie on your hands) Why did they turn the humans to dust at first instead of capture them? And another thing, they should have explained how the Martian tripods got underground. I know the crazy guy said they were there for millions of years, but he wasn't believable.

I really enjoyed watching this movie (mostly because of awesome effects), but later I thought about how much better it could have been. If you cut out some of the slow parts and add more effects (or intensify current ones) this movie would totally rock.

Even tho I've dissed this movie a tad, you still have gotta see it. Few remakes make the grade, but this one does.

title: War of the Worlds?
review:
It did keep my interest but it by no means lived up to it's namesake. The original works bring the invaders down from somewhere else (Mars) along with all their machines. This one had the invaders from clouds, not even ships, moving into pre-set machines, buried in the earth... skipping over lots of other issues... IF the battle units were preset millions of years ago, it would be like us burying a catapult in the past to use in the present - I do not see the invaders technology being stagnant for that long... Then there is the issue of the bacteria... If the machines were preset, would not the original force have died from the same bacteria? this would have given them the chance to create a vaccine or similar way to survive it...Maybe what happened is millions of years ago these invaders tried attacking and the bacteria defeated them and as they died they buried the machines then this time they came back thinking that they had developed immunity or something??? no, maybe they should have stayed with the running title "Out of the Night" I could have accepted it better and would have thought how strangely similar to the War of the Worlds it was... I just cannot think of rational explanations for a few of the issues the movie includes and that degrades its value as a good movie.

I truly think if I had access to all the used and cut scenes, a good video editing program and about 15 min of look-alike actors with a small amount of script re-write I could make this into a better movie than it currently is... I really do.

title: Didn't we call this movie Independence Day 9 years ago?
review: everything about Independence Day is in this movie...except ID did it a million times better...the aliens have shields that the military has no idea how to get past but fires an amazing amount of ordnance at anyway...initial alien success of devastating major cities...people for some reason still feeling the need to travel in large groups where we're most vulnerable and easy to kill...for some reason the main character and family manage to escape while the people around them literally standing two feet away are nailed between the eyes by the aliens ray guns...the aliens had the same triangular shaped head and weird looking eyes...they were brought down by a "virus" which was hurriedly explained at the end...there's tons more that makes this movie suck but these are what bugged me the most...

title: I didn't think it was all that great.
review: OK, basically the movie is fill with action and suspense, but in the end it doesn't sum everything up for you. How did the aliens get to earth? How did the ships operate? What was the red stuff? How did the aliens die? How did the aliens know that life was going to live here? How did the kid make it back when the hill burst into a fireball? Who was the lady that knew Ray at the Ferry? These questions, and probably more were not told after the movie had ended, which is why I gave my vote for what it is; a whole four points. If you're up for the scare, then go for it, but you'll be left with a bundle of questions. Or if your just checking the differences between the old ones and this one, either way, just be ready for an OK/scary movie with lots of questions.

title: boring
review:
I am very down on the movie. I was terribly bored, looked at my watch a lot, and even fell asleep for a few minutes in the middle of the film. The special effects were nice, but we are getting used to that, so they are not so special anymore. The movie lacked much of a plot. It was "sound and fury signifying nothing."

You can understand my concern when we compare this film to the 1953 version. That film was INTERESTING, despite its flaws, because you had many important adult characters with adult concerns and interactions. There was something to put your teeth into, something to follow -- for example: the hero is a scientist; he had a girlfriend; her relative is a clergyman who wants to talk peace to the invading Martians; so do some of the townspeople; and there are government scientists, police and military trying to cope with the menace. In the Spielberg flick there are just three main characters and no one else important to interact with. And the three characters are an adult (Cruise) and two complaining children, one of whom (the son) is particularly annoying. Most of the movie seems to be their pointless (to me) trek from New Jersey to Boston as they are chased and threatened by Martians.... .... .. And then there is the abrupt ending.

title: Spielberg is older, darker, more refined
review:
This year's blockbuster season continues to impress. After the superb Batman Begins, we now have Spielberg's War of the Worlds, surely one of the more impressive film-making feats of the year. One might say this is the anti-Close Encounters: rather than being a somewhat quiet, almost understated meditation on the benevolent capacities of extra-terrestrials, here we have a pure action movie that simply never lets up, hardly allowing pause for breath - if you do, the aliens will get you!

War of the Worlds marks a return after almost 25 years to Spielberg's interest in alien life. The influence of the films he has made since E.T. is apparent - his vision is much darker, and less eager to embrace the idea that beings are inherently good. For it is not just the aliens that are evil in this film; in fact, one of the more disturbing scenes highlights the extremely sinister capacities we humans have when faced with crisis and hysteria.

The influence of Schindler's List, Jurassic Park, Saving Private Ryan, and Minority Report (to name a few) is not restricted to plot. In fact, the way in which War of the Worlds is filmed represents a technique refined by Spielberg and Janusz Kaminski over the past two decades, and is one of the film's most impressive attributes. Rarely is a scene played out through several quickly cut shots; instead, the horror is simply presented and allowed to have its full impact without the assistance of epilepsy-inducing intercutting.

Another IMDb user commented on the realistic, personified nature of the camera, which is something I noticed too. We see the action as a person in the midst of it would: half running, half looking back, with no time for close-ups or lengthy, lingering shots. The characters are in mortal danger and their flight response is engaged, so it follows that the audience should feel the same. This is not to say the camera-work is merely functional; we have frequent camera vibration, and panning which is extremely effective. All of this combines to illustrate how readily Spielberg now takes risks with the form, and how often they pay off.

Tom Cruise and Dakota Fanning are effective in their roles, expertly playing an initially uneasy father-child bond which steadily becomes strong. But we didn't go for the acting, did we? Also, John Williams' score is one of his more effective - never overly oppressive, but often present and menacing. The tripods' two-note call is the equivalent of Close Encounters' alien tune, and could become just as legendary.

There are one or two contrivances of plot involving the good fortune of the central characters, and the ending seems a little abrupt, but these pale in insignificance when compared to the sheer enormity of what has been achieved on-screen. War of the Worlds is a true big-screen experience, and worthy of its substantial price tag. Bravo, Mr. Spielberg.

title: To call this Disappointing is the understatement of the year.
review:
The same sense of disappointment most people felt after watching "The Matrix Reloaded" or "Phantom Menace" likely will be rekindled with this film. Yes, I know giving in to hype can be a dangerous thing but it's STEVEN SPIELBERG for God sake. I was excited about this movie. After seeing it however, I now hope it lands in theatres with a resounding thud. I doubt it will but it deserves as much. To call this disappointing is the understatement of the year. I'm extremely sorry that I braved the opening night/day crowds to see this one.

This asinine collection of computer graphics and insane dialogue is just a disgrace to the fresh and revolutionary original book.

title: This movie is like a punch in the stomach!!!!!
review:
I've just seen "War of the Worlds" in a theater here in Frankfurt. I honestly have problems finding the right words for this movie. Spielberg barely gives you time to get settled in your chair before the action kicks of, or should I say the horror? Yes you heard right, don't think this is another no-brain-required action flick like ID4 was. This movie is brutal, frightening and merciless almost till the very end. Some scenes were so gut-wrenching that I had to look away (Namely when the ferry carrying Rachel and her family capsizes, or earlier when their car gets raided). Spielberg has truly managed to the pure terror of an invasion, regardless whether by human armies, or (in this case) by beings from an unknown origin.

one of the reason this movie works so well is the cast. All actors (Tom Cruise, Dakota Fanning, and others) really do a good job, but the one who blows them all away is young Dakota. I've seen a lot of child actors so far but only one other(namely Natalie Portman) did such a convincing job at playing a small frightened girl.

The Special Effects of this movie are top of the line. Look for the scene when the bridge gets blown away, or when tripods are snatching people out of the water. It is just incredible, almost to real for my taste.

The soundtrack (together with the German voice-over) is a bit of a letdown, and the reason why I refrained from giving this movie a perfect ten. There just is no recognizable theme, and while the soundtrack does accompany the scenes nicely, it doesn't stay in your mind, like for example the Jurassic Park Soundtrack. The Sound effects themselves however, are great. Even If you couldn't actually see the tripods, you would still be able to imagine how horrible they are by listening to the sounds.

All in all, I'd classify this movie as a must-see. It is just fantastic.

title: Wrong director in the wrong place at the wrong time
review: It probably would have been an excellent 1977 replacement for Close Encounters. Too bad nothing has changed since. The script sticks too close to the novel not to be out of date, not to mention that for the millions who did not read the book it's gonna be too tight. Excellently played by Tim Robbins and Dakota Fanning, too bad Tom Cruise will never be able to pass the action hero stage and do some real playing, because the action hero of the film has no action to take part in. This leaves Cruise with no part in the movie (except for the running). Not to mention the film is heavily loaded with major script bugs, unacceptable for a film of this size. Here's a short list of the most obvious: 1.Check for a guy with a digital camera and another one with a mini camcorder that are shooting right after the EMP storm that has supposedly knocked over every electrical/electronic device in the city - even cars not running. 2. All the cars that we see in the movie are out of commission except for the one Cruise steals... - was he the only one with an extra neuron that allowed him to think he might change a solenoid? 3. Not to mention that all military vehicles are up and running... Probably all US military vehicles were under orders to ignore the EMP storm. :-))

title: Stupid ending, in the vein of Signs and stupid plot
review: Yeah, awesome special effects, whatever... I recognize it was a nice movie to see as long as it was for the effects and it has some tension and that's why I didn't put this 1 star,but I also have to say some parts were boring. The thing that annoyed me most of all apart from the obvious stupidity in the connection of the scenes, when for example, there are thousands of machines and the son goes away and Cruise takes his daughter to the house of the maniac, they always destroy everything, but ohhh...miracle! they're safe now. And then how a mirror can cheat the aliens? that's stupid as hell, they don't have mirrors there right? Well...to what I was saying...the ending is retarded. They've been millions of years studying the earth, they planted the machines in there and they are a super-advanced technology but yet, they don't know there exist virus! Luckily I didn't pay the entrance to the theater, because I'd like to kick the asses of both Cruise and Spielberg for so much hype again for a stupid movie *cough*minority report*cough*... what a retarded movie, seriously. And that actress Dakota only made things worse, I wanted to kill her every time...if I was a kid I'd be scared as hell, not whining and screaming all the ****ing time. Again, this movie is useless.

title: Mixed signals
review:
As a fan of the classic movie and the novel, I must say this film, was worth my money. It was different, but the important parts of the original story, that's where it was faithful, though it seemed a bit plot less, but it had one. Here's my analogy of the film:

How it remained faithful(spoilers ahead): 1.The narration at the beginning, the only thing that changed was the year, instead the narrator says 21st century, but hey, it took place in our time right?

2.The way the aliens came, not through flying saucers.

3.The structure of the ships, they were pods with tentacles, that tore down buildings, used blood from humans, and shot heat rays, and they didn't use flying spaceships, or saucers.

4.The three escaped into the country side.

5.The military fought hard but it was in vain.

6.There was a scene where they escaped to the sea though a ship.

7. How they were stopped.

Changes: 1.The story focused on a family, the Ferriers and not a scientist.

2.The way the aliens came, instead of a cylinder, it was lightning.

3.There were no reports about invasions, just storms.

4.No fight at sea.

Despite these changes, I must say that this was a very promising movie, that is worth checking, and a great performance by the actors, and great return to alien sci fi for Spielberg. But, stop comparing this to Signs, OK? Thank you.

title: Huge Disappointment
review:
For all of its nonstop action set pieces and narrow escapes, "War of the Worlds" is a strangely inert piece of film-making. There's absolutely nothing in the film to retain your interest. Tom Cruise plays a completely anonymous character who you learn nothing about, and his kids serve little purpose beyond being mere plot devices and giving Tom Cruise something to do besides save himself. Steven Spielberg directs this film with a grim relentlessness; there are scenes to frighten and disturb, but there is absolutely no sense of fun. It's as if he brought the same sensibility he did to "Saving Private Ryan" to this film, but here the approach and the material don't match. "Private Ryan" was about an actual event, and there was some value in depicting it as realistically and disturbingly as possible so that those of us who've never lived through something similar might be less inclined to treat the subject casually. But come on--this is an alien-invasion flick, the stuff of pure fantasy. Spielberg's obvious efforts to take advantage of the movie-going public's post-9/11 jumpiness seems calculated and rather tasteless.

There's no point to talk about the acting, since there isn't any. But I do have to mention Tim Robbins, who gives a ghastly performance in a pointless role. His minimal storyline should have been left on the cutting room floor, with much of the rest of this film.

This is one of those movies that doesn't even follow its own logic; the kind where all electronic devices stop working, until someone needs to be able to use a cell phone for the convenience of the plot, and then miraculously their phone works. I was actually quite surprised at how bad this movie was. It's shoddy storytelling, which is not what I've come to expect from Spielberg. He's never been one of my favorite directors, but I've always given him credit for being far more capable than he is here. Maybe he was just directing this film to pass the time before "Munich" (his Oscar-bait movie of the year) was ready to start filming. Whatever the reason, his heart was obviously not in this one.

Grade: D (some splashy visual effects prevent it from receiving an F rating)

title: Shaggy Dog plus Deux Ex Machina plus Narration equals Bad Movie
review:
The Good: Character interaction very believable. The Bad: Wacky ending. The Ugly: The overall story telling.

In this movie, Spielberg made three major and common film making mistakes. Shaggy Dog, Deus ex Machina, and the use of a Narrator.

The film is a shaggy dog story. A shaggy Dog story builds, and builds, and builds to a climax, but the climax has nothing to do with how the story (protagonist vs. antagonist) ultimately resolves, nor does it inspire any visible change in the protagonist. For example, the protagonist does something monumentally spectacular toward the end, but afterwards, doesn't seem impacted by the climax at all.

The second problem is Deus ex machina. The term refers to an ancient literary tactic. When the characters and plot don't resolve, a 'god' character... (in this case, nature) appears on the stage out of nowhere to resolve the plot. So, if the characters and their story had nothing to do with how the plot resolves, why did we have to sit through a story about the characters?

Finally, Narration. The movie starts and ends with narration. A film maker can use plot, characters, audio, video to tell a story. If the film maker must resort to using a narrator to 'explain' the story to the audience, that's bad film making.

So the movie makes three major story telling blunders: A useless build up, a plot resolution that comes out of nowhere, and a voice over. That's really bad. No one should ever think this is a good movie, except in one case: It should be the perfect movie to test out your new wide screen panel monitor and surround sound system... but that's about it.

title: Is this a sequel?
review: I know its a remake of a TV series, which remade an album which came from a movie that formerly was a radio serial that came from a book. Each version had their own unique qualities and a certain 'feel' that made them special unto themselves. But in this incarnation I didn't end up leaving the theatre with the experience I'd hoped for. It felt derivative of his other movies. It was like Schindlers List II! The aliens carry around a bunch of humans in a holding area that is a blatant visual tie in to the Jews getting shipped around in Schindlers List! Quit shoving this in our face! I wanted a classic story of invaders from mars but instead I got more of the typical Hollywood reminder of the Holocaust*TM. Enough already. As a side note, whatever happened to the British version of War of the Worlds. Will it ever be released in North America?

title: No, not like Europe
review: Greetings again from the darkness. Let's start with the positive. This film boasts the greatest special effects on film to date. It easily surpasses the latest Star Wars or Lord of the Rings films. Some of the effects will leave you breathless and wide-eyed. The best compliment I can offer is, everything looks real ... even the unreal. The relentless pace will leave you feeling exhausted until the ending ruins that feeling. With world destruction going on how does anyone have pressed clothes, make-up and brushed hair? I will also say that the entire Tim Robbins (flashing his "Mystic River" accent) sequence was confusing and ridiculous except for the "Jurassic Park" type shot (remember the kids hiding in the kitchen?) Tom Cruise proves he is best at being Tom Cruise. In other words, he is no Tom Hanks as an actor. On the other hand, Dakota Fanning ("Man on Fire" "Cat and the Hat" and little Melanie in "Sweet Home Alabama") shows off a much greater range than her overpaid, over-hyped and overexposed superstar screen dad. Film historian Steven Spielberg does a tip of the cap to the 1953 original by offering a quick shot of that film's stars, Gene Barry and Ann Robinson. Did anyone else notice that the sound emanating from the aliens sounded suspiciously like the opening chords to Black Sabbath's "I am Iron Man"? Also, why is it that every Tom Cruise film has him running at least one wind sprint? Despite the negatives (and there are many), the film scores high due to the phenomenal technical film-making of Spielberg and ILM craftsmen. A must see for film buffs and sci-fi types.

title: Don't believe the hype.
review:
The Spielberg / Cruise publicity machine is in full swing now, and I guess most people will be going into this film after hearing 'best film I've seen this year' and other such niceties from various reviewers.

However, take away the emperor's new clothes and see the film for what it is, a mishmash of borrowed ideas and appalling casting, and of course, the Spielberg schmaltz.

Let's get the good bits out of the way...

Awesome affects. Awesome. Mindblowing set pieces and classic Spielberg moments. Genuinely unsettling and very dark in places. But...

SPOILER ALERT.

How to make War of The Worlds.

1. Borrow the entire basement scene from 'Signs.'

2. Borrow the Tripod Human Harvesters from 'The Matrix.'

3. Borrow 'Birds flying away in panic' from 'Day After Tomorrow.'

4. Borrow 'Alien snake-like surveillance device' from 'The Abyss.'

5. Borrow 'Trees trembling because there's something big underneath them' from 'Jurassic park 2.'

6. Borrow 'Exposition by way of numerous news reports on all channels' from 'Signs' and 'Strange reports of weird atmospheric events in Russia' from 'Independence Day.'

*sigh*

Tom Cruise is simply too big to take on this part, his sheer starpower oozes onto the screen and we find ourselves watching Tom Cruise escaping the aliens, as opposed to a forty- something crane operator with a failed marriage. This is a sad miscalculation by Steven Spielberg, it worked in 'Minority Report' as Cruise played an extraordinary man (as he did in 'Collateral.') It just doesn't work when he plays one of us.

The other problem is those cheeky, unrealistic family conversations that Spielberg loves. They're cute in Jaws and ET but not here. This is supposed to be darker. In fact, Cruise's 'wisecracks' occasionally made my audience giggle - completely ruining the atmosphere in supposedly the most dramatic places.

Quick tip.

Watch the film, then replay it in your head, this time replacing Tom Cruise with Russell Crowe. It suddenly becomes... better. It's an interesting glimpse at the difference between Tom Cruise, a massive star in the classic Erroll Flynn vein and Russell Crowe, an actor much more accomplished at hiding himself and allowing us to invest in his characters.

Hmmmm.

title: War of the Worlds
review:
Nathan Pacheco

War of the Worlds Film Review

The science fiction action film, directed by Steven Spielberg, is probably one of the most "eye-catching" movies out there. The amazingly talented star Tom Cruise takes the lead role. Tom Cruise really gets you to believe that he is actually the character Ray Ferrier, a divorced dock worker separated from his children Rachel and Robbie (Dakota Fanning and Justin Chatwin) and living separately from them. As his ex-wife drops their children off for him to look after for a few days, the planet is invaded by bloodthirsty aliens and the earth's armies are defeated. As this is all happening, Ray tries to protect his children and flee to Boston to rejoin his ex-wife. When Ray is visited by his ex-wife, she drops off their children, Rachel and Robbie, at his house as she is going to Boston to meet her parents. When Robbie takes Ray's car out without his permission, Ray goes out to search for him and notices a strange white cloud in the air. The cloud isn't any ordinary cloud, this cloud was sending "electromagnetic pulses" in the form of lightning. This is also called an EMP. It disabled all electronic devices in the area, including cars, forcing Robbie to return home without knowing what was going on. Lightning struck the ground and Ray went to go investigate. He then finds a huge hole in the middle of the ground, and a huge 3 legged robot alien appears. After emerging, the alien opens fire with destructive heat rays. vaporizing bystanders and destroying everything in sight. Ray manages to leave and the alien destroys the entire city. As the aliens move on to different parts of the city, state, and world, Ray still encounters many obstacles. Ray finds the only working car and tries to flee the city. He is stopped by a raging mob. ray is escorted out of the car, being held at gunpoint. As this is happening, the mob attack the vehicle with Ray's kids still inside. Ray again manages to escape this scene without injury as the man with the gun begins to shoot everyone in sight. Ray and his kids find an abandoned basement to hide in. While hiding in the basement, they witness the Tripods spreading a strange red weed substance over the ground, and avoid detection by aliens who arrive to explore the basement. The following morning, the man who was hiding with them, Ogilvy, suffers a mental breakdown after witnessing an alien harvesting blood and tissue from a human to fertilize the weed. Ray, trying to protect his and his kid's life, kills Ogilvy to silence him. From here on end, it is a constant battle to save the life of his children as well as his own. He does intend to encounter more obstacles along the way, but that is the life you have to face to escape flesh eating, bloodthirsty aliens. The acting in this movie is absolutely outstanding. Every scene, every hour, every minute, and every second, each actor really makes you believe and inspire each role they play. This movie looks as if it takes a lot of skill, talent, patience, and time to act as well as each individual did. Not every day you encounter bloodthirsty aliens, so to act as if it was a real event, takes so much time and talent to really make you believe it was actually happening like the actors did in this movie. This entire movie from beginning to end was just eye-catching, breath taking, and fingernail biting. The acting in this movie will make you want the cast to either make a number 2, or make another movie together because they did such a good job. Phenomenal, amazing, fantastic, terrific, and intense were the first few words that popped into my mind after watching this movie and trying to develop the mindset of each individual actor. One of my favorite scenes when the cast did a phenomenal job acting is when the aliens started to take over the earth. When the aliens started killing and destroying everything in site. The actors put on such a believable act and really made you believe that they actually see what is going on and that it is actually happening to them. The background music was so well chosen for every scene. The director put a special instrumental song to inform the civilians the aliens were approaching. When the aliens were either approaching or were about to, the civilians knew what was happening and began to get afraid and scream. I think the director chose this type of music because it makes you feel a little tension is about to rise and you know something bad is going to happen. The type of music chosen really fits the mood set for the film. If it was a happy song, it would fit any of the scenes because every scene is destructive. Personally, I think the background music is well chosen for this movie. My overall reaction to the film is that it is my personal favorite. I like every minute and second of the movie. It really makes you jump to the edge of the seats and leaves you wanting more. From beginning to end my heart was pounding, wondering what will happen next. The cast did an overall outstanding performance. I also think the quality of the film was excellent. As I said before, all in all, the movie was thrilling and I would really like for there to be a part 2. I highly recommend that you go see this film if you are the type of person who likes to see a action packed science fiction. If you are the type of person who likes to leave the movie wanting more, talking about the movie for days, and goes see the movie twice, this is the movie for you. Personally, I would give this a 5 star rating (10/10).

title: Entertainment as it should be
review:
This is the Dakota and Tom show, with the latter graciously conceding to the little starlet. Cruise pretty much lets Fanning steal the shared scenes - why even bother to compete with such a cute and adorable child?! Fair play to him, and well done Dakota, despite being a tad heavy in the trademark "hysterical screaming banshee" mode.

She may have to try harder to keep up with Cruise, who literally does live up to his name by effortlessly cruising through this, but she shows depth of talent and is obviously at ease in front of a camera, and in front of one of the biggest movie stars of the last 20 years.

With so much action and CGI on display, it would be easy to sit back and let the tech boys make the movie for them, but all the main players really turn on the style here. Add in that stunning action and cinematography (minus the usual gratuitous violence and gore) and expert direction and editing, and we have here a very slick, polished and visually exciting movie.

They really don't get any better than this - movies are primarily meant to entertain, and anyone not entertained by this must be a very jaded person indeed.

title: Awesome remake of the 1898 novel
review:
Since the last movie they made which it was Minority Report, they took the remake to an exhilarating next level in the film "War of the Worlds".

It stars Tom Cruise, Dakota Fanning, Justin Chatwin, Tim Robbins, etc.

Ray Ferrier (Tom Cruise) is a working class man living in New Jersey. He's estranged from his family, his life isn't in order, and he's too caught up with himself. But the unthinkable and, ultimately, the unexpected happens to him in an extraordinary sense. His small town life is shaken violently by the arrival of destructive intruders: Aliens which have come en masse to destroy Earth. As they plow through the country in a wave of mass destruction and violence, Ray must come to the defense of his children. As the world must fend for itself by a new and very advanced enemy not of this world, its inhabitants must save humanity from a far greater force that threatens to destroy it.

They did a really good job remaking the classic novel, which it was written by H.G. Wells.

War of the Worlds gets 10 stars.

title: Too Much Hatred
review: When I walked out in the cinemas just watching the remake from the 1953 version, I was exceptionally pleased. War of the Worlds is a thrilling dark action/adventure starring Tom Cruise about a supernatural piece of high destructive equipment decides to take over the planet earth, leading to a rampage of survival, war and justice. It's not just all war and violence, it tackles and illustrates deep emotions such as trust and family. Family is a big important issue in this movie as Tom Cruise's character has a weak relationship with his daughter and son, through-out the movie you see their relationship develop either for the good or worst. Spielberg's War of the Worlds has a servilely weak rating on IMDb, and receives far too much hate and hatred, it's a break-through for Spielberg and a highly entertaining piece of work. Each Spielberg and supernatural fan should give this a watch despite it's general criticism and shown rating. To me, War of the Worlds is a strong remake from a strong director.

title: Great Movie!
review:
I saw "War of the Worlds" last summer in theaters with my family. I found the movie to be very entertaining. The acting was well done and the special effects were excellent. The script was also well written, it kept me hooked.

"War of the Worlds" tells the story of a man and his 2 kids trying to escape from aliens who have invaded Earth. There were also some pretty scary scenes. In my opinion the beginning of the movie was the probably the scariest part.

Overall I really enjoyed this film, and I suggest everyone should see it. I give "War of the Worlds" 10/10 stars.

title: A RAWK-AWESOME movie!
review:
If you haven't seen this movie yet and are looking through comments, ignore all of the lame reviews... This movie is AWESOME!

Dakota Fanning and Justin Chatwin were amazing actors! If you look at their faces all through-out the movie you can believe they are really truly terrified. Tom Cruise was good too.

The special effects were totally awesome! The aliens were creepy ... the whole foghorn thing whenever the tripods were coming was great, too.

One of the best parts of the movie was when Robbie tried to save some of the people on the ferry by climbing up the ramp and helping them over, even though the authorities there were determined not to let anyone else on.

A few bad things though:

1. Why was that guy's camcorder on?!

2. It could've been a perfectly good movie without so much swearing.

3. Why didn't the aliens just attack now? Why were they underground for so long? I think it made more sense that they came from space, like in the book ...

One last comment: H. G. Wells needed some counseling! o.O ha ha just kidding.

~Allie and Eliza

title: Wake Me Up When Spielberg Ends
review: This movie was not good. The acting was decent, but not great (besides Tim Robbins, but he's only in the film for 10 minutes). The directing was weak and very Spielbergian in its traditional and cliché feel. The ending is so stupid. Things happen which are completely unbelievable - characters are resurrected from the dead. And the word "Anti-climatic" can not be said enough. Every time you get an ounce of suspense you get another 20 minutes of boredom. Don't expect a shocker ending, you'll be lucky to still be awake at that point. Did I mention Dakota Fanning? I really hate her. And Tom Cruise? He was good, I guess, although I'd rather see Denzel Washington. He's the only man who knows how to protect Dakota. The one good thing? The gallons and gallons of blood in this film - its a BLOODFEST. But I don't feel that makes it worth watching. Not recommended - strictly for the tardcore.

title: close encounter of the dumb kind
review: Just rented the DVD (thank God I didn't see it in a theatre) and was surprised how brutally awful it was. On the awful scale it was even worse then "Temple of Doom" and "The Terminal", Spielberg's previous low points. It's hard to say when and where he lost his "chops", but old Stevie boy doesn't even try anymore. The first 25 minutes of the movie were really amazing and my wife and I were giving each other high fives over the special effects. From the point they got into the only car working and decide to drive it to Boston, you could just remove your brain for the next hour and a half. Nothing makes any sense. Every encounter they have with other people, or aliens for that matter, is just goofy and inane. In "Jaws", Spielberg had some top notch actors (Roy Schneider, Richard Dreyfus and especially the great Robert Shaw) in a blockbuster where they portray actual living, breathing characters. In this "blockbuster", he has capable actors (Cruise, Fanning,Miranda Otto) and dumb-ass dialogue. I felt sorry for the actors. Their director was missing in action and their performances showed it. Hey Steven, step aside and let a hungry director take on your next project. It won't hurt you to miss a few meals, so to speak. I'm waiting for the day when I'm happily standing in line again and smiling from ear to ear after watching one of your movies.

title: No redeeming qualities
review:
I normally see some good in any movie, but really... I honestly can't find any with this. I couldn't even watch it all, which is again rare for me as I'll normally suffer through a film just so I've seen it.

Cruise and Spielberg's previous collaboration, Minority Report, was a brilliant piece of work for both of them. Why they came together to do this piece of tripe is beyond me.

Where do I start? The main thrust of this story is that some people want to get from point A to point B. To me, that's not good drama. The world is being destroyed, and getting to Boston is the overriding theme. The theme of survival is secondary to this, and that' just ridiculous.

Everything is so by the numbers. Cruise plays the typical American hero in this film: an ordinary guy, trying to be a good father, who becomes a hero. People (like news reporters) don't mind stopping and filling him in because he is The Hero. So clichéd.

There is never a sense of real emotional depth or a feeling of impending destruction. I mean, the world is being destroyed and we have time to spend talking about peanut better sandwiches and toilet breaks. It doesn't add realism, it detracts from it.

Attempts at humor are blatant, and could only have been more blatant if they put up a note instruction people to laugh. The moment where the son asks if the machines have come from Europe just gave me this vision of the writers sitting there, tittering, marvelling as their own comic genius as they wrote the line.

There were vague moments where the film seemed to try and capture a little 9/11, the fallback idea of the lazy writer these days. Dakota Fanning having to ask if it's terrorists attacking, and people turning on each other to get a car, seemed liked desperate attempts to add some grit. It fails.

I also have to make special mention a moment when Cruise's character and his two kids are speeding along a road, dodging between cars. I don't know what was worst here: the fact that they don't wear seat belts while hurtling along at god knows what speed, that Cruise's acting is just plain bizarre, or the cringe-worthy moment of the brother calming down the sister like she's a neurotic adult. It's a shame when a small kid is being bred into problems of adulthood, needing "space" or whatever other barmy self-help book stuff they were embodying her character with.

All in all, worthless. Really. The effects were appallingly blatant CGI, the acting was poor, the writing was poor. No artistic or unique merit. I think they only positive thing I can say on a final note is that the DTS soundtrack was quite good at times. But that's not enough of a reason to watch this stinker.

Get Minority Report instead for a better Cruise/Spielberg collaboration, and if you want humans in danger then I think that even Deep Impact does a lot better job.

title: Amazing
review:
Wow. That's what I said after this movie was over. War of the Worlds is one movie that you MUST see this summer. I'm sure you all know about the plot. Aliens invade, wanna kill us, all that jazz. Now that's all been done before (Independence Day for example), but this isn't about the aliens coming and blasting us to kingdom come. It's about the characters. The sheer terror they go through. I was literally on the edge of my seat with my pulse quickened during several scenes. You see exactly what the characters see, which draws you in more and more into their experiences with the alien Tripods.

The acting was pretty good for this movie. As usual, Tom Cruise did an awesome job, and Dakota Fanning was perfect. Everyone else did a good job as well.

This movie is not perfect by any means, but it is a very great movie, worthy of anyone to see. Many parts are open-ended, so the viewer can interpret them in the way he or she wants. As I said earlier, you see what the characters see. So you might not know during the movie why the aliens are here and their motives. It requires you to think, which I think is a good thing. Too many movies hand out every little detail on a silver-platter, and everything not explained is dubbed a "plot-hole." This movie has no plot-holes, it requires you to think.

All in all, this film was terrific, worthy of seeing twice in theaters. It's a horror movie with aliens. Scary aliens with big, nasty, walking death-machines. And they're already here.

title: An extremely poor mass-produced catastrophes film
review: In spite of the utmost respect I have for Mr. Spielberg given the great quality of his early works, I am afraid that this movie in particular has little or nothing worth watching: being extremely kind we could highlight the camera management and photography and some bits and pieces of acceptable acting seen among the dazzling special effects, as well as the inclusion at the opening and closing scenes of the actual voice of the unequaled Orson Welles (which anyone who dares see the "movie" should pay attention to). Outside of that, the film is a disgrace to cinema: the plot is absolutely non-existent, the ending lacks any type of logic (concurringly with the rest of the movie), the rhythm of the movie is appallingly slow despite the quick motions it tries to compel and the stupidity of the featured aliens that are supposed to be a superior race is just insulting. I personally would not recommend this movie at all to anyone (it is not even entertaining). The respect we profess towards a director should not tie us to his works, specially if he has given up to the studios will, producing mass-oriented films completely lacking any content or art.

title: Out of control
review:
Has Steven Spielberg lost his touch? In my opinion Mr. Spielberg brought us quite a number of amazing films; amazing in terms of their vision, their film-making and also their box office success. However, looking at A.I. and this one I have the impression that he might have lost his touch. It certainly is a challenging thing to adapt such a book and transform it to the present time. Hence, one would expect the director to guide the audience carefully through the script. Unfortunately, this attempt failed miserably. The film seems to be a melting pot of scenes that were put together without having any logical connection that is consistent throughout the film. Many things happen without a motivation that the audience could understand and some scenes seem to be there, to keep the actors busy. Tom Cruise's metamorphosis from ignorant playboy to caring family father is simply too smooth and miraculous. The film certainly sports stunning effects and, as expected, ILM did a wonderful job on the visual magic. However, this does not help to cover the rough spots and holes in the scripting and very soon one starts to ask the question "why has this just happened?"

I went to see the movie without great expectations after I read/heard mixed reviews. Still, I was honestly disappointed with what came out of a promising effort.

title: Relevant
review:
***CONTAINS SPOILERS***

Most of the great science fiction films are relevant to its time. Steven Spielberg's War of the Worlds is no exception. I know that most fans of HG Welles' novel might be somewhat disappointed, but I think Spielberg and the writes made a smart decision. Notably because there are many images that are close to home. For instance, a scene in which Tom Cruise and his children are walking towards the ferry, we can see a wall filled with pictures of missing families. I don't know about you, but that reminded me of 9/11. Then there is another scene where we see that the Martians are trying to turn Earth into Mars with red fungus. I don't know about you, but doesn't that remind you of what the United States is doing right now. Aren't we trying to change everyone? Whether you agree with the films politics or not I applaud it for being relevant.

In addition, I loved how Tom Cruise was not the hero. Under the wrong hands Tom Cruise would have saved the world. Here Spielberg decides to have Cruise save his children from the Martians. This is a character who isn't interested in saving the world. He is only interested in saving his children. I find that refreshing in a world where Will Smith has saved the planet countless times.

Overall, I think this is probably one of the best films of the year. It is smart and relevant. Of course the film isn't flawless. Like many I thought Robbie should have died. It seemed to convenient for Cruise to accomplish his mission without some loss.

RATING: 4 STARS

title: Mindless screen writing at it's best. (SPOILERS)
review:
Here is a classic case of many talented people and hundreds of millions of dollars being put into a movie, and the end result is mediocre at best because of idiotic screen writing and plot holes that somehow evaded everyone involved with the films production but seems obvious by many of the people paying to see the film, like myself.

I won't bother with a long review of the film, I will just point out the rampant stupidity. Sure, the CGI effects are impressive, the Tripods are intimidating and there is some decent action, but it takes more than that to make a good movie.

SPOILERS AHEAD: Okay, my biggest gripe is the screenwriters deciding to completely change how the Martians invade Earth. H.G. Wells vision of the invasion was fine, and the original film got it right. How does this new invasion mess things up? Simple. They decide to have it go like this: The Martians came here before (no real time is given, except for one crazy character who says it was "millions" of years ago) and buried the Tripods underground. Then, when they decide to invade, they send lightning down to Earth, which knocks out the power to surrounding areas and transports the Martians (inside little coffins) into the Tripods who then activate them. Later on, the Martians die due to bacteria, water, food etc. That part is fine, since that is how they die in the book. But what makes this film stupid is, if they all die from our bacteria etc., then when they came here before to bury the Tripods, why didn't they die THEN? And how did humans NEVER detect the Tripods underground? And what about the ships that sent the Martians down in the lightning? Why didn't we detect them? There must have been quite a few of them considering Tripods appeared all over the world. I noticed all these plot holes as soon as they appeared on screen. How did the films screenwriters, editors and director miss them? Why couldn't they have left it the way it was in the novel? If you're going to change things from the book, at least change them so it makes sense.

Like I said, mindless screen writing at it's best. Sigh.

title: Seriously flawed... still extraordinary...
review:
The film suffers from the inheritance of the title. This is not a film about a war of worlds, but about a man who needs to become a true parent. If the powerful early action scenes haven't said it clearly enough, it's said explicitly soon after - this is not a war, it's an extermination. Hence an irresponsible father of no material use to his children is brought into direct contact with issues of life/death/survival/responsibility in the most extreme way possible.

The film's journey is his journey, and we never leave his point of view except (from memory) a couple of important scenes where we stay with the daughter.

I was reasonably content with the abrupt "ex-machina" defeat of the aliens, since this was extraneous to the central father-son-daughter story.

The final reunification of the family certainly feels peculiar and slightly mishandled, but also have some sympathy with it - Its logic felt a bit inconsistent with the rest of the film's world but otherwise worked on the symbolic level.

The serious flaw for me was the climactic killing of the tripod, which just didn't work for me at all. The father goes through a symbolic death and rebirth, which is great, but the use of hand grenades just feels meaningless and lazy.

I loved the way, continually, after all seems lost, there is still hope, but it stopped short. The process of his "going into the dark" didn't complete.

This climactic and symbolic death of the father is one of the few moments in the film in which we do not stay with him, and it's a moment where we absolutely should have stayed with him, at least symbolically - even (and especially) if his experience in there was dark and hardly comprehensible.

Also, I'd have liked to have seen something like (say) the man in the basement having half an idea of the aliens' weakness and the father exploiting this knowledge somehow. This would have fulfilled the man's archetypal role in the story and connected the father's story more solidly to the final defeat of the aliens. (In the end, we're saved by a "parental" planetary environment, which is a thematic connection, but not a symbolic one.)

I've focused on flaws in the narrative, but the resolute cinematographic focus on the family for the entire film, always over and above the spectacular effects and epic scale of surrounding events, is absolutely true to the story and makes the sense of imminent physical threat all the more palpable and nightmarish.

It's enough to make the film special.

My only other qualm - a 12A certificate??? I don't think any kid younger than 11 should see this for all sorts of reasons. There were whole families when I went to see it, with kids as young as 5 or 6.

title: It was okay, I guess

You don't care. And it has nothing to do with whether or not this is a good movie or not. Even if every little nuance in this film was dead-on technically accurate, it wouldn't help.

The terrible truth is, idiosyncrasies or not, this movie is nothing special--whether it's believable or not. It doesn't live up to the hype, it doesn't live up to the trailers. What could have been a great alien invasion movie with major special effects (to be expected from Spielberg), suspense and terror--winds up being a ride on the Kiddie Coaster at the Fairgrounds on a Sunday afternoon.

The plot seems to center on Tom Cruise's character's immaturity, family values, responsibility, blah, blah, blah. It is not about alien invasion. That, sadly, is just something that happens to be going on in the background, during all this other family drama. And unfortunately for us, who expected this movie to even remotely resemble the original renditions of this story, it's unacceptably boring.

I've been waiting months for this movie to come out. I entered the theater totally expecting what was hyped to be delivered. What a letdown. No increased heart rate, no sharp intake of breath, no 'close my eyes because I don't want to see this part'.

When I came in there were 3 little boys (probably around 10 years old) sitting in my row. I thought "wow, this is probably going to be pretty intense for these kids". I tell you, they looked as bored as I was and more interested in their popcorn and candy than the movie at times. When Mom turned to them when it was over and said "So, what did you think?" I heard the kid closest to me reply, "It was okay, I guess". That about hits the nail on the head.

You know how people tell you that you have to see this at the theater on the big screen? Well, they're wrong. (Yeah, yeah, the sky looked cool, but for effects, as a whole, this movie was lacking. I'm thinking 'Tremors'... 'any B movie I've ever seen'.) This is one movie that I don't think will lose anything on your 25" Sony (because it's got nothing to lose to begin with). Wait for the video. I predict it'll be out in a month.
