title: Good start, disappointing ending
review:
The first hour of 'War of the World' was mesmerizing; I can't remember the last time I was glued to my seat, with goosebumps running down my spine. It was all too real, too scary. And the strong effect continued until about midway. Then it all started to go downhill.

It's a well-known cinematic principle in horror films that the less one sees of the creature, it is bound to be more terrifying. Therefore, before we actually see the aliens, they are as scary as can be. And then they come into full view, looking, as a friend of mine put it, like "bad ETs". They were just too cute, too cuddly, too, well, Spielberg-y. It seems that the acclaimed director just can't let go of 'Close Encounters of the Third Kind', which featured kind and benign aliens. The creatures in 'War of the World', despite their frightful spacecrafts, are nothing more than a metallic version of Gizmo (of 'Gremlins' fame).

In addition, the relationship between Tom Cruise's character, Ray, and his son is absurdly simplistic. It seems that it takes an alien attack on earth for them to finally hug and admit that they love each other. And how the son survived his woes is another unbelievable mystery, which, conveniently, remains unexplained. The one redeeming character is Ray's daughter, Rachel (Dakota Fanning), who so convincingly conveys the emotions of fear and confusion one assumes would be felt during such a catastrophe.

Don't get me wrong - 'War of the Worlds' is not a bad movie; it is simply too ambitious for its own good. If you choose to ignore the underlying (and totally ridiculous) Oedipal undertones and philosophical arguments, what you get is one effective and frightening horror film.

title: extremely boring movie
review: honestly, i have never seen such a bad Tom Cruise movie. There is no storyline and therefore no point. This movie was so not what i expected. If you really and truly believe in Martians then this movie will totally rock you but if not then you'll just sit there, as i did, and think "what a waste of time". Spielburg: you could honestly do better. What happened to blood, guts and glory? what happened to people that are supposed to dead, staying dead? The ending was the worst. It never actually ties up the story. You are just left there with endless amounts of questions, which i suppose if the movie was done correctly, could be a good thing, but it wasn't. I don't recommend seeing this movie.

title: Could you waste a little more money?
review: I can almost see Steven Spielberg rubbing his greedy little hands together. "I knew that America would fall for the old special effects/ Tom Cruise trick. Ha ha ha!" Don't get me wrong, I love "Minority Report". I own it. But this was a sad excuse to fart around with CGI. The story was SO WEAK! I guess Tom Cruise just thinks every movie set that's graced with his presence is pure gold. Wrong. And I am actually starting to feel sorry for Steven Spielberg. He used to be an amazing director. It's of his own doing though. Maybe if he went back to putting TIME into his films instead of MONEY. Or even better yet, maybe if he stopped trying to please everyone with these big Hollywood blockbusters and went back to worrying about the film more than the box office revenues. Just maybe...

title: Two words:
review:
This sucked.

War of the Worlds ends up being a disappointing vanity trip for Cruise and Spielberg. Typically predictable special effects and a non-existent storyline had me fighting to stay awake for the entire picture. I was sort of hoping that Tom would start running down the street screaming "TECH SUPPORT!", and that we would both be shaken loose from this soporific nightmare of mediocre movie-making. Thank god I snuck into the War of the Worlds after catching a Batman Begins matinée and didn't have to pay for this waste of celluloid; the box office returns are overinflated as it is. Spielberg has a track record of box office genius that is rivaled by very few directors in the past and current century. To allow him to skate by on something as disappointing as this picture was would be a disservice to him. I hope his UNTITLED 1972 MUNICH OLYMPICS PROJECT represents a better effort than WOTW.

title: Disappointed by Spielberg
review:
Very disappointed by this movie. I took the Liberty to go and see it today, expecting it to be great because I'm a fairly big fan of Steven Spielberg. This however was a stinker.

It starts off to quickly getting straight into the plot without knowing much about Ray Ferrier. Next it just seems to repeat itself in different scenarios by Ray running from the aliens and escaping in the same way. At the last part of the movie, the machines are destroyed by crows! How can a crow destroy a huge killing machine?!? To silly and unrealistic there.

This is not one of the best movies of 2005. If I was you I'd spend your money going to see another blockbuster of 2005, because there is going to be plenty this year.

title: This isn't a war, it's an extermination...and an 8/10 movie
review:
"War of the Worlds" contains such astonishing visual effects and graphics that multiply Independence Day by fifty, if not more. The look of the aliens that have the similar appearance to that of the immense shielded machines they 'drive,' is quite interesting and cool.

However, the annoying screaming of that darn little girl (Dakota Fanning, daughter of divorced Tom Cruise, "Ray") which lasts for a couple minutes near the end is ignorant and irritating. The end ends way too abruptly, which you should still see for yourself (cuz i ain't gonna spoil it) since this is still a great movie. acting was done well, especially by Tom Cruise. Nonetheless, the complete STUPIDITY of the people (including Cruise) at the beginning witnessing the devastating arrival of these alien machines is itself annoying and stupidly ignorant.

Despite the cons, however, "War of the Worlds" is a must-see and great for controversial.

Hey, WHAT IF? ...and remember: it's not a war, it's an extermination.

title: People don't get it
review:
One of the reasons why War of the Worlds gets such mixed reviews, is that the trailer showed us an action film. But this movie is not a action film. People expect to see a mixture between Independence Day and The Day After Tomorrow, but they are disappointed.

This film focuses on only one family. Therefore we do not see all the action taking place against the invaders, or we do not get all the explanations we would want... We are thrown into that invasion with that family, we see and understand only the things they see and understand, and that is a reason why people see "plot holes", where there are none... Another thing is that that focus on one family is all the more terrifying. The movie begins without music, just showing us a very usual day, before terror arises with extraordinary events. And some of the scenes in the movie are really tense, and we, spectators, can easily change our places with the characters...

And what about those who accuse the film of being a CG sci-fi flick? If you just take time to WATCH the movie BEFORE writing very dumb reviews, you'll notice that the CG is absolutely not the main point in the movie. You could almost forget it, and if you think of it, there are not that many big huge mammoth visual effects in this movie, and the effects only increase the sense of threat. This movie was not made to show how good the guys at ILM are, so please, stop with those ready-made ideas you get only watching a trailer.

To conclude, this film is not what I expected after seeing the trailer. It is NOT a big destruction film, but a slower-paced and tense one.

title: We rarely walk out of films
review: My wife and I saw WOTW 4th of July weekend. After Sith and Batman, I was prepared to be blown away with top drawer effects and solid acting, but was sadly disappointed on both counts. It was flat on all counts. ** Spoiler - Was there some reason other than a sweet tooth for humans that prompted the aliens (were they from Mars?) to plan an attack thousands of years ago? And why wait so long, a few tripods in the 1700s, or 1800s would have found a population far less able to resist at all. End of Spoiler. ** Anyway, back to the only plot in the theater - I thought my wife was enjoying the film and she thought I was. Either one of us by ourselves would have walked out - but we both stayed to the end out of deference to each other. What a surprise ending that was!

title: Watch Independence Day again, it's better.
review: The movie starts off with some shots of earth from outer space and how humans have been watched for years and for some reason the aliens are jealous of humanity. It then goes on to show Tom Cruise in New York, where lightning strikes the same place multiple times, and these giant machines come out of the ground. The general public are idiots, and instead of running away from the giant alien machines, they gather in a crowd and stare at it, making it easier for the aliens to incinerate them. The first part of the movie was pretty good at introducing the aliens and Tom Cruise's character, but then it all breaks down after that. The remaining hour and a half of the movie consists of Tom Cruise staring dramatically at something and Dakota Fanning (his daughter) screaming at the most inopportune times... repeatedly. No real motive was given for the alien invasion, which would have been OK if they focused the story of Cruise and his family, maybe getting back together with his ex-wife or something meaningful. Instead, they're running and hiding the entire movie. Halfway through it I found myself just wishing they'd be caught and killed just so the movie could be over. The only sympathy I found for Cruise's character was that he had to deal with the annoying screaming of that banshee Dakota Fanning. Yes, there's aliens and they're destroying everything... we heard your first thirty screams, now let the man drive his stolen car. I was hoping Tom Cruise would reach to the backseat and just slap the living taste out of her mouth, yelling "I'M RICK JAMES, BITCH!" She certainly deserved it. Dakota Fanning actually shuts up for more than 5 minutes during the scene where they're hiding from aliens in a basement cellar. It was your typical hiding scene... decent but nothing stellar. Spielberg can't make something out of nothing as well as M. Night Shyamalan. The ending was abrupt, stupid, and made no sense. Maybe if we knew more about the aliens, we'd actually be able to understand it. Part of me was hoping for Will Smith and Jeff Goldblum to pop out of one of the machines and killing things Independence Day style, which would have made this movie 100x better, yet would have still sucked compared to Independence Day. In conclusion, don't watch War of the Worlds. Watch C-Span governmental debates instead. You'll be more entertained and less confused. On yeah, Dakota Fanning is annoying.

title: Not what i expected
review:
Well i just came from watching war of the world, seeing that i love cruise and have enjoyed most of his past movies,I thought "cruise and Spielberg.. wow, it must be a must see movie". Horrible........ this is the only word i can describe it. No story- except that of an Invasion (and we ve had too much of that). In the first 15 min, you are taken back by the graphics of the aliens , and the sound effects, which is a little horrifying for my taste, then you get over all that and you try to desperately find a story,, or a tag line which the story is heading towards,,, Nothing, Zip.. People running around, getting evaporated and sucked dry out of blood. Even the ending no one did any thing, the things just broke down on their own. The whole movie is based on scaring the audience with the sound effects, which is some times miss used.

This is not what i expected,,,,,,,

title: Selfishness?
review:
Apparently we don't need invaders to defeat us, we have already rotted to the bone. Simply look at how things have changed from the 1953 film version. In 2005, everybody is on their own. Right away we are hit with a divorced father having to deal with children whom he hardly knows. When the big trouble arise, none of the citizens team up. The hero has a van but it is only for his family. How can he drive past others without offering help? People act stupidly and selfishly throughout the film, and the protagonist is not a role model and is, in fact, a murderer.

There is no human dignity in this movie, no conquest performed by the minds and hands of our civilization to overcome impossible odds. Just our good fortune that the Creator fixed things for us way back when. Yet there is not thankfulness nor respect for this miracle in the movie. Just a cursory explanation in voice over to what happened and then grab the hat and get out of there. H.G. Wells said it more eloquently in his novel. Obviously, those words do not meet with modern morality. A pity, I say.

In 1953, the humans are saved as they gather together in a sanctuary, to comfort and be with one another to meet the end with grace. In 2005, a church is destroyed immediately, and there is no one to call to a higher power throughout the the movie. I suppose in 2005 we are all too smart to believe in anything beyond ourselves. If we are all there is, then that is the actual horror of this movie because from what I saw, we are nothing to brag about.

The aliens in this movie are not much different from ourselves. We hold a mirror up to them in one scene, perhaps we should have directed it at ourselves, instead.

title: Another dud from Spielberg
review:
This film is a turkey.

The plot holes have been well documented by other commenter's in this forum however I would also like to add that the aliens in this film are about the dumbest critters in God's creation.

If they planted those giant tripods in the ground thousands of years ago why did they not just take over the earth there and then when there were no pesky humans around? Sheesh! The acting and characterizations were ridiculously hammy and the family trauma angle was absurd. The scene where Cruise and his son have the father-and-son angst while tanks are roaring by and being obliterated borders on being the most laughable in modern cinema history.

Still what else can you expect from Spielberg? The most over-rated film maker in the history of the medium. His penchant for bringing children into his films nearly always result in a trashy maudlin sentimentality which belongs in a cereal commercial - not the real world.

title: War of The Worlds Was Terrible
review: I went into this movie wanting to like it as I am a big fan of both Tom Cruise and Steven Spielberg. I left this movie telling myself that I can earn back the $9.75 I paid for my ticket, but I can never earn back the two hours and ten minutes I spent watching the movie. The plot (aliens invading earth) could have been well presented, however, not in this case. So many things just didn't make sense. First of all, Cruise's kids were obnoxious and irritating. Had this been an actual emergency, I firmly believe that these children would have lived up to the challenge and not maintained their bratty attitude. Second, the story just didn't make sense. In the first scenes, the aliens' tripod machine comes up out of the earth in New Jersey (just outside NYC). Rather than run at the first tremblings of the earth (from where the tripod came), Cruise stands their and simply looks on. Then, with all of the electronics fried, he is able to find the only vehicle that is operable. As Cruise and his ill-behaved kids run from the aliens, his teenage son runs off to join the defending army against his father's direction. Not very realistic. What really made this movie horrid was the fact that everything seemed to tie itself up at the end (almost without warning). It was almost as if the producers had run out of money and needed to wrap up quickly where the money ran out. Finally, the happy ending that reunited Cruise with his son (and ex-wife) in the ex-wife's parents' house in Boston (with all the electricity back on) was totally at odds with the "reality" of total and complete devastation presented during the preceding two hours. I expected more from this Spielberg/ Cruise collaboration. Save your money - don't see this movie in the theaters, don't buy this movie on DVD - don't even waste your time watching it in 5 years on USA Network's middle of the night movie program.

title: I expected too much...
review: I have seen the 1953 version many times and always enjoyed the story and special effects, which were very good for that year. I expected to see some great effects, especially from Spielberg and then...nothing. What happened? Did Spielberg just give up on this one? This movie really blows. I guess if you never seen the original movie, you may think this is a good film. You need to rent/download or buy the original just to see what this great story should look like on screen. -------------- Spoiler: Will somebody stop that little girl from screaming!! If the machines were underground all this time, don't you think somebody would have found one by now? The blood... Whats up with the blood thing? Who ever wrote this screenplay took too much license and screwed up the story. This is a classic story.You can change a little here and there to fit the modern times, but you don't completely leave the storyline. --------------- This movie will never amount to anything. Just a flash in the pan. George Pal did a far better job on this story than Spielberg. Hey, Steve...Time to retire. The only thing true to H.G.Well's vision is the tripod machines. If you look on the internet you will find many artist' conceptions of how Mr. Well's described these vehicles. In the original (1953) movie, the machines were sleek, cobra like hover craft with magnetic "legs" and green "death ray" tipped wings. Yes, this was a deviation, however, even so, the machines still followed the storyline. There are those who will say this is a new style for Spielberg and the personal lives of the characters are important and so.. Just don't use a classic to try these 'experiments in film making'. Find a new story to play with, leave the classic stories alone, after all, it's a cheap shot to TRY to improve on perfection.

title: War of the Worst... and More Plot Holes than a Downtown Detroit Street
review:
Has Steven Spielberg really stooped this low? Or, is this a logical conclusion to a building collection of dreck he's put out over the past ten years. Hard to believe this is the same filmmaker that put out 'Schindler's List.' So much 'suspend your disbelief' (and your intelligence) - Ray is the only person to get a car running during the initial attack; Robbie goes over the hill into an onslaught... and makes it; Ray gets his family on the boat even against the odds of 5,000 people pulling a stage rush; Tim Robbins opens his house to Ray and kid, but no other humans can find it. It goes on and on. The human lobster trap from which Ray sets all humans free by use of grenades is so unbelievable it's embarrassing. Shame on you, Mr. Spielberg, I would have thought you gave the movie viewing world more credit.

No fault to Tom Cruise - he was simply playing Tom Cruise - cocky ('ever see me deal') limited intelligence (how come he pretty much always plays borderline dummies?). And, what's so great about the little blond kid? One high-profile appearance, some throw-away one-liners a lot of screaming and we're all agog with awe. Can you say Haley What's-His-Name? Geez, we're so easily enthralled.

Nice effects though. Very 'Independence Day / Day After Tomorrow.' Could have used Randy Quaid to give it some credibility.

The best part of this film was Gene Barry and Ann Robinson.

title: Like an unsatisfying orgasm - all of the buildup with little climax
review:
I'm literally just back from seeing this at my local cinema. Personally, I thought it was a good bit of entertainment with lots of tension, impressive effects and nice action. Cruise is Cruise and Dakota pretty much does what you'd expect from a child prodigy. Some bits feel a bit slow though and there's a lack of character from the performers. I think Tim Robbins' character had the most personality amongst the others, although nobody really knows why he is the way he is...

As far the much talked about ending, it's a fair bit unsatisfying. As I say in my title, it's like an unsatisfying orgasm - all of the exciting buildup with little climax. Good entertainment though. Worth a watch.

title: Plagiarism?????
review: As best I can tell, the tripod concept is from John Christopher's The Tripods series for kids, not from the Well's novel. This should be obvious, BBC did a series on this. Christopher's books are about an earth conquered by these tripods which run around the planet in large numbers. Christopher's books have much more to do with what happens after the basic conquering. But the marauding tripods which grab people from the ground with automated arms is from Christorpher's books. Christopher's tripods have extending cables which pick up people. In the original movie, the aliens had spaceships. I can't remember what the Well's book had. So, it looks like the new movie is a composite of the 2 books with a modern story interwoven. All badly done. Basically the movie is about a couple days of running away from the tripods and then it ends.

title: Incredibly disappointing from Spielberg
review: I'm just going to start this with a few questions: What was the point of burying the tripods a million years (or however long it was) before invading earth? Wouldn't it have been easier to just invade from the sky? Why did the camera that filmed the emergence of the first tripod work when nothing else did (even watches stopped!)? Why did the aliens take blood from people and use it as a fertiliser's? What were the red plants that started growing, and what was their purpose? Why on earth was a man lowered down from the tripod, knifed to death, and the blood sucked out of him an BACK into the tripod?!! How could our main characters (and all the other people) be stupid enough to go to a crowded place, where the tripods were most likely to attack?! There are just way too many lose ends and illogical occurrences in this film. You also get pretty tired of Dakota's screaming after a while. Tom Cruise is just Tom Cruise, but there's not really much he could do to improve the film. This was very disappointing to be Spielberg...probably the worst one he has ever made. That is why it only deserves 2 out of 10. If you are thinking of seeing it, don't bother.

title: Biggest letdown of the summer
review: I waited months to see War of the Worlds. Let me say that the first thirty minutes of this movie is great. Great performances all around, and by now everyone knows that the special effects are some of the best ever seen. Then after thirty minutes the picture turned into....GARBAGE! Steven!! What has happened to you? You were at the top of your game. Then during A.I. you fell apart (except for Minority Report). I don't mind plot holes. But some of the holes in WOW are outlandish. I had heard how bad the ending was. But nothing prepared me for the stupidness of it. This is not the work of anyone with intelligence. Don't take my word for it, though. Spend your money, and you'll see for yourself.

title: Popcorn Seller
review:
I was really looking forward to this. The trailer was excellent and boded well for the film. Unfortunately I left the cinema very disappointed.

I'm not a nit picker and on the whole enjoy many Steven Spielberg (and Tom Cruise) films but there were plot holes all over the place in this one. On top of this the dialogue and acting weren't good enough to make me believe in the characters. Worst of all was the moment the son, "Robbie", decided he wanted to watch some aliens zapping humans rather than stick with his father and particularly his sister who he was supposed to care about.

The tedious alien mechanical eye on a bendy telescope was laughable as was Tim Robbins character in the same time of the film. An absolute waste of time and space in which the story went nowhere.

I don't mind suspending belief in terms of little green men and tripod craft but I do when it comes to characters who seem as cardboard as the sets in "Plan 9 from Out Space".

It was nice to see when Cruise got to Boston that his ex-wife's relatives had their Sunday best on. Not a mark on them either.

On the positive side it did have some jumpy moments throughout but that didn't make up for a very poor film. One which had enormous potential but was ultimately little more than a popcorn seller.

title: Is this a B movie? Stiff acting!!!
review: On the plus side I found this movie to be great with all the special effects. You'll see the best of it in the first 15 minutes. The FX aren't just one scene closeups, they engulf the whole screen and cover sky to ground and whole city blocks. Some of it is VERY far fetched even for sci-fi like the fact that he is the only one in the world that has a running vehicle (except the military vehicles) when all electronics are supposed to have been stopped. Also, if you see the movie, take note of the video camera that records the initial invasion when no other electronic device works. WARNING: This movie is not for youngsters with active imaginations. Some of the gore is .... overwhelming. Now...the bad side: This was by far the worst Tom Cruise movie I've ever seen. It was apparent throughout the movie so much that it distracted from the good parts. He seemed stiff and awkward in the role and displayed extremely poor emotions at the very end considering the outcome. It reminded me of when a mother forces their child to say I'm sorry and mean it. Did the director have to threaten him to show emotion? I thought this guy was paid the big bucks because he was a good actor. If he's not that, what is he? Summary: Watch it for the FX not for the acting.

title: Absolutely Awful
review:
SPOILER ALERTS (though there's not much to spoil)!! From start to finish, this movie was ridiculously bad. It's an alien invasion film, but the most implausible things happen at the very human level. A massive crowd gathers around a small hole in the ground, yet our hero easily slips to the very front. The space invaders fry everything electronic, but there was Joe Schmo filming the action on his digital camcorder as the mechanical behemoths rise from the ground to lay waste to everything in sight. All cars are disabled, yet our protagonists manage to find the only one in operation (which shouldn't be in operation at all). Away they rush along roads and interstates where all of the other disabled transportation conveniently leave a path of escape. Deadbeat Dad Cruise and his emotionally alienated kids find refuge at Mom's house while she and her new hubby visit the grandparents in Boston. Does our haggard father rush to a TV or radio to try to figure out what's going on and what to do? Nah. Instead, he makes peanut butter sandwiches. However, the tranquility is short-lived as a jumbo jet (curiously devoid of passengers) comes crashing down on Mom's abode. Not the house next door or the one down the street but Mom's house. But worry not. Though devastation abounds, the family truckster lies untouched by the carnage, once again with a convenient drive thru left vacant.

It only goes downhill from there. A pointless chance encounter with a recognized woman and her daughter who are immediately lost in the throng of fleeing people. Eight or so unarmed soldiers who can hold back hundreds (there's Cruise and Co. right at the front again) but manage to let our heroes slip by. Then there's Cruise's son, anxious to fight the invading hordes, rushing off with the armed forces only to seemingly get lost in a massive ball of flame that engulfs the pesky human resistance, leaving unmanned Humvees rolling along ablaze. Yet, there he is, nary a scratch, awaiting our fleeing father and daughter team at their final destination, a destination surprisingly intact and virtually pristine. Our beloved Mother figure emerges with Grams and Gramps with that, "What's all the ruckus going on out here?", look on their curiously clean faces.

We never know why the aliens come, how their machines got here, what the heck all those root things are, or the point of this entire film. The invincible aliens trample and terrorize for the entire length of the film only to be laid low by bacteria in the course of fifteen minutes, a fact we are given postmortem by our handy Morgan Freeman narration. Dakota Fanning gives an admirable performance as the daughter-in-distress by, if for no other reason, how much it distances itself from the lackluster performances of Cruise and the remainder of the bit-player cast. Tim Robbins is passable as a rural survivor slowly sinking into madness, but, like most of the other contrived set pieces in this debacle, his character's participation is short and pointless.

Where is the Spielberg from "Close Encouters" and "Jaws"? As the filmmaker ages he continues to give himself more and more liberties with blatant plot holes and blundering plot lines. Does he think that little of his audience? Has he grown that lazy? Or does he just not care anymore? Where is the Cruise from....? Oh wait, this is always the Cruise we get.

As alien invasion films go, this "War" makes "Signs" and "ID4" look like Best Picture material.

title: War of the Critics
review:
You've all got to be kidding me; I've seen plenty of haters on this film, and I cannot even begin to gander at... why!? I really loved this film, as did the six people who accompanied me. We all thought the effects were mind blowing, the acting and direction superb and the story, although sub-par at best, makes for THE greatest summer blockbuster. Let's get this started.

Direction - 10/10 - Never can Spielberg do a HORRIBLE job. His imaginative camera angles and shots really bring this picture to life.

Acting - 10/10 - Cruise has always been a good actor, and this proves it even more. His crying, his worry for his daughter, Rachel, really come to life. But as most people would concur on this topic, Dakota Fanning as Rachel really fills the spotlight with her chilling, and almost eardrum piercing screams. You really thought these characters were alive! Plot - 7.5 - The plot is just another invasion flic, but with Spielbergs mind it just blows you away.

Average - 9.5 (Imdb rating - 10 )

title: Tom Cruise: the "Huh?" hero
review:
OK, first of all, War of the Worlds is an entertaining movie -- there are cool scenes and good visuals, and the aliens are just plain freaking mean. When their ships show up, you know something bad is going to happen. For that reason, this movie is worth watching. And of course, this movie is typically Speilburgian -- lots of interesting camera ambiance and tons of scenes of people looking at stuff instead of running for their lives like normal people would do (until it's too late, of course).

Tom Cruise on the other hand: you see him being pimped on practically every station and every talk show in order to build hype for the film, but when you actually see him on screen... Mr. Cruise's character is pretty-much a nobody, nothing really special about him. In fact, he's almost deliberately UN-special. Yet for some reason, he's always the first to notice stuff, the first to do anything, and always seems to want to be at the front of the crowd; it's like watching a kid beat a video game with the cheat codes when you know he's not really good at playing the game. If anyone should be shown on every talk show selling the movie it should be Dakota Fanning, the Lil' Drew Barrymore of her day.

Story-wise, this movie is almost identical to the original War of the Worlds (which I personally think is better), except that as fore-mentioned Cruise's character is a nobody that figures out things, whereas in the original the male lead was a leading scientist, which made more sense when he uncovered truths. I would have liked to see the alien vessels more in the movie, but when they did appear it was scary as heck.

All in all... Watch the movie with a friend if you just want to entertain yourselves for a night, but don't go in expecting revelations or to leave in some kind of awe.

title: Disappointing!!!
review: The best thing in this film is the visuals which lifts the film from awful to mediocre. The start of the film is relatively exciting but it goes downhill from there, the film hits a 30 minute rut where absolutely nothing of interest happens and the film becomes painful to watch. Good acting could have saved the film to a certain extent, however the girl in the film is far too over the top to feel sympathy for. The ending seems tagged on as one minute the Earth seems to be doomed and then the aliens begin die. It seems that an overlong ending (that Spielberg is famous for) may have been necessary to leave the audience satisfied. My main problem with this film is that the Alien's die due to the Earth's atmosphere and food, but they had been plotting the invasion for millions of years I would have thought that some research would have been undertaken of the Earth by the a so called extremely intelligent race. All in all movie goers will be disappointed with this film.

title: Next failure of the greatest dreamer
review:
First of all I would like to say that I was a great fan of Spielberg films. That's why I still call him the greatest dreamer, although not all of his work was my cup of tea. As time passed and I grew older I got more and more annoyed by the endings. Starting with Schindler, almost all the endings were so naive as written and directed by some old weeping lady passing her sixties. WOTW is unfortunately the same case. I am not a film critic, I am screenwriter, so usually I keep my right to remain silent. But not this time. WOTW was an insult to me, not only personally as to paying viewer, but also as an insult to all filmmakers. Welles wrote a magnificent book and no one was able to film it properly. Then Spielberg came - and made it a crap.

WOTW has some strong moments, like the burning train, or the landscape bleeding with red roots. But they just can't overweight the silly ones. That means NOT just the ending - main characters hugging each other after surviving extraterrestrial holocaust, watched by relatives which survived in Boston (why Boston remains almost untouched, anyway) can be bearable if the script is good. And it's NOT good. Koepp did a miserable job. For example - the scene with Tim Robbins is just badly written and the moment when Cruise slays him just seems that he did it just for his daughter. In the book main character just don't have any other chance to survive. Cruise has plenty of chances and when he is finally trapped, good soldier and good people around get together to save him. That's just stupid, not silly, STUPID.

To cut it short - not even great budget and great director can make great film from the great book. When I left the cinema with my friends we were glad that LOTR was made by Peter Jackson and not by Spielberg. With his approach the Tolkien Trilogy could be just like another Hook.

5/10 just because I liked his work ten years ago

title: Not so bad, despite T.C.
review:
Spielberg made an interesting film with a magnificent Dakota Fanning.

It's a pity that he has not been able to find a real actor for the main character. Cruise does not achieve to convince me about the character he plays. Not in the very starting of the film, nor the very last frame (you'll understand it when you'll see it).

Despite this all, it's a must see. Dakota Fanning deserves an special mention, if not a nomination to any acting award.

Tim Robbins, he appears a little late in the film, but also in a great role.

The fx, the making-up, setting and music are excellent.

title: Bleh
review: If you want to see scary, take a look at Joan Crawford in the late 60's...the acting was overdone, save for Dakota Flanning, and the story line was poisoned by the ending (including the wealthy family untouched and the son returning)! It was suspenseful, but more so, disappointing. Tim Robbins' part was unexplained, random even, although understood to show the idea of human nature. The whole entire ending, specifically, was most troublesome. All the world is being ravished by the attacks. However, a wealthy block of brownstones remains untouched, the french doors flying open to a well-receiving unblemished mother, husband, and grandparents. And to top the whole film, the son magically returns, demonstrating the strength of humanity. I support human strength in film (i.e. Saving Private Ryan), but to push a story that far seems more ridiculous than necessary. For graphics and a good jump, pushing for the characters, see the film. Just don't expect more than that.

title: And the Winner isn't
review:
And the Oscar goes to....Billy Gates, job well done Master William, you keep on keeping on; building the computers that are categorically depriving world's film industry from making good old fashioned sci fi movies.

A more fitting title for this brand new Sci-fi 'mini - Epic' is "Independence Day - The Steven Spielberg Cut"

It does all the things ID4 did badly, well. And that's about the limit of its ability. It really is ID4 in sheep's clothing.

The plot development and storyline are about as deep and involving as the infants pool at the local public swimming pool.

Dude, where's my plot development? Three quarters of the way through this colossal dooms day film, the aliens have completely overpowered Earth and all its inhabitants, magically the next day *BANG* the movie is over....the human race has once again overcome adversity to emerge triumphant.

In addition to an utterly bewildering lack of plot development; there is an even greater chasm in this movie - CHARACTER development. Sure, Tom is one of the hugest names in Hollywood and definitely has the ability to draw a crowd - but do we have to sacrifice other characters stories just so we can boost his screen time and therefore boost his already scientologically proved huge ego??? I THINK NOT.

There are aspects of this movie that are refreshing; its not your usual "come out all guns blazing and waste em" movie; in fact in total there would be less than 5 minutes of this movie that concentrates on the militaries attempt to destroy the cretins.

I am definitely not happy about bothering to see a midnight session of this pre-release...

Go home and rent a real classic...ALIENS!!

title: not that great
review:
Just saw it, did not love it...

1) Don't know if it's the fault of art direction or cinematography, but the Eerie blue light + washed-out skin + water is so dull. I probably liked it the first scene I saw it in, but it gets old very quickly. Just like Minority Report and AI - at least in those movies, I guess it was supposed to represent "the future" or some such, but here it shows up, among other places, in an 'old west theme' basement. Played out.

2) The 'old west theme' basement. Went on and on, and good old Tom had to try to act a little with another person, which pulled me right out of the movie. And three, count em, three Tom and Jerry cartoon style cat n' mouse segments. And what's the point? People can be bad too? Boring.

3) The pale quiet child with the big wide eyes (or child-like psychic with the big wide eyes) in this, AI, Minority Report - is Spielberg trying to recapture that ET magic? Definitely not working for me. Yeah, innocence in the world, whatever... the focus on a freaked-out kid is a little weird. Compare to the Aliens movie where at least the kid wasn't carrying the metaphorical weight of the world in a never ending series of washed-out, wide-eyed reaction shots.

So, bugged me for the same reason Minority report and AI bugged me. I didn't hate sitting through them, but I've got zero interest in seeing them again. In fact, caught a few minutes of Minority Report on hotel cable or something a while ago, watched a bit, thought 'oh yea, this movie' and changed the channel. I'm sure it will be the same with this.

Too bad, I like these type of movies - Aliens, Terminator, even a few of the big disaster movies.

What's the deal with Spielberg? It's like his attempt to add depth just makes the movies ponderous and visually dull. And that's a pretty big knock given this movie's great special effects.

Worth seeing once in the theater, if you love disaster movies.

Cheers

title: The tripods are wiping out humans as revenge for appearing in this film!
review:
So disappointing. The source material has so much potential and this is just a quickly slammed to together summer blockbuster FX laden mess. The Tripods are remarkable, but they belong in a good movie. Not this one. I think they are wiping out the humans as revenge for appearing in this film.

Where is the mighty battle between the Thunderchild and a war machine? One of the most amazing things in the book was not realized in this film. So sad. Now it will be decades or more before anyone else can take a big budget shot at doing this great book justice. What a pity.

Stay home and read the book. Now there's an idea.

title: Misses the mark; an unfortunate Spielberg failure
review:
Like the giant tripod robots from hell that invade Earth, War of the Worlds is shaky and collapses easily under its own weight. Sure, the effects are typically extraordinary for a Spielberg film, but the invasion itself is illogical and the scenes in which the human characters interact with each other fall flatter than the buildings that the robots stomp.

A freakish lightning storm knocks out all power, including cell phones and automobiles. This shouldn't have been much of a shock to anyone, since apparently every news report leading up to the storm discussed electromagnetic pulses in other parts of the world that... knocked out all power. I guess that might have been a comment on how Americans don't pay much attention to world events. As the local denizens scratch their heads in consternation and frustration, giant machines rise up from underground and then obliterate everyone in their paths. Madness ensues.

We see all of this death and destruction through the eyes of Ray Ferrier (Tom Cruise) and his kids Robbie and Rachel (Justin Chatwin and Dakota Fanning, respectively). Robbie's a typical sullen teenager, veering between responsible older brother and impudent jerk. Unsurprisingly, he doesn't have a strong relationship with his father, and neither does Rachel. The kids have been conveniently dropped off for the weekend by their very-pregnant mom (the seldom-seen Miranda Otto), all the better for them all to potentially reunite at the end of the movie.

Much of the movie involves ducking and running and running some more, and mobs of angry people who resemble zombies without the cold logic, and tentacles, and aliens, and about a zillion shocked looks on Mr. Cruise's face. That's about it. Run, run, take a breath, run some more, peek around a corner. It goes on like this for a while, during which time we see humans alternately being vaporized or eviscerated. In fact, the violence is pretty intense, and I wonder what had to be cut in order for the film to attain a PG-13 rating.

The scariest movies are the ones that have at least a strong hint of realism - the audience, in other words, must feel as if what is happening on screen could definitely happen to them. And it's easy to imagine the events in War of the Worlds happening. Oh, perhaps not a full-on alien invasion, but a gigantic catastrophe of some stripe. That's why Independence Day was so popular, and it's also why Close Encounters of the Third Kind was so special.

Of course, Spielberg was responsible for Close Encounters, but this one doesn't approach the magic of the earlier film. At least with Close Encounters, we had a vague idea of why we were being visited; here, although we know they're here to kill us all, we don't know why, exactly. And how is it that giant machines could be buried underground for millions of years without anyone knowing? Surely we have the necessary equipment to detect giant metal.

While the effects are a huge credit to the movie - and ultimately save it - the script and the acting are two major debits, particularly Cruise and Fanning. Cruise normally plays characters who are the Smartest Guys in the Room, exuding coolness at all times. Ray's not a smart guy. He's an idiot and an incredibly bad father, as he seems to have a knack of putting his kids in danger (although he gets better at that as the movie progresses). Unfortunately, Cruise simply doesn't have the range to play an idiot; Ray comes off as just an obnoxious and selfish. Indeed, he spends much of the movie shocked, shocked at what's going on - which would be anyone's natural reaction, of course, but this movie needed a hero of some sort, kind of like Dennis Quaid in the similarly themed The Day after Tomorrow.

Once upon a time, Fanning was cute and talented. She's all of 11 years old now, and she's neither cute nor talented. True, her character spends much of the movie fleeing in terror or screaming her head off, but any actress could have done that. Rachel is far too broadly written, and inconsistently so; sometimes she's precocious, offering Ray advice on dealing with Robbie, and other times she's dumber than your average 10 year old.

Why couldn't this movie have been better? Spielberg and Cruise worked very well on Minority Report, and Spielberg's gone the aliens route before with E.T. and Close Encounters, so why did this one fail? I don't think it's unreasonable to expect their collaborations to be pretty good, given their track records, and War of the Worlds simply misses the mark. The action scenes are very intense, almost draining the audience of emotion, but the scenes with actual dialog are terribly shallow and predictable, not to mention unintentionally funny.

title: Very Disappointed with WOTW
review:
From a pure special effects perspective, WOTW is OK, but unfortunately there was no plot. Why did the invaders invade? Where did they really come from?, etc. As I watch each special effects scene I hoping these questions would be answered. But nothing happened. The plot centered on the main characters trying to survive; but in a movie of this type you need to really explain the "antagonist(s)" in order to keep the audience interested. If you really want to see a great WOTW film, rent or buy the original from 1953, or better yet, rent or buy Independence Day (1996). Now this movie really has it together from beginning to end.

Julius

title: Boycotting War of the Worlds
review:
...because of Tom Cruise...a great idea, send a message to Hollywood that a star's off-screen life has consequences. Tom Cruise's efforts on behalf of Scientology are far more dangerous than the consequences of a wife-beater, drug user, bigot or the like, however abstract they might be in comparison. Show Hollywood that featuring a cult member as a star is barely more acceptable than giving a feature role to a terrorist.

WHY WAS THE ENTIRE THREAD (NUMEROUS POSTS) ABOUT POSSIBLE BOYCOTTS OF WAR OF THE WORLDS DELETED BY AN ADMINISTRATOR (THUS INSPIRING THIS POST)???!!! WHY THE CENSORSHIP???!!! IS IMDb BOWING TO Hollywood PRESSURE???

title: This version of War of the Worlds is very disappointing
review:
I have never been as pleased with visual effects and at the same time disappointed with acting, character development, and story line. The inconsistencies within what is available as a story line were too obvious to have been overlooked which causes me to believe this was truly a sloppy production. Example: an electronic pulse has knocked out every thing electronic, yet a pedestrian has a cam-corder video unit taking pictures of the destruction taking place.

Tom Cruise, as good an actor as he is, never makes the character in this film believable. He doesn't come across as genuine. His young co-star Dakota Fanning was better at getting into her part than was Tom. I blame this on script as much as acting.

All in all, I wished I could get my money back on this one. It's a dud. Not because of cinematography or special effects, but because of story line and character development.

title: A movie that brings you'll all the way to the end, crashes and burns.
review:
This movie is by far Spielbergs weakest. It's surely a summer block buster to remember because my friends sister got pregnant. When the movie came to it's end Myself and 600 others in the movie theater laughed at it's cheese.

Well's should be rolling in his grave right now . If some one is going to make money off this man at least do it honorably. The SFX were awesome. which is all in a days work.The 120 million dollar budget is there that's for sure. I hope next summer you don't disappoint me as much because I am honestly just looking to watch a good movie.

Thanks

SSJR

title: Was Awesome!
review:
I just got back from seeing this film. Despite Dakota Fanning's supremely annoying performance as "Constantly screaming at very high decibels girl" I thought it was awesome. It was true to the spirit of H.G. Wells classic story, while at the same time modernizing it quite a bit. Yes there are holes, but the entire film being based on a hokey early 20th century alien invasion storyline will do that to a film.

It's very fun to watch, had spectacular explosions (always important) and lots of death and mayhem and property damage so severe I would advice any insurance company agents to steer clear of the film as the mere thought of the accumulated damage would send him or her into instant cardiac arrest. The film would have been better if instead of Dakota Fanning they had oh I don't know..say Devon Aoki...

title: "Is it terrorists?!"
review:
Nope, indeed it is not, it's forces beyond our understanding from the other worlds! It's War of the Worlds in fact! LOL! Well, after the huge TomKat craze I think everyone felt in 2005's summer, I felt like I had seen enough of Tom and that kind of effected me seeing the movie, I know that's sad, but I think most of us felt the same. But to my surprise, actually I shouldn't be because of Steven Spielberg, this was a great movie. It kept me interested and it was quite a ride!

But once again, Tom's crazy antics kept me just being sarcastic and wanting him to call the man in the cellar that was trying to help them "glip!" :D I had fun though, this had such an eerie and very real feeling to it that kept you screaming and wanting to know how to defeat the alien forces. The machines, even though I'm not a fan of CGI, were awesome and frightening! The acting, especially on Dakota's part, was really amazing. Yes, Dakota went a little crazy with the screams, but she reacted like most ten year olds would. I was a little confused with the son, Robbie, going off into the battle fields and later on was in Boston waiting for his father and sister. Didn't make much sense.

Steven has done it again, this has to be one of the better remakes of this year so far. He had a great cast and great ideas, I just feel bad that Tom gave all that bad publicity for him onto the film. But like I said, it's a good movie and should be given a chance. It has cool effects, good acting, a great scenery and feel, and just a sense of horror of this possibly happening! The truth is out there! :D

8/10

title: Better to watch the old version
review:
After one dud after another, I have decided that whoever the genius was that did all of the early work Spielberg took the credit for is either retired, dead, or was fired.

I was disappointed in the movie, but my poor friend was devastated. He has been reading all the hype on this movie for several months and I believe expected the book or at least something entertaining.

The characters were not likable. I am still trying to figure out the plot. The effects were good but fell way short of making the movie. The money spent the hire Tom Cruise was wasted. This was a movie of screaming and running; it wasn't for me.

My advice is go rent or buy the old version with Gene Barry, it was a much better movie and you can pay for it with the money saved on this flick.

title: Terrible
review:
has spoiler: This is one of the worst movies I have ever seen. Dakota Fanning is annoying, and by the end of the movie I wished she would have been eaten by the aliens.

This movie has no coherency, nothing is explained. Tom Cruise throws a grenade in one machine...VOILA! All of them are screwed up. don't expect any rhyme or reason for this one. Red roots start growing everywhere without explanation, And Cruise decides to kill a dude because he wants to dig a tunnel.Not only is the majority of the movie pointless, the ending is supposed to be some dramatic reunion. But even that lacks any emotion. This is without a doubt the worst 7.50 I have spent. I can't believe these critics say this is Spielberg at its best. He should be ashamed.

title: Very disappointing, felt like all effects, no story!
review:
After the first 20 minutes of repeated scary effects, I kept thinking the story was going to "start", then after a certain amount of time had passed, I realized that this was it. Repeated effects, scary music and lots of people trying to get away from it all. Even the ending did not explain itself very well... (a voice telling us how the end of the situation came about) While watching it, you get no sense of who are these aliens?, where did they come from?, and why do they want to kill all of us anyway. Who is their leader? There were some moments that lead me to think more was coming story wise, such as when he touched the rock and said it was freezing, and put it in his pocket, when he saw someone he knew with her child at the ferry.. ( what was that all about?)

Too many implausible situations, some of which were really quite annoying... the one car in the city that works?, the only people who aren't hit by the death rays, the one house with light, being able to drive on those roads! the fact they could swim like that with all their clothes and shoes on?? I don't think so How did they all get to Boston? Then the end with the family on a clean, quiet street happy and safe? What was that??? Very unbelievable. This had potential to be interesting beyond special effects, it flopped badly.

I like movies that make me think This one didn't give me anything to think about!

Look for a War of the World video game soon, it fits.

title: the money pit
review:
so why did they make this movie?? how is it possible to get a child prodigy and still screw up the acting... are they in cahoots with the executives from enron...cause I don't know where all that money went... no screen play, none of the characters are likable, and the special effects both pale in comparison and rip off any trilogy made in the last thirty years...

I heard someone in jersey is challenging Spielberg's film with a film he made for $99... it is called "Night of the Day of the Dawn of the Son of the Bride of the Return of the Revenge of the Terror of the Attack of the Evil, Mutant, Alien, Flesh-Eating, Hellbound, Crawling, Zombified, Living Dead Part Three"...and despite the title I don't know how it can't beat War of the Worlds

title: Best movie in years!
review:
I just saw "War of the Worlds" today and I have to say, it was a home run for me. Best movie I've seen in years. It's not often there comes along a movie that I want to go right back into the theater and see again that very minute. "War of the Worlds" is one of those movies.

Despite all the negative publicity around Tom Cruise, Spielberg picked him well. He carries the part beautifully as a two time loser, who is determined he won't strike out keeping his two children alive, and returning them to their mother.

The movie has terror, chills, grisly horror, and most important, the movie has heart. I'm not going to elaborate because to do so would cheat you of all the fun I experienced.

Suffice it to say if you see one film this year, make it this movie.

The movie of the year!

title: There are no words to describe how bad this movie is ...
review:
having just sat through this film with a bunch of friends, we are now engaged in a non stop attempt to find words to express our disgust. I have a constant chorus of voices sat behind me right now saying 'what the hell was that all about ...' Never have we all agreed so completely on a movie, and never have we found it impossible to find a redeeming feature. The Special effects are painfully bad, the script childish and amateur. Every actors performance was obviously a secret attempt to deride Spielberg by being deliberately bad. The characters were so inhuman, so opposite to how anyone would act, as to have convinced several of my gang to believe the film was intended to be a comedy taking the mickey out of serious movies.

It was really terribly bad. How it ever got made is beyond me, but that it was allowed a release by the stellar crew of film makers connected to it beggars belief. Every scene was painful to watch, the ones I manage to stay awake for and the rest of the party remained sitting through. Those of us who didn't walk out in frustration and utter disbelief wished we had done by the sudden and rushed ending.

I beseech you, save you money and 2 hours of your lives and just poke needles into your eyes instead. It will certainly be more pleasant. There is none of the brain dead popcorn entertainment you expect from Cruise, no simple but well directed Spielberg magic. There is just unremitting drivel, a butterball of a turkey.

title: Pathetic loser!
review:
One has lots of expectation of a movie from Cruise and Spielberg backyard. I am in fact, a fan of both and haven't missed any of their movies. I am still coming to terms with the way they made this movie. Forget the visuals and sci-fi jumbos. The movie lack essential direction and story telling.

And Cruise, you don't need my thoughts, but here is my 2 cents: it would do you good if you stop acting like a jerk and arrogant ass in real life. We appreciate you work hard, and so does everyone. Keep your nonsense with yourself, and make a better movie next time.

Dakota Fanning: you are talented, no doubt. Don't let this go to your head this early in life. Screaming and staring is not acting. You need to work real hard. Learn from giants like De Niro, Hoffman, Hanks, Cuise and many others.

Tim Robbins: Man, what happened to you. Next time, check your role and the pay check.

Spielberg: I think you want to show contrast between Terminal (excellent direction) and WotW. But yes, to give you credit this is not as pathetic as A.I.

title: War of the Worlds
review:
Warning there is plot given away here!

Steven Spielberg director of such films as Jaws, Close Encounters of the Third Kind and ET takes us on a journey into our world at war with an enemy we know nothing about and one that can't be defeated by mans best weapons. No I am not talking about the Chinese and their economic policies. The Martians have attacked us or so we assume. In H.G Wells classic The War Of the Worlds, Mars attacks us because they have long coveted our planet and also they screwed theirs up apparently. But here, we are not exactly sure who they are or where they are from, all we are sure is they are not terrorists.

Instead of taking a step back and looking at this through mankind's eyes we step forward and see it through one mans eyes. Our hero is non other than Ray Ferrier (Tom Cruise Holmes aka Dr. Cruise no Xanax for me thank you) a divorced and emotionally negligent father of two not so wonderful kids. Ray who by the way works for a living (he tells his daughter this) on the shipyard docks as a crane operator has no food in the kitchen for his two kids but does have a deconstructed engine in place of the pot roast, tasty. We find this out of course because the kids have been dropped off by his ex and her new (rich) husband (Tim) for their alloted quality time together. Oh and guess what, the ex (Miranda Otto) is pregnant with Mr. Wall Streets baby, how quaint. Moving forward, the son Robbie (Justin Chatwin) is a dick (Rays words not mine)and the daughter Rachel(Dakota Fanning)is a hypochondriac health nut (who later on states that she has a bad back). I should mention a baseball through the window but there is not enough time.(funny though).

Moving forward we find Ray having to sleep. (He works for a living like I already said) Ladies, he takes his shirt off here > < right after telling Rachel (futhur known as Sick) to order food and before his son Robbie (lets just call him Dick) steals his Ford fastback Mustang. Upon awaking our hero feasts upon a hearty humus meal (the look on his face is priceless)discusses a splinter, finds out that his car and Dick are gone and low and behold discovers lightning strikes at least 27 times in the same place.

Moving quickly. Ray runs out the front door and leaves the splinter infected 9 year old there alone to wait for her brother. So what was Ray looking to find out in the street? 1. His Dick, B. His Stang or 4. Everything at a dead stop. The answer is ding ding ding E. All of the above! Ray sends Dick into watch Sick then runs like a lemming to find out where everyone else is running to like a lemming. On the way he verbally repairs a van and chums around with two ethnic(the only memorable ethnic speaking parts) lads thrown in (I guess) to show that Ray is at least culturally diverse and not a total sh-t head. I digress.

Meanwhile a crowd has formed a circle around the 27 lightning strikes in the middle of an intersection. New Yorks or New Jerseys in this case finest are there controlling the crowd um well looking at the ground anyway (Krispy Kreme must have been closed. Then...The ground shakes, cracks, splits, explodes and all hell breaks loose. Ray, right in the middle of it all. Herrrreeesss Johnny, all dressed in metal with three legs and a giant triangle head standing 150 feet tall. Or so it seems. Needless to say Ray is stupefied along with the horse he rode in on (ok, there's no horse). And this all happens in the first 10 or ah 15 minutes, I forget.

To make a long story short (to late) there is a lot gnashing of teeth and wailing and the national guard trying hard but failing (I guess all the good soldiers were in IRAQ). A van ride, a plane crash, another van ride, more teeth gnashing and wailing. Some more van riding, a pee pee break with a water adventure, some more van riding, a van hijacking and a lot of walking. A ferry ride, a water ride, more gnashing of teeth and wailing. More national guard trying, more failing, oh and cool jets and helicopters failing. Dick being drawn to the flame like a moth and Sick almost being taken by a morally terrified woman or is that I terrified moral woman? Then there is the basement with a pedophile and the snake machine not to mention four of the aliens from independence day only in midget form with a third leg. What does that mean? Well then there is a murder behind a closed door. Oh wait more gnashing of teeth and wailing, blood, plants, blood plants, 1 grenade, two cages and then 2 grenades. I forgot to say some more walking, bacterial infestation, birds, national guards not failing(recalled from Iraq finally), rocket launchers, walking, Boston, hugging, Mary Ann, Sick, Dick and the two leads from the 1953 George Pal classic The War Of The Worlds.

All in all I give it 4 stars and 32 bucks since that is what it cost me for 2 tickets, 2 drinks, a popcorn, a candy and two hours of my life I can't get back. Wait I saw it twice already. Add another 32 and 4 hours of that life thing. Oh hell am going to see it again on Saturday. That's another 32. OK then I give it 4 stars, 96 bucks and 6 hours of my boring life that even if I could get it back I would just go see a movie anyway. Mr. Spielberg keep up the good work and uh could you loan me a few bucks?

title: aliens attacking the world, Tom Cruise let us witness it - worst film ever
review:
Usually, i'm not so much into blockbusters. But since SFX and action are quite fun from time to time, we thought let's go and see the new Spielberg/Cruise movie, that shall save this years earnings of the US film industry. Well, we saw a blockbuster, so much is for sure. But: _ Is it still the time for invisible speakers, telling us what to think? _ Is it necessary that the audience should be given the opportunity to follow the plot?

I think that you have to see the film before you understand what happens there. I've been sitting five minutes after the end not being able to move, to tell you how shocked I was. What an INCREDIBLY BAD, not to say insulting end.

What Spielberg got: _ He believes in god (well, in the US, that seems to be quite common) _ He makes us know it (WATCH the end, even if it's hard to stay in the cinema for so long, but it's REALLY worth it, worst end EVER!!!) _ He makes us think that god has given special respect to humans (that's what the bible say?!?) and that those bad,bad aliens (why did they come for, what do they want, nobody knows, nobody cares, since we have so many dead people, so much fear and so many SFX) deserve to die (maybe some parts of the bible got rewritten while crossing the ocean, who knows..)

What Spielberg lacks: _ a plot (actually, a plot that is SOMEWHAT logically sound) _ a main actor (well, sorry ladies, but Tom Cruise was handsome and sexy in Top Gun, but, well, he doesn't do Shakespeare very often, does he? But I have to admit that he plays the illiterate guy from next door who got chased by his wife for a guy that has money quite convincingly.. ;) _ sense of humor - or why does the story end this way(the ones interested in the history of this movies will know what I'm talking about)? IT SIMPLY CANNOT HAVE BEEN SERIOUS!!!!

Anyway, watch it, you will not regret it, you will have witnessed a historical moment: THE WORST FILM OF ALL TIMES, WITH PERFECT SPECIAL EFFECTS.

title: 2 stars because its only the 2nd worst movie this year.
review: I don't know what I was thinking when I went to go see this movie. I knew it was going to be horrible, but rottentomatoes.com cost me $8 and 2 1/2 hours of my life with its 80+ rating. That being said, if you like the Revenge of the Sith (the worst movie of the year) - you'll probably like this movie as well. Crap story, no real emotional motivations, lack of charisma, bad writing, and did I mention crap story. All great elements for an excellent summer blockbuster, ripe to make hundreds of millions. Since no paid critic will say it - Spielberg, George Lucas, Tom Cruise, Warner, and anyone else associated with War of the Worlds and or Revenge of the Sith has been reduced to peddling crap. Thanks, I enjoyed the $20 worth. I'm just too much of an optimist that I thought maybe you big names had some unique talent to offer.

title: Great, won an advance showing ticket!
review: I am a huge Jurassic Park fan, and Steven has made his next classic! I have not been this pleased with a movie since Jurassic Park (so a long time coming). title: Spielberg, what have you done?
review:
On September 11th, we all watched as the two towers came tumbling down. We were all affected in some way. Those who are in the creative fields looked at the world and saw something they wanted to capture. Spielberg thought he'd make a poignant look at the American family in the days following the crisis.

So. War of the Worlds. A movie that lacks any sort of subtlety (like most Spielberg films). From the grey ash, to the terror in the streets, to Dakota Fanning shouting "Terrorists!" every five minutes. We are looking at people reacting to something horrific. People under pressure. People doing what they can to make the best out of the situation.

Though since Tom Cruise's character, Jay, is always on the forefront. He's not an average American or the working class guy they make him out to be. He's too in the know. It's easy to see how poor his relationship with his kids is, because they say it. Over and over again. As I mentioned, this movie lacks subtlety. Still, he's one of the witnesses to the attack. After seeing something hit the ground, and a large "Tripod" emerge, he automatically knows everything about it's origin. How does he know everything? How was he able to piece all of it together? An average family in this situation would be in the basement, hiding, and fleeing. Just as confused, trying to make sense of it all. Instead, he's got all the information and he's even fighting Aliens that the entire U.S. Army couldn't scratch.

This is thematically different from any incarnation of War of the Worlds that has been done. I don't mind differences between books, or other films. Thing is, I should still be able to watch this, not knowing anything about it, and be able to say, with no question in my mind "This is War of the Worlds." Instead, I start thinking "Is this War of the Worlds, or Independence Day?"

title: pulse-pounding sci-fi thriller
review:
With his stunning remake of H. G. Wells' "War of the Worlds," Steven Spielberg has created one of the most intense and terrifying visions of the coming apocalypse in motion picture history. Here is a film that makes "Independence Day" look like a Sunday school picnic or a casual stroll through Central Park on a warm sunny afternoon. The utter darkness of this film is rather amazing considering the fact that Spielberg practically cut his teeth as a director on benign (albeit brilliant) sci-fi fantasies like "Close Encounters" and "E.T," movies in which visitors from outer space were seen as emissaries of peace rather than invaders bent on destroying the human race (I don't think it's merely a coincidence that the unnerving sound the alien machines make in this film resembles some of the notes from Bernard Herrmann's score for "The Day the Earth Stood Still"). In "War of the Worlds," the aliens are anything but benign; they are cruel, vicious, bloodthirsty and unstoppable, creatures more akin to the ones in "Jaws" and "Jurassic Park" than those in "Close Encounters" and "E.T." And, indeed, there are far more echoes of scenes from "Jurassic Park" in "War of the Worlds" than any other previous Spielberg work. "War of the Worlds" is certainly a case of Spielberg returning to his more "primitive" roots, for after his recent ventures into the world of cerebral sci-fi ("A.I." and "Minority Report"), the director pulls out all the stops in this film, turning out a full-throttle, no-holds-barred orgy of non-stop death and destruction. In "War of the Worlds," Spielberg has found the perfect source material for his roller coaster ride mentality and it pays off beautifully for all concerned. As always, Spielberg turns a mere "genre" picture into a work of art.

Tom Cruise stars as Ray Ferrier, a working class stiff living in northern New Jersey who seems barely able to take care of himself, let alone the teenaged son and eleven-year-old daughter who have come to stay with him while their mother is away in Boston visiting her parents. Ray is obviously anything but a model parent, having alienated both children, particularly his son, with his absentee parenting style and casual indifference to the lives they are leading. All that is about to change, however, when, without any real warning, the earth suffers a massive invasion by creatures from outer space whose killer machines have been lying dormant underground for seemingly millions of years. As the monsters wreak havoc upon the planet, Ray flees with his children, searching for a place of safety in a world suddenly turned upside down and apparently headed for extinction and annihilation.

Spielberg has wisely chosen to paint Ray in less than heroic terms. In addition to the fact that he has trouble assuming the role of protector and comforter for his own children, he is often at a loss as to what to do to escape the threat and ensure their survival. The director has Cruise work against type here, helping us to identify with his plight in a way we might not have were he conceived as a more conventional heroic type. Although it's a little hard to accept Cruise as such an uncaring father, we go along with the premise, knowing that he will eventually become closer to his kids though the life-threatening situation in which they find themselves.

As this is a Spielberg film, it goes without saying that "War of the Worlds" is a model of state-of-the-art visual and sound effects, and that the director exploits every moment for its full intensity and impact. This is as tightly-wound and suspenseful a thriller as I have seen in years. But what really puts it over is the way in which Spielberg manages to bring an end-of-the-world eeriness and paranoia to so much of the film. The first half, in particular, is almost unbearable to watch, so unsettling is the sense of inexplicable dread and doom that hangs over the work, so intense our feeling of powerlessness before the unknown. About a half hour into the picture, I realized that this film was striking chords in my psyche that most movies never even come close to touching. Spielberg really makes us feel what it would be like if everything we took for granted were suddenly snatched away from us and we were forced to confront a menace we didn't understand and against which we had no defenses. In a post-9/11 world, that is a very chilling and powerful concept indeed.

Cruise and young Dakota Fanning do a beautiful job playing off one another in their many scenes together, making a real connection with us in the audience. Tim Robbins is effective as a somewhat crazed survivor who allows the family to hide in his farmhouse, even if the scenes there, though good, turn out to be the weakest in the film.

Some people have objected to the rather abrupt ending of the movie, but anyone familiar with the Wells original knows that Spielberg is merely being faithful to the author's own vision. It seems rather petty to be getting on the man's case for his fidelity to a well-respected source when movie makers are so often criticized for not remaining true to their material.

"War of the Worlds" is that rare genre film that seeps into your bones, taps into some of your most primal fears, and makes you look at the world in a different way the moment you step out of the theater. But then that has been Spielberg's hallmark as a director all along. Chalk up another triumph for the master.

Some movies that fall into this trap are "Independance Day", and "The Day After Tomorrow" plus numerous others. These films all fall into a new-sub-genre of *End-of-the-World* Films. They're have been more that have been forgotten about over the years. See Kyle MacLachlan's "Trigger Effect" also by Koepp.

I never thought I would see this film because these kinda movies have been done over and over again add nauseam (and furthermore they have never been done very well either). But ultimately Jaws is a B movie plot idea taken straight from the 1950's Drive-Inns. I was hopeful that I might be surprised and delighted by Spielberg. He has and undeniable way of charming, shocking and surprising us, the audience, time and time again.

That is why I am SO surprised to see Spielberg drop the ball here! But then again I missed the point of AI which in my estimate was one of only a few bombs that he has ever made.

My question is how do the aliens die at the end? What kills these invaders? What did I miss? Was there even a reason given for there invasion? Whats with the spray of blood all over the ground when people seem to just get vaporized? What ever happened to all the cute little Spielbergian aliens who just wanna raid the 'fridge, drink all the beer in the house and make collect calls to "phone home"? There's more questions but right now I just NEED answers!!!

title: Solid, intense movie
review:
This movie managed to surprise me in a positive way. For a Hollywood blockbuster, this movie is somewhat different then you might expect. The overarching theme of "War of the worlds" is a world-wide alien invasion on Earth. Like most disaster movies on this scale, you might expect scenes of mass destruction from all over the globe. Not to mention huge battles between human resistance and the invaders (like those in Independence day). Well, in this case those expectations are wrong. Instead of showing an epic struggle between mankind and aliens, this entire movie is shot from the perspective of an average Joe called Ray Ferrier (Tom Cruise) and his children. The real theme of this movie isn't the alien invasion, but the desperate struggle of the average man (or family) to survive in times of crisis. What do you do when everything you took for granted is wiped out in mere seconds?

I guess this might be a bummer to some who'd like to see as much explosions on screen as possible. But this perspective turns out to work wonderfully well, thanks to the execution.

The acting and dialogue in this movie was mostly good and felt realistic. Tom Cruise does a pretty good performance here. A fine example is the scene when he comes back home after just surviving the first encounter with the alien invaders. He's utterly lost, confused about what he just saw. There's only one thing he can think of: RUN! As fast as you can! He portrays all of this very well. There's no typical American action hero's here. There's panic, desperate attempts to escape. How this can lead to very extreme behavior, is shown in a very effective scene were people fight with each other like animals over a car, which finally even results in murdering. Quite disturbing.

The scenes where the alien machines actually appear and start blasting everything to oblivion are very intense and sometimes downright scary. During the first encounter it feels like you're actually THERE running along with the crowd, trying to get away. The gigantic "Tripods" are really menacing and add a real sense of danger and fear to the movie, something that is often lacking in Hollywood blockbusters. Spielberg still knows how to create tension and intense action.

That said, the movie isn't flawless. After nearly two hours of intense and fine footage, the ending feels a bit rushed (beware: some major SPOILERS here).

The way the aliens are "defeated" is pretty refreshing. Finally it's not because of great American heroes and lots of firepower, it's because of bacteria. It might disappoint many viewers though, since this means the movie doesn't go out with a "bang". It all happens quite fast (maybe a bit too fast). What really feels out of place though is the family reunion at the end. It's a bit too happy and almost seems to pretend that nothing happened (you'll see). Besides it'sa bit unbelievable that everyone survived.

Other then that, this is a very exiting and intense movie experience. Recommended!
