title: Aliens come to earth and invade with their indestructible war machines.
review: Well, Mr. Cruise, you did it again, got in the way of a movie while pretty much playing yourself, undoubtedly to simply continue staying in the limelight. That aside, this movie was quite uneven in quality. The alien war machines were amazing, and the one close to true element from the great novel by H.G. Wells. Otherwise, this film was often an excuse for a Tom Cruise fest, which, for me, doesn't make for much, particularly within a story that has quite a thought-provoking premise but is not given its full due. One thing I can say is, thank goodness for child actress Dakota Fanning. She was the most genuine, interesting person on-screen, out-acting Tom Cruise big time. Way to go, Dakota! As for the story-line, it was sloppy in places, and I will not say just how and where here for fear of divulging a spoiler or two. Oh, yeah, and then there were the aliens; rather disappointing for me, albeit technically well-done. If they were portrayed as author H.G. Wells had described them, a whole new type of movie alien could have been born. But, no, alas, not even that was meant to be. The script seemed poorly written here and there, leaving me sometimes scratching my head and thinking, "Huh?" or "You can't be serious?!" Dear Mr. Wells is probably turning over in his grave now. Borrowing from Ebert and Roeper, I'd give it one thumb up and one thumb down.

title: Felt like a big budget version of "signs".
review:
I thought signs was an awful movie - but this I'd say was worth seeing but flagged towards the end. You did care a bit for the characters (well except the teenage boy whose reason for leaving the family group was 'I've got to see this'). The idea of keeping it close to the family, as signs had, was mildly successful and you got to see enough of the aliens to see how generally nasty they where, but it would have been good to see more interaction with others, get a feeling of what was going on outside, apart form seeing it on screens in the TV van.

Some scenes where laboured, the basement scene with the alien eye on a stalk (it's the same as the scene out of the abyss) could have been much shorter and some of the camera panning did look a bit fake as well (trying to be too clever I think) but there where some nice touches, such as the train on fire.

So not bad, but could have been turned up a few more notches to turn it into something more epic.

title: Steven Spielberg's "War of the Worlds"
review:
I am a huge Steven Spielberg fan. To me, this film was never about special FX, how well it would do against Episode III, or Tom Cruise. I was just eager to see my idol's next project. He seemed excited to be doing it. All involved seemed excited too.

And then something happened.

Tom Cruise was jumping all over couches and spouting lessons of Scientology, people who loved Episode III became haters inadvertently, and audience members left the theaters disappointed at the abrupt ending, somehow forgetful of how the original literary material ends. And the attention to Spielberg's "War of the Worlds" detoured from a critique on the craftsmanship involved, to the silly circus of people around it.

By all accounts, this film is excellent on many levels. The pacing is right on, the special FX are indeed superb, John Williams' score is a great parallel to the action on screen, and Spielberg again shows his knack for creating unforgettable images laden with emotion, horror, and pulse-pounding adrenaline.

Although I personally feel that this film could've been so much more plot wise, I also feel that it redeems its' faults with its' plethora of virtues.

Spielberg makes movies with his heart. It seems that some audience members are surprised at this. Some people may not like this film. Some may like it. But the fact of the matter is that one of the great director's of our era has composed a great summer blockbuster and more went right than wrong.

If anyone should doubt Spielberg's elite place in the annals of the world of film, show me another filmmaker who has managed to stay on top for 30 years.

Just Enjoy!

title: THe war of the wannabe's
review:
What can I say but that Spielberg And Cruise Deserve each other. The film is a hidden commentary of an "Imperial power dominating the less powerful and that even a dead beat narcissistic dad (Cruise Character and from what I hear in real life..at least the narcissistic part) heeds the call and becomes hero and warrior. I thought the special effects were the best character in the movie.

Tim Robbins is awful in this and one wonders why he was cast. Dakota fanning screams a lot but she does well terrified.THe script goes south in different parts of this film. Meaning some things that seem to be pushed emotionally suffers from underdevelopment. Other wise if you like to see shoot um up action flick on crack you will like this one. I did ....its a nice movie with unbuttered popcorn.

title: War of the Worlds a major disappointment
review: I only went to see this movie because of Spielberg. Tom Cruise is to creepy for me. Anyway, Tom Cruise's character isn't a good father, or even a very good person. Suddenly he has his children thrust upon him just as the aliens are invading. He shares no connection with his children and they prefer each other's company to his. As the movie progresses their bonds do grow a little. But I never felt any empathy for his character. The best performance of all belong to Tom Cruise's daughter. She will blow you away. The special effects are amazing but the story isn't. There isn't the tension that the 50's version has. Even worse is the ending of the movie. After 90 minutes of carnage and destruction Tom Cruise arrives in Boston to find everyone in his family has survived the alien attack. What makes it even more astounding is that not only are they alive but their untouched, I mean their clothes are clean, no rips, and they look like they've been out to Church wearing their Sunday best. The ending ruined this movie for me. I left the theater went home and watched the original 50's version on DVD. By the way the 50's alien is better looking than the Spielberg aliens.

title: Stupid characters - moronic children
review: I am a huge sci-fi fan. So much that I like almost all large budget sci-fi films, even if their acting or storyline is a little bit poor. But I have never been a fan of sci-fi movies that are family-oriented. This is due to the fact that most them have kids driving parents and audiences nuts. WOTW is one of those irritating family driven movies that fail to deliver the message that the maker has so consciously sought at the expense of compromising the integrity and fun of the film. When will they ever get 'our' message that we don't want heart-soaking lectures in family matters messing up what should have been blockbusters. I don't deny that every writer/director has his own issues that he wants dealt with in his work but they should not be forced upon us in this most inopportune manner. People making blockbuster sci-fi films have a duty to fans not to indulge in their personal obsessions. In hindsight, we should all be grateful to Spielburg for not having directed Star Wars. Otherwise, Annakin Skywalker would never have become Darth Vader. He would simply have been a defiant child who always caused trouble for Obi-Wan and in the end embraced as if one could be forgiven for all his stupidity in the name of love. The problem with that is that fans don't forgive the moron because fans don't love him.

title: a waste of time
review: I went to see this movie after my husband said he liked it. well, this is the last time I am going to a movie. Time after time I am disappointed by the plots, no characters to identify with and frankly, what exactly is the point of this movie? Not to mention it's just one remake after another. As for this waste of money, how did they expect to drive so far without getting gas? The kid screamed way too much. The son needed to get slapped. The ending was just blunt and no explanation. Maybe we need to go back to the time when movies touched our hearts because it just seems movies these days are just a reason for the actors to scream and yell. I guess it makes sense since they are like trained monkeys, paid to entertain us....

title: Tom's son was the true hero
review:
The old film followed the usual 50's sci-fi conventions of trying to figure out the invaders' weakness and develop an appropriate weapon. The twist was that humans could not do that, and that ultimately the aliens were stopped by a providential Creator. The ending addressed the problem.

In Spielberg's film, the bulk of the story is an incredible journey survival story. The protagonist's goal is to reach Boston, not to stop the aliens. Well, Tom and family actually reach Boston--mission accomplished! Oh, and by the way, the aliens die--almost coincidentally. "Welcome to Boston. And you might want to avoid that falling alien on your way to grandma's." There's a moderately entertaining bit in the middle with Tim Robbins and aliens and a game of hide-and-seek. But that has nothing to do with very much. Tom's son turns up in Boston for the reunion at the end. We don't know how, because we weren't shown his story. But I can bet it was a lot more interesting that the story we were shown in this film--because Tom's son wanted to stop the aliens and separated from Tom just for that reason.

The initial huge and realistic devastation of a city was extremely depressing in light of the experience of recent years, and showing that our nation was impotent to deal with the problem was even more depressing. The ending where the aliens die from a common cold did nothing to relieve the depression. Maybe Tom's son was the real hero of the film--maybe he coughed on them, or popped a zit in their direction.

title: It sucks
review: Spielberg should know better. If I wanted to see vignettes on dysfunctional fathers and wacky survivalists, I could have watched Oprah or Jerry Springer Show. HG Wells should have been more closely followed. For example, the underlying reasons for the alien invasion could have been better defined (Martians having to leave a dying planet due to environmental factors, etc...) and the cause belli was never fully explained. Special effects were well done, but there was too much weirdness, strange red goop, etc.. that really did nothing other than be creepy. This was not a science fiction movie, but just a running daytime soap opera that happened to have an alien invasion as a background event.

title: War Of The World Doesn't Look Like One
review:
Wasted some bucks just to sit on premier class to watch this movie after hefty persuasion from friends, let me pinpoint several criteria that the movie should not be rated good.

Based on the title "War of the World", most people would imagine a war that is happening around the world, across every country, from east to west. After watching, I seen only helpless civilians walking on the same direction in most of the movie length. Then, some US soldiers arrived and waged war with the aliens. There are two scenes of war between the US soldiers and the aliens only. One is during the time when Robbie wanted to look how's the battle like when Ray trying to stop him. Second part is when Ray reached Boston, and AN alien invaded nearby the tunnel (there's only one alien against SOME soldiers?).

So, where are the scene of war between Russian soldiers versus the aliens, or China, or Japan, or Europe? Isn't it suppose to be war of the world? Instead of supposedly watching thousands of soldiers against hundreds (thousands, how I wished) aliens, there are only tiny numbers of human soldiers struggling hard to fight off the aliens.

Another odd thing, Boston's buildings are seen untouched, unlike the neighborhood where Ray was staying which has turned nothing but rubble. And, if you would think logically, Ray and his daughter was still few meters away, and the mother just opened the house door calmly and confidently and immediately rushed out to hug her daughter. Previously, we have seen Ray and the rest were hiding as deep as possible within the house, the basement.

The aliens turned weak just because of bacteria. It's a surprise if these I-see-it-as-ordinary germs able to spread that fast across the states that all aliens were actually infected, like pandemic (or should say, epidemic, because all I see the war was happened in the same region seen in the movie, not across the world).

And something has been annoying me. The nuisance of loud frequent panic breath. Though panic in this situation is natural and human would have fast beating heart and loud noise of releasing breath, but throughout the movie, it's VERY loud, especially during silent moment. Audio engineers should have aware on adjusting volume level of panic breath.

The scriptwriter should have done a lot better in the storyline. Nevertheless, Steven Spielberg's directing should be praised. I like the scene where the soldiers battling against the aliens when few copters released rockets towards the aliens (the scene were shot from land angle).

title: Action: OK. Plot, technical holes and stupid behavior
review:
One of my peeves, and this movie had enough that I noticed watching it once, are stupid technical inconsistencies. I.E., something a simple as a plain wristwatch stops working, but video camera works just fine!? And, replacing a starter solenoid fixes only that one car? Starter solenoids are not used at all on cars already running, yet all the cars died.

But an even bigger peeve is when main characters act just stupid. Especially when they have an responsibility such as taking care of their children. I could go on and on, but even the little dumb things like they're in a basement, and all the windows are blowing in. Action stops, so main character sticks his face RIGHT IN A WINDOW very soon after?! Duh. Or, much bigger - announce that he is aware that people may want to take the only running vehicle. Then, drive it right into a huge crowd of unruly people. Amazingly, the vehicle gets taken from them. But, leave the child in the car while he jumps out to physically fight EVERYONE in hand-to-hand combat. Real smart. Then, uses his gun - but not effectively, since that should have been used to quickly get away, not stand there until someone stronger comes along. Double duh. Okay, during the initial attacks, how long and how many times did he need to see everything being completely destroyed and people being vaporized before he "gets it", and actually keeps getting away. No, buildings are being destroyed, so hide behind a building. Smart. And, leave the kids - constantly. Leave the girl to go pee out of sight. Leave the kids in a house while you go far away to wander around - and, not obtain useful items, but ask stupid questions of others I.E. "where you on that plane?" What does it matter?! Or, you know you have no food, so tell the kid to grab all the food. Then, scold him for not grabbing food! Then, run to where the aliens are likely to attack - they already survived the initial attack - twice, and keep running from where they were safe already! Go to the mom's house, but don't grab ANY useful supplies. On and on. What a stupid, intelligence insulting movie. Appropriate for a cheap horror flick. Bitterly disappointing for an "action" movie, and shocking that this was a Steven Spielburg film.

title: Yuck!
review: Although it is obviously well made, I found this film an extremely unpleasant experience. It's obvious 9/11 imagery and a premise based on basically threatening a cute little girl with gruesome death for 2 hours just did not appeal. Additionally, the lack of almost anything new to the story--no new twists--really left me wondering what the whole point of the exercise is. Does Spielberg need to waste his time with this? Does Dreamworks need a quick cash infusion, or what? That said...I think that all of the acting was top-notch. Dakota did a great job with being threatened with gruesome death for both of its hours. Tim Robbins also stood out. Cruise delivered a very believable and nuanced performance. All the technical credits were solid--except that the alien craft bore a striking resemblance to those in Half-Life 2. However, all the positives give it a one star bump, because of the aforementioned unpleasantness.

title: This movie is WAY overrated
review: The film is entertaining, but is also very silly. Tom Cruise overacts (again) and isn't believable as a lousy father with principles. Also, the depiction lacked believability. It was hard to suspend disbelief throughout this science fiction story. How can an airplane destroy an entire neighborhood, yet miss the one car they need to escape? Stupid mistakes like this abound in the picture. It felt like a lazily-done and hackneyed story. Other examples like the entire 20 minute sequence with Tim Robbins could have (should have) been eliminated entirely. The movie also wraps itself up much too quickly and is all TOO tidy to be believable. Gets only an average rating by me.

title: Extremely disappointing...
review: When I went to see this, I was expecting to see a good action/sci-fi thriller flick. The previews were deceiving! Instead I get this totally plot less movie, with a terrible script, and almost emotionless characters (with the exception of Dakota fanning's character whose constant screaming was extremely annoying). Ray however is an "a**hole" father and gets worse and worse throughout the film. Was the throwing the peanut butter sandwich at the window totally necessary? The script is just plain uninteresting. Tim Robbin's character was okay. But I mean come on, if they aliens are as intelligent and advanced as they supposedly are, then they would know that Ray and them are hiding behind the mirror. And all the electricity is out but a guy still manages to use his camcorder?Huh? Overall, the only reason I gave it a two is because the special effects were pretty decent, but that's it.

title: Save Your Money
review:
Okay, I go to the movies about 5 times a year, saving my money for the really "big" ones. I fell for the hype and had to see Tom in his new movie. Well, this movie had me from the beginning when the attacks started to happen, but then I sat for the next 90 minutes waiting for Tom to DO SOMETHING. Honestly, the whole movie is him running away from the scene of the attacks and just yelling for his kids the entire time. I was really hoping to see him get together with his buddies to kick some alien tail. When Tim Robbins appeared, I thought "finally they are going to figure out how to kill them", but no it was just wasted minutes on the screen. I wish Will Smith appeared to kick some ass. At the end, Tom finally made it to his destination. The family there just looked as if they just finished their morning coffee in their perfect house in there perfect neighborhood while there is thousands of people walking aimlessly in the streets. If I were Tom I'd been so ticked that they were not out trying to get to him.

Anyway, Steven Spielberg needs to get back to telling good stories, with plots and characters I care about. I'd never watch this movie again unless I needed to test my surround sound system.

title: Yawn!
review: Let's see! We have a daughter whose mode of communication is a combination of primal screams and contrived cute comebacks, a teenage son caught up in the battle between angst and rebellion, an ex-wife who specializes in snide bitchiness, a hardhat hero whose personal demons were created by The Three Stooges. Did I mention that the script (or lack thereof) is a mixture of sophomoric mutterings and general boredom. For all the hype this film received, it fails miserably. Even the inclusion of a baseball rivalry (Yankees vs. Red Sox)fails to add spice to the film. Good science fiction is more than loud background and glittering special effects. There must be a story to go with the glitz. I found myself actually rooting for the aliens. This one is a stinker and totally wastes the talents of Tom Cruise and Tim Robbins.

title: Tighten it for DVD
review:
First of all this is the best invasion flick there is...

Okay I don't want to be Mister nay say, but there is just one thing that gave me a bad feeling after seeing this movie. The acting, oh it was just fine. Tom Cruise did quite a good job, but who really impressed me was Dakota Fanning.

The special effects are great, the music score was excellent. The scenes, damn what a terrific work. Spielberg's unexpected surprise moments had certainly given their impact. Those moments made me think of surprise scenes like in Indiana Jones. So thats a good thing.

Well the content of the movie. The plot, the story, now there we have the problem. There is no real strong plot. I don't care that there isn't much explaining about the aliens. Cause which doctor would be able to do a thorough scan on them right? But the missing of a good story, like about why they invade earth is a big disappointment.

So Spielberg do me and all the other people who have mostly positive feelings about this movie, bring out a Director's Cut or Extended, Revised version of this movie on DVD. Make sure it has a strong plot.

So folks if he does this, I think we have an great movie. But until now I can only say it is the best invasion flick that needs tightening in the plot.

title: omfg someone stop HG from spinning in his grave.
review: Okay yeah we have all seen bad remakes, but this one takes the cake and and sits on it to ingest it anally. What happened to industrial light and magic did they have any input on this little effort, maybe they were all suffering of hangovers from the revenge of the sith party. Yes we had some decent actors/actresses and Tom was doing his bit for the girls. But to be totally honest the whole plot of the classic epic was flushed down the drain. The story was not about a guy and his issues with his children now was it. I mean jeez the planet is being invaded by aliens and the movies focus is on trivial matters. Maybe its just me but it all seemed like a perversion of a truly great piece of literature. Spielberg you should be ashamed. Go See one of the old versions people their all better than this one.

title: The entire cinema laughed at the end
review:
A bit of a rant I'm afraid:

I need to stress something - the 4 points I have awarded this are for the visual effects and the visual effects alone. Well done ILM! But I'm so tired recently of walking out of a movie and commenting that "well, the special effects were good". Unfortunately, War Of The Worlds deserves exactly the same kind of postmortem analysis, crudely disguised as compliment, because the effects are the only good thing about this entire movie.

Like many, I grew up on Steven Spielberg and I love a lot of his work, let's face it, the man is a legend. So what has happened with his latest piece? A disaster movie - in every sense of the word!

No, I must be fair - for the first half an hour, forty five minutes, I was intrigued, interested and impressed, right up to the point even when the first Tripod starts blasting the hell out of a downtown street. Then, however, the film takes a turn for the worst. Let's analyse: When you set up a narrative, you introduce certain elements that act as tools for the storytellers. There are so many elements introduced that simply get forgotten about here - story beats that could have the potential to go somewhere that have been missed - for example: 1) The splinter in Dakota's finger - a conversation that seemingly is given importance and weight withing the first twenty minutes simply vanishes - and, knowing the end of the story - i.e. germs kill aliens - surely they could have used this splinter story to greater significance. "When it's ready, my body will simply push it out" - a fine metaphor for the world rejecting alien life - but as I said - forgotten, dismissed. 2) Tom Cruise places a piece of lightning-struck rock in his pocket - again, something that could have gone somewhere and didn't. 3) relationship between Tom Cruise and his kids VERY stereotypical - and never really given room to develop beyond the fact that his son always MOANS at him. By the time his son wants to go with the army to fight the tripods telling Tom Cruise "You have to let me go" I was practically screaming at the cinema screen - "YES! Please Tom, for God's sake, let the whining idiot GO! Spare us all another scene with him!" 4) How are we supposed to forgive a lead character who kills another man in cold blood - the entire Tim Robbins scene is absolutely appalling - what does it say about humanity? Human spirit in the face of adversity? I felt physically ill watching these scenes as all Tom and Tim seem to do is fight, then Tom decides to kill the "crazy guy". 3) What the hell is with Spielberg and his crappy, sappy sentimental endings? So, what - millions of people die horribly at the hands of the tripods, but - no, wait - Yes! there they are - ALL of Tom's family, including son who we are led to believe is dead - PLEASE!!!!! At this point, people in the cinema were in hysterics laughing!!!! - I'm sorry, but that kind of sappiness won't fly anywhere except in the States - it just doesn't work on British audiences. 4) What a completely crap end to a film - "and so the human race had earned it's place to survive" - whilst germs kill off the tripods - I know this is the ending to the novel, but come on - where is the story here? There is none. They should have changed this ending. At least in ID4, it was human actions that figured out how to kill the aliens.

If the people behind this are so-called "master storytellers" I worry. I am currently training to be a screenwriter and see, all too often, people with far more storytelling capabilities get put down time after time and then along come two really big names who have a new bag of tricks they'd like to play around with and the waves part for them to make their film, with no coherent story, no convincing character arc or anything like that. It sickens me, really.

But, War Of The Worlds will gross millions worldwide, so what the hell do I know, hey?

title: Not so bad..., but different
review:
Story: If you walk into the cinema with the expectation watching a movie like Independence Day, you will be disappointed. This Spielberg-Movie is different, not showing a President of the USA in an Airforce One.

Showing the invasion from the point of view of Tom Cruise's family ONLY was very unusually, but no disadvantage for quality of the movie.

Sound&Visual: The Sound and Special-Effects are excellent.

Actors: Tom Cruise doesn't really fit for the role of a family dad, therefor Dakota Fanning (Rachel) plays very well in the role of Ferrier's daughter.

title: Wet Firecracker
review:
One of the most memorable experiences I've had at a movie theater was the first time I saw "Saving Private Ryan". The relentless action and horror of the Omaha Beach sequence left me in open mouthed amazement. Spielberg has always been a master at creating memorable imagery, from the runaway Ferris wheel in "1941" to the boys flying on their bikes in front of the moon in "ET". But the opening of "Ryan" surpassed anything he had done with the medium of film. Not so co-incidentally, "SPR" was rated R.

Of course, Spielberg has made stinkers like "Lost World" and "A.I.", too. Lazy, sloppy, disjointed snoozers. Add "War Of The Worlds" to that list. What's so maddening is that sometimes the movie that might have been is glimpsed. The first tripod rising from its subterranean lair is a compelling sequence, and I thought the film was going to take off on a series of ever mounting action scenes. But the whole thing reminded me of a wet firecracker. You light the fuse, and feel the anticipation of the explosion. But it just sits there, inert. You think, "It's just a slight delay. It'll go off." After a while you realize you got ripped off. This firecracker is made from a soggy rag of a script wrapped around the stale gunpowder of a once potent talent too lazy to exploit the resources at his command.

I think a big part of the problem is that this movie is hobbled with a PG-13 rating. This is a war movie. Of course it's going to deal with gruesome death and horror. So why bother making this film if the graphic content is defanged out of a fear of offending old ladies in the audience? It's like turning Goya's "Disasters Of War" etchings into a coloring book suitable for the tender sensibilities of third graders.

title: Much Ado about Nothing
review:
Spielberg's War of the Worlds is pretty awful. I expected much more after all the hype, but what a disappointment. With all the resources Spielberg has he seems to have lost his way here, this movie is just gimmicks and spends too much time in wallowing in tricks and too little time on a proper story line.

There was at least a story in the H G Wells book. This version was just far fetched, so distant from anything remotely believable it became boring. The whole thing was badly written, at least try and make the scenes appear believable. The TV crew outside the house with the stupid reporter who looked more like she was doing a candid camera sketch than in the middle of an air disaster that was part of a martian invasion. Were you on the plane? she asks Cruise: No! Cruise replies, she retorts: Oh what a pity it would have made a great story. Who writes such rubbish, surely, these days audiences get hacked off with the way Hollywood dumb down everything.

Unfortunately, I started to get itchy feet before an hour had gone by. I tend to judge movies by the watch factor, how long before you check how long it is before the end. I never get restless or look at the time with truly good movies.

Regarding Dakota Fanning, she was good in a child star sort of a way and she may very be the next Drew Barrymore but who can tell with one performance in a no money spared Spielberg epic.

title: Classic Spielburg Popcorn Flick
review: This is the summer popcorn flick you've been waiting for! Overall, I'd have to say the original War of the Worlds is still one of my favorite alien movies but Spielburg proves he can do suspense, horror, and action again in this well made remake. The legendary director also makes sure he has plenty of homages to the original film but there are a few surprising twists as well. He also does something that few other directors do: he has the actors act like real people. Dakota Fanning screams in fear like a ten-year-old would, Tom Cruise is a bit of an asshole jaded father, and Tim Robbins plays a man whose gone over the edge because of the invasion. There are some tense moments and all the classic Spielburg camera shots are present which only make it better. The CGI is also well done on the aliens and I'd say it's worth the price of a movie ticket if you enjoy this type of flick.

title: No humans allowed at the finish line
review:
In 2005,no more "oh wow's" with regard to computer effects. Just assume that anything can be done and that anything can be shown. Do not get breathless over an effect, unless you are in the business of making them yourself.

So the tripods take over and, as ever, the invaders are stopped by our little earthchildren friends the microbes. Suppose the invaders had done a little research in the eons since they buried their assault weapons and come up with a vaccine. You wonder why they hadn't thought of that. But suppose they did. Then we would have been cooked, Tom Cruise, screaming vegetarian brat and all. No amount of Tom Cruisery could have saved the planet. That might not be a bad formula shift for a different aliens-take-over movie. I mean, let the aliens kill everything and everybody, watch the last human die, and then watch the aliens start to build their own colonies which could scuffle with one another or whatever. The end of such a movie could be all-alien, no humans allowed. Some brave director needs to think about this.

title: A Dark Vision of Invasion
review:
This is a pretty harsh look at what an alien invasion might be like. The brutality and horror of such an event is not sugar-coated here (except maybe for the ending, which I'll touch on later). It seems that Spielberg's Holocaust influence more than 9/11 was responsible for how terrible some of the images in this film are, but it made me appreciate the fact that Spielberg was willing to take what could have been another summer popcorn movie (like, yes, Independence Day) and instead made a strong statement about what genocide really means. There may even be a connection with current events in Africa.

Maybe it's because I happen to be the divorced father of a 10-year old blond daughter myself, but I found this film to be more disturbing than some of the commenters. In fact I find some of their comments to be more glib and callous than insightful. Nothing Dakota Fanning did rang false to me, and many of the viewers (I guess because of their lack of life experiences) missed the point of a lot of the things that both the daughter and the father did. I am not a fan of Tom Cruise (his interview with Matt Lauer was one of the biggest displays of arrogant ego that I have ever seen in real life), but nothing he did in this film rang false, either. Real life is messy, folks, and in this case the film made the necessary connection with that real life in order to ground the fantastic nature of the film with true human emotions.

Yes, the film has flaws. The "Machines buried under the Earth for one million years" plot device just doesn't work for me for multiple reasons (Why was H.G. Well's original concept of their simply coming down from space unacceptable for Spielberg?), and yes, the ending undercuts the tragic elements of the film -- although personally speaking, I only laughed because I recognized some familiar actors among the characters in the final scene.

Still, this film is a worthy achievement, and by no means a failure of either film-making or vision. Although I must confess, I'll always prefer Close Encounters of the Third Kind myself.

title: Great Directing...But Acting and Writing Stunk
review:
First off, the one thing about this film that got under my skin like a bizarre South American parasite was the fact that the whole movie barely showed any resemblance to the original H.G. Wells novel. Despite the great CG and fleeting moments of social consciousness, the film lacked the most basic ingredient to a great film: a decent script.

Jesus H. Christ! This script has to be the most mindless dribble ever excepted by a major modern studio. For example, never explaining the drive for Robbie being so eager to fight the martians; much less his miraculous survival after a whole hillside is lit up like the jungle in Apocalypse Now. The script also got so caught up in delivering something modern and fresh, that Wells' original story got lost in the unimpressive drama typical Hollywood b.s. (i.e. Tom Cruise's character bringing down the martian tripod with couple of hand grenades...please!) The only real character that is carried over from Wells' novel is Tim Robbin's character of Oglivy...poorly. The character bares almost no resemblance to the character described in Wells' novel. Plus, Oglivy being killed by Ray...that was definitely a wtf? moment.

Finally, the acting wasn't really that impressive for so many A-List Hollywood names being attached to it. Honestly, Tom Cruises character of Ray could have been played by any leading male actor in Hollywood. His character seemed to serve only one purpose: to keep his family together. He delivered no prolific lines or did anything that contributed to the conclusion of the film. I looked at this in contrast to Gene Barry's character in the original WOTW film and how he was compelled to find a way to fight them--despite the odds.

I believe Steven Spielberg is genius because he manages to hold the film up from his end of things. This film is a great film if you wish to relax see a mindless alien invasion film just south of 'Independence Day' and just north of 'Invaders from Mars.' Bottom Line: If you wish to see a sci-fi/horror/fantasy film this summer, save your money to go see 'Batman Begins' or 'Land of the Dead.'

title: Spielberg makes a good movie, but not great one. No excuses for him.
review:
War of the Worlds contains enough suspense and good acting that this movie should be hailed as a "good" movie. The "tri-pods" are effective and scary, and the haunting attack scenes are well done. But what went wrong in this film ? I have a list:

1. The ending. Bravo for staying true to the original film / H.G. Wells, but it seemed rushed. Take your time, this is a perfect time for Spielberg to follow Wells version, and show the aliens attempt to communicate. Show their downfall in force. Instead we just get a glimpse with some commentary by Morgan Freeman. And also the "happy" reunion with the family. I could of forgiven this ending , had he actually took his time with the ending. He didn't.

2. Yes, this movie does show the "panicked" view of the attack. Nobody knows anything, nothing is really explained. But the more you think about the aliens and what they did, the harder it is too swallow. They travel thru lighting rods to their underground ships.....hmmmmm. Where did this lightning travel from ? How come nobody happened to stumble upon these ships ? Had this movie been based in the 1800's, I would believe, but today ..........naaahhh. We have satellites and machines too now.

2b: The overall invasion. In the original, they travel from space, comets , and wreak havoc. We assume this is their first visit. In this one, we have to assume they have been underground for thousands if not millions of years. Don't you think they would of attacked before man advanced so much ? We can fight back now. Also, didn't they test the air ? They have this complex eco-system with red vines. Talk about bad research on their part. Killed by germs.

A better ending would of been : The aliens die of germs, but germs released by us. We actually did find the ships and were preparing for this day. Big government conspiracy cover up. It would stay true to the original, with a major dose of reality and "Area 51" feel to it. The government though, of course, was not aware of the alien's true power.

Overall, it's worth seeing and Spielberg still knows how to make a great movie. It's scary, creepy, suspenseful and memorable. But Spielberg did seem to get lazy on us. What could of been a classic, was only above average. Bravo to some directors, but for Spielberg. No excuses for him. We expect more.

title: Spielberg Could've Done Better!
review:
War of the Worlds is a good blockbuster movie, but I was disappointed because it could've been a lot better.

The story had its flaws. The ending in particular, was abrupt and lame. It made sense, but I preferred a darker ending for our weak human race. Just think about it for a while - these aliens, far more technologically advanced and intelligent than we are, are so close to taking over Earth when they get defeated - by bacteria and microscopic organisms. You'd think the aliens would have thought about that when they were planning millions of years for their little takeover. In the end the real heroes of the movie were microscopic organisms - please... Furthermore, the story didn't focus a lot on Ferrier's family as much as I would've liked. Most of the time it focused on the action and invasion rather than the family issues. The ending resolved all these family issues, particularly the one between Ferrier and his son, but I had to ask why? What made Ferrier and his son love each other again? Something was lacking.

The acting and characters were at least better than the story. Tom Cruise delivers an excellent performance as Ray Ferrier, clearly defining a struggling father trying to bring his family together in the midst of a great disaster. Dakota Fanning is enchanting; War of the Worlds was a way for her to act out fear pretty damn well. Justin Chatwin as Robbie Ferrier was good, but his character was annoying and stupid. What was up with his hero complex? Why risk your life just for looking at the aliens? His teenage rebellion was ultimately agitating too... GROW UP, kid, it's an alien invasion! War of the Worlds does have its strengths. Action and special effects are the highlight here, and they do satisfy. I was blown away by the imagery. Steven Spielberg knows how to paint the picture of destruction, doom, and mayhem, and it helps that you have a $125 million budget for some beautiful special effects. There isn't a dull moment, trust me.

Conclusion - War of the Worlds is cool, but it doesn't reach the depth it could've reached. Problems with characters and the story hinder it a bit, but it could've been a masterpiece if those two elements were up to the challenge. Watch it for the action and visuals, but if you're expecting something more, then you'll be disappointed. At most this is a beautiful popcorn flick.

title: Aw.. Too much visual effects and less a story.
review:
I didn't have high expectations of this movie, which didn't make me disappointed when I finally watched this movie. I expected it, anyways, even though Spielberg is a good director and has done many well-done movies in his past - E.T., Close Encounters, Saving Private Ryan, Schindler's List and Jurassic Park just to naming a few. This is just not a movie that even Peter Jackson would be able to make good. The problem is that War of the worlds was written in the end of the 19th century and when you will make a movie about it and change the time to the 21th century, then the story gets too simple and the visual effects take over too much. The beginning had deep, the rest is flat. I prefer the original War of the worlds, when everything had deep but the end was flat. Maybe there is a curse about War of the worlds being filmed.

The story seems promising in the beginning, but gets too fast with the machines from outer space - they start to attack already after about ten minutes and don't finish until five minutes before the ending scene, which made it a pity to see the movie. The story is too simple - it is just about Tom Cruise and his two children escaping from or fighting the machines. But there are some deep scenes during the entire movie - the scenes between Tom Cruise's role as the father and his relation to his son, Robbie. And how he takes care of Rachel (Fanning). Those scenes are very deep, but it doesn't make the movie any better. Despite that fact, the visual effects are very spectacular but the sad truth is that visual effects can't make a movie good if there is no great story. And the ending is also too predictable, it becomes too Hollywoodish, excuse my saying this. Too much clichés.

But anyway, like I said before, nobody could have made it any better than what Spielberg did (Jackson would probably have done it at least as good as him, but who knows? You can always be surprised) in this century. If you really want to see a good version of any of H G Wells's novels, see the original Time Machine from the '60s.

title: I enjoyed it...right up until the last ten minutes.
review:
(Note: Major spoilers occur only in the clearly marked paragraph.) Spielberg. Cruise. Aliens. How can you go wrong? Well...

With "War of the Worlds", director Steven Spielberg has crafted a paradox: a movie with the subject of alien invasion that is more about familial relations. Similarly, the film treats the audience in an oxymoronic fashion: entertaining throughout yet leaving them unsatisfied as it follows the adventures of Ray Ferrier (Tom Cruise, in a somewhat disorienting out-of-type role), who is a blue-collar New York City divorcée, and his semi-estranged children as they endure extra-terrestrials, each other, and everyone else.

After the brief requisite introduction of characters, the wonderfully intimate portrayal of the dysfunctional father-child relationship (one of Spielberg's most frequent themes) embarks on a wildly successful roller coaster, both physically and emotionally. This dominant portion of the movie is very good, as Cruise and family encounter a raging mix of frightening aliens and equally scary people, some purposeful (the mobs) and some not (a creepy Tim Robbins), and explore their relationships in the process.

I don't like to reveal much about a movie when I review it, but I feel the need...

MAJOR SPOILERS IN THE NEXT PARAGRAPH!!! (clearing throat for rant) My biggest issue with "War of the Worlds" is that too much didn't make sense, and I don't mean that in a scientific way. All of the momentum crashed and burned in the last moments, raising a cacophony of questions and providing few answers. You're telling me that these engineering geniuses bit it because they didn't get their shots? That's it?! I don't care if that's how the book ends; it's completely unsatisfying considering how badly they dominated us. Even the typical exploit-their-weakness ending ("Signs", every other alien movie) would have been sufficient. Beyond that, what is the purpose of the red vines/roots? Why were the machines affected by the atmosphere? Where is the backup? Why didn't the aliens take over the planet back when they buried their vehicles? And what are the freaking odds that the boy survived, let alone made it back to his grandparents' miraculously picturesque house while they were (from appearances) having tea?! I know that holes can be poked in most any sci-fi movie, but 1) a movie with this pedigree is going to be held to a higher standard than a fun romp like "Independence Day"; and 2) all of these irksome questions immediately came to mind because they were not evidently answered, except for the purpose of cinematic convenience, which has its place, but not to this degree.

END SPOILERS!!! (calming deep breaths) Featuring a less sweeping, more jittery score from stalwart John Williams, "War of the Worlds" still manages to intensely entrance for ninety-plus minutes while displaying often violent interactions of humans and aliens, and it is a testament to Spielberg's ability that the movie overcomes the aforementioned obstacles for so long. Whether or not you like his work, you have to admit that there are few better storytellers, and his tools are on full display here. Rarely was I bored while watching, with a slightly muted color palette and plenty of eye-twinkling shots courtesy of Spielberg and his regular cinematographer Janusz Kaminski, like the handful of shots through holes in glass, tracking cameras along cracking pavement, and more. Making a big-idea movie is difficult enough without focusing on the small moments of father and daughter, but Spielberg balances the extremes well, and putting the viewer in the shoes of an everyman is ideally effective in retelling this classic tale. That talent merges well with the again excellent work from the effects team at Industrial Light & Magic, which creates alien beings congruent to and unique from (tripods...nice) previous cinematic incarnations, with a sci-fi realism that impresses throughout.

For most of its running length, "War of the Worlds" is very good, still not the great science-fiction that "Minority Report" was, but very good. But even during that time, an inquisitive undercurrent flows, asking Where is this going?. Unfortunately that question is never satisfactorily answered, resulting in a bifurcated movie experience.

Bottom Line: Enjoyable but ultimately disappointing. 6 of 10.

title: Fine movie except for the people in it. Great FX!
review:
I was favorably impressed by the first 80 minutes of WotW, which in part is why I was so bitterly annoyed at the remaining 40 minutes.

To start off, Tom Cruise did a decent job in the lead as Ray Ferrier, he cried believably, flashed the pearly whites when needed, but otherwise seemed overwhelmed when called on to be manly. For the Ray character is a feckless wimp. His kids have contempt for him, his ex-wife patronizes him, even her new husband pities Cruise. He's irresponsible, a sloven, a cipher that I found it impossible to like or even care about.

Unfortunately, Tom Cruise is the best character in this movie.

His son Robbie (Justin Chatwin) is the usual Hollywood version of an angst ridden, rebellious teen who hates his dad. In this movie, he comes across as spoiled, rude, and downright stupid.

**SPOILER ALERT FOLLOWS**

For some reason, after the aliens attack, instead of helping Ray take care of Robbie's sister, Robbie starts behaving erratically, trying several times to join with soldiers deploying to fight the aliens. While he doesn't succeed, he nearly manages to get his sister killed. At one point when the Ferriers are escaping in a ferry, he tries to help several latecomers aboard, which was an attempt to make his character more sympathetic. Trouble is, 10 minutes later when they're fleeing for their lives, he decides to stay and watch the army fight the aliens. **Even though he's seen the alien's superior weapons and should have realized that no army could beat them!"" So essentially he abandons his little sister so he can watch the show!

You're supposed to believe that he gets killed in the ensuing all-consuming fireball, but at this point it was obvious that Spielberg wasn't playing fair and that Robbie would reappear just before the final credits.

Robbie's sister Rachel (Dakota Fanning) is the kind of precocious child that only exists in movies. She is calm, centered, much wiser than her old dad and perfectly willing to tell him how to live his life.

She also has a scream that'll shatter the fillings in your teeth. Imagine Fay Wray in King Kong, then hit yourself with a hammer--that's what she's like. She screams over and over and over and over again...until all you want is for an alien to put her out of our misery.

Finally there's that old coot Ogilvy (Tim Robbins) who hides the Ferriers in his basement. Will someone please tell me what the point was in his being in this movie??? Ogilvy's nuts, driven insane by the things he's seen (I guess) and all he wants is to attack the aliens for revenge. So you get one tiresome scene after another where the aliens are searching the basement after hearing noises and Ray has to fight or otherwise convince Ogilvy so he won't give them away. Ogilvy's end is supposed to be tragic, but I found it to be a relief.

That's it for the people. Now let's talk about the good stuff in this movie: the special FX.

Here are the gems: - The scenes in the city during the aliens first attack are amazing and almost terrifying. When they use the heatray, it instantly destroys whatever it contacts, which makes for great visuals when they turn the beams on an elevated highway.

  • There's a moment when the Ferriers, along with other refugees on a road, are stopped by a train crossing gate, moments later the train, engulfed in flames, flashes by. Very cool!


  • The crashed passenger jet is a surreal moment.


I thought the bit that occurred after the ferry overturned, when it's propeller almost killed the the Ferriers as they struggled to the water's surface, seemed too much like a ripoff from the plane crash in Castaway.

I was also mystified as to why so much of what happens in the movie is unseen. A big budget movie like this should have had one jaw-dropping scene after another, but this one was unsatisfying. For instance, the electrical lightning strikes are only shown for an instant-- instead you see people's reactions to them, hardly dramatic when you can't see what they're seeing. And the battles between the US army and the aliens are brief and not as exciting as it should have been. Did the producers run out of money for FX?

Finally, it made sense when Wells wrote WotW that aliens might not know about our germs. But after the rewrite, when they've been watching use for a million years, how could they not know??? And why is it that aliens who've developed sophisticated weapons and power systems never thought of using infrared devices to scan for body heat?? The clunky camera they used was laughable (although it might have been in homage to the original WotW).

Prepare yourself for disappointment.

title: too many holes
review: The only good thing about the movie was the special effects. There were too many holes in the story and they completely ruined my enjoyment of this film. For one thing I don't know anybody in NY who would just keep standing there and watching as the ground starts shaking and cracking, and why were all those people including the mom and baby just watching that whole lightening scene. My kids and I are inside at the first sign of thunder or lightening, also if all the cars in New York city stopped at once there is no way anyone would be able to drive around like he did. Another point when they got to the kids' house in Jersey he didn't even look to see if there was any food there. Also the guy he followed into the basement looked like a serial killer or psycho. So I already knew something was up .

title: Not Impressed!!
review:
After all the hype - and because Spielberg is a favorite director of mine - I was expecting to be blown away by this movie. I was sorely disappointed! The story line was not solid. There were loose ends when it was over that left you saying, "Wait a minute! How did they...? How did he...?" There were unbelievable survival moments - that left you saying, "Oh give me a break!" The ending came too soon without enough wrap-up. It was just suddenly over.

Tom Cruise's acting was typical of every other role he's played - smart Aleck rebel. Dakota Fanning screamed just a bit too much in the one - and I really like her. I think Justin Chatwin (who played Tom's son, Robbie) did a pretty good job. He should be getting a lot of work in the future.

I went with five other people - and we couldn't even sit together because the theater was full. Separately, we all had the same evaluation - two thumbs down!! Overall, I would say this is NOT going to be the summer blockbuster of 2005. (That honor will go to Batman Begins.)

title: All the special effects in the world couldn't save this movie.
review:
Every single movie that I have seen this summer is a better movie than War of the Worlds, and none of them cost nearly as much to make.

Beneath a veil of absolutely stunning (and insanely gory) special effects, lies a plot that is so implausible that I left the theater laughing at first, then cursing Spielburg later. I want my $7.50 back.

I will not tell any secrets or spoilers, but I will say that an entirely superior alien race made a plan a VERY long time ago to wipe out the human race. In all that time, they couldn't find a better and more cost-effective method? Those really cool toys (that seem like Star Wars rip-offs) seem to be able to destroy anything, so why did they wait to attack for so long? If you're willing to accept all of this, one might wonder what the alien motive is? What are they getting for their effort? I saw the movie and still don't understand.

What I do know is that the ending, without giving anything away, is going to leave every self-respecting, even mildly intelligent person asking, "Does Spielburg really expect us to buy into this?"

title: uhmm.... i hated the ending **spoilers i guess**
review: i watched the movie being a fan of the old time radio broadcast, and the book being read as a child. I came in suppressing my excitement and was happy that the motion of the film was progressively futile. The probably i had was the ending. It was toooooo happy. Not the way that the world survived, but the unexplained reappearance of his son. It was ridiculous. The father was no longer an outsider. I like that he was in shock. But when a child runs face first into a maelstorm. Where the military failed and not only got there first, but didn't change his clothes, which would be presumably blood drenched and torn at least from all the heat. It's a damn happy ending film. And since when can old people run fast enough to escape a death ray?

title: one sentence with spoiler
review:
I enjoyed the movie greatly, and i will sum it up like this: alien farmers land on earth and tom cruise gets his children back to his ex- wife a day early while the major theme of War of the Worlds unfolds around him. The special effects were not over done and not the primary focus of the film. the story does leave some perplexing questions, such as when and why the aliens buried their war/farming equipment on earth

I wish other directors would consider doing other h. g. wells stories. he has some interesting ideas. when you put wells in the context of the period he was writing he is as forward thinking as a man can be, not just sci-fi, but some of his social /political stories as well.

title: Big-screen movie with a small-screen look
review: This would have been an above-average effort if it had been a made-for-TV movie, but it was not impressive as a big-screen spectacle. Everything in it looked small, as if it had been made with a limited budget on a tight schedule. The tripods looked neat enough, but they were obviously state-of-the-art CGI in most scenes. In several big, important scenes the film-makers must have been influenced by Greek tragedy, because actions that would be spectacular (and the kinds of things that audiences pay to see) are left to occur off-stage. Crowd scenes, city scenes and battle scenes were all creditably done, but there just wasn't anything that said "epic" about them. Don't dismiss this film out of hand, however. There are scenes that I'll remember forever for their eerie beauty, and one that was so jarringly out-of-character that I can't stop thinking about it, but to describe them would necessitate using the "spoiler" tag. See the movie, just don't expect to be blown away (or see things blown away, for that matter!).

title: ...but I so wanted to like it.
review:
The CGI was incredible and Dakota Fanning was amazing but they couldn't cover up the holes that simple reason left in this story.

I understand that this is a sci-fi adventure and thus it requires a bit more "suspension of disbelief" than the normal story but I found that I just couldn't do it. The very first thing that pulled me out of the movie was use of the disembodied narrator used to set the scene for us.

At first it was because I was excited, I hadn't realized Morgan Freeman was in the cast. My excitement quickly turned sour as it became that he wasn't in the film, he was just there to let us know we were watching a film where the earth was unaware an attack was coming by an unforeseen alien menace because, apparently, we were not able to grasp it on our own...from the title... and the hundreds of times we had been exposed to the ads. Sure I realize I may grasp mundane, painfully obvious details better than most but I didn't think that this was something that needed covering. When the disembodied narrator (God..? no, wait I'm thinking of Bruce Almighty) spoke up at the end of the movie I understood why he was there: someone needed to be able to combine a three minute scene that would have explained what happened into a few lines.

Watching War of the Worlds was like watching a Saturday Night Live skit that started strong but leaves us disappointed because we realize they couldn't figure out an ending (you likah dah juice? dah juice eeze goodah). Of course I don't spend five dollars on SNL (matinee) and they don't have a $130 million dollar budget. The idea that keeps coming back to me, and that bothers the most, is that some people may miss out on seeing better movies because they decided to see this one instead. Please, save your money and your time. If you need to see it wait for the DVD. NOTHING will be lost by seeing it on the small screen.

title: um...well
review:
I had such high expectations for this film, that I guess I should of expected to be disappointed. First off, Tom Cruise and his family really have no back story, and the audience doesn't understand why those spoiled brats who live in a gigantic mansion are so angry all the time. Oh cry me a river that they have to stay with daddy and share the same bedroom...My God! How tragic! I'm not a violent person, but there were times I just wanted to give Dakota Fanning and Justin Chatwin a good back hand. Sure he might not be the greatest dad in the world, but at least he's trying and doesn't need two snot-nosed children second guessing him at every turn. Can someone explain to me how Justin, survived the gigantic explosion considering how many alien tripods were on the other side...and beat them to Boston? Spare me, it is just industry standard...kids and pets cannot be killed in movies. Why not? A little more realism would be nice. ...Is it just me, or is it not possible to care about these Hollywood movie character's anymore? I mean I didn't give two hoots if Justin Chatwin died or not...Or if Tom Cruise was going to make it...

Lastly, about the ending, I don't think that it was a shortcoming that the aliens all-of-a-sudden die, I believe HG Wells couldn't figure out a way to kill them off and came up with the ham-handed bacteria approach. I mean these aliens are in their tripods...who knows what type of air they breathe, their capsules/tripods would most likely be air tight. I've read the book, watched the original and now the remake, and the endings always suffer.

title: Not what i was expecting
review:
The Opening scene to this movie is, for lack of a better word, incredible. It starts out with great potential, the characters are set up well (even though, the initial "uncomfortable" meeting of the divorced family was a little cliché) the story introduced evenly and smoothly, and the first attack scene is beautifully filmed, the first running sequence is perfect (as long as you bite your lip at the digital camera flop). Then the film starts to slide a little bit. The acting by Cruise and Fanning is spot on, and Robbins does an excellent character role, but the way the action is presented bugged me a little.

It appeared that Spielberg was trying to keep the audience on the wars effects on the family and not on the world. Its kind of a "third person limited" perspective, and that would have been fine with me in a situation where the event was well known (say like a WW2 setting) but this story is of course unknown to the audience, so the fact that we never get to see the whole picture, the devastation in its full glory, that we only see the edge of the large battles and hear glimpses of the attacks on other country's gnawed at me the whole time. I was hoping that they would reveal all that at the very end, that we would be stunned to see that the huge effect on the family was minuscule compared to the world devastation, but because that never happened I feel like I can't really appreciate what the family went through.

The Cinematography and the score was beautiful, and the effects were completely stunning but the story left so many loop holes in my head that i couldn't come out feeling entirely satisfying.

Although i must say that any movie narrated by Morgan Freeman has got a place i my book

7 1/2 out of 10

title: Disappointing
review: It is very rare for the modern cinema goer to be truly impressed by the image in front of them when going to the cinema but I was by War of The Worlds. The effects where incredible and imaginative creating the type of awe-inspiring feeling that has been missing in recent cinema. However, this doesn't extend to a fairly mediocre script and performances. Tom Cruise fills the 'all-American' dad role well enough without ever having us care about his character and the development of the relationship with his children is clumsy and negligible. It must also be noted that the children are perhaps the two most irritating characters in any film this year and it doesn't help the flow of the story when you are actually hoping they get killed.The end of the film is too abrupt and feels rushed (though in fairness this is due to the way the book ends - at least Spielberg stayed faithful to this) but doesn't explain it clearly enough to people who haven't read the original book.In summary this is worth seeing for the effects but doesn't have the substance to extend it pass a 'popcorn movie' and into the realms of all time classics where some of Spielberg's other Sci-Fi epics (Close Encounters/E.T.) reside . Read the book for a fully appreciation of the story.

title: why?
review: I love Spielberg. I think he is the most INVENTIVE filmmaker of all time. My question after seeing this film is WHY???? Why did he not reinvent the genre yet again? Why did he not surpirse me? Why did he not scare the bejesus out of me? WHY????!!?!?!? Spielberg failed to obey the most important rule of the disaster flick-the rule of killing off someone we care about in every act. Why did he fail to do this? No killing = no fear = no emotional weight = not a really scary movie. Spielberg---I love you...but you really really really failed to come through with this one. Minority Report this ain't (that was the most suspenseful Spielberg film in the last 10 years). I really hate siding with Ebert on this one but I can't help it. Watch at your wallet's risk.

title: Great film
review: I gladly enjoyed it while watching it with my wife and my son, it was also the best day for me!...

title: Since it was a Spielberg movie i had expected much more
review:
War of the Worlds is a Sci-Fi action movie directed by Steven Spielberg and stars Tom Cruise, Dakota Fanning, Justin Chatwin, Miranda Otto and Tim Robbins.

When you see the name of Tom Cruise in the lead and Steven Spielberg as the director you raise the bar of your expectations and to be honest i am highly disappointed because i might be expecting a lot after seeing these two big names.

The start of the movie is good and acting is superb and a special mention for Dakota Fanning who did a rather tough job commendably well. Tom Cruise was as always impressive. Tim Robbins is wasted in the movie.

The Screenplay is ok but with few stupid scenes i really doubt the wisdom of the screenplay writer as i failed to understand the reason behind some of the scenes. For instance In one of the scenes Robbie played by Justin Chatwin just starts running in the direction of Aliens in order to fight with them and that too empty handed means i can't understand the reason behind the bravado as the army were not able to fight with the Aliens with ammunitions and he wanted to fight with them empty handed. In another scene when the alien tripod sees the Ferrier father and daughter sleeping Rachel started shouting and flees but why? If you think form the perspective of a kid they will never leave their parent in such scenarios and will try to be as close as possible. The ending of the movie is also abrupt and little disappointing.

Overall the movie is a decent entertainer but could've been better. The movie can be watched once and should be watched for some strong acting and great visuals.

title: Weak movie decent effects
review: Tom Cruise rarely does a bad movie but this a movie he should not be proud of m, although not his fault really. The blame is with Spielberg. It is very loosely based on the book with horrible acting, decent CGI and very annoying kids. Extremely weak plot and very forgettable.

title: Classic tale retold just fine
review: TinyTom, Dakota Fanning and all the cast do a grand job. Pacey direction of a classic tale. Plenty of action, tension, edge of the seat moments. What's not to like?. One of my favourite interpretations of this story. Just watched again in 2020, 15 years after it first hit the cinemas (gulp!) .... Its still a really great movie

title: The best film version of War of the Worlds
review: The 2005 version of War of the Worlds is the best on screen adaptation of the H. G. Wells novel (I haven't seen the Fox/Canal TV version.) This version of a ground view of an alien invasion as seen through the eyes of a struggling man. Tom Cruise goes against type by playing an ordinary Working Joe and a bad father as he gets caught up with the extraordinary events. Steven Spielberg knows how to make a popcorn film and his version of story does have excellent CGI effects and destruction. The film came across as a Spielbergian attempt of a horror film because there was panic and dread when the Tripods approach, social order breaks down, and characters have to hide from the aliens. It makes War of the Worlds more terrifying.

review:
This movie is definitely worth a watch. Just keep in mind that this movie is the reason that I don't want kids. I am too afraid to have a daughter like the girl in this. review: This is a great movie based on the famed HG Wells novel of the same name. A list actor teams up with A list director to make a good entertaining film that needs to be appreciated. The effects of the alien tripods are amazing especially the sound design- they evoke fear. The plotting and pacing is efficient which should be expected from Spielberg and the acting is good. You know how the film ends and yet this film keeps you engrossed. If you haven't read the famous novel I suggest you read it before seeing this film.

title: technical amazing, disturbing if it's intent is to be a mirror of the society, otherwise for brainwashing
review:
The film starts with the image of a disintegrated American family and ends with a reunified one. To get this result, 2 hours of non stop fighting against aliens were needed.

The aliens are using huge robots which walk pretty clumsy the earth, XIX - Jules Verne style, with snake like tubes which get people like a monster. The people attack the car. Tom Cruise gets out, and only when he sees that someone would pick the car not leaving out his daughter, he takes out his gun. This is a second powerful symbol. And now, only in an extreme situation, he threats the others to keep the distance. These are all interactions! conclusions: the isolation of people, the only support is from the army and a little from the Church. This movie has so many clichees, and use so much makeup, that it might be a parody, a trick to deceive the censorship. If this is the case, bravo, if not ... it's very said for its public.

title: Good could have been better
review: Scariest of all the alien invasion movies. Special effects brilliant from the master Spielberg. The only irritating part of the movie was the portrayal of the 2 kids; Especially Robbie who looked retarded and behaved erratically all throughout the movie. The girl kept screaming at the drop of the hat so much that it starts to bore a hole in your head. Tom Cruise was OK in his typical distracted manner. The backdrop to the invasion was to show the dysfunctional family of the protagonist and in that attempt the director went a little overboard. That's why I drop the rating from 7 to 5. The ending was a bit anti-climatic for the earlier buildup but nevertheless thanks for letting me put in my 2 cents.

title: Nothing special besides the initial Alien attack
review:
The initial invasion is brilliantly depicted. The sound design is just awesome. I bet those scenes can be reused to make a really good movie.

The rest is just one of a million "american father tries to save his family in peril" stories. One of the war-based ones. Not among the best of those although Tom Cruise makes a more likable and less stereotypical father than most. Usually it's an old fashioned patriarch. Tom Cruise is more of an supposedly irresponsible young guy with a big heart. Apart from that: lots of special effects, a variety of Sci-Fi threats, a not too complicated story in many small adventures.

Well that's it I guess.

Oh wait: one thing about the original might be worth mentioning. The intro contains a passage that somehow doesn't fit this film at all as I see it. The neat assortment of good and evil this film brings about somehow isn't to be found in this one...

Here it is: "And before we judge of them too harshly we must remember what ruthless and utter destruction our own species has wrought, not only upon animals, such as the vanished bison and the dodo, but upon its inferior races. The Tasmanians, in spite of their human likeness, were entirely swept out of existence in a war of extermination waged by European immigrants, in the space of fifty years. Are we such apostles of mercy as to complain if the Martians warred in the same spirit?" -from "War of the Worlds" by H.G. Wells

title: Some goods, some bads
review:
You know, when i hear covers of my favourite songs, i expect them to be as accurate as it can be. You can play them in a different style, different keys, take some liberties, change the solos, but don't change the lyrics or the melodies because that's the core of the songs. Same thing with movie remakes.

I liked the crescendo of the beginning but it didn't took long before i started to frown.

Yes of course all visual aspects are very neat, the cinematography is interesting and the sound design is very cool but the whole wrecked family thing is boring as hell and does not help the story, it seems like they tried to put an unnecessary depth to this and the movie suffers in my opinion.

The acting is down to earth enough, i don't like Tom Cruise but i can recognize he's a good actor. Tim Robbins is amazing as always, i didn't expected him to be in this movie at all, great surprise. There's some epic scenes but sometime too much action for nothing and yes, that little girl with the strident voice screaming all the time was really annoying.

A lot of clichés in this movie like the single dad with a garage in his messy kitchen having trouble managing his anger and arguing all the time with his rebel and introverted son; it gets old very quickly. At some point Ray Ferrier (Tom Cruise) tells his daughter to «stay right here i'll be right back» (wow, really? How lame!) then another family took the girl with them by force because they didn't believe the girl's story, i saw that coming from miles away, so unoriginal.

There's a lot of incongruities too, like when Ray is looking in the fridge: no light, the next shot: he turn on the light switch to check if there's electricity. The crowd just staying there, staring at the first tripod emerging from the street instead of running like deers, etc...

They could have removed only 4 or 5 key scenes and nobody would have notice that this was "war of the world". The way they ended the film was so predictable it's embarrassing.

In one word: watchable.

title: Great sound, scare-inducing ridiculousness
review:
Steven Spielberg's 2005 "War of the Worlds," is an audio tsunami featuring the greatest subwoofer mix ever to make its way on to a DVD. You'd better hope that fans don't decide to all play the film at the same time and turn the sound up because every embedded fault line in America would shift.

The sound design is outstanding. It is meticulously detailed, elaborately separated and directionalized. It is jacked up on its own before your personal speaker system even comes close to it. There is both a 5.1-channel Dolby Digital track and a sharper, more shearing DTS track. When they let loose, everything shakes. Yet there is color to the bass line as well, with different types of low-level vibrations for different situations and different levels of impact. It is so well put together that even the silences are exciting.

And there are images and a story to go with the sound. Spielberg's ending -- not H.G. Wells' -- is obnoxious as all get out, but there is a point at about the 99-minute mark where Tom Cruise's character gets sucked into an alien ship. If you just imagine that everything which happens after that point is an "Occurrence at Owl Creek Bridge"-type dream, then the ridiculousness of it all doesn't bother you nearly as much.

The whole movie has less scientific logic than a Republic serial, but it does, more importantly, capture the massive, unnerving and downright fear-inducing atmosphere of a nightmare exquisitely well. I must admit that, like jestdecerts, I too was reminded of riding Chicago's Clark Street bus.

The one other component that allows the 117-minute feature to hold your attention and keep stringing you along is the young Dakota Fanning, who plays Cruise's daughter. Acting in earnest, her performance constantly recenters your attention to the emotional core of the story and keeps you interested in the fates of the characters. It is only because she cares about Cruise that you do.

title: War of the worlds (2005) VS. War of the Worlds (1953)
