Special effects were absolutely mind-blowing. The photography was just perfect. Some shots were so impressive, that you have to admit, that there is but one man today who can do such perfect crafting. BUT WHAT A WASTE OF TALENT...!!!

The Story is just awful, because he had to do it AGAIN. The small family survives, no matter how logical that is considering that all around everyone is dying. And not only this but the dis-likable becomes loved, the broken becomes steady, the unwanted becomes welcome everything about our hero's family has been repaired while the whole world is distorted. This moral impetus -or the "our-love-is-stronger-than-death-family-ideology" is absolutely out of place. It ruins the whole atmosphere. There had been so much room for real character development with fear, disbelief, guilt but Spielberg decided to cover it with thick layers of warm glibbery corniness - and thats so foreseeable so predictable that you exactly know what will happen next. All tension is ruined and every hope that Spielberg would change his pattern of creating plots at least in this movie fades with every minute and so did my joy that converted more and more to boredom with every minute.

However, there are some positive conclusions:

1. You can see the movie, if you want to see a visually good crafted piece of art and really have nothing else to do.

2. Its not only effects. It still is plot, acting, actors and characters by at least 60% to make a good movie - this one fails in this section.

3. Even though Tim Burton sometimes just does not get to the point, his alien invader's movie MARS ATTACKS is the best compared to ID4 and WotW. All movies share the same genes. But MA does tell the most realistic and entertaining story - not regarding the aliens design but human fate and character - and still contains enough irony to never become boring or solemn. So there is a good movie to cover this theme. See it.

title: You shouldn't take film to seriously
review:
Some little spoilers (trailer-content) First of all lets put that this film has an high potential. I recently saw this movie in Utrecht (NL) not knowing what to expect. Actually I did expect something: I expected the worst, a very disappointing and overdone experience. But in face it was very much worth watching. Of course there are some lacks... you shouldn't expect the story to be very deep-going, and people shouldn't be to petty about things that cannot actually happen since the whole genre is science-fiction. I think the main goal of this film is to make a convincing terror for the audience to experience. It's all about the experience. And when talking about the experience I think the filmmakers did a really good job. When I watched the movie I by and large felt very threatened because they underlined the fear of people experiencing such an terrifying event. They made this to be very convincing.

In one article I read about all the equipment (cars, camera's, watches, etc.) disfunctioning together with the appearance of lightning. Why would it be impossible to use a digital camera after a time of error, while standing next to one of the tripods? The source that withholds the equipment from working could be dissolved in the meanwhile? All I think is that people shouldn't be to petty for all these things which make the experience of film-watching a disappointing experience.

Filmmakers (more then sometimes) add drama to a movie by doing things that actually can not be. Another example: when the little girl looks into the beautiful river, coincidental dead bodies are floating by. Coincidental? This has also been done to add drama. Why argue about it or just take it for real and experience it. Sometimes people should not try to ask to much of a movie to enjoy it.

title: One word...WOW!!!!!!!!!
review: I just walked out of a packed screening and all I can say is WOW!! Spielberg has created a movie that literally had me on the edge of my seat the entire time! It instills an accompanying sense of awestruck wonder, and delivers long stretches of heightened, delirious excitement that remind you why people started going to the movies in the first place. It truly holds the audience in a grip of fear and doesn't let go! I feel like I really experienced and know what it must feel to go through an actual alien invasion! Spielberg was sooo good at making it feel real, authentic and identifiable to modern audiences. Its as if you strap yourself into a theme-park ride and don't get off until after 120 minutes of thrills and suspense. Not to mention the CGI is breathtaking! I wish you internet fanboys would actually go see a REAL movie directed by a REAL director instead of that self-conscious, pretentious garbage called SIN CITY and KILL BILL. Which wasn't made for a real audience, but for fanboy nerds who sit around and analyze Tarentio's references to bizarre Kung-Fu cinema. Ugghh! Thank god the greater portion of the American mainstream audiences still like their movies only the way Spielberg can make them!

title: Best Movie Of the Year!
review:
Do go see this movie!!!! It is a great movie. Again, I read mixed reviews when I looked up the movie on this web site. But I decided to go see for myself. I loved everything about this movie. Steven Spielberg knows how to make movies...he is a genius. He knows how to connect emotionally to his audience. His magic weaves it's spell and if you allow yourself to pay attention to this movie, you feel as if you are right there. I was completely riveted the entire time. The story (of course) was excellent, Tom Cruise was at his BEST and so were the other actors...especially the talented Dakota Fanning.

A movie like "War Of The Worlds" is WHY I go to the movies. I go because I am hoping it will be as great as it sounds. Well, this movie was even better!! A+ to the movie, to Spielberg, to Fanning, and especially to Cruise who makes it all believable. Thank you for finally offering such a wonderful, suspenseful movie to us!! Please continue to make more!! I am sick of most of the trash out there, but it makes this stand out even more as a true gem.

COME ON PEOPLE...I really do not understand how anyone can put down such a great movie...tell me, is there really a better movie out there???,

title: Great movie
review: This movie was excellent. I had my doubts but there was not one dull moment. The cast was excellent and Steven Spielberg did an outstanding job in direction. Whatever personal opinions I have about Tom Cruise's remarks about the mental health issues cannot overshadow the fact that he is a great actor. I would highly recommend this movie to anyone who enjoys action, sci-fi genre movies. Dakota did an outstanding job as Tom's daughter. She is mature beyond her years. I look forward to any movie that Steven Spielberg directs. I hope Tom Cruise and Steven Spielberg will team up again, they make a great team. This is one movie that I will be adding to my DVD collection.

title: Exactly what I expected from Speilbore
review:
On my deathbed, I will have many regrets. One prominent in my mind is the $15 Speiberg still owes me that I spent to see A.I. Now, adding to the tab is "War of the Worlds", a perfectly good book and seminal 50's classic film blasted to smithereens by Spielberg's Death Ray of Boredom. Let's admit that, with a decent movies such as "Schindler's List" and "Amistad", it's hard to go wrong, unless a little song-and-dance or comedy were included as people were killed. Even Spielberg isn't that stupid, but he simply has no sense of what causes suspense in a film. Aside from the endless plot and logic holes that destroy the story faster than any invading aliens could, (no one on Earth ever noticed hundreds or thousands of fifteen-story metal machines buried in the ground?) and the vending-machine acting performances I find the main problem here is that the important conflict (for conflict is what drives characters to move through the plot) is between the aliens and the people of Earth. Instead of spending film time developing the "us-versus-them" convention that is demanded by this story, Spielberg wastes the energy on developing conflict between father and son, husband and ex wife, main protagonist and stranger, etc. He gets so distracted with those relationships that it's possible the aliens could have gotten bored and gone home, and we wouldn't know about it because we're forced to watch Sentispeilbergmental plot-diluting scenes. The end of the movie, which should be based on the the relief that everyone on Earth still alive is now safe, is passed over in favor of a smarmy father/son reconciliation of a schism that should never have happened. Spielberg's greatest clue of how to handle this story is right in the title, "War of the Worlds", not "Jimmy and Jenny learn to like Daddy again." I have generally found that this is the main problem with all of his films. Think of the Velociaptors-in-the-kitchen scene from "Jurrassic Park." How stupid would it have been to have the two kids arguing over something mundane instead of trying not to be eaten? It would have robbed that whole scene of any direness crucial to its effect. Spielberg does exactly that with much of this movie.

Lastly, a plot hole that made us laughing in our seats. Everyone is hungry. Robbie has brought only bread, peanut butter, and condiments as sustenance. Rachel is allergic to peanut butter. Ray is furious. He throws the slathered bread onto the window resulting in a lucky once-in-a-lifetime adhesion. Hunger! What will they eat! Where will they find food? This all takes place in the kitchen of an obviously well-stocked home. Personally, I would have looked in the refrigerator, duh.

title: disappointing
review: Well the movie starts off really nice with both funny and cool scenes, and it's ain't getting worse later on. I don't think I have seen Tom Cruise acting better ever, and for the first time I found him funny! Spielberg, always trying to be ahead of the other directors shot this movie strangely enough to follow Tom Cruse and his children all the time. It means that the camera isn't moving away from the family, only for very short moments... This can be bad because we miss some big battle-scenes which I expected to see. The only sign of war is the marching troops. Anyway it's still no problem but the ending is so thin that you can laugh at it, we hear a man reading the last 5 sentences of the book...and THE END. As such a "big" director Stephen should had tried to make this ending different. and. It could have been a good movie indeed, but what's a movie without a fair ending? 5/10 DOESN'T DESERVE 10 NOR 1

title: Superb alien invasion, Spielberg style! The effects are mind boggling
review:
*** Tom Cruise, Justin Chatwin, Dakota Fanning, Tim Robbins, Miranda Otto, David Alan Basche. Directed by Steven Spielberg.

Third times a charm, right? After Spielberg did two dud alien movies E.T the extra terrestrial and Close encounters of a third kind. But with the help of writer David Koepp and based on the classic novel by H.G Wells not to mention great actors like Tom Cruise and Tim Robbins and a up and coming actress Dakota Fanning the movie was bound to be good. And if that wasn't enough the loads of CGI on the tripods. But... but the aliens, Spielberg you can not make aliens. First "E.T" then whatever was in "Close Encounters".

The story over the weekend a dead beat dad Ray Ferrier (Cruise) gets his kids Rachel (Fanning) and Robbie (Chatwin)for the weekend after his ex-wife Mary Ann (Otto) throws them on him with the help over her new boyfriend Tim (Basche).While the kids are over the invaders come in and ruin their weekend. While on the run they bump into a helping stranger Ogilvy (Robbins) who is eager to kill some aliens! Cool CGI and special effects and after three tries Spielberg you finally got it right. My final rating 8/10.

title: I liked it
review: I read the book and thought he did a good job of applying it to our times as if to say, "What if..." Dakota Fanning was excellent as a terrified 10 year old. Tom Cruise captured the feeling of a parent trying to protect his children from the horrors of a world-wide catastrophe. The fact that he has children with bad attitudes is realistic and adds tension to what's going on around them. The battle scenes that Spielberg kept just out of our view were depicted well enough by seeing jeeps rolling down the hill on fire or the train on fire flying past the crowd. Your imagination took over from there, as it does when you read the book. I go to the movies for entertainment and I was entertained.

title: 1898 science fiction story can't be easily transformed into 2005 science fiction
review:
The original story was written for a late 19th century audience. It was wonderful, not just in its time, but in reading it set in that time period and understanding it in its context as early science fiction. It could even be produced again as a 1930 era radio story, and even a 1953 movie, because science fiction was still naive, and we were still naive about space travel. But the story itself is simplistic and naive, and cannot be effectively translated into a 21st century (or even late 20th century) science fiction story. The result is a lot of great special effects (that, the story allows), but other than that this is a silly and simple story that was great as a book, just can't stand up as a modern classic. And, boy, for an advanced intellect, as Morgan Freeman as the narrator tells us they are at the beginning of the movie, are those aliens dumb! Aside from not being well prepared, can't they do better than picking us off one by one? That's their plan?

The story is a typical Spielberg science fiction exercise in smoke, mirrors, and noise, but lacking in substance.

title: War of the Worlds = WOW indeed!!!
review:
I just came back from seeing the movie a second time and after reading some of the awful comments here, I felt I had to add my own comment.

First of all, yes, I am a Spielberg fan, mostly because I was 10 years old when I saw E.T. and ever since I've had a passion for his movies. That said, each time I see a new movie from him, I keep expecting to be as thrilled as I was as a kid or a teenager. However, even though I like his recent films, I never felt thrilled or awed watching Catch Me If You Can or the Terminal. I still enjoyed them, but they didn't seem very "Spielbergy" to me. Minority Report was close, but not jaw-dropping.

I went in to see War of the Worlds with HUGE expectations, and I was bracing myself for at least a slight disappointment. After all, I felt as excited for Revenge of the Sith, but came out bitterly disappointed. And just before War of the Worlds started, I was sitting in the theater reading a 2 star review from the Evening Standard, that was quite harsh so I got a bit worried as the lights went down.

Well that didn't last. Spielberg fan or not, I was absolutely BLOWN AWAY by what was shown on the big screen. It's one of those movie experiences when you are glued to the screen in total awe, your mouth wide open. You can't believe what you're seeing because you've never seen anything like it - ever. For me it felt like seeing the dinosaurs in Jurassic Park for the first time, or seeing the first Matrix for the first time. It was that awesome, and my jaw was on my knees quite a few times. There are some incredible images in that film, that stay with you after seeing the movie. Classic Spielberg! As for the ending that lots of people are complaining about: well that's exactly as Wells wrote it, and as it happens in the original film. You don't like it? Blame Wells! If Spielberg had done it differently the fans of the book and the original would have been screaming for his blood. It could have been extended a bit, yes, but frankly this is a minor gripe when you consider the whole movie. How people can give this movie a 1 simply because they didn't like the faithful ending or because they hate Tom Cruise is beyond me. A 1 is for Catwoman OK? There is so much genius on display here... just go and see it and be awed. I can't wait for the DVD!

title: A faithful and stunning revisit to an earlier age of science fiction
review:
Spielberg learned all of the lessons he would need to make an excellent alien invasion movie from Signs and his Close Encounters of the Third Kind. This movie seems reminiscent of both of those movies in many ways, but it is not simply a combination of the two, either. It is also an effective and modernized science fiction story for one of the oldest science fiction stories in the genre: the hostile alien invasion.

By focusing the camera on Tom Cruise and his dysfunctional family, the movie takes from Signs its personal feel, although the movie also manages many scenes of sweeping drama on the scale of such flicks like Kingdom of Heaven or Ben Hur. These scenes in particular are aided by subtle and stunning visual effects, but beyond all of the high-tech wizardry that obviously went into the movie, Spielberg's skill with lighting effects was maximized to the n-th degree. Remember the kitchen scene from Close Encounters combined with the dark moodiness of Jurassic Park and you'll get the gist of it.

There are some serious problems with the movie that should not be overlooked, despite all of the aforementioned awesomeness. I take serious issue with the manner in which the aliens buried their war machines on Earth tens of thousands (maybe even millions) of years ago and then proceeded to enter them via riding lightning bolts from the sky down into the earth where they are buried. It's cool, sure, but from a scientific standpoint there are much easier ways, like H.G. Well's original idea (one of the few departures the film makes, and not coincidentally one of its weakest points) of dropping the war machines to earth in giant artillery-shell-esquire spaceships. Duh. But instead there is the lightning, a phenomenon which doesn't even "push" things and therefore provides no help to the alien drop pods "riding" them down. Ridiculous science, if cool to watch. Also, the movie seemed to end abruptly, almost as if Spielberg said "ok, this is cool enough and I have other things to do, let's start the end here" and went with it. Not to say that these things ruin the movie - there is so much more good stuff going on that I don't have the space to write about - but it is there.

Perhaps the most important thing about this movie, however, is the manner in which it melds new and old concepts of sci-fi together. You have all the character complexity and general concern for technological feasibility (the aforementioned aside), combined with things like human-disintegrating death rays, energy shields, and soulless alien conquerors. What's more, the subtle ways in which the special effects introduce these things make it seem totally acceptable to the modern movie-goer. It is great to watch it all unfold and not feel like I have to suspend belief on purpose.

Here you have a well-thought out alien invasion movie with good acting, few obviously moronic science moments, and great cinematography. Go see it, go enjoy it.

title: Good movie, and thats from someone who wanted a "period" piece.
review:
Maybe SPOILERS!!!!!

I am not a critic, so don't expect much useless verbosity. I like science fiction, and I really like the old science fiction stories. So I really wanted a line by line telling of the H.G. Wells classic. What I got was a good updating of the story, but without the cool meteorites or mention of our Red neighbor. Some of the people reviewing this movie seem to want a in depth, personal, heart wrenching story...and were disappointed by a fast paced, at times creepy...and a few laughs thrown in for good measure movie?

The BIG MAJOR complaint I have is it focused more on the main characters fight against the invaders than mankind's struggle, can you say "Thunderchild", tho seeing Tom Cruise close to a big propeller has it's merits ;)

Now that Mr. Spielberg has shot a old scifi classic, I wish he would tackle H.P Lovecraft, "The Mountains of Madness" would be a great place to start.

All in all, worth your money, but your kids may not sleep for a week...

title: A great thrill-ride from start to about 20 minutes before the finish---8/10
review:
Steven Spielberg's War of the Worlds is a classic alien invasion flick. Not too much time is wasted before the aliens invade and start zapping humans into dust and flipping cars over. Tom Cruise plays Ray, a regular guy with regular family problems who is trying to get his son and daughter the hell out of dodge. Now that we got the story out of the way, let's get to the goods. The alien tripods are huge and terrifying, with superlasers and tubes that suck blood, a far cry from E.T.'s bicycle and Reeces Pieces. Spielberg's cinematography is amazing once again, from wide shots of the aliens destroying cities to a river of corpses. This is his most gorgeous film since Minority Report (while A.I. was also pretty to look at, it was painfully boring and confusing). The non-stop thrills includes an alien attack on a boat of refugees, the family hiding in a basement from a huge alien eyeball, and Cruise actually being swallowed by one of the tripods. The pace is lightning quick, Cruise is as good as ever, Fanning is proving to be better than most adult actresses, and the action is non-stop. A really great movie...

And then comes the ending. The standard Hollywood cop-out, spic and span ending. Not only does the film include one of the weakest and anti-climactic ways to defeat an invading alien force (Can't the aliens just destroy us for once) but all the main characters live, even after making you think one of them is dead in an emotionally powerful scene. This almost ruins the movie, but the rest of it is so good, i can forgive. Maybe.

However, this is still a blockbuster alien invasion epic with amazing special effects (ILM strikes again) and great performances. This is a must-see in theaters. The price is worth it for enhanced picture and sound. Enjoy the ride.---8/10

title: Better than the Critics say
review:
I keep reading comments about how its depressing, some things don't make sense and so on. My response to all of those comments is READ THE BOOK! The book is not warm and fuzzy. It is about aliens coming to Earth and killing everything in sight. This is not an Adam Sandler flick. As for the complaints of some things don't make sense such as why did humans not discover the alien crafts buried in the ground before, or why didn't the aliens know the germs would kill them? It's a movie! When was the last time you went to a movie where everything was accurate and made perfect sense. It's a story. The point of the story is good overcomes evil, and little tiny things can beat big giant things.

The movie is entertaining, creepy, suspenseful and a good watch. If you want to play mr. big-time movie critic and complain about pace and lighting and blah, blah, blah be my guest. If you want to go to a movie and be entertained for two hours go see War of the Worlds, or better yet read the book!

title: A good screen version of H.G. Wells classic
review:
Having heard the radio play I knew the outcome, but those I've talked to haven't, so this movie would be even more exciting/intense for them. It's certainly NOT FOR KIDS though - I don't know how it only has a PG-13 rating. Tom Cruise covers his daughters eyes and does what he can to protect her from the slaughter - both literally and viewing it. Parents in the real world should heed the caution that accompanies the rating.

ILM does their usual great job with effects, and there's nothing wrong with the acting, but I confess I'm getting tired of seeing the same actors (Cruise in this example) on screen over and over in so many movies. It takes away from the intrigue when you know the character is going to survive the whole movie. That's probably one of the aspects that made the first "Lord of the Rings", the first "Star Wars", the first "Matrix", and Spielbergs own "E.T." such great movies. "War of the Worlds" feels a bit like "Minority Report", although upon seeing the aliens it seemed more like an "Independence Day" sequel.

title: Everything you would expect from a summer blockbuster.
review:
After what seemed like years and years of listening to anti-Tom Cruise press, I walked into my local movie theater yesterday wanting to see War of the Worlds just so I could put this whole fiasco behind me. However, I was pleasantly surprised. Tom Cruise and Steven Spielberg have united to give audiences a film that is probably the most thrilling and entertaining of all the movies in this summer's stellar lineup.

The film's strongest point is it's realistic portrayal of America in a time of severe crisis. Spielberg shows a country full of citizens in full blown survival mode, where morality and decency seem to no longer exist, and as an audience member you find yourself sadly realizing that the horrors on the screen are probably what would happen. This alone makes it much different than Hollywood's more recent alien blockbusters. Independence Day wanted you to believe that Americans would quickly unite against a common enemy, and Signs wanted you to think that people would be too shocked to do anything at all, neither of which seem as accurate as War of the Worlds.

Perhaps the film's biggest mistake is it's characters, none of whom come off as appealing or likable. From the beginning, Tom Cruise's character, Ray, is regarded as somewhat of a deadbeat dad, making him instantly unappealing. His son, Robbie, is a rebellious teenager who at first appears to have some legitimate depth as a character, but then quickly descends into a world of clichés. Dakota Fanning once again delivers a spectacular performance as Ray's daughter Rachel. It's just too bad her character had to be so annoying. The screenwriters have Dakota spend so much time yelling and whining that eventually you stop caring when her character is in danger, because her death might be a little bit easier on your ears. Tim Robbins drops in as one of the few supporting characters in the film, an older man hiding out from the aliens in his basement. From the second Robbins appears on screen, you know what his character's purpose is, but the movie does a good job of keeping him from becoming a walking stereotype.

Despite it's character troubles, War of the Worlds delivers where summer blockbuster's are supposed to - in entertainment. It's an exciting movie from start to finish. If you like alien movies, you will especially love War of the Worlds. Better then Indepence Day, and almost as good as Signs, it will go down as one of the all time invasion classics. War of the Worlds is so engaging and realistic, I can't imagine anyone disliking the film.

title: Good film but not as good as it could have been
review:
This could have been a great movie but unfortunately it fell way short on so many levels . The special effects particularly the sound, were the movie's only saving graces. One major thing above all else ruined it for me. The irritating child played by the exceedingly precocious Dakota Fanning was a pain in the ass from the start and all throughout the movie. Before the movie had even reached its mid-point I started to wish the aliens would blast her to a painfully deserved oblivion and stop her incessant screaming, then we could concentrate on the movie itself. I know that Cruise was portrayed as a father that was trying to look after his family but in her case I wondered why.

I have also seen this 'child star' interviewed about the movie and she is just as annoying in real life. She is a child that has the glib starstruck attitude of a 60 year old, and trots out all the usual trite clichés such as ' It was wonderful working with Tom and being directed by David, I learnt so much to enhance my acting talents'.....pass the bucket I want to barf.

Oh by the way everything electrical was 'fried' by the lightning bolts but somehow a guy still managed to get his camcorder working. The ferry was fully operational, the TV truck had no problems, etc.

The ending was the worst. Had his wife and her family got an anti-alien force field around their house that prevented them from getting as much as ruffled hair. They all looked as though they had just finished a dinner party whilst the rest of the world was being devastated - pass the bucket again.

title: Wow!!! I wasn't expecting this
review:
I am writing this literally minutes after leaving the cinema.

I am a sucker for sci-fi. I had to see it and was expecting to bag the hell out of it all the way through. Having been a bit jaded by Spielberg's work of late, and not at all a Tom Cruise fan, I really wasn't expecting much from this film.

But Spielberg clearly still has the knack, he just hasn't used it in a while.

This film was GREAT!!!!!! It's seriously frightening, and keep you on the edge of your seat all the way through. Given that we are 107 years on from the book, it is still reasonably faithful to the themes. Tom Cruise is playing himself as usual but it fits in with this film. Dakota is great.

This is an exciting film, I highly recommend it.

title: Wow is WOW!
review:
As a lifetime fan of the H.G. Wells novel and the George Hal motion picture, I can honestly say that Mr. Spielberg's adaptation of The War of the Worlds is nothing short of fantastic! This film highlights the major differences between truly legendary film makers and all the rest. Spielberg cares about story. He concentrates on theme and consistency. He makes films with a complete understanding and appreciation for the audience, not just for the sake of his own ego and for the sake of making a movie.

What a great and faithful version of the classic tale this movie is! Spielberg does a great job of moving the tale into the 21st century without all the subliminal political baggage you so often see in today's movies. What a relief to see a film that doesn't have underlying criticism of today's events or with barely hidden political agendas.

Cruise is believable as the self-indulged absentee dad who has neglected his family. As a father myself, I saw true-to-life interaction between Cruise's character and his troublesome teenage son. It was subtle, it was natural, and most importantly it was real. So is his relationship between his character and Dakota Fanning, who should get an Oscar for her performance in this film. She is so absolutely vulnerable and plays her character with such flair and depth that it would be a shame if she wasn't at least nominated for an Academy Award.

The story itself is very solid and believable. Sure there's an unexplained hole or two (like where do the aliens come from?), but they are relatively insignificant, because the whole purpose of the tale is to completely undermine your sense of complacency and the total confidence in your superiority in the world. The lesson is that at any time, any thing can happen to bring you down. There are 9-11 type images in the film, but don't think it's intentional. If anything, 9-11 brings home the reality of the theme of the movie and serves as a real-world example (albeit on a smaller scale) of what happens in this story. The original novel tells of a man who witnesses the ravages of the ultimate war, and this movie stays with that plot faithfully.

The quality of the film making is outstanding. Spielberg does not dwell on special effects, nor does he depend on them to propel the story like some other lesser film makers do (take a hint George Lucas). You aren't barraged with images of tripod after tripod after tripod  in this movie, you are given a ground-level, personal experience point of view (the tripods in the background, buildings exploding around you, people right next to you evaporated by heat beams). Spielberg focuses on the personal, not the grandiose, and it brings the movie home in a very real way. As a young child I often had horrifying dreams of large monsters or robots chasing me, hunting me down. I couldn't escape them, they were always on my heels. WoW brought back those fears in a big way, and I felt a real sense of dread every time those tripods made an appearance. Speaking of which, the first appearance of the first tripod is a masterpiece of modern cinema. No music to over-dramatize things, you are left to just experience the awe and wonder as if you were on the scene standing right in the crowd.

The aliens themselves weren't that forbidding, but I wasn't expecting much there anyway. Again, the story is not really about them, but about the human experience.

Tim Robbins plays a character in the movie that is actually amalgamated from two different characters in the novel  the groveling priest and the lazy dreaming soldier. In one of the most powerful scenes in the film, Cruise must deal with this dangerous person who threatens to bring the aliens down on them all while they hide out in an abandoned house. Spielberg does this with power and infinite grace, choosing to let the action play out behind a closed door with Dakota Fanning singing a lullaby to herself in the next room.

All in all this was a thoroughly enjoyable motion picture. It's so refreshing to see a classic brought to the screen with such grace and attention to detail as this movie. My hat is off to Spielberg once again for making movies so much fun to not only watch but experience as well.

title: Hour forty of excitement followed by 10 minutes of boredom.
review: Some parts don't connect. (Cruise covers hundreds of miles in a second and with no space ship.) But for action this movie has it. I was on the edge of my seat. Special effects were great. Scene setups and "eye of view" of the camera give a deeper level to the movie. A few technical items don't match. Thanks to the invasion everything electronic stops working, except for one video camera. Some things to watch for..tributes to great movies. One example. Cruise stands on a hill with the glow of red behind him = Gone With The Wind. If you are fan of the original War of the Worlds from 1953 look for Gene Barry and Ann Robinson in the final scene. All in all this is a good movie, not a great film. Absolutely do not take a child under 10 to this movie. It may be very terrifying to a younger child.

title: Could have gone the distance...but didn't
review:
Spielberg had me for most of the movie. I was actually able to ignore the improbabilities presented in the plot, the obvious contradictions, and the rather choppy back and forth between touching moments of father and children, scenes of horrendous carnage, and just Tom Cruise running from one horrible thing to another. I'm normally a pain when it comes to wanting movies to only ask me to make one leap of faith, but even though this one left more questions than even Soloman could answer I was willing to let it slide because the scenes were well constructed and photogenic, even when the rational part of my brain was chuckling softly to itself at the flaws. I watched the situation grow more and more desperate, and Tom Cruise fighting to hold on to his two children as he comes to realize how much they actually mean to him. Holed up in a basement with a madman (Tim Robbins...who knew?), having just watched his son get incinerated; we still find it traumatic that he doesn't know any lullabyes to sing his daughter, and still find tears welling when he sings 'Little Deuce Coupe'. That's the magic of Spielberg.

His magic is such that I actually thought Hollywood would have the guts to leave a mixed ending, one where not everything turns out hunky-dory for everyone involved. I mean, Cruise is heading to Boston to find his ex-wife and the mother of his children. Boston. Major City. Probably destroyed with all the other major cities, right? You'd think. So we assume from the start that that won't end well. Then, as said before, the son gets incinerated, and we feel bad, but we're still pulling for Tom Cruise to somehow survive this with his daughter. (Who, by the by, is this cute little blond with femme-nazi tendencies and panic attacks...of course...Fortunately, her lines in the bulk of the movie consist of screaming in terror and looking pitiful while asking daddy what's going on.) Then the aliens are sucking blood out of people, and they grab the daughter. This looks like the end. But no. Cruise gets himself picked up with a belt of grenades that he finds conveniently just in time, and gets put into a bin where other people are being collected; again, conveniently. He gets chosen like a claw machine toy, and is sucked in, then is grabbed by a marine in the bin, and pulled out, having left the grenade inside.

Well, the thing blows up, and Cruise is saved with his daughter from almost certain disaster. Then, we cut to what must be at least 100 miles away (from somewhere in CT to Boston). This trip must have taken days for two people, one a little girl, to make on foot. Even given that they don't get harassed by aliens the whole way (which would be odd, since every minute of the trip so far has been them running from one problem to the next) It would still be a horrible trip. But this is ignored, and we cut to Boston, where the aliens are just dying all around the survivors. Now, I know that's how it went down in The H.G.Wells story, so I run with it. But still, even though Cruise and the girl survived, the son is dead, and we still haven't found the mom. Then we emerge onto a city street that looks a little windswept, but otherwise undamaged. Cruise is carrying his daughter to what we presume is the completely undamaged home of the mother, to find her waiting at the door. the little girl drops from her father's arms, and runs to her mom, and the mother silently mouths 'Thank You'. I'm already choking on the saccharine, but still know the son died, so it isn't all good. Or is it?

In one of the biggest double-take moments in a motion-picture, just as we think the credits are going to roll, the son comes out of the house and runs to his father who embraces him. We then cut to a shot at the doorway, revealing the mom's parents and the step-dad all perfectly fine. They don't even look like they've been without power and running water for at least a week. As the credits roll, we hear Morgan Freeman reading what I assume is the script from the original, saying how Earthly diseases wiped out the aliens. But while this is great for humankind, it does nothing to wash out the bad taste left in the mouth from all the sugar dumped into the movie in the last moments to make the medicine of the horror wreaked by the aliens go down into the over-stimulated, self-esteem obsessed 'minds' of the average viewing public member. So, instead of a bittersweet ending where people emerge from tragedy to new hope, we find that nothing irreplaceable has been lost to Cruise. The world may have been destroyed, but his family is all OK. I wish that just once Hollywood would actually go out on a limb and show that sometimes everything doesn't work out perfectly in the end, and you need to accept the good with the bad. Oh well...at least this one was better than A.I....

Few parting shots: Yes, the plot was problematic, but it was shot beautifully. Yes, we really have no idea what the aliens are doing (incinerating? sucking blood? why both?) but it's fun to watch. Unfortunately, the end left me with no faith in the ability of people to deal with bad things happening. Let's just hope this doesn't happen in real life; people would spend the whole time whining about how it doesn't make them feel good.

title: Pretty Good Movie!
review:
First Thoughts: .... *speechless* ....

Pro's: Overall, I thought this was one of Spielberg's better films. I preferred this one to E.T. *gag* Tom Cruise, who I'm not a huge fan of, does a pretty convincing performance. It seriously is a Doom's Day kind of movie. I mean you see people getting blown up and killed. Don't take the kids to see it. No kids under the age of 11, I would say. But, for teenagers, it's a pretty okay movie. Adults, you'll enjoy this. This version is more true to the book and not so much to the 1950's version. My dad, who is a huge fan of the old version, thought it was a pretty good movie, and he wanted to see it again. Previously, I had neither read the book, nor seen the original film, but I kind of enjoyed this movie. If you're wondering what it's about, the title gives it all away.

Con's: The action sequences are very long, and just keep going on and on. It's bloody and gory, so it's definitely not a kiddie movie. In the movie, the people keep looking back, watching what's chasing them instead of running away. I was saying, "Run! Stupid people, run!" at the screen.

Overall: Go see it if your a fan of the book, movie, or if you're just interested and/or curious. The ending is surprisingly simple.

title: Not your average alien invasion film. War of the Worlds is a blood fest.
review:
This movie was very disappointing. Furthermore, in my opinion it was down-right disturbing is some scenes.

A lot of people are comparing this to Independence Day, which I would say is a better film. Independence Day was a light-hearted movie with a feel-good ending. It had a ton of action and was very well-rounded. Of course it wasn't a masterpiece, but it was entertaining. I don't have so much praise for War of the Worlds. There are just too many scenes with masses of people in desperation, about to be massacred. There was way too much shock and awe in this film and I question the reason for it. Was Spielberg trying to use the same technique as in Schindler's List, in the film? I really had to turn my head in some scenes. In fact, I continually saw parents escorting their children out of the theater.

Still more, there are no great scenes that stand out from the rest. No great protagonist or scenes of the human race coming together to defeat the aliens. What you see is very contrary to what you'd hope for. Its a very pessimistic movie. And the ending? What a let down. It was there only because the movie had to end.

This is basically a horror movie. Its the worst Spielberg movie ever made.

title: Cruise and Fanning don't disappoint
review:
Wow. What an experience. This movie makes Independence Day look like Mars Attacks! First, let me address the Cruise nay-sayers, as he is often cited as a one-dimensional actor. I believe it's a normal reaction to his cocky, hail-fellow-well-met, testosterone imbalanced performances in most of his films; and to some degree, such a preconceived notion does indeed do him disservice in this movie as it's hard to see him as: a.) An emotionally detached absentee father, and b.) actually in danger of harm at any time during his plight against the unnamed attackers (unlike the original, this movie makes no mention of Martians). However, I think that Cruise did an outstanding job of balancing the emotional evolution of his character from beginning to end, the whole time making himself believable, and showing a range of emotion that one might expect to see from a theatrically-trained stage actor (think Adrien Brody in The Pianist).

That said, I think most are in agreement with the talent of Dakota Fanning, and to be sure, she does not disappoint. The chemistry between her and Cruise is palpable, and I'm sure that this would have been a lesser movie experience without her. Supporting roles are fine as well, especially Tim Robbins in a somewhat odd role as a survivalist type.

I'll forgo the storyline, as everyone knows it already, but I'll add that the effects were outstanding as one would expect from a Spielberg effort. The aliens and their machines were not overwrought, and show respect for H.G. Wells' written word. Additionally, and as an unexpected surprise, the movie does not gratuitously hang it's hat on these, but focuses more on the characters and their interaction.

There are moments of visual awe, headache-inducing tension and visceral horror from the moment lightning strikes. This movie is what Independence Day should have been.

title: Excellent!
review:
***POSSIBLE MILD SPOILERS*** When I first saw a poster in a movie theater lobby for War of the Worlds (back in February) and saw Steven Spielberg was the director, I began counting the seconds! I always hoped a legitimate director would do a good sci-fi that was somewhat grounded in reality - unlike, say, Independence Day which ended up being very cartoonish. Signs I thought was much better, but relied too heavily in the psychological with not enough visual to hammer home the point.

Spielberg gets it mostly right. This film contains all the great aspects I was looking for: terror, drama, suspense, irony, and humor all rolled into a 2-hour package. Tom Cruise is very good as the indifferent-turned-super dad Ray Ferrier, but the show belonged to Dakota Fanning. Justin Chatwin is also good as the wise-ass kid who clearly resents his almost non-existent father. Tim Robbins was wonderful in his role as the unstable and off-center Ogilvy.

The special effects, as expected, were brilliant but not overdone. The tripods were amazingly real and terrifying - not to mention ubiquitous which adds to the tension. The scene where the first one emerges from beneath Bayonne, NJ will go down in cinema history as one of the most tense and startling.

We do get a look at the aliens: they are other-worldy but inquisitive and cold and calculating. Just what you might expect from beings who presumably traveled a zillion miles to wipe out humanity.

The only problem I had was the one shot Tom Cruise gets at heroism - he, of course, succeeds but I didn't think it fit with the theme of realism so well executed to that point.

The ending was a bit hurried but not so much as to ruin the rest of the film as some people have complained. A longer ending sequence would have been more gratifying, though.

This was a great achievement in science fiction ans will leave you white-knuckled and tense - and believing that indeed they may NOT come in peace after all.

title: Watch it, but don't get too involved in the holes like I did.
review: For what it is worth, I am a huge sci fi fan and have been waiting for this movie to be released for awhile. I will say that I thoroughly felt entertained , but at the same time totally ripped by Spielberg. For all it's special effects and spells that cast on the audience to keep us watching, there were also equal amounts of complete implausibility scattered throughout. I believe aliens can be believable.. I believe an alien invasion could actually happen. Not one where 1000's upon 1000's of people are running, but only Tom and his daughter are asked into the celler by Tim Robbons character... Not one where the robot machines themselves are set on tripods (every engineer knows that is a no-no) ... not one where aliens are so smart to have planned everything, yet are unaware of our germs... not one where everything is shut off, electricity (emt bursts) clocks, cars ..everything not working yet a man is able to videotape it... not one where people stand around gawking instead of running their butts off... not one where all the main characters survive. I am thoroughly disappointed by Spielberg's need to Hollywoodize it. Earlier into the film it is made evident that people will do anything to stay alive at the expense of other's lives, yet they want to Save Tom from the alien robots anus sucker? Man, why can't someone just make a movie like it really would be if we were invaded like that? Hollywood always has to put their pretty bow on it and I for one am tired of that.

title: Works for this genre
review:
Given the constraints imposed by the original H.G. Wells novel, Spielberg and Cruise acquitted themselves very well. Entertaining and gripping without getting deep. I have not had this sense of satisfying made-for-Summer blockbuster experience for quite a while. Nonetheless, some images will stay with you. Some reviewers have commented with the resonance with national fears about "outsiders" and changes to our status quo but this is still based on a pioneering 19th century yarn that defined the invasion genre.

Those of us from Boston will particularly appreciate some of the landmarks that appear.

Don't bring the kids though unless you want to deal with the subsequent nightmares.

title: Another 2005 disappointment
review:
I couldn't wait for this one. As a kid War of the Worlds was my favorite film. That is until Nov. 1977 when Close Encounters came out, and has since been my #1 film. I hate long reviews so... Not as dumb as ID4, though could have used some of the thrilling moments from that flick. Not as bad as any Shamalan films, those look good on paper but always LAME! Signs, anyone? yuck!

If you are expecting Jaws meets Close Encounters like me. sorry! This is too much Tom Cruise and not enough fun. It starts off great. Good tension and development, but after the first attack in New Jersey, starts to flat line. I kept waiting for Spielberg to kick in and deliver a Jurassic Park moment...waited...waited...nope.

title: Major mistake...
review:
...when the electricity goes out in the beginning of the movie and Tom Cruise's character checks all home appliances if they work he also checks his watch to see if it works, which it doesn't. This is a mistake since it is a mechanic Omega watch and contains no batteries and therefore should not be affected by the electro magnetic impulses. How do I know it is mechanic? I can tell by the model that it is manufactured in the 50's or 60's and to the best of my knowledge there where no battery-driven Omega watches at that time.

Apart from this the movie was OK but I can't help but to just hate the kids and their annoying behavior throughout the movie.

title: Cool, but
review: Too much of the little girl screaming, too much Tom, not enough military action shown. The only military action shown is a doomed attack on one of the tripods, by troops, M1A Abrams, M3 Bradleys, F-16 Vipers, AH-64 Apachies, and Ray's son. Also at the end several troops attack a dying tripod with M203's, Singers, and some sort of anti-tank weapons. The only thing I would have added was a montage of tripods getting blown to hell at the end like ID4. Also it could have been a bit more true to the book, although I never read it, some who did say that the movie missed several things, and was more focused on Ray, but it may have been to allow people to more closely associate with the protagonist. But still great overall.

title: {yawn} Zzzzzzzzzzzzzz
review:
Disappointing is the best word for it. It did follow the book pretty well, and also the 1953 movie. No surprises at the ending. There was one (irrelavant) twist to the storyline in the beginning, but otherwise...{yawn}. Besides, new story changes were silly, and highly implausible. It could have been scary, but they didn't make it very scary.

Dakoda Fanning was great. She easily bested Tom Cruise, who was flat and uninspiring. Cruise played an uninspiring loser father, who's kids have more brains and guts. Other than the special effects, the original movie was better. I can't imagine how they spent $200 million making this. It'll be another Waterworld. Batman Begins is a better movie. Spielberg's direction was disappointing, as was Tom's acting. I just seemed like a sloppy sci-fi remake, not a $200 million blockbuster. I was glad it finally ended. I don't think it'll do that well in the box office.

Tim Robbins performance was weak, but I think his scenes were poorly directed. If you want to kill a few hours on a so-so remake with a few good special effects, then see the movie. If you expect a great movie, be prepared for disappointment.

title: One of The Greatest Movies of All time
review: This movie has been the subject of controversy and disagreement for quite awhile and this is my take on it. The thing that has most viewers puzzled is the ending. Maybe a lot of you were expecting an Independence Day ending where that go to battle against them. This ending is what makes the movie so great. I think the thought of the tiniest particle of of the earth can help change the universe intriguing. It was original and superb. And need I mention the special effects the shot of the tripods coming up from the ground and blowing up of the bridge outstanding. The interaction of Tom Cruise and Dakota Fanning as on screen father and daughter was brilliant. So don't listen if a friend or family member says this sucks don't listen go out and see this movie now!!!!!!!

title: Hard to not give it a 10.
review: I've read the knit-picky reviews here and am saddened that people can't be entertained anymore, even when the entertainment is as great as this. The cynical criticism - hating a movie because it wasn't written a particular way or because it had a discontinuity here or there - is really too bad. The reality is, Spielberg has captured the heart of H.G. Wells work and translated it more than a century into the future, making it relevant to we who are alive today. The technology he chose to use for the invaders tripods is so raw- almost steam-engine like- capturing the look and feel of the invaders from Well's original story, and yet the weaponry hearkens back to the terrifying ray weapons from the 1953 classic film. There are nods to the original film, but done with a Spielberg twist that takes the whole thing up a notch. The family dynamic that Cruise, Fanning, and Chatwin bring to screen is awesome. Some have argued that the gushy family stuff could be done without- but what is a story if not about humanity and human relationships? I'm not interested in a shallow and sterile shoot-em-up. I want a film to wrench at my heart and make me care about the characters. Otherwise, what's the point? This is a great movie. Terrifying, heart-wrenching, hopeful. I thought hard to pick out something that would make me not give it a 10. If I were cynical, like others, I'm sure I could find many reasons, but for now, I am astonished and entertained beyond my expectations.

title: think of Spielberg's adaptation of War of the Worlds as his darker relative of Close Encounters
review:
Upon a first viewing of Steven Spielberg's latest big-action/suspense summer blockbuster War of the Worlds, I can say without a shadow of a doubt that this is what I love about going to see science-fiction thrillers. In the vein of Spielberg's best thrillers (Jurassic Park, Jaws, even Duel in some circles) not only is the story not predictable like the other dumbed down, less satisfying actioneers, but one can sense who is the real star of the film. Despite the fact that the director has a mega-star (as nutty as he may be off camera at times, Tom Cruise is dependable in good hands, better in great ones), and some supporting players who stand-out (Tim Robbins and especially Dakota Fanning), Spielberg's total control over his medium is without a missed mark. For better or sometimes worse, when one sees a film directed by him, it's not going to be standard stuff on the screen. Like Hitchcock or Kubrick or Scorsese, there's a personality coming through the storytelling, acting more often than not as a manipulator, but not in a way that cheats too much like in films that become forgotten.

Examples of Spielberg's mastery of set-pieces of destruction and of stylized horror film-making can be found in, admittedly, greater Spielberg films (Jaws comes to mind, but also Jurassic Park and Minority Report too), but he's not just playing old tricks here, but still making his mis-en-scene and build-ups/pay-offs work well, very well. A prominent example to give from War of the Worlds isn't one involving the hundreds of extras on the run from the aliens, but one in an enclosed space. In one scene, which I won't reveal the circumstances to how it comes to this, Cruise, Robbins, and Fanning's characters are in a basement, and a sinister presence is surrounding them, searching, at every corner following their beats. This is the kind of scene that might be in a slightly different permutation in some of those films I mentioned before, but it doesn't lose any of its impact. The harder work- getting to care about the characters- is placed in so strongly that its hard for the scene not to work. That the pay-off in this scene, and several others, don't flounder is not just a credit to him, but to his team (i.e. editor Michael Kahn, the great cinematographer Janusz Kaminski, and of course John Williams).

Truth be told, some elements of the film are almost too good or too expectable at times (such as a rather Spielbergian ending, though this may be similar to the H.G. Wells novel, un-read by me), and it is aside from Schindler's List and Saving Private Ryan the most violent and riveting action-wise (as un-real as it is, somehow believable at the same time) and probably will act as more of an adrenaline rush to the younger ones. But for one who has grown up on Spielberg's films, who understood really what a director does from first watching his films, this is another fine touch to the lot. Even if you're not much of a Cruise fan it's entertaining- in fact, at the core, that's what the film wants to do with its continuous sense of urgency, to entertain the hell out of anyone, young, old, any race or creed....

Having said this though, just know, it might be slightly less effective on repeat viewings, as I've come to see. 8/10

title: TOTAL FAMILY DRAMA!! Not a sci fi movie!
review:
I watched this movie since I thought it would be a sci fi. I wanted action, cool alien stuff, humans trying to get the aliens down, humans trying to understand the weakness of the aliens. This movie has none of that stuff.

This movie is about how a self centered person tries to save his children from an alien attack. The movie is excessively gross, has lots of drama, and has only a few scenes that actually contribute to the story of the movie.

If you want to watch the movie expect LOADS and LOADS of family drama. DO NOT expect cool sci fi stuff, or action, or logic.

YOU HAVE BEEN WARNED. ;-)

title: A poor dull invasion film
review: In preparation for his upcoming film bridge of spies I thought I would watch Steven Spielbergs war of the world's. The premise of this film sees a guy being put in charge of his kids when an alien invasion starts to happen. Now tom cruise is the lead in this film and he is definitely the best part of this film. You wanted to root for his character and you understood his motivations to protect his kids in this apocalyptic scenario. Dakota fanning played his daughter and I couldn't stand her in this movie, all she did was scream and it became incredibly annoying so I ended up not caring about her. Her brother was even worse, I hated this guy from the very start. He was just so irritating and just a dumb character that I really didn't care about. They run into this crazy guy and he was just a cartoon. The story was garbage, we have no idea why the aliens are invading, it gives no indication on their motivations. Also I didn't care about anybody in this film except for tom cruise which goes against the whole point of the film. The end sucked as well, it was as cliché as you like and it was really abrupt making me feel like 30 minutes of the film was missing. The script just didn't have much weight to it at all. Moat of the drama didn't work and there was no humour at all. The style looks so outdated now, the aliens for the most part looked really bad. There were a few scenes where it looked decent but for the most part it wasn't good. Overall this is a movie that you should skip of Spielbergs.

title: No Climax, Bad Acting from Cruise - Dakota only shinning spot.
review: Honestly, I'm not sure what people are raving about this movie for. It was simply a huge let down with no climax and horrific acting from Cruise. It had lots of unnecessary propaganda (Pro Church of Sciencetology AND Pro G.W. Bush references) that was so obviously - it became quickly a groaner at times. The special effect were good, but not enough to carry the film. As is typical with so many films today - it felt like the set up for a sequel. The movie itself can not stand on it's own. Though, Dakota Fanning did an incredible acting job. Far more sophisticated then her years. Almost like watching a young Drew Barrymore - but even better. It's a rental - maybe not even that.

title: Best Science Fiction Film
review:
War of the Worlds was the best science fiction film ever created. It beats Star Wars, Star Trek, Battlefield Earth, and all the rest. It was deathly scary, not in a jumpy way, but in a very creepy powerful desperate way.

A lot of people are complaining about Dakota Fannings acting, but she acted as any child of her age would act if the movie was in fact a reality, so I think she did great.

There are also complaints about how the ships weren't scary. First of all, super-intelligent species, such as these aliens were, do not build there ships to be scary, they build them to be a reliable and efficient machine, which they were. Secondly, they were picking people up from the ground, barreling through concrete, and turning people to ash. To me, that is pretty scary.

So, yes, to me, this movie was a stunning display of art direction, acting and story, and I was absolutely blown away by it! --Kandace C. Long

title: not as good as the 50's original
review:
Just got back from seeing the new WOTW and what a waste of time. Cruise is as bad as always but in addition to that you have to consider that there is no plot. Camera angles, camera angles. Can we just see a scene please with unclouded distortion? I don't want to observe things through a reflection, windows or car door mirrors, or water.

Plot holes abound. Continuity disjunctions. Scrambled explanations. Also, if the end of the world comes via invasion, if it were me I'd like to at least turn on the nearest TV in a house that has working electricity.

What a load of garbage. Consider that you pay for this movie, then have to sit through 15 minutes of commercials, then 15 minutes of previews. Eh, why does the movie industry need commercials money on top of my ticket price. Last time I'll be going to the cinema. Back to my 50" plasma TV at home and I won't be buying this stinker of a movie on DVD.

Gotta laugh at the guy with the working camcorder after the EMP! What brand was that?

title: sucked
review: this movie sucked. Spielberg has let me down. The score even sucked too, and that was by John Williams. Nothing unique in this movie, the aliens come, tom cruise cries, the aliens come, tom cruise yells, the aliens come, tom cruise holds his daughter. Real f#$@$%! entertaining. Don't waste your money on this piece of s%#@. See "Desperate Living", now thats a good movie. The plot was formulaic, there was hardly any character development. Just a bunch of cgi bull%@#$ that would entertain a three year old. The more cgi, the less intelligent dialog. Hollywood is going down baby, and I'm looking forward to its demise. Don't see this movie. People are starting to wise up to the fact that Hollywood only wants your money, they don't care about the quality of films. They drag you in with Tom Cruise and cgi, and expect you to be impressed by it.

title: This movie sucked
review: This movie was horrible. The first minutes of the movie were cool, when the first tripod comes up, but the rest of the movie sucked. It was just like Spielberg's other horrible movie A.I.. Both had awesome special effects, yet the movies themselves suck. This movie was so bad i don't know where to begin. The plot to this movie must have been thrown together in 5 minutes. The movie starts with the ever so talented Morgan Freeman narrating. He says that Earth is being watched by aliens that are envious of our planet and that is why they attack us. If they wanted the planet so bad why didn't they take it when they dug their machines here in the ground millions of years ago, before humans were around. And wouldn't they have noticed back then that the tiny organisms that live on Earth and killed them in the end of the movie, were harmful to them. And that's the other part of the movie that sucks. I'm sure ending a movie like this is hard to do, but did Spielberg really have to just give up. He ends it with the family reuniting and all the machines and aliens die. Then Morgan freeman's voice has to come back into the movie to explain what the hell is going on.That's how bad the ending is, we have to have someone tell us what's going on because the movie does a horrible job explaining things. And not only that, but it's a mega happy ending, because the son who ran into a wall of fire somehow lived and showed up at the ex-wife's house at the end. Not to mention that for some reason the part of Boston where the ex-wife lives, is totally untouched by the attack and her, her new husband, and her parents are completely unharmed without an ounce of dirt on them. The whole movie is ridiculously unbelievable. Tom Cruise explains to a mechanic how to fix a car after the lightning breaks everything electrical. Yet the spare part he said to use works, along with all the other electrical parts of the car. And somehow there is a path that they can easily ride through on the highway with hundreds of broken down cars on it. Then, the tripods blow up a neighborhood, shoot down a plane that lands right on the house that Tom Cruise and his family are in, and kill everybody. Yet the family comes out of the debris, hop into there untouched van, and ride down this path that is carved through all the crumbled houses, plane parts, and other vehicles, which of coarse are smashed. There was the one part that was believable, when half a dozen people fight off a tentacle that is pulling Tom Cruise away, even though a few seconds earlier an identical tentacle threw Tom Cruise and a car around like they were nothing. But I'm sure six people could fight a tentacle like that off. You suck Spielberg. I want my $9 and the two hours i spent watching this dump back.

title: flat out amazing
review: SUPERB IS A HUGE UNDERSTATEMENT saw this movie last night and i was left breathless i mean i have never felt this way about a movie before it was like i was actually in the movie i jumped every time something happened if you like to be scared and actually enjoy a good movie at the same time this is without a doubt the movie you should go to the acting is very good except for dakota fanning who i personally think is Oscar good in this film and steven spielberg has really done it this time i am a huge fan of e.t. but this is just something you have NEVER EVER seen before he really shows you the dark side of the aliens in a very realistic but yet entertainingly scary way i think the ending could of been better but all in all i think it deserves a 10 out of 10 and this is probably the most intense and exiting movie of the summer

title: Run, run, run for your life
review:
Yes. Run, run to see it. Are you a Spielberg fan? This is going to be your cup of tea. You are going to find all the elements of Spielberg. His famous dolly shots and main characters staring away from camera. Some funny moments in desperate situations. And of course the world of special effects.

If you saw the movie "Close Encounters of the Third Kind", you will find this movie has the same caliber of production. Perhaps scarier at times. May not be suitable for younger kids. It could be terrified how people die.

Anyhow, people has to die. It is an alien invasion. They are not here to chat.

There was no other director to bring you this movie. According to an interview Spielberg said, "because I still believe in intelligent life out there I made this movie". He was asked the same question about believing in intelligent life at the "Inside the studio" and he answered a strong "yes".

He's been fascinated by this subject for years. So, you are one of those escapist of the movie goer. Well, this is your movie. Get ready to be scared, yell and please don't damage the seats. You'll be holding the edge of it.

Enjoy the run. It will be wild.

Until next time.

Signing off.

title: Oh, my, god...
review: This is bound to be on many people's Top Ten lists. I went into the theater hoping that the human race would finally lose. As the movie progressed, I was praying that the family would live. It has been one hour since the movie ended and my stomach is still in knots from the suspense. This movie does an excellent job of showing how people react in a crisis. The acting is incredible by ever character, and it really pulls you into the movie. The true desperation of people is very accurately represented as well. As far as special effects, I had a hard time telling what was real, and what wasn't. A truly gripping movie. Well worth the admission price. If you don't like it, at least you can have an opinion if you have seen this masterpiece.

title: Great
review: I went to go and see this movie..it was Awesome!! It is one of those movies that keeps you on the edge of your seat!! I wanted to watch it over and over!! Cruis is awesome in this movie!! Along with Dakota Fanning!! They make a really good team!! I recommend this movie to anyone who enjoys a thriller or just if you want to go see a movie!! My kids loved it!! They didn't want to leave their seats!! Of course neither did I!! My husband doesn't ever want to go see movies but this time he LOVED it!! Hopefully you will love this movie as much as I did!! GO SEE THIS MOVIE!! Of course you might have a different opinion than me but we are all different!! Well I give this movie a 10!!!!!!! Thanks Ashlin

title: Scary, Intense, Thrilling!
review: Wow, Spielberg really let loose and did not hold back with this film. It really defines "thriller" whilst being a fun and visually appealing summer action movie. The "tripods" are really done justice from the book, and H.G. Wells would have been proud. Then there are homages to the 1953 film which fit in quite well. And after that are the modifications made to make the film original and modern. Everything--acting, directing, writing, CG, music--comes together perfectly. Forget the whole recent Tom Cruise deal, he pulls through in the role and makes you forget what's going on in the real world. As for Spielberg, this is probably one of his most frightening movies ever, arguably surpassing "Jaws." The guy is so brilliant it can't even be fully explained. Many will say that they were unimpressed with the CG because the movie was so rushed, but I am amazed at how great it was especially considering the timing. This movie is incredible, and a summer movie that is not to be missed.

title: A True Summer Film, this proves Spielberg still has his Magic, though Cruise was miss-cast in this role.
review: This is a Review of War of the Worlds, Released By Parmount and Dreamworks, Directed by Steven Spielberg and Stars Tom Cruise, Dakota Fanning, and Tim Robbins. Story: Lets start of by saying this is no piece of original work, not only is this your typical alien invasion that has been seen in movies like ID4 and mars attacks, but it is based on the H.G. Wells novel of the same title. It features a dead-beat dad named Ray(Cruise) watching his children for the weekend when the invasion begins. They are simply running from these aliens seeking refuge wherever they can. This story is hard to pull off and most people usually fail but Spielberg takes something like this and makes it work and it will redefine the genre again. The ending was a little odd and kind of took out of it but it was still well done. However this ending I do not understand may make much more sense to me in the long run. Special Effects: This is a summer alien invasion film so the special effects really have to be where it is at. The effects are really well done they took good care in constructing all the explosions and creating the aliens. There are some effects in this movie that just make you feel a little chill down your spine and thats what it should have definitely went for. They were well done. Acting: Almost everyone in the cast gives a top notch performance. The only real problem I had with the movie, which is what dropped the score, was Tom Cruise just being completlely miss-cast as Ray. Tom Cruise just cannot be a slob or a dead beat he's just too Tom Cruise for that role, they definitely could of cast someone better in it. Dakota Fanning again gives a great performance as the little girl and this time she is actually giving a real performance and does not look like she is possessed by total evil. The best performance was by Tim Robbins who just perfectly played the paranoid man looking for a way to survive and kill these creatures. With the exception of Cruise, the cast is terrific. Direction: Like the top says, Spielberg still proves he has magic left in his sack. The pacing was good, and the shocks and action just kept right on coming. It was a little short but nothing to get in a fuss over. It could have been way too long and it could of just got boring. Great Film, Great Effects, Great Acting, Cruise was miss-cast but I can cope. 8.5/10 The Best Alien Invasion movie to come out in recent years and is truly in the top 5 films of the summer or 2005 and just may be one of the best of the year.
