title: could have been a great movie...not even Tom Cruise's son, fueled with the power of his father's love for Katie Holmes, could have survived
review:
(Spoilers looming, you can read this, but heed the warnings when you get there)

War of the Worlds could have been a great movie. It should have been a great movie. It could have been a good movie. It should have been a good movie. It could have been an okay movie. It should have been an okay movie. It was a bad movie.

This said, let me introduce a few positives: Special effects were good, and great. Tom Cruise was solid. Casting was good. The acting was good. As a courtesy to the future of the world, Dakota Fanning should donate DNA samples to every family in America that wants to raise children. The world would be a better, cuter place.

Why is it a bad movie? It is bad because it fell completely apart about 2/3 of the way through, ending in a cheap cliché. Bad because Steven Spielberg lost sight that HG Wells wrote the novel 108 years ago, and I'm not even sure the end would have worked then, or in the 1953 version of the film. Bad for having special effects that were modern marvels, but a plot stuck in the dark ages. This is a shameful mess-o-Spielberg (and I am a fan).

What went wrong? Two words...Spielberg, Steven.

He seemed to get confused somewhere along the way. He should never have released this film, and instead pre-screened it to a bigger test audience, then called the actors back for a re-shoot of the last 1/3 of the movie, even if it meant delaying the release a year or two. He can afford it. War of the Worlds attempted to superimpose its 108 year storyline onto a modern world, and present it to a modern era of film goers. It failed.

Could it have worked? Yes. But the best special effects in the world can't make up for a weak plot. Modern audiences are monumentally more sophisticated when it comes to the movie going experience. They have the reasonable expectation that a plot should be dynamic, unfolding in an intelligible and logical way. This plot was stuck in 1898. The basic premise was sound...Aliens invade the earth, attack and eat the humans, they battle it out, and ultimately the humans win. That's an almost universal truth with the exception of Jerry Springer guests, whom I fear are aliens winning the battle of ignorance.

This plot was in desperate need of tweaking to meet modern needs. There were even a couple annoying sink holes in the beginning of the movie, but tolerable among the balance of action and special effects. And now, the spoilers...DON'T READ IF YOU WANT TO SEE THIS MOVIE (which despite my condemning review, might be worth your time just for the special effects, and for Dakota Fanning).

'da Spoilers...

Early on, the world is under attack and Tom Cruise is "borrowing" a car from the mechanic shop. All the other cars on the earth are not running, but this car is fixed within minutes after the attack. The mechanic (continuing to work while the world is under attack), is telling Cruise not to take the car because it will anger the owner, all the while people are running around in a panic being chased by giant tripods, tripoding around zapping people, yet this guy is totally oblivious and exclusively concerned about what the owner will think.... an extremely weak scene which should have been spotted and revamped.

From that poorly constructed scene War Of The Worlds becomes one long chase scene, Cruise and kids running from safe spot to safe spot, narrowly escaping a gruesome alien death all along the way. Then Cruise's son runs up to the top of a hill to watch a big battle between the army and aliens. The aliens win with a blast of atomic proportion. NOTHING, not even Tom Cruise's son, fueled by the power of his father's love for Katie Holmes, could have survived that blast.

Fast forward to the end of the movie, Tom drops his daughter off with her mother whose upscale brownstone neighborhood was miraculously spared, and out from nowhere comes the son, not even a limp - except for the one in plot.

Cruise and Fanning seek shelter underground with Tim Robbins. Something feels off in this scene. Soon after Cruise's character kills an alien tripod, and suddenly all the aliens are dying -- under attack from birds . Huh? Then it's over. Huh?

Then the screen fills with an image of the night sky, full of stars, and Morgan Freeman is heard narrating that the aliens were killed by microbial organisms. This leap to the end might have worked in 1898, and possibly 1953, but it doesn't work today. They needed to unfold that ending in the context of the movie. This, and letting the son die, would have made this movie a solid 7, and worth seeing.

Should you see it?

If you absolutely have to see some cool special effects, mostly in the first half of the movie, then you should see it because chances are they will not be as impressive on TV as they are on a big screen.

If you like seeing Dakota Fanning's toothless smile, you should see it, though her character in Man On Fire had far more depth.

If you like the idea of seeing Steven Spielberg make a flop, then see it.

If your name is Katie Holmes and your boyfriend is threatening to make you convert to a new a religion, then you should probably see it.

title: Disappointing
review: For a story with such great potential and coming from a great producer, the movie should have been better than it was. If you are a big fan of special effects, they were fantastic and it is one of those movies that is best seen on the big screen in a Cinema with an excellent sound system. If you like storyline and character strength though, you will be disappointed. I left the movie feeling non-plussed by the experience, it seemed as though all the efforts were made to have the biggest and best special effects with no time spent creating a suspenseful (or interesting) story and associated characters. There are numerous flaws during the movie, and the producers obvious use of 9/11 terror attack aftermath themes in some scenes is appalling really. Unfortunately my opinion is that the movie promises a lot but delivers very little.

title: Stupid, Stupid, Stupid...looks like rip off of Independence Day
review: So it had some cool moments, it had some neat effects, but it was a terrible movie all together. I normally love Dakota Fanning as a young actress in every film she is in, but she is annoying in this. All she does is scream for most of the movie and about half way through you wish Cruise would just open the car door at max speed and throw her out. His son sucks plain and simple. He trys to make the character seem like the everyday American who would fight for his country no matter what,, but the problem is, is that you wish he would just be killed off quickly. The movie itself looks like Independence day all over again. I know that WoTW was originally made back in the 50's and i am sure that it was cool back then..but in 2005 its a overdone topic. We have had too many movies about invasion in the last 10 years that just like other war movies are just getting outdated and stupid. The aliens look almost exactly like the ones from Independence day, almost like they ran out of money and said "well at least we have the others in a closet somewhere in the warehouse so we can just use them." Cruise has been better as well, he is on screen the entire movie and just cannot cut it in my opinion to be THAT prominent as a the ONLY attraction to the movie. Tom Hanks did it great in Cast Away, but Tom Cruise is NO Tom Hanks..and this is coming from a Cruise fan. Seriously Tom..STAY AWAY FROM SCI FI!!!

title: SF Classic Gets a Modern Treatment
review:
A great pop-corn munching movie, worth seeing for the special effects alone, but don't go looking for any deep meaningful insights into the human condition....

There are some wonderful special effects here, warfare (or extermination?) on a massive scale, great lumps of heaving technology, weird alien creatures, endlessly screaming children, buttock-clenching moments of sheer terror, and even some of those "didn't I see that in another movie?" kind of moments, and the film rocks along at such a cracking pace and you don't notice that that it is all empty, meaningless fluff.

The film sticks closely to the book -- even though it is set in the WRONG COUNTRY MR Spielberg -- though Well's pontifications on colonial imperialism gets dumped in favour of vaporizing bodies.

A lot of critics here seem to be hung up on the peanut butter sandwich sticking to the window when it shouldn't, but any fool can see that it is a reflection we are looking at...a reflection of Tom Cruise the self-centred father, who is in turn a reflection of OURSELVES as modern man with our modern self-centred way of life, who are about to be exterminated like "moggots" by and even more self-centred species, and er... so on. Not quite sure what you are getting at Mr Spielberg, but thanks for the entertainment.

title: I've got questions...
review: Why, in all of the northeastern united states, is the minivan, that Tom Cruise is driving the only vehicle (with the exception of the military convoy) that is operating on the highways? I thought it was absurd to see him picking his way around all those stalled vehicles. Are we supposed to believe that no one else around, or no one else can get any other cars started? Also, after the plane crash, as the three leave the area, I found it unbelievable that their mini-van; which was parked just outside the destroyed house and next to the crashed jumbo jet could still be driven, let alone still be in one piece. I can suspend reality long enough to enjoy a good science fiction movie, but when it's riddled with silly oversights, I lose all interest.

title: Waste of money, waste of their time
review:
Just a waste. Its disappointing. Cruise, Spielberg, $200 million+ budget - its fair to have some high expectations. Spielberg made the best movie he could with his material, but the undying question is, why did he choose this material? Its a dated, paper thin story by today's standards in terms of a FILM narrative. A great read, a great radio play, not a great film.

I think most viewers will walk away rather disappointed, and bored. Its essentially two hours of Tom Cruise carrying his daughter around, with some spiffy CG spliced in between. If thats enough for you, than enjoy. If you expect more from a film, a SPIELBERG film, avoid.

5/10

title: Aliens from Outer Space attempt to take over the world.
review:
This is quite an exciting big screen adventure film, and surprisingly, it has many of the same elements as its 1953 predecessor.

My recollection is that the aliens look much the same as the ones that were in the earlier film, and the exploration tube which they use to enter houses has a very similar lens design. But, this one, of course, has the Spielberg trademark regarding alien appearances. There has to be dark, stormy clouds. Their scout vehicles are different than the ones in the first film. In the first film they arrive on earth, if my memory is correct, in spaceships which create a crater from which the scout vehicles emerge. In this one, their method of arrival is quite different.

And Tom Cruise, whom I detested in the past before his last three films, continues to be a very good actor. He plays a father who is divorced, and does not know his two children very well, and seems to have not had an interest in the past in correcting that. As for Dakota Fanning... as always an incredible actress.

title: This will take your breath away...Almost!!
review:
At the Theaters eagerly waiting for this one to start because of all the talk around and the good reviews on mags about the movie. The first 20 minutes or so into the movie and I am just enveloped in the fast paced action on the screen in front of me. It didn't let go and it was starting to become a great roller-coaster ride where the speed was increasing by the minute, it at times left me gasping for breath and had me giggling with glee at the end of the scene.

This is a must see for people who go nuts over special effects and this movie really does deliver and won't stop till the final credits start rolling. The sound in the movie was exceptional it had me ducking for my dear life in some scenes. This is a must own movie if you are a sound maniac like me and own a home theater speaker system and love to crank up the volume while watching movies, this movie will definitely test your speakers and it will have you grinning like a loon because of the top notch sound.

The end will leave you feeling as if your roller-coaster ride was short lived and truly, it is. The movie loses it's legs at the end and just wants to get it over with but all in all it was a pretty good movie and a must have if you can live with the short lived glory and a flimsy ending.

title: An entertaining summer movie with many questions unanwered
review:
First off, this was a solid movie. I'm a fan of Spielberg, but a few of his current movies are below par. I did enjoy Minority Report which was really entertaining (ending could of been better). I really didn't want to see it because of Tom Cruise's behavior but whenever Spielberg is directing you will most likely be entertained.

There are a lot of questions that might go through your mind which I'm sure every critic is talking about right now. I agree of what my friends say: "You can use your imagination to intepret these answers for yourself". I guess that's OK but some of the questionable plot holes become annoying (especially for sci-fi fans and people that want explanations for everything).

The characters were likable. The acting was good. The special effects were very entertaining. Spielberg did a great job portraying the human emotion of this event.

I wish the ID4 team could of teamed with with Spilberg's team (with Spielberg directing) and could of made a great sci-fi alien takeover movie with a lot of believable emotion (which ID4 lacked).

This is a good movie to see in theatres with all the special effects. This is a definite guilty pleasure (7 stars).

title: The most likable feature of this film is
review:
that it's not left to the U.S. armed forces to save the world, for a change. Besides that, there is not much going for the plot.

All actors did their best to portray their characters believable but a script, which can only be described as utterly poor and full of flaws made all their effort void. Besides plenty of technical faults defying the laws of physics and logic, on a number of occasions the characters are made jump to the stupidest of ideas and actions without any reason given, leaving the viewers puzzled.

Other than title and trailer suggests, this is neither a war nor science fiction film but is better described as a road movie. Of course there are much better ones out there.

Like in most road movies the film ends as our "Hero" reaches his destination, and in this movie quiet abrupt. Rather suddenly all enemies are defeated and all is over in a flash.

The ending is definitively the worst part of the movie and will leave you unsatisfied.

title: Was excited, now appalled..
review: Originally, I heard that the movie was great. Was extremely excited to see it. I find that Tom Cruise has always done a great job of acting his roles and for the simple fact that he and Dakota were going to be playing in the same movie, I was ready. Beyond that, the trailers looked awesome, as though they had a lot of plot. Now, the movie itself, didn't have a single bit of plot. Almost the entire movie could have been considered long and drawn out. I give the movie a lot of credit for the acting. Tom and Dakota did an EXCELLENT job. Though, I did not like the acting of "Tom's Son." Thought he was a little 'corney'. To top it off, 3/4's of the way through the movie, I found myself very excited that finally something was going to happen, and found soon afterward, deciding that nothing was going to happen, at all, the rest of the movie... All in all, good acting, excellent graphics, awful plot.

title: Excellent...then great..then good..then, by the end....
review: ugh....all that plot build up to this... some hidden political garbage filler for a conclusion. the action was awesome.... Special effects very good...suspense GREAT...intensity of action.. pretty damn good mixed with suspense at a lot of times. the little girl could've been replaced w/ someone less psycho. there didn't need to be a narrator... I think that helped ruin it too...at least for me. for this... it only gets half of 10... because.. it did make me scared at points! It takes a lot for a movie to make me grab the arm chairs in the theater. the acting was fair, tom came off like kind of a moron in this movie...but it was cool to see him act like a regular joe... maybe he's a regular joe in real life too... well this movie was supposed to be real life? I also hated seeing the reality of how cruel everyone was to each other when they tried to steal his van.. but then again, he stole the van from his friend..then his friend got fried....so what comes around.... gets you! whoops - spoiler!

title: Oh, it's OK, I guess...
review:
Frankly, I think it's time Hollywood rethought the entire Summer Blockbuster formula. We're rapidly reaching a saturation point, where everything within this formula has been done, and all that's left is to make it louder, faster, and more obnoxious.

To be fair, War of the Worlds makes an effort to step outside the formula. Unlike the odious and terminally boring ID4 of evil memory, Spielberg attempts to infuse some of the humble-pie spirit of Wells' story into the confines of the big budget SB. For most of the movie, Cruise does the intelligent thing --- he runs away, since there is clearly no way (yet) to fight the invader. Towards the end, he's obliged to satisfy the audience with a few heroics before nature takes it course and brings the story to a close.

Yes, the tripods are cool, and so are the death rays, but Cruise's performance is awful. I don't particularly like Cruise anyway, but when he gives a good performance ("Eyes Wide Shut", "Rain Man") I can easily forget that it's him and get lost in the movie, which speaks very well for his acting ability. Unfortunately, there's little for him or anyone else to do much except act horrified, and how can you keep that up without getting monotonous.

One of the problems with this movie is that the premise has been done to death, and there aren't many places to go, particularly with Spielberg's spread-the-saccharine approach. I can see that he's trying to move outside that formula, but the result is a flat, curiously dull, routine film that has no real story to it.

I'm looking forward to fall, when some serious drama can be found on the screen as the Oscar campaigns gear up.

title: Questions I have about the movie
review:
Having read the HG Wells novel, I enjoyed the movie and the subtle references to the book and the novel and the double entedre to his previous movies IE the alien playing with bike( in the book the martians did not invent the wheel and the bike being so important to ET) but I believe Spielberg could have added some more touches to make the film more interesting and terrifying. Here are my observations and comments. If you have answers to my questions I'd love to hear them.

First, why didn't Spielberg go into the 747 plane crash. The movie seems to take up nearly three to four minutes of sound and effects resulting from the plane crashing, but all we see are flashes of light and terrible noises. The plane crashes but the next morning the plane was empty of people. From the sounds it seems like one of the alien machines got a hold of it. That would have been exciting and scary to see.

Second, when the fighting begins the Army is holding a hill against the Aliens, the Air Force is attacking and the helicopters are going in, but we can't hear what the commanding general is saying as he shouting on the phone and we hear a soldier screaming about refugees and the next thing we see the army is rushing in to engage the alien war machines. What did the general say? Was the Army at that moment simply buying time for the refugees to escape? Third, in the HG Wells Novel the red vegetation seems to be a stow away from the Martian machines. In the movie am I correct in assuming the red weed is a result of human blood being used as fertilizer? The character played by Tim Robbins sceams the aliens won't get his blood for fertilizer. And near the end, Cruise's character grabs a dying piece of the red weed and crushes it leaving a white powdery dust similar to the dust covering Cruise in the beginning of the movie when the Machine incinerates fleeing people.

What I found haunting was the rail road crossing scene. The crossing arms come down, the bells ring, and the crowd watches helplessly as a passenger train, probably fleeing NYC, rushes by completely engulfed in flames, automatically making its way northward with it dead passengers. The message, there is no escape.

Finally, I find it disappointing that so many of us hated the ending. Read the book, the Martians die not by our hand but by bacteria and viruses we have long since acquired an immunity to. To have it end with the military blowing up the tripods (as satisfying as that might be and believe I loved when the Boston soldiers blew up one of the tripods) would have turned the movie into Independence Day.

title: What...? Not great, but fun special FX. - 5 of 10
review:
Well, this one misses the mark slightly. Some implausible story turns cause some confusion on this one. I didn't understand why some things happened when they happened. Or why they happened at all. Character development should be more important to some film makers.

*****Possible Spoiler Alert*****

My main gripe, though, is that it's a premise of this film that they placed the Martian walking machines in the ground some while before the attack. With this in mind, I would think that there would have been a sampling of the Earth's microscopic life as that occurred. I just can't buy that they died from microbes in this scenario. The original did not propose this in my memory which makes the ending more plausible. Or did I miss something? This doesn't make much sense. Neither do a couple of other things, but I'll let them slide.

Passable acting, no deep dialogue, but then, it's an action film. The action is sometimes slow, but there are some pretty good FX. All this adds up to 5 of 10. Maybe a fat five, but no better.

title: Why I would and wouldn't go see this movie.
review:
Hmmmm Tom Cruise, negative! I am surprised by this choice. This alone almost caused me not to see the movie. Then I heard Tim Robbins was in it, OMG! Let me put it this way, any other director and I wouldn't have wasted my time.

The story is an old one. Nothing new, at least to me. I think this was the weakest part of the movie for me.

Now with that said, I will say it was a very scary movie. I put myself in the situation of being a dad with small children and what would I do in that situation.

Steven Spielberg did not disappoint me with the special effects or how the story was told. It was very well done, and I was able to buy into it. I don't think I've seen a movie this scary since "The Exorcist".

Bottom line? Tom Cruise - he did a good job, but I didn't like him in the role. Tim Robbins - Better than I expected, but I would have rather seen anyone else in the role. Movie - Stunning visual effects, good story telling, and scary.

Just as we have all come to expect, Steven has done a very good job. One has to wonder why Tom Cruise was chosen though. I think a normal middle age guy would have been a better choice.

Just in case you a movie mogul and you are trying to figure out why people are not going to the movies? PRICE you idiots! My wife and I went to see this movie for $15. I didn't take my children (3 of them) to see it because it would have cost TOO DAMN MUCH! I haven't seen 3 movies that I would like to have seen this summer because of the price of the ticket. I think I'm going to get a job as a critic just so I can see the movies for free. GEEZ!!!

title: Disappointing movie
review:
I am a big fan of Steven Spielberg since Empire of the Sun, but I find this movie is the huge disappointment. The plot is lame, and it contains several absurd and unnecessary scenes. Even The Independence Day seems way much better than this movie.

I don't understand why the smart aliens can missed out Ray and Rachel even though they already used the advanced tracking system ( the snake-alike machine ). The scene is really disturbing....the intellectual-harassment. But the most disappointing scene is the ending. It is very illogical and unacceptable. Robbie is alive. Even one of my friends who were with me was saying that she would give applause if Robbie is alive ( of course, in a cynical way ). And, she was dumbfounded when the screen showed that Robbie was very alive....very disappointing. Too many logical explanations were required to explain the fact that Robbie could survive. And to make it worse, the aliens were not smart enough to prevent themselves from the germs,contradicted with the explanation that they have been watching and observing the earth and the human beings. Very careless and illogical.

I am not saying that my standard is high, but if we are talking about Steven Spielberg, of course, we expect the best. Unfortunately, he fails with this one. We really hope his upcoming movie will be able to meet our expectation, or even exceed it ( cross my fingers ).

title: I love Spielberg, but I didn't love this.
review:
As per usual, the hype and teaser trailers took me to the cinema.

The film started fairly well and kept me watching, but as soon as those poorly designed machines appeared well I just knew something was going to disappoint. Once again Industrial Light & Magic have done overtime to create lots of unbelievable effects that ruin a film. If I wanted to watch an animation then I would go and see a cartoon for gods sake!!! Unfortunately the film adopts the cliché storyline of the father/son angst and does nothing to make it feel or look different. It constantly reminded me of the latest flop "Day after tomorrow". Cliché and worn out.

There are a LOT of scenes in the movie that get you starting a sentence in "But what about.....?" because they simply don't add up. An example, without giving away too much, is a crashed plane that has hurtled thru the sky at a vast rate of knots. After impact with the ground, the debris is all nicely contained in a former cul-de-sac and not spread over miles and miles. Convenient I suppose if you want to show it as an obvious plane wreckage.

If you also like cellar scenes then this is the one for you. There is one that goes on and on, creating the same type of suspense twice in a row. Once again it didn't add up.

The behaviour of the son, well I just didn't get that at all.

What did I like though? Cruise and Fanning - always great to watch perform.

The way humans were zapped - different.

The river scene - spookyly eary.

Summary. I was sat there in the cinema waiting for the film to finish. I hate this feeling, especially if I am watching a Spielberg movie, and I would struggle to recommend this film.

Will I buy the DVD: NO - Huge pity, but I would never want to watch it again.

title: Nothing Like The Book.
review:
Well just got back from seeing it and..

What the hell!!!!! Sorry but gotta say great special effects, but why oh why do these directors take a story that works great as an original story then totally change it and make film of it.

When you talk about war of the worlds everyone knows about the green flare from mars, what do we get in the film, oh they have been underground for millions of years.yeah.er.OK.

And what was the lightening thing about !!!!!

Oh they came down with the lightening, that must have been shocking for them, but just how did they get into the atmosphere?

And the Martiansthis is from the book.

"A big greyish rounded bulk, the size, perhaps, of a bear, was rising slowly and painfully out of the cylinder. As it bulged up and caught the light, it glistened like wet leather. Two large dark-coloured eyes were regarding me steadfastly. The mass that framed them, the head of the thing, was rounded, and had, one might say, a face. There was a mouth under the eyes, the lipless brim of which quivered and panted, and dropped saliva. The whole creature heaved and pulsated convulsively. A lank tentacular appendage gripped the edge of the cylinder, another swayed in the air."

What do we geta bloody prop from Independence Day arrrrrrgggggggg.

Great film if was an original story but as it stands sorry, big disappointment, this is the second film this year that has let me down the other was the hitch hikers guide to the galaxy, again nothing like the book.

title: Fun movie to watch, but weak storyline
review: The movie started out great, with the first alien coming out of the ground and killing everything that moved. Also, the special fx in this film were unbelievable and made this movie very entertaining. It was when i got home afterwards and i started thinking about the movie when i found a lot of mistakes and or problems i had with the movie. First ,in the very beginning after the lighting storm an emp zaps the entire city destroying everything electronic including things that run on battery however when the alien comes out of the ground one man pulls out a digital camcorder after another lady takes a picture with a disposable camera with a flash. This movie also left me very confused in the end, they hardly explained why the alien machines collapsed except that it had something to do with single celled organisms. This movie would have been much better if they explained the alien race we were fighting a bit more. Showing chilling digitally made images of a much further advanced alien society inhabiting a horribly polluted planet marching around in lines would have been very appropriate. With Morgan Friedman's voice explaining what we were seeing. Everyone in the theater and the characters on the screen (except Morgan, he knows everything) were left clueless and confused by the end of the movie.

title: Oh....God.....Help
review:
Okay....This movie is Okay if you never seen the original version before....

But having said that, there is nothing special about the story. I always though Spielberg might alter the story to make it much more interesting....unfortunately but he did not. This is one of Spielberg's worst films and definitely does not carry his trademark greatness.

There is nothing too great to see, since Spielberg just repeated the same story from the old version...But I guess the special effects saved the film. Cruz is a great actor and you can clearly see that on the screen but other actors and their roles have some annoying characteristics. Example will be: the daughter and the son...if you see the film, you would have realized that they play the characters who act before they think...not very wise when going against super intelligent world invaders.......

Anyway, if you had to put it in perspective...Watch Batman Begins...that is a far better film then this one. It outweighs this film by 3 to 1.

title: Mr. Spielberg, I'm disappointed...
review: I went to see this movie yesterday, despite all critics I've seen on the net said this had been a bad one. I've asked myself, could it be so bad? The name Spielberg was a trademark for me. His films not always meant to have Oscar, but one could bet that the film will be enjoyable. This film has streams which I think can not be mixed in one mature plot. We have a story of a family drama (Ray versus his kids, many film has the same "don't care" divorced father against the children story), also one with a nature like disaster (maybe like Dante's peak?). Then we have the intruders from the Mars (a bit Matrix like tripod machines, with Alien like crew). We had also some scenes with Tim Robbins, who had the only interesting character, he was disturbed a little by the invasion (I think, I've also seen something like that before... :) I have to say, at the middle of the film, I waited Yoda to enter with his laser sword... It is not just the plots. Despite them, this film could be average, but for me, it was boring! Maybe I saw too many movies before (hmmm... :). I hardly could guess every next moment in the film. About the Tom Cruise. He had his average shape. But in this movie, It was useless. Till now, Spielberg film did not disappointed me. It always had good actors, good story, nice pics. But for now, I'm disappointed

title: Excellent sounds and special effects
review:
I just came home from movies... still feeling a little shocked and excited. I wasn't expecting too much. Maybe something like Independence day, Armageddon, all those total annihilation movies where humankind is about to be destroyed. Mostly I was concerned about Tom Cruise. I really expected this one to be Cruise's macho stuff with lots of American flags around and small NASA shuttles carried by running children in India, maybe even The President himself taking down the big alien in the end.

Thank you Mr.Spielberg for not making this one one of them annoying America-saves-the-planet movies. Instead, you created an exciting movie with lots of action and intense atmosphere. And maybe set the new movie body count record of all time.

I was really positively surprised. The film started right away and the suspense lasts really to the very end. The sounds and visual effects are awesome. Hopefully you'll have good sound system in your theater because this one has really well mixed sounds. Loud and low but without any painful hi-pitched ear-piercing sounds. You can feel those quakes and weird alien tuba sounds in your stomach. Tom Cruise acts well in this one, didn't annoy me at all. In fact quite the opposite.

I gave the high points for the sounds and visual effects, the two reasons why I went to see it in the first place. So for me this time it was money well spent.

title: Absolutely stunning
review:
Not for a while have I seen such a brilliant film. Not only are the visuals perfect the acting is this time top notch. A Spielberg/Cruise pairing is usually a good indication that the film is going to be really good. Minority Report was also fantastic.

The premise of the story is that Alien beings have for many years been plotting the total extermination of the human race and one day it happens. It starts off with a simple lightning storm, and what follows is some of the most intense action scenes that I've seen in a 12A/PG-13 rated film. This really is not a film for children though, some of the sequences are quite frankly going to be scary, but for a more mature audience it is a stunning film. The casting is spot on. Tom cruise plays Ray Ferrier, our main hero of the picture and father to Robbie (Justin Chatwin) and Rachel (Dakota Fanning). Fanning inparticular is exceptionally good in this, she is one of the best child actors around at the moment. But Cruise and Chatwin also deliver a fine performance as a slightly estranged father and son. A surprise addition to the cast was Tim Robbins who played a not quite all there man trying to come to terms with what is happening around him. As for the visuals they are brilliant. The combination of CG and live action is seamless and the look of the alien vehicles (tripods) are creepy and otherworldly, I was most impressed by them. The fact that the movie only starting shooting 7 months ago does not show in the slightest, the effects are up to standard and beyond

In summary it is a fantastic film, definitely worth a view, but I wouldn't recommend taking your kids with you if they are under 10.

title: Oh my god! This movie was incredible. Just incredible.
review:
I haven't been on the edge of my seat like that in a movie theatre for YEARS. Most the audience just sort of sat, dumbfounded, after the credits finished rolling.

Movie FLOORED me! Saw it at Mann Chinese in Hollywood. What an awesome experience. Spielberg is an expert craftsman, at the top of his game.

STUNNING performances by all talent. Cruise just keeps getting BETTER AND BETTER! Fanning is extraordinary, expect her to get an Oscar nomination, at least, for her performance.

I had NO IDEA this movie would grab me and hold me like this. Just no idea. Went to sleep with images from it BURNED in my mind; WOKE UP with images still catching my attention.

A MUST-SEE. Tell and take all your friends to the theatre to see it. They will thank you for it.

title: Straight to the point "review"
review: I thoroughly enjoyed War of the Worlds, though I know the critics and IMDb junkies will have it torn apart by the end of opening weekend. Spielberg did amazing things with this flick and I was impressed. The casting was great - Dakota Fanning is the most unbelievable little girl. She is amazingly talented. When she screamed, I could feel her terror - when she cried, I just wanted to reach out to her on the screen. She is SO convincing and the movie would be lacking so much without her. Tom is great as Ray, but not because of the reason that I expected. It's because he's just a blue-collar guy trying to protect his kids. There is absolutely nothing extraordinary about his character and I think that's why it worked so well. I wanted to smack Tim Robbins so bad and I think that was the point - he was a great choice for the role. Morgan Freeman as narrator was a nice touch. Yes, there are plot holes (big ones) but the movie is quite entertaining. This was the first movie in a long time that I just sat back and let the special effects fly. I'm really not a big fan of Spielberg in general (ordinarily I just don't care) but the effects in this movie were awesome. The machines look strikingly similar to the old, old comic, so they're a bit cheesy but the stuff going on around them makes up for it ten-fold. There's a scene where Ray is looking for Rachel and comes up over this little hill and the landscape as far as you can see is red from the "extermination" and it is eerily beautiful. It's the Spielberg touch. Go see it - it kicked "arse!"

title: Worst Movie Spielberg has ever made, i want my money back...
review: Wow, the worst movie i've seen in years...How does Steven Spielberg expect people to walk away from this movie happy? so how and why did the aliens begin attacking? how does tom cruise single handedly destroy all the aliens with a single grenade? why in the Heck does Tom Cruise make a big deal about the ground being cold where the lightning struck 26 times... I don't know, nor does anyone else who saw this movie... Spielberg does not answer any of these questions, he simply says at the end that the friggin aliens were killed by micro organisms of bacteria? WTF mate?! How does someone who created masterpieces like ET, Close Encounters, Back to the Future, Band of Brothers, and tons of other incredible movies and TV shows go about making this steaming pile... if there is one thing i can say about this movie is don't waste your time... go rent the old version or read the book, i want 2.5 hours of my life back and $20 for my tickets back.

title: Worth the money!
review:
Possible spoilers ahead Feels good when you go to the movies and you come out feeling like you got your money's worth. I enjoyed this movie and like others pointed out, really liked the cinematography and styling that Spielberg used for the effects / action scenes. I vaguely remembered the original 50's version and recall some similarities but this movie seemed quite different too. While I recall the 50's flick aliens ships had shields too, they were flying saucers with sparklers for the main gun rather than the tripods in this movie. Also I don't remember them abducting anyone and were bent solely on destruction. Never read the book, so I don't know which is a closer adaptation. Obviously the reason for their destruction remains the same, which is why it surprised me that other posters said that it ends abruptly, which is how I remembered the original one ending too. So I was not surprised at all by this, little confused as to why others were though.

I have to say the entry sound the Tripods made was pretty damn scary, and is an important part of the fear factor for this movie, that being said, see it in a movie theater with good sound, otherwise this important and scary aspect is lost. I thought the acting was good and both cruise and his daughter put on good performances and made it believable. The son kind of bugged me, but not to the point of affecting my opinion of the movie itself.

While I vaguely remembered the basement scene in the original movie where they chopped off the head of the robot camera and studied it, I didn't remember Tim Robins character and him needing to be killed as it happened in this movie. It was the only scene that kind of bugged me a little bit, well that and why that guys video camera worked. Speaking of which I couldn't tell what part that guy had fixed on the car to make it run again, but I'm guessing that only the transportation lightning affected the power of things and not the actual robots roasting everyone.

I guess the one other concept that bugged me was the theory that the robots were always there and the aliens simply beamed down there and then broke through the surface to start attacking everyone. It raises some interesting questions like why didn't we ever discover any of these tripods before the aliens beamed down in them? And if they had been down there for thousands of years and all, why didn't the aliens take over the planet back then? Why bury thousands of robot machines all over the world only to take it over hundreds of years later? Doesn't make sense to me unless I just missed something.

On a larger scale, I didn't make sense to me why you would have these walking Tripods reeking havoc all over when you could more effectively and efficiently kill off people with some sort of harmful ray gun like in Independence Day or some sort of biological weapon or something. Granted the movie was much more entertaining and action packed the way it was done. I guess while watching it it just occurred to me that these things are grounded with there 3 long legs, don't appear to move that fast (meaning you could out drive / out run them) and were killing people individually with the lighting guns that tuned people into popcorn dust. It would take quite a long time to exterminate city's that way. Kind of like trying to kill every bug in the house by spraying each one when you could bug bomb the whole place. I do realize that the book was written back in the 30's and all, but still just doesn't seem very realistic I guess.

Anyways getting little off topic. I did think the movie kept you glued to your seat throughout and kept me entertained the whole time

title: As Flat as the Original
review: Steven Spielberg himself, some several months ago, in reference to how good this his new movie is stated that "it has some really scary moments" and that was about all. That left one curious about whether he himself thinks the movie any good. Having now seen this movie it is indeed that, it does have intense moment, and yet like the original decades ago it leaves you fundamentally unsatisfied as it is somewhat shallow. You would think that the most powerful director on earth and leading man could muster up more talent and ability in making this movie better than it is. CGI aside, Surely 50 years should be enough time to make this thing better than it was last time it appeared on the big screen.

title: Too Much Cruise not enough Martians
review:
My favorite Sci-fi movie as a kid was "War of the Worlds" by George Pal. I have seen that movie at least 25 times so I was curious how this one would be. I liked the effects in this movie. The Martian war machines were great! They looked scary, menacing and most importantly, REAL. However we did not see them enough and Cruise to much.

This version is a little ridiculous. First of all how the Martians came to earth. This was changed from the Pal film in 1953. In that version they came in cylinders and fell like meteors that left craters and then climbed out of the hole. In this version they came to earth centuries ago to bury their machines when we were not here, leave, then return centuries later. They arrive in beams of lighting and activate their machines to capture the earth and destroy us. why didn't they stay when no one was here the first time? Second, no mention of using nuclear weapons against the Martians like in the 1953 film.

There were flaws like the video camera working when the first tripod comes out and when what looks like the biggest plane ever built crashes near Ray's ex-wife's house and they survive the explosion just by closing a door. That's Hollywood using it's dramatic license for you.

The effects were great but as a story, I still like the 1953 film better.

title: Not as good as the 50's version!!!
review:
I have to say I went into this movie with huge expectations after reading heaps of stuff about it but came out somewhat disappointed after all.

What I wasn't disappointed in was the incredible talent of Dakota Fanning, that young girl never fails to thrill me with her acting range and I think that as she matures she is going to be amazing.

One thing that did surprise me was that I came out of the movie having found, in Tom Cruise, a new level of maturity i think. To see him play a father figure, one hell bent on looking after his kids, gave me a new insight into his acting abilities. I was very very surprised as I usually find that Tom Cruise plays Tom Cruise, but not in this movie. I really believed he was a dad trying to protect his kids at all costs.

As for the movie in general, well i heard Steven Spielberg say it wasn't a remake, but, i have seen the 50's version and apart from moving this movie to another place, another time frame, well, to me it is a remake. Plain and simple... nothing different in the basic plot... a remake!

The 50's version was awesome for the 50's, this was standard for this time so it wasn't anything fancy in my book. It would have rated a lot lower had it not been for the amazing acting of Tom and Dakota... as for the kid who played his son, well, i guess we can't get all the good actors can we???

title: Completely Pointless
review: Yeah you heard me! Completely pointless movie! A Tom Cruise commercial. News flash, Tom Cruise is not that great. As always the child actor, Dakota, stole the show. Indeed, was this film a father daughter/son story? No. A disaster movie? I guess. Was there a plot? No. Just massive destruction. Suspense? Not really. Maybe the film was suspenseful for a 1950s' audience but not for today's. Not that we have become incredibly sophisticated, the movie just wasn't very scary. I gave it one star for the special effects. That is all the movie deserves. I want my time and money back! Well actually, it was what I expected going in: a disaster flick with some heart. But unfortunately the movie didn't connect on any level.

title: Finally They Got H.G. Wells's Vision Right For Once.
review:
"But who shall dwell in these worlds if they be inhabited?...Are we or they Lords of the world?...And how are all things made for man?"

I have always been a big fan of the author H.G. Wells since my youth. I always enjoyed his works like 'Time Machine', 'Food of the Gods', 'The First Men on the Moon', 'In The Days of the Comet',and so on. I love Wells's vision and his books are always short and easy reading. When I heard Hollywood wanted to do yet another version of 'War of the Worlds' I groaned. Surprisingly this turned out to be the definitive version of the book. Much better than the original George Pal movie (which I liked), and far better than the subsequent TV versions.

Most everything Wells envisioned is here. The tripod aliens, the deadly vapor heat rays, the horrifying red vines, so many of the situations are similar to the book. Of course the book was happening in England a hundred years ago and there were no children, just the man and his wife.

It is also interesting to note that the action and Fx of different disasters are so much more believable and real than the cornball action in something like '2012'. The optical composite shots may have been more advanced in '2012', but the action was ludicrous. Nothing in '2012' was remotely believable. I'm not saying the alien effects here were realistic, of course not. But the scenes of buildings crumbling and streets cracking were way more real. The FX in '2012' may have been more advanced, but nothing was staged with any attention to actual reality. In Spielberg's film they are very convincing.

Tom Cruise is also excellent. The character of the father is a average, blue collar, working class joe. Cruise brings this off convincingly. It is also a little ironic to note that his performance here as an average guy has more emotion, personality and depth, than Cruise the actor seems to have in his real life. It's almost like a person who isn't very real playing someone who is real. Strange huh? The children are also convincing too. They seem like real kids, difficult and hard to manage.

Usually I like more realistic sci-fi like '2001' or science fact like the excellent 'Apollo 13'. But H.G. Wells's story was a fantasy and Spielberg does justice to it, mean and nasty aliens and all.

I'm not even all that into Spielberg sci-fi either. I thought 'ET' and 'Close Encounters' were so corny and simplistic. I liked his film 'AI' though.

This was a great adaptation. now let's hope we can finally get a good adaptation of 'Food of the Gods' and 'Empire of the Ants'. Maybe Spielberg should try his hand at those. He did so well with this project. A real first rate sci-fi classic.

title: Spielberg and Cruise, a winning formula
review:
Steven Spielberg can do no wrong by me. Even with the few films made by him that I felt weren't his best, I still enjoyed the experience. He never talks down to his audience and the craft is always top notch.

Here, he helms a high energy action movie about a man, who has his teenage son and young daughter for the weekend, when alien war machines arise out of the ground and intend to wipe everyone out.

WAR OF THE WORLDS gave us a great big story, written by screenwriters Josh Friedman and David Koepp (based on the novel by H.G. Wells) and many things could have gone wrong, but in the hands of Spielberg, it all worked.

Tom Cruise, in the lead role, is always intriguing to watch. I feel his fine acting talent and skills are overshadowed by his superstar status. He carries this huge action movie very confidently.

The cinematography by Janusz Kaminski is breathtaking. And, as usual, the score by John Williams is wonderful.

title: What a film!!!
review:
PLOT SPOILER (as if you didn't already know how it ends) I watched this film at the cinema, now on DVD. It is excellent. From all reviews I've read, viewer fall into 1 of 2 categories, they love it or hate it. I love it. and heres why * The main character is a real person, someone you can relate to without being special forces or some hot shot pilot (independance day). * Any parent will empathise with the main character as he strives to keep his daughter from harm. * The end (which seem to attract the most criticism) is the most plausible ending there could be. Disease has killed more, far more than any war or weapon. So isn't it quite reasonable, alien invaders would be so intolerant.

Only one negative point. The original book which was first released in 1898, written by HG Wells and was based in England. It would of been good if the film reflected that. However, its made with American money and they make much better films than we Brits do.

title: Why???
review: i have been reading messages left on other boards and it seems people are having difficulties understanding parts of the alien technology. i think the idea of the aliens is that they are FAR more intellectual than mankind, we shouldn't know how they got there, how it all works. why don't we ask the question how did those storms appear? how did the aliens get to earth without detection by our numerous satellites? they just did! the idea of the story is to show the extermination of a species and the reality of the anarchy. one thing i didn't quite get was that Spielberg was trying to show how humanity stands together to fight off a common enemy (i think he said pretty much that in an interview) but he also showed how evil and brutal mankind can be in that situation (the gun/car scene). overall this movie is a masterpiece, i mean all you could do if everyone around you was being slaughtered and the only thing you could do is run and be lucky enough not to be terminated as well. so harsh, so true. it scared me, and if this movie didn't touch you in some way, you're an idiot

title: Two words... ABSOLUTELY INCREDIBLE
review: This movie was incredible. I definitely got scared. It's the little things that get to you. Things like lightning without thunder and trees moving without wind... spooky. I really liked. Spielberg used amazing special effects. The aliens are completely believable. I have never seen graphics like this in my life. The reason this movie is a 9 instead of a 10 is that Rachel (the little girl) screams entirely too much. Half the movie I felt like telling her, "If you just stop yelling, the aliens won't see you." Anyway, Tom Cruise did an excellent job in this roll. He captured the film. The thing that outdid all the rest, though, was the music. Without the score, this movie wouldn't have been half as creepy. The silences are actually what brought the horror out. I don't recommend taking anyone under 10 to this movie.

title: Fathful to the original while being original
review: The last time I sat on the edge of my seat for an entire movie was Poltergist, another Spielberg creation. And, while War of the Worlds is based on H.G. Wells' story, it is definitely a Spielberg creation. Mr. Wells' plot is evident, as is the basic story line. Mr. Spielberg has changed it enough to be fresh. He has also, as is typical, gotten the best out of the actors. I have read the original book and have seen the 1953 movie with Gene Barry (see if you recognize his cameo in this new version) and enjoyed both. Yes, the story 'peters out' at the end. But, that's the way Mr. Wells intended it. Yes, it is full of explosions and frights. Again, the way the Mr. Wells designed his story. If you are looking for another victorious war movie ala Independence Day, then you'll be disappointed. Just rent Independence Day at your local video store and pop some popcorn in the microwave. If you are looking for a fresh, faithful depiction of War of the Worlds, this is an excellent choice. Go see it before it leaves the big screen.

title: An edge of your seat, roller coaster of a movie!
review:
I just came back from seeing a late show of War of the Worlds. What a movie! This film takes what we loved about the "B" sci-fi's of the 50's and brings the genre into the 21st century in a suspenseful and gripping way.

This film does not pretend to have any "big message". It's simply the story of an incredibly powerful alien invasion as seen through the eyes of one family. It's a story of survival. It's a story of how you might expect humans to react under such intense pressures. And the film is visually stunning.

If you're considering seeing this movie, you should. I recommend you ignore the negative reviews. I suspect many of those so called "reviews" were written by people with an agenda. To those IMDb members who gave this film a vote of "1", I find it sad that you would attempt to denigrate a film of such quality and put it into a category that is shared by films like "Manos' the Hands of Fate". Your vote only demonstrates that you truly are not really criticizing the film, but instead are trying to make a statement of your possible dislike for Tom Cruise or Steven Spielberg. Having said that, if all of the "1" votes were removed, this film would probably be at an 8.0 or greater. And that would be more representative of it's true overall rating.

And to those IMDb members who complained about the little girl's screaming, what other kind of reaction should she have had? And to those members who complained that there didn't seem to be sufficient character development or that characters were not as "likeable" as they would have liked them to be, they don't need to be.

On a side note, I think Tom Cruise has publicly acted like a jerk as of late. But it's important to keep things in their proper perspective. He's just an actor. And if he didn't get his big "break" years ago, he'd be someone that you might see coming up to your table in a restaurant and announcing, "hi, I'm Tom and I'll be your server tonight". But simply because I think Tom has gone completely off the deep end in his personal life doesn't mean that I can't look at this film objectively.

This simply, is a roller coaster of a film. If you're up a for a good ride, take your seat and make sure that your fastened in! 10/10

title: Spielberg shows why he is the master!!!!
review:
When I see a Steven Spielberg film I look to how much I will like the film , not if I will. An average Spielberg film is better than most directors good films. In the last couple of years though, there hasn't been a film from him that has really stayed with me since Saving Private Ryan. A.I. was under-appreciated, but Steven hasn't wowed us in a while. War of the Worlds is Steven at his best, he takes what is a B movie and makes it into memorable and at times scary story. The premise is as we all know is that the earth is attacked by aliens bent on destroying the human race. From HG Wells story, he takes the story and modernizes it. Tom Cruise does a good job as an average Joe that protects his kids from the horrors around them. The good thing is that Cruise is not suddenly made into Rambo, he is a pretty lousy father that comes to realize that his kids need him. I will say that the set up of the characters is alittle too fast, the film goes into thriller mode a little quickly. When it does though, it never lets up, Spielberg is a master at creating tension. The tension comes from the human aspect, the desperation of the people fleeing from a certain death there is panic and paranoia.

There is no doubt thatr this film will be compared to Independence Day. I enjoyed that film, it was a big loud stupid blockbuster that was fun to watch. This film, even though it is a thriller, focuses on Tom Cruise trying to survive with his kids, the other film was more about the spectacular visuals. This film has them, Spielber creates some haunting images, but the most tension comes from the desperation that comes from the characters. Tim Robbins has a great cameo as a paranoid survivor.

The one big complaint about the film is the ending, the film comes to an end very abruptly, the resolution feels rushed and tacked on. It is faithful to the HG Wells story, but the ending could have been more drawn out. The film is too good to have such a weak conclusion.

Is this movie as good a Close Encounters? No, that film did have a more rounded script, it fleshed out the main character much more than it does here. This film is a thriller in every sense.

Grade: B+

title: War Of The Worlds - Blew me away!!
review:
I remember reading the original novel by H.G Wells when I was at school, and although it was set in Victorian Surrey, rather than America, the film still allowed the audience to be drawn into the lives of the characters... without ruining the content and in turn portraying it in a modern way which more could relate to.

I particularly like the way the audience is starved from information like an explanation into why this is happening. In films like this in the past there is always a scientific outlook a look into the aliens... for example in 'Independence Day' there were them scenes where they were at Area 51 researching the Aliens, and attempting to contact them. But no not in this film... it is all out war... and not romanticised in any way at all... even the Tripods look menacing not the cutesy U.F.O's but towering indestructible machines bigger than anything we have. I think it works very well and I truefully disagree with simondix's comment it is well directed, and at times truly magical. I noticed a few amazing perspectives shown in filming, for instance in the scene where the Ferrier's are escaping from the Tripod attack in the people carrier, the shot looked to the side and all the destruction behind them before merging back to the expression of pure fear from Ray (Tom Cruise). The lighting brought a lot to the film also, along with the musical score which all seemed to blend seamlessly. I would watch this film again, because I believe I would notice something different each time I viewed it.

Tom Cruise's performance was quite fantastic, and I can't honestly say I rate him that highly as an actor but credit where credits due... although Dakota Fannings performance was by far the best in the film.

I found myself truly emotional in many instances... it really was amazing seeing something as powerful as American refugees walking the streets in their millions with boards looking for loved ones, and the army powerless to defeat such a power that the Tropods possessed. I found my mouth wide open at occasions by the sheer effects and destruction... wow!! I know everyone will have different views of this film, and they are entitled to them... but take a look further than the script, and look at the overall film, score, screenplay and setting, then say its rubbish... I doubt you will

title: I don't see what the complaints are about
review:
I was a little skeptical about going to see War of the Worlds. I had read some pretty disheartening reviews for the film, many of which were from IMDb users, so War of the Worlds seemed kinda "ify." After watching it though, I thought it was pretty good and I just don't think the complaints with the film are justified (aside from the fact that everyone is entitled to their own opinion and just like any other movie some people are gonna hate this movie). Like everyone else I thought the special effects were great--didn't look cheesy at all. Unlike some other people, though, I thought the story was good and--in light of the situation--realistic. There's not much character development except for those initial insights that we get at the beginning of the film between the members of the main character's family. I think this is appropriate though. The world is being attacked by aliens; there's no time for Tom Cruise to look at his son and say "Hey, I'm sorry I wasn't there, I'm a bad father, blah, blah." His main concern was getting the hell away from all the killing and finding somewhere safe. For me, the lack of character development really emphasized the sense of urgency that dominates most of the film. The machines were popping up everywhere, I for one would have thought it to be ludicrous if the father would have sat down with his kids and asked them how can they make their relationship better.

And so what if the end was kinda sappy--okay, really sappy. After all the dying (it's a really dark movie) I welcomed the happy, sappy ending.

The film did have other flaws, but they're easily overlooked. It's not a documentary, it's a fun film that you can sit down and watch and see stuff getting blown up and say, "Dang, that was kinda cool."

title: Frightfully realistic
review: As an avid H.G. Wells reader for years I suggest those who want to watch this new version of "War of the worlds" read the novel first. By doing so you will gain insight on the machines and their functions and will not be dumbfounded when watching the movie. H.G. Wells was quite the genius and ahead of his time as were other classic writers of the past. As a writer myself I thought the movie was extremely frightful. Remember, its just Hollywood and anything can happen whether logical or not, it need only be entertaining. In my opinion, this version is truly an epic, and Spielbergs best and finest piece of work yet. Ironic as it sounds I must say, this movie was so scary to me I would not want to view it again.

title: Movie was SOOO GOOD!!
review: This movie was so awesome!!! It had so really really good special effects, all in all the movie was just Fanominal!! I love it!!! Steven Spielberg Made a truly awesome movie when he made this movie... Tom Cruise was the perfect man to play the part he did in the movie! In the movie he plays a man who is really not a good father but all though the movie he has to protect his children from the alien invasion... and all through the movie he is bonding with his children in a weird kind of way... in the movie his son hates him and doesn't call him dad (He calls him by his real name) but at the end he keeps them alive and him and his son are closer then ever! the movie was just truly awesome... I would go and see it again a THOUSAND times over!!!

title: not Spielberg's best but still delivers
review:
Let's get a couple of things straight.

I wouldn't say "War of the Worlds" is Spielberg's best movie, but there were lots of things I liked about it.

1) It is NOT just another "Hollywood disaster epic".

2) The humans don't come up with a way to vanquish the aliens at the last second.

3) The special effects (though EXCELLENT) are not allowed to overwhelm the story of one family, which is what it's really about.

4) BECAUSE its about one family, and Spielberg allows us to get to know them, we actually CARE about what happens to them, unlike the characters in "The Day After Tomorrow", who were distinctly underdeveloped for the sake of the action.

5) Spielberg's use of pacing; he knows just when to let the viewer breathe, and when to ramp the tension up again; movies like "Charlie's Angels II" leave me feeling numb because there is no letting up on the action and eventually you get to the point where you can't respond any more.

6) Creative use of shots and attention to detail; Spieberg can tell us so much in a short amount of screen time. The beginning sequence, of the drop of water on the leaf, turning into our earth, turning into Mars, which turned into the red traffic light, for one; beautifully done. His use of mirrors, and framing shots through broken window panes. Also his use of the birds; as soon as Rachel sees the birds flying away in a panic in the boat scene, we KNOW the boat won't be making another trip without a word being said!

7) No famous landmarks getting demolished.

8) Dakota Fanning's acting.

Granted, the ending felt rushed; it is however faithful to the ending of the book, if less developed.

I trusted Spieberg to make this movie far more than another "Independence Day" or "The Day After Tomorrow". As far as I'm concerned, he delivered, even if he didn't do so perfectly.

title: Good movie - not something that Spielburg will be remembered for though
review:
It was a really good watch, but lacked a kind of end an beginning feel, plus the dialogue was catchy but not too prominent. The action was absolutely incredible, with literally the best special effects I think I've ever seen.

Tom Cruise + Dakota Fanning were superb and the stereotypical teenage son Justin Chatwin was pretty impressive.

I think what the negative posters have seemed to forget is that this film is based on a book by H. G. Wells. The number of times I've heard comments about how the plot is cheap/not very good is really disappointing because everybody should know the plot by now.

Definitely see this movie, but if you are to get it as a DVD, it's the kind of movie that deserves to be rented, not bought.

title: Superb Movie but not a good ending
review: Everything till the end was great about the movie. It was very fun to watch. However, for the ending, they either weren't thinking or they figured the movie was going on too long and thought of ending it fast. Now, in the beginning of the movie the machines that came underneath the ground had shields that rendered them immune to our attacks and all throughout that point we've been fighting a lost war. But at the end, they showed the birds flying around these machines and making the pilots blind. My question is how could the birds fly so close to these machines when their shields can literally fry them. Secondly, I saw a rocket able to penetrate their shields while they were flying blind at the end of the movie. How could their shields possibly go down? This didn't made sense and the whole ending wasn't making sense either. But overall if you enjoy thriller and suspense and Sci-Fi fictions then this is the movie for you.

title: Steven still has it
review: Even though I have read the H.G.Wells book when I was a kid and still vaguely remember the storyline, even though I have read many reviews that all say this movie is quite suspenseful, the movie still kept me on the edge of my seat for the entire 2 hours. The special effects, the sound effects were astounding. And it has some good acting too, Tom Cruise did a decent job and Tim Robin was superb as always. The seamless flow screams Speilburg. One surprise after another and with some quite moments just to build up more tension, and surprise you again even when you were expecting a surprise. You may feel you have seen many of the scenes in Jurassic Park, Minority Reports, Saving Private Ryan or even in Jaws, but they are so beautifully woven together it left no room for complain. The plot may be sketchy, it is just enough to deliver a very good movie, and it was amazingly loyal to the novel. With a lot of willful suspension of doubts, it even made several good points. Many people does not like the ending, the original novel ends like that and, let's face it, a sci-fi flick with entire humanity senseless slaughtered just won't fly.

title: War of the Words!!
review:
This movie rocks!

First, I want to say a little something to the very astute commentary of the deep thinkers who chose to compare WotW 2005 with WotW 1953. WotW 1953 was directed by Bryon Haskins, not George Pal, with a most excellent screen play by Barre Lyndon. The opening narration by Sir Cedric Hardwick out does Morgan Freeman, although Morgan Freeman's voice isn't bad. Its just that Sir Cedric Hardwick's voice is truly mellifluous, cultured, and beckons in eloquent tone to the era in which War of the Worlds was written.

Whoever started the false information that George Pal directed War of the Worlds 1953 is just full of it! Nice try poser, but try to keep the facts straight, OK? Although I do like some of the commentary regarding hero worship and the lack of such in the current rendition of WotW, spreading false information kills your credibility.

Many critics point out that the video cam guy is able to video his approaching death while the electromagnetic pulse has taken out supposedly all electronic devices. Yes, it seems like a huge flub...but the moral here is that when 200 foot tall alien tripods are wrecking everything in sight, forget about trying to get something on America's Funniest Home Videos, "put the video cam down and RUN!!"

Regarding Tom Cruise's level of acting and all the collateral damage that surrounds his life. Yep, I totally agree. A more sympathetic actor that doesn't have so much controversy in his off-screen life would have been welcomed. Instead of going with a pretty face in the "hero" role, I would have liked the father figure to have been cast with someone like Paul Giamatti. I know Giamatti is a character actor but that guy CAN act!!! Giamatti would have knocked the character of the feckless, disrespected, loser father out of the park. Transforming someone like Giamatti into the unlikely hero to me, seems like a task more worthy of the talents of a director of Spielberg's reputation.

Regarding the observation that with all the carnage going on, someone in Ray Ferrier's family needed to die. OK, I can go along with that, but I don't think it should be Robbie. I think Spielberg keeps Robbie alive for a reason. I believe that if Spielberg comes back with a sequel Robbie will play a pivotal role in the next segment! Here are the clues: Robbie's obsession to see what was going on might not have been an obsession to join the war and fry. Robbie is a slacker who despises his father, and if not careful will turn out to be just like his father. Seeing the alien war machines might be the catalyst that gets Robbie to apply himself and become an authority on the alien vehicles. Robbie becomes the unlikely hero in the next segment that his father Ray became in this one, but on a much larger scale. I'm thinking Robbie becomes the future Dr. Forrester character(i.e. Gene Barry's role in the 1953 original movie).

Regarding why the machines were buried and abandoned by the aliens. Millions of years ago, the earth was mesozoic...with molten pools of lava, very hot atmosphere, very dense vegetation and populated with dinosaurs. Its possible that the alien's mission was to excavate minerals and ores, and the tripods gigantic size would be necessary to wade through pools of lava, and wrangle a T-Rex or two. They probably got a lot more mileage out of milking dinosaur blood too. The aliens probably abandoned earth when the event that killed off the dinosaurs occurred. The machines became buried over millions of years. The earth's crust is very deep, indeed. Unless you're specifically looking for 200 foot tall alien war machines buried thousands of feet deep inside the earth's crust you probably won't find'em.

Regarding the way people act in the face of the unknown, when the tsunami hit Indonesia earlier this year, many people on the beaches had no idea what was happening when the ocean receded so far from the shore. The indigenous peoples saw this as an opportunity to go out and pick up the stranded fish, not knowing that they were only mere moments away from being killed! Also, if you're convinced its the end of the world, it is only natural to want to spend your final moments with your loved ones. For Ray to risk everything to get his children into the arms of their mother is probably the most poignant motivation in the film. Imagine just having a gun held to your head, your car stolen, and your chances of surviving this catastrophe have just gone from zero to negative ten! You're sitting in a café crying your eyes out because you realize you can't protect your children from the aliens or the human beings for that matter, but your own children do nothing to console you because you've been a total mess of a father for most of their lives? This is why Spielberg is the master of what he does, he knows how to bring the nuance of human behavior and emotion to the screen, in all of its delicate beauty, or violent brutality, but in every case Spielberg manages to keeps it totally real.

Finally, the movie does have a Hollywood ending, but hardly a happy ending. If you're Ray Ferrier, you've already lost everything you ever should have cared about when you were an absentee father. With the invasion over, and your kids are back safely in the care of their mom, you've got nothing to go home to. Heck you don't even have a home to go home to. This is probably another reason why the ending manages to really grate on some people. You never know how much something means to you until it's gone.

title: Only Spielberg would end it like that!!
review: As Spielberg matures, and certainly he has earned the right to be considered one of the great commercial film directors in American film history, he has become unafraid to go dark (Minority Report, Shindler's List) In the case of War of the Worlds, very dark indeed. The film is riveting and relentless. I will disagree with a previous poster to say that tension is created very quickly and then sustained to nearly the end (and I'll get to that in a minute)and all the classic effects you come to expect for SS are there. It's a white-knuckle ride with sudden frights, impossible escapes, things getting blown to bits and really nasty aliens. Spielberg does for evil aliens what M. Night Shyamalan's "Signs" only hoped to do. It's all over-the-top and true to H.G.Wells. Any complaints, direct them to the author (who is only mostly dead); except for the ending. Against all odds, a character that had clearly been incinerated comes back for the sappiest, most disappointing ending of all time. Another poster justified the ending as actually "sad" in the sense that Tom Cruise's character is left alone after a global holocaust while his loved ones are reunited apart from him. Baloney. He'd lost almost everything and where War of the Worlds could have ended on a hard, but upbeat note, it ended on a test-marketed commercial ending that is truly a painful contrast to an otherwise brilliant thriller. Maybe American audiences just can't handle an ending that isn't neatly sewn up with a smiley face and a lovely red ribbon tied to it. But than again, what's the #1 summer box office success for 2005? War of the Worlds. Spielberg knows his audience.
