Forget Cruise's antics, forget him and Katie Holmes and go enjoy two hours of great thrills and chills. And have fun!!! Happy 4th.

title: A Thrill Ride!
review: This film is a roller coaster ride! Great action scenes, sound effects that knocked my socks off! I have to say the way the film unfolded from a peaceful planet, to the main characters (Tom Cruise, Dakota Fanning etc.)relationship then very slowly the terror unfolds from these invaders from space. Tim Robbins character was brilliant as he appears towards the middle of the film. At first he appears as a calm and collected guy wanting to hack those aliens heads off to a crazy guy. We were hoping it was a longer film with more laser shootings from the invaders but other than that I give it two thumbs up! Great suspense and a thrill ride.

title: War of the Worlds represents the classic 1950s alien movies with a great story of a family trying to be a family
review: As soon as War of the Worlds ended I made a comment to my friends about what this movie represented; It is the greatest classic 1950s Sci-Fi movie ever made. If you were to go back to the 1950s and make an alien invasion movie with better acting and believable special effects, you'd get this War of the Worlds. The first 30 minutes give you a great run-for-your-life sequence which pulls you into the film. The rest fits nicely into the world facing total destruction without going overboard with SE (ahem, ID4). People tend to forget that this film was based on a book. The adaptation is amazing. I would say that WotW is the best summer movie so far and the best alien movie to date. The actors give great performances that make you feel emotions. Would I recommend this movie? Yes and no. If you like Sci-Fi/aliens/action then YES. But if you don't like aliens (such as my sister-in-law) I would tell you to stay away. You wont like it. Too many people flock to the theaters every weekend only because its a "summer blockbuster" and a "must see film", not because of personal preferences for a film. I also noticed that a lot of people on here do not like the end of the film. Remember people that the story of this film is not about an alien invasion! It is a about a father trying to be a dad for his kids and to get his family back together. The movie ended perfectly seeing how the family was reunited! Use your imagination for the final destruction of the aliens. Why do people need everything pointed out to them in a film. The plot holes people talk about? They aren't plot holes because if you use your imagination you can figure stuff out. So if you want to see a great sci-fi movie like classic 1950s cinema, War of the Worlds is your pick. The people who claim that theaters booed are full of crap. It was the nerds trying to act cool. Go see this film if you love these kinds of movies.

title: Just See it....
review:
Ray has divorced from his wife Marry. Ray has custody of their kids for the weekend; Robbie and Racheal. He's not much of a father, caring more about himself. When a strange storm starts to shoot lighting to the one spot and all electrical appliances shut off, Rays off too see what has happened. The lighting has created a hole into the ground, unearthing what was hidden beneath; an alien tripod. When the tripod starts to destroy everything in its path, people realise the aliens are here not in peace. Now has to protect himself and his kids from the impending doom of the alien invaders.

I have read a lot of what other people have been saying about this movies and most of the time its about what Tom Cruise is doing in his personal life. I don't really care what he does with his life, he can act as much of a dick as he wants, it doesn't discredit his as a good actor.

One thing I've noticed about Spielberg is that he either hits the bulls eye dead centre, or he'll miss completely; here he hits the mark perfectly. This has been so far been the best movie i have seen so far this year. At first i thought it would be like most other alien invader movies but this is so much more. This movie is like a world war II movie. It was an interesting twist to see a refugee situation from an American perspective. The action is so intense, though its not always constant. The action only come every now and then; as the story is focused more upon the family, but the action sequences are really intense that it doesn't need a lot of it. There is also a grainy look to this, giving it a hyper-real feeling, making it a lot more realistic.

With the use of all these and other references, this movie is dark and very intense. there were times i wanted to look away but couldn't as i couldn't miss a moment. The special effects were mind blowing. Unlike Star Wars where it was mostly special effects and you knew it wasn't real, here the special effects were so integrated, you thought the tripod ships were real. Though what i thought was better was the sound engineering. The sounds effects were flawless and the cinema was shaking from them.

The acting was very good. Tom Cruise earn't my respect again, though Dakoda Fanning was just brilliant. She is one of the best actresses around. Spielberg's directing is just great; like it always is. Though what made this one of his greatest movies is he didn't take the sentimental cop-out at the end, which he has done with most of his movies.

Many people have been complaining about the ending of the movie, though when you think about it, there are more layers to it than what they say, it is very ironic.

In all just see this movie.

title: loved it - old time radio style
review: Man, i thought that i had seen all the great movies this year - i think this one takes the cake - it was really neat how he kept the realistic approach to all the characters - this is no trashy Will Smith film were he saves the day with a load of crappy one liners - this movie made me feel as if i were there in the middle. another reason i loved it - it felt a little Goonies or Indian Jonesish - meaning the adventure never stopped, once everything started / thats when the crap just keeps hitting the fan - and then your on a trill ride to the very last scene! great job - this is a movie for movie lovers - not action star seagull movie!! go see it - seriously it rocks!!!

title: I saved our family from extermination, "you're welcome"
review: 99% of this movie is well worth the time I spent at work getting the money I used to buy the ticket but then we get to see Cruise go through all that, which is quite a bit, inside and out... doing anything and everything to make sure his kids are kept alive, even kills? a man to see that through, in the end gets tossed a 30 yard slant "thank you", as though he was delivering mail...neither sleet nor snow nor extermination...at the least he could have gotten a "thank you for saving our child, by the way, how are you doing?" or "I'm glad you made it also" or even "Boy, I bet you're glad you didn't get vaporized"...actually moved me to say "boo" out loud, embarrassing my nephew and having me apologize to the other movie goers near me. The peanut butter sandwich scene said a bit, he had to step out of his safety zone to care for others and summarily get the finger. The ex-wife and her folks at the end looked like "was there some sort of human extermination thing going on outside of this neighborhood of intact brownstones and upper-middle class comfort. The working class neighborhoods and rural communities had no chance baby. ha ha ha. Spielbergo strikes again.

title: Just enjoy the show
review: Unlike the droves of would-be movie critics out there, I went to the theater to ENJOY myself watching a remake of a science fiction movie I saw as a child. I didn't go with an ax to grind for an actor, nor to look for holes in the plot. Personally, I'm tired of technical gimmickry taking over the starring role in many of today's movies, I prefer characters to do it. And that's what I got. Raw human emotions, the suspense as they try to flee, the terror in the eyes of a child, the narrow escapes from danger all drew me in. Cruise and Dakota give very good performances, with Robbins adding a believable fringe factor. The special effects rock, but aren't the centerpiece. If you go watch this movie and don't find any enjoyment then you can only blame yourself for wasting your $9.00.

title: A film of two halves!!!
review:
War of the Worlds starts out great - it's exciting, intriguing, things are happening and happening fast - but then as soon as Tim Robbins enters the movie everything just becomes stale. It begins to turn into another type of movie entirely and a far less exciting one at that. Something good the second half did contain (as well as the first) was an outstanding performance from the young Dakota Fanning. The movies special effect, it must be said, are pretty special but another thing which lets it down is the confusion of the storyline. The end might as well have been in French it was that confusing.

My recommendation - watch the movie until Tim Robbins comes into then leave and check out what happened later on an IMDb message board.

title: Not as good as I had hoped
review:
I'm a big Spielberg fan and when I heard he was doing WOTW, I thought there could be no one better to attempt it. I saw it last night and have to say, I'm torn. It wasn't what I had hoped. We see all the tanks and Bradleys firing at, what, obviously the alien walkers, and to build up to it we see the son begging, "I have to see this." Through that entire sequence I was thinking, this is gonna be cool. We're gonna see the alien walkers in a valley surrounded by tanks, and helos and jets will come soaring in. These feeble weapons will quickly be wiped out, but it could have been one of the coolest shots in the world. But we never see it. I felt cheated.

I will admit the visual effects were good and I was startled a few times. The sound effects were insanely cool, especially the initial "call". It sounded like someone stuffed my head in a tuba and blew as hard as they could. Some of the performances were strong, but where was the story? This film could have been a lot better. I've seen the older version, but have never read the book. I'm going to assume the older version is a whole lot closer to the book.

Overall, I was mildly entertained.

title: Mixed Emotions
review: If you were expecting to see Indipendence Day do not see this movie. There is a difference between seeing what we want and seeing what really happens. This is the case with War of the Worlds. Everything worked for me yet I don't understand why I have mixed emotions about this movie. I suppose it was to real for me. Everyone that hated the movie complained about the ending. They wanted the Humans to find a way to defeat the Aliens or the Aliens to exterminate us completely. For me the ending is the only logical explanation. We wouldn't stand a chance against the Aliens without killing ourselves. Mother nature is the only thing that will stop them. They do not have immunities built up like we do. Over the years man has built up immunities that have allowed him to breath, drink and eat safely. It's like sending someone who is highly allergic to humidity to the Yucatan!

title: Flawed brilliance.
review:
I wasn't sure quite what to expect when I walked into this one. On the one hand I knew that Spielberg would pay due homage to the H.G. Wells classic, and that the movie would be undoubtedly visually stimulating. However, I was nervous that Spielberg would pull...well... a Spielberg on us and douse the movie in schmultz. I suppose, thinking back to the movie, he did. Oh well.

Visually, this movie really was stunning. In one scene we find our protagonist (by appearances a world-weary Tom Cruise) running for the first time from the invaders, and the visuals present here blew my mind as people were, almost literally, blown away. The level of detail present in the CGI is truly fantastic, and it not being "obvious" CGI did wonders to suspend my disbelief. There is some very 'Saving Private Ryan' style camera work implemented throughout the movie, furthering the realism of each scene. At times, Spielberg must have used just a camera in his hand. This technique really brings viewers into the movie as a part of the fleeing people.

Unfortunately, all is not perfect. The movie becomes a little laboured when Cruise and his daughter are hiding in a basement with the (increasingly tiresome) Tim Robbins. The audience I watched the movie with chuckled as he skulks into view. This segment proceeds far too slowly, and the "mirror part" was plain silly. The allusion to 'Jurassic Park' is obvious here.

I also question Spielberg's ending. Though by no means completely unsatisfying, it was skimmed over rather quickly. I'm very much a fan of the invaders being destroyed not by humans, but by what we fight every day: bacteria, but the Spielberg ending didn't have the finesse of execution I was hoping for. It's as if it didn't really matter that the aliens failed in their attempt to annihilate humans. It was as if the narrator was really saying "humans were being slaughtered. It was devastating to us. But then the bacteria got the aliens and they died. The end." Slightly anticlimactic, non? When you add this to the grandparents standing by their door in Boston, looking like horrifically stereotypically smiley-faced American grandparents, the gag bag just has to come out.

So, in conclusion we have a superbly visualised movie, bogged down by an unnecessarily long middle segment and a rushed and vomit-tastic conclusion.

Oh, but see it.

title: Decent adaptation of an excellent book
review:
Having read the original HG Wells book recently, I was impressed with the way the movie remained faithful to the novel while telling it from a modern person's perspective. Sadly, it seems to me that the authors of many of the negative reviews on this site have obviously not read the book, which was written in 1898 and was groundbreaking for its time.

The aliens' ultimate demise to earthly bacteria has been criticised by many as a weak ending, but I believe it is the modern audiences that are lacking in perspective. Given that humans have had little understanding of the spread of disease until the last few centuries, I find it quite plausible that an alien civilisation which has developed in an environment free of communicable diseases, would be caught completely unawares by this threat. Furthermore, the aliens have been observing Earth from a distance, so it is unlikely that they would have a deep understanding of human biology.

It should also be noted that Wells' book, when written, was partly a social commentary on the state of the British Empire at the time, which had inadvertently caused the decimation of many Aboriginal peoples in their colonies throughout Australia and the Pacific islands through introduced diseases.

Having said this, I do have criticisms of my own to level at the movie. Some glaring mistakes, such as the one involving the camcorder, have been noted by many reviewers already. I was puzzled as to why the movie went to the trouble of introducing two close friends of Tom Cruise's character at the ferry, only to have them die immediately.

My main gripe is with the brief scene where we see the aliens themselves. Gone are the carefully conceived Martians of the novel, who were weak creatures, completely unsuited to conditions on Earth, unable to move around without the aid of the machines they controlled. Instead, we are treated to a surprisingly nimble race of stereotypical aliens, running and jumping around on a world with 3 times the gravity of their own. I am constantly disappointed with the usual kind of humanoid aliens in sci-fi films, so it is particularly disappointing to see this movie deliberately reject the above-average effort seen in the novel.

In summary, I was mostly impressed with the film. I feel that the movie would be appreciated more by people who have read the novel, so for those who didn't enjoy it, try reading the novel and see if your opinion of the movie changes.

title: Special Effects and Acting fill in the Holes
review:
War of the Worlds (2005) takes a classic science fiction drama and does what most remakes do, add a preponderance of special effects and explosions in an attempt to bring in the audiences. In this case, it proves effective. Perhaps the most positive aspect of this movie are the ultra-realistic and more importantly, believable, special effects. Add to these effects an all-star cast including Tom Cruise showing that he has come into his own as an actor, making anyone seem foolish to be a naysayer on his abilities anymore. Furthermore, I half wonder if Tim Robbins didn't submit himself to shock therapy to come across in a manner quite creepy to me. Finally, Dakota Fanning shows that she, much like Haley Joel Osment, can pull off a singular performance that at times holds the center of attention, despite being somewhat one-dimensional. It is on these features alone that I would recommend this movie, despite the many flaws that many will find so annoying that they, like me, will walk out before the final credits roll.

Let's start with the numerous holes in the science of the film. Now, a science fiction film must deliver some sense of suspension of disbelief for the audience to buy into the experience. Science can be thrown on its heels left and right, but some semblance of order must remain. Too much disorder occurs when science is twisted more for dramatic effect than believability. For example, an electromagnetic storm knocks out all of the electrical devices, including those that are not running at the time. However, replacing a part fixes the problem. A part that was damaged if it was sitting in a vehicle shut off at the time of the storm, but not if it was sitting on a shelf. Then, a man who spends his nights loading crates at the dock is more knowledgeable than the local mechanic who comes off as a country bumpkin. Apparently mechanics are too stupid to even notice a massive explosion occurring behind them. We then find that Tom was the only one within driving distance smart enough to fix a vehicle, and that driving distance seems to go on forever without filling a gas tank, although perhaps they managed to reach an area with power in time for this. But when they reach an area with power, they are the only ones around. If the area has power and has not yet been attacked, it should be swarming with refugees, but not this neighborhood. The issues continue until the end, when the space craft no longer has a shield. Why would the aliens getting sick affect their shields. Let's give a benefit of a doubt and say that they were somewhat biological, but then we have to wonder how such a biological device survived buried under us for so long. Explain to me why anything would bury their ships on a planet, and then come back. First off, why not just terraform the planet to begin with. Why wait for civilization to build up on a planet just so you can come back later and risk your own life with equipment that would be severely outdated by your standards. Maybe they like the challenge like some intergalactic genocidic, sadistic hunter, but then why terraform it the second visit. One science flaw that many have mentioned is that right after all of the electrical devices go out in an area, for some reason, digital cameras and camcorders still work. Television crews can even get slow motion footage of lightning strikes during the storms that knocked all other power out. I almost had to leave at that point. Spielberg obviously put the whole scene in just as a jab at the media.

One flaw that really stuck out was when Robbins calls to Tom and Dakota to hide in the cellar. A small editing flaw then occurs since he enters the cellar, but when the angle changes, he is at the door shutting it, but those are to be expected in any movie. The problem is that hundreds of people are running in every direction, but for some reason, Robbins chooses to only call to this one family, and then shut the door before anyone else could be saved to join his cause. Hellooooo. Next, we have the ironic plot point that wasn't even made point of. Right after Tom takes Robbins out, they are discovered anyway, making his murderous attempt at saving his family all for naught. You'd think he would have had a hard time dealing with that, but it never hits him apparently. But then, right after taking the camera out, it takes a good two minutes for the tripod to show up. Apparently they weren't concerned much about it. Then we have Tom, being the only person in the world smart enough to throw some grenades in the machine after being captured, even though other soldiers were captured along side of him. Then everyone falls 50 feet in a metal cage onto pointed branches and walks away.

Lastly, the MOST ANNOYING ENDING IN HISTORY. Apparently, while the rest of the world is in turmoil, Tom's ex-wife and her family are dining in luxury and safe. Not only that, but his son miraculously survives massive explosions that took out a military division, and then finds his way to his mothers, apparently not much sooner than Tom, since he hadn't changed his clothes, which must have smelled to high heaven by then.

Heres the worst part of all of this. Despite all of these flaws, I liked the movie, simply because of the background, but I didn't like it enough to get the DVD when it comes out.

title: not as good as the original, but still a good summer popcorn movie...
review:
Just saw it tonight. My 8 1/2 year old movie buff son went with me... we gave up our seats for the D-Backs getting pounded by the Giants for this, so this was better of the two choices. He's been waiting quite a while for this one - a huge Star Wars, Jurassic Park and classic film fan who has wanted to make movies since 2 1/2 years old. He liked it, but still preferred the original, as did I. It was still very good entertainment, though... I gave it 7/10 on IMDb - the original got a 9 from me as I rated it for its time, previous to CGI effects. This wasn't one of Spielberg's best, but it wasn't one of his worst, either. The original got more scientifically involved as to the origin and biological makeup of the alien invaders and had more narration. The original was somewhat campy (mostly due to the 50s film era), but this one was a little, also - with far too many narrow escapes for Tom and family for my taste. This version was more of a casual observer's (Tom Cruise's character, Ray) POV vs. the 1953 version from a scientist's (Gene Barry's character, Dr. Forrester) POV. This also lacked romance which the original touched on somewhat... there was good sexual tension between the two charismatic leads, Barry and Robinson. Also, there was much more deference to the Almighty in the original - this one barely touched on His intervention in mankind, other than the narration at the end. I guess He isn't needed to be called upon in the 21st century in times of peril such as HUMAN EXTERMINATION.

This version had too many plot holes that were so blatantly obvious - such as why Tom's vehicle was the only civilian vehicle (a mid-90s Dodge minivan) running/moving due to a change of just one part (solenoid - what happened to the computer that it also runs on?); how they drove over so much debris/vehicle wreckage and never got one flat tire, how they managed to make it through clogged interstates with just enough clearance space to get through at high speeds; the radio coming on just for a "test of the emergency broadcast system" and then going back to static; but the biggest whopper was at the beginning of the film with the now-infamous "camcorder" shot. OMG, that was so stupid! How in God's name when all electronics were zapped by an EMP could one camcorder function perfectly and record the invasion for no one other then the movie theater audience to see. Awful - Spielberg's biggest guffaw ever. They could not discover that in the editing room or during screenings? Pointless, unnecessary effect - really hurt film's credibility. Even my 8 year old boy whispered that was dumb. The scenes with Tim Robbins were a cutting room floor decoration - a complete waste. I won't even begin to address the end scene as to how ridiculously Hollywood that was. The narration helped cover the sugar somewhat.

This film COULD have and SHOULD have been a great classic - it had all the ingredients - instead it was a modest attempt at an updated remake consisting of a roller-coaster ride of awesome CGI effects with little or no character development or impact on the classic story itself. The SL did leave an opening for a sequel, however - should these aliens ever get another whim, but be more ready when they do. Without the great effects, this film would have been just average sci-fi/action fare. It's worth the nine bucks to see the effects on the big screen, but do not expect another Jurassic Park, albeit there were many similarities with kids in danger, screaming in panic, narrow escapes, etc.

7/10 stars - mostly for the effects, photography, music and nail-biting suspense - just forget all the story holes and outright goofs Ted in Gilbert, AZ

title: Worth Watching
review:
Spectacular images throughout the film. There were scenes that were brilliantly done and held you on the end of your seat the entire time. Spielberg has an incredible way of showing you exactly what you want to see exactly when you want to see it. I imagine seeing this in theaters must have been close to seeing the T-Rex first appear in Jurrasic Park - huge, deadly, and the characters are at its mercy (not to mention breakthrough special effects). It is worth it to see it in theaters simply to get the full effect of the imagery.

That being said, this is no Oscar film. The plot was essentially watching people run away and trying to survive. The most character development was Tom Cruise learning to care for his children (and honestly, no surprise there). The best acting goes to Dakota Fanning, whom I adore, but even that wasn't a great performance.

Basically, see it because Spielberg puts on a great show. As long as you don't go in expecting your entire life to be changed by its insight, you won't be disappointed.

title: Good Movie Good VE(Visual Effects)
review:
Well Let me start by saying that Tom Cruise's Car at the beginning is hot. Now on to a different subject, I thought the movie was good. It has one mood, Intense. Now if your the kind of person who liked Jurassic Park. Go see this it has the same kind of Intensity. Now this movie is no happy alien story like E.T. This movie is about alien's who have come to annihilate all of mankind. This was not as good as the original but it was more modern, and Steven Spielberg's kind of thing. 8/10

title: Great until the end
review: I went into this movie with great anticipation and was not let down throughout all but the final three minutes of the movie. Yes there were a couple of plot holes, but overall it was incredible. The score was excellent, Cruise was very good, Dakota Fanning has a big career ahead of her if she keeps acting like this. But above all this Spielberg was in his element. He kept it tense, fast-paced, enough character development to keep it interesting, but not so much as to bore us. He never bothered to question man's existence or anything like that. He was just taking us on a no expense spared thrill ride. I had no idea what would happen next for most of the movie. This had some of the most fantastic camera work, unbelievable effects. All in all i was having a heck of a time. Then they killed the final Alien and walked up that Boston street to find....... the mother and the son both alive. Not only that but they happened to be looking out into the street right as Cruise comes walking up it. After doing about as good a job as a director of a disaster picture can do in avoiding clichés, Spielberg unloaded a giant dumpster of them on the audience in the final minutes. If it had been just Cruise and Fanning, Cruise would have had to become the father he had already started to change into, Fanning would grow to trust him and they would rebuild their life as civilization rebuilds. THat would have been a far superior ending and I would have given this at least a 9 out of 10 without hesitation. But the complete breakdown of holding off Hollywood, even though it only occurred in the final seconds was very disappointing. In any case its still worth seeing, especially on a big screen.

review:

Just nature can destroy them.

review:
I just saw this movie and thought it was awesome. It's the third movie this year that has been awesome. The other two are Star Wars Revenge of the Sith and Batman Begins. The movie has some of the best special effects ever and was just an entertaining movie.

review:

title: Well worth seeing.
review:
Spielberg's skills -- both in special effects and scene creating suspense -- are admirably on display. But these skills would have been of little use without the superb performance by Tom Cruise. As is often the case (most notably as in Rain Man), Cruise's performance is likely to be overlooked or minimized. He holds the movie together and keeps it moving, while he is very effectively supported by Dakota Fanning.

Many reviews state that the first 100 minutes are superb but are diminished by a weak ending. Basically, that's true, but don't blame Spielberg. It's the inherent weakness of the underlying Wells' story, not the director's shortcomings.

The movie exceeded my expectations and was summer time well spent.

title: Better than I expected
review:
My expectations weren't very high when I went to see this film. I was expecting a typical "special effects extravaganza" that has been hyped up too much and nothing more. The fact that it's based on a famous book (which I haven't read) didn't improve my expectations at all, but, after seeing the film, I have to admit that I was wrong.

First of all, the special effects were extremely impressive. Everything had been made really well, from collapsing buildings to the aliens and the tripods. The sound effects were also very nice and completed the symphony of destruction. I couldn't help but grasp my seat during the scene where the freeway collapses and trucks start to fall from the sky. The only thing that started to annoy me towards the end was the sound of the tripods' "horns".

The music complemented everything. John Williams did, as always, a magnificent job. One other thing I liked about the music is that they didn't use it at all in some scenes. In my opinion, it felt really dramatic when the tripods started to kill people and all you could hear were their screams and the sound of the lasers.

And then we get to the acting, which probably divides opinions. Personally I liked most of the characters in the movie. Ray (Cruise) was a harsh man and it was interesting to see him fall into apathy and despair at times. Some of the cruel choices he had to make made me think how I would act in a crisis to save my loved ones. Some might find Ray a bit wooden and undramatic, but I think it suited the movie since it told the story of an average man and his family and some people are like that in real life as well.

Ray's daughter, Rachel (Fanning), was a perfect addition to the characters. Her freaking out increased the feeling of chaos perfectly. Something about her innocence made me want to see her survive and her fragile presence was nicely in contrast with the surrounding havoc. The only character I didn't like in this movie was Ray's son, Robbie (Chatwin). His zeal to fight the tripods was, in my opinion, a bit unrealistic. His survival in the end was also a bit too cheesy for my liking.

Otherwise the ending was OK, since one of the main themes of this movie was man's helplessness. It was very fitting that man was saved by the forces of nature, not the US military forces.

Altogether, this is a movie that definitely divides opinions. Those who don't like Spielberg and/or Cruise at all should just rent it on DVD. I recommend this movie to those of you who like to see disaster or sci-fi movies. This solid piece of work gets 8/10 from me.

title: Great FX, but too linear
review:
*may contain spoilers*

Damn, that Tom Cruise can look good. On screen, at awards, even when he gets squirted in the face with water. But something is lacking when we're on the subject of War of the Worlds. Could it be his co-stars? His director? Or maybe it's Mr. Cruise himself. Lets start off with the great parts. First off, the CGI was on a grand scale. I've never seen a movie pull off some of the things WOTW pulled off. It really is a breath taking experience when you watch it. Sencondly, Tom can act. It wasn't Oscar worthy, not even close, but it was better than some of performances in your local theater right now (can you say Bewitched)? Thirdly, the....umm...well that's really it. Notice how the second paragraph was so short. Now for the bad parts. The co-stars. I found them to be awful, maybe with the exception of Tim Robbins. Dakota fanning really got on my nerves. Her screaming every time something bad happened was really really annoying, and it needed to be changed. Secondly, the CGI. I know I said it was great, but only the first time you watch it. The spectacle wears off pretty fast. The last, and major part for me, was the script. Don't get me wrong, the story was amazing, but it only focused on Tom and his two kids. I know that's what it's intention was, but it took away from the total chaos of everything else that was happening around them. Oh and one more thing, the ending. Lets just say I almost wanted to ask for a refund because I felt so ripped off. But no spoilers, and I hope you can enjoy it besides the movie having some major flaw. Definitely not Speilbergs best, but a good effort.

title: Asside from a few plot holes, War of the Worlds is a good film.
review:
Warning !!! Spoilers quickly approaching...

The original "The War of the Worlds", has always been on my list of my top favorite films. As a kid, I remember seeing it for the first time (on television---I'm old, but not that old!), and remember how intense some of the scenes were. Not much is different in how Filmmakers of "Today", build-up the suspense level a given scene, as was accomplished by filmmakers 50 years ago. Filmmakers attribute this type of thing to good "Pacing" of the events in a film. Like the original, the new "War of the Worlds" installs a great amount of this "Pacing", but even more, it does so through the majority of it's scenes.

SPOILERS!!!

Spielberg manages to accomplish what so many filmmakers fail to do in remaking films of the past. Rather than retell the story, Mr. Spielberg does what he does best, which is "Invent" the story, or in this case, "Re-invent" the story. Part of what makes this movie worth the time and money to see it (not to mention the months and months of anticipating it), is that, much like every film with the Spielberg signature, is done BIG. Big Budget, big stars, big scenes, big visual effects, (did I mention, big sound effects?), most certainly is the formula for a "Big" film that is certain to bring in "Big numbers".

If you are a "Die Hard" fan of the original, you most likely will approve. But be aware that this one, and the original, differ in many ways, and not simply in a "aestetic" difference, either. I liked the idea of the alien "war machines", being planted in the ground, rather than showing up in the skies. This idea shouts originality by observing the mere fact that for years we've looked to the skies above for such an arrival, yet "they" were right under our feet the entire time. The lightening strikes, and having the aliens being transported to the giant war machines, was interesting. Being on the far side of far-fetched, it was a very unique idea, so much that it works, and works well. I also liked the idea of these giant machines, the "Tripods", walking about, instead of the classic hover above the ground effect. They're huge monster looking things, yet take on a sort of personality all to themselves. One of my favorite things, is the sound the Tripods make. It's almost impossible to describe, other than it elevates the terror the audience feels while listening to it, and watching the characters scramble around, countless ones being cut into pieces by the huge beams emitting from these machines.

Like the original, the scene in the cellar is there, and it's very intense. It seemed a bit longer than the in the original, but then again, the length is because of some originality to it. Tom Cruise of course does an excellent job playing a divorced father who cannot connect with his kids, yet despite his inability to be close with his kids, manages to shift gears into the survival mode for his family, and get the hell out of Dodge. But where? Where do you go, when you have these huge three legged tripod things, cutting and torching everything in their path---and worse, more keep showing up? Where do you go when there is rapidly becoming no safe place to go?

Errors in Continuity, plot holes and the like, include (but not limited to), all power, electronic devices, battery operated devices, and cars going dead -- yet one guy video camera that works, is seen videotaping during the scene when the first tripod we see cutting thru people.

A news van, with all the ENG/EFP equipment inside powered up and working like a charm, yet virtually everything else in the surrounding area is dead. This is the scene where we find out that the aliens "ride" the lightning down in capsules.

Those are only two of several. But hey, it's still very good fun!

Be aware that this film does have more than a fair share of scenes that many would see an inappropriate for small children. Such things as people being cut into pieces in a millisecond, burned into ash, and frightening scenes of terror, would most likely leave certain little ones scarred. Sure they'd get over it, but it's enough that just leaving the light on at bedtime, wouldn't fix such a thing.

1 out of 10, I give this one a 7.

Favorite quote of the movie - Ray (Tom Cruise) to Military guy - "What happened to it?" Military guy to Ray (Tom Cruise) - "About a half hour it started behaving erratically... started walking around in a circle about a then it just fell over."

title: Spielberg FOR PRESIDENT!!!!
review: DO NOT, I repeat DO NOT listen to the haters calling this film a bomb!!!! If you do you will miss out on the thrill ride of the summer! We rushed to see this film last night specifically because of some of the comments I am reading today. For the first time in a long time we were offered the opportunity to go and see a film without having any preconceived notion of what to expect. BRAVO for the media blackout! By no means was this a perfect film, in fact there were At least 3 or 4 moments where we laughed out loud because of things occurring on screen (don't worry I won't spoil anything for you) However, in hindsight, Thank God for those moments because it gave you an opportunity to breath and shake off the terror that is piled on from the beginning. Steven Spielberg has made one of the most terrifying films of all times . You could hear a pin drop in the Theatre when we saw it from the first lightening strike until the end. only broken up by nervous laughter every now and then. title: Vintage Spielberg
review: I've been reading reviews of War of the Worlds and to tell you the truth they seem somewhat negative. Why, is beyond me. This movie was fantastic. Flawless? No, but fantastic,Yes. I find that Spielberg stayed true to the original book by HG Wells. In fact he at least explains the existence of the aliens and how they planned their attack. This is something that was never depicted in the original movie with Gene Barry. Also, the tripods are exactly that, tripods according to the book, not the flying discs that we saw in the original film. Spielberg also proves again his mastery of special effects and cinema technology. Unlike many "action" movies, there is nothing gratuitous here. He maintains depth in his characters and they become the story amid all the destruction. The acting was very good, especially Dakota. I will say the ending was somewhat abrupt, but not unlike the original film. I find this a very minor flaw and should in no way take down this film as many of the reviews suggest. If and when you see this film remember it is SCIENCE FICTION !! This is something the critics seem to have missed.

title: The movie was great , loved it .
review:
I just saw it...just amazing . The theater was almost as big as an IMAX, I sat on the 3 row.I had to move my eyes and such , the experience was more than great, it was unbelievable.I felt like I was in the movie. Spielberg pulled this off, really well. The only thing that I didn't like was the ending but its OK, because as a whole movie it was almost flawless. title: Deeper Thought
review:
As soon as i saw the first trailer for this movie i knew Steven Spielberg couldn't let us down...

and in reality he didn't.

the action in the movie ultimately makes up for some of the slower moments where questions needed to be answered. Like most films that are based off of books a lot of the little subtly things go unnoticed. The film slows down at points to make way for a deranged man to answer these all. Other then that i found myself on the edge of my seat more then once and holding my breath.

The reality of the film is what makes it amazing.

Tom Cruise plays a man divorced from his wife, and his children hate him. Though Dakota Fanning decides to be almost reciting a prophecy at points, and screaming her head off (which does get annoying after the tenth time) she ultimately portrays a young innocent child. What Cruise is doing as her father is protecting her from losing that while trying to hold on to his son who doesn't want to be.

H.G. Wells' book probably describes more accurately the deeper meaning of the novel, but for me as a fan of Catcher in the Rye i most easily saw the protection of innocence while the thrilling nature of the film created tension. This movie has many layers to it which could only be answered by reading Wells' book, which i suggest everyone should read. The story is easily seen on screen without the deeper knowledge of the book, but the ending leaves some questions unanswered, and i have a good idea where they might be found.

this is one of those movies that you have to see in a theatre. The complete surrounding of this story brings you into it and yelling at the characters to do something else and then ultimately wondering, what would you do?

title: A great piece of filmmaking
review: The genius of Steven Spielberg combined with the intensity and perfection of Tom Cruise's acting could only give birth to a masterpiece.

title: far too many basic errors just make it unwatchable
review: Much of the issues I have with this film have already been covered by a plethora of previous reviewers, so I won't go back over them, suffice to say, in every scene there is at least one 'issue' that is so noticeable and off-putting to even the most oblivious watcher, that they continually build upon each other until it gets to the point where one just says to oneself "this really is unwatchable". For me, this point came at about one hour in. Mr Cruise has been driving along and has now arrived in a town somewhere. It is late in the evening and dark. There is a large angry mob of people crowding the streets; they are all very aggressive and we can only assume their anger is because the earth has been invaded by equally aggressive aliens who intend to take the earth as their own (although their anger is directed at their fellow humans). After a fracas with the mob, (in which we must assume, are made up of 100's of Americans, but only 2 have a gun!) Cruise is now sat in a late- night diner (which we must also assume is closed as there's no-one there the and lights are off). Now, bearing in mind the story line up to this point, we know that the earthlings are battling to save their plant: death, extinction, total obliteration is looking imminent/certain - this is not a spoiler, this is the story. In the diner, THERE IS A MAN CLEANING THE FLOOR!! WHAT!!?? The world is under attack and you are going to die (possibly quite) soon, no worries, i'm going into work to tidy some stuff up. This total lack of attention to detail just about sums this film up for me: so many 'things' in this film just aren't the way they would be.

title: Not 'War of the Worlds'
review:
I tried for a very long time not to watch this, as too much seemed to have changed from the book. However, having recently re-read the book I have given the Cruise/Spielberg version a try!

As a disaster movie it had certain merits - explosions, an unbeatable enemy,panic in the streets. As 'War of the Worlds' it failed to deliver on almost every count. Moved from London to NY (one assumes in order to 'sell' to an American audience), a complete change in the main character, simultaneous attack across the globe, and the red weed feeding on blood(!).

The book is still read after almost 120 years, and is still relevant. Why did they have to change so much?

If you've never read and are a fan of disaster/apocalyptic films it may be worth a view, but read the book instead - it's on Gutenberg!

title: Pretty Damned Good
review:
I had high expectations for this movie because I saw it was produced by the legendary Steven Spielberg. I also heard the superstar Tom Cruise was behind the thing, like it was a labor of love for him. Such talent, resources, and star power meant that this remake of the 1953 classic should be something more than an excuse to show off modern computer graphics.

My expectations were actually exceeded. It's not just a top-notch, popcorn- munching hide-and-go-seek game with giant alien monsters. It's actually SCARY. Being a lifelong horror movie fan, this surprised me.

I don't know how they did it, but the film somehow tapped into a primal dread of vast, unstoppable monsters. This is interesting because this is the only "giant monster" movie I've ever seen that's made me feel this way. I literally walked out of the theater dreading to see one of those tripods on the horizon.

They're the size of tornadoes. They're utterly invulnerable. And despite their size, they're stealthy and agile.

I don't think it's a profound movie, but it made me fear its alien monsters. I think that's remarkable.

title: Unbelievable
review:
It's interesting how times have changed. The original book by H.G. Wellsfeatured a protagonist whose first actions are generous and kind, rushing forward t try and help when he encounters the first of the invaders thinking that they'd been injured or trapped in their ship of space due to the crash following the plummet of their craft to the earth.

By way of contrast, the hero in this version seems merely stupid, taking no care whatsoever for his own safety at first, much less the safety of other human beings, including his young daughter, who depend upon his continued safety and survival. The story rapidly degenerates into a testosterone-fueled series of set-pieces which amply demonstrate the shallow immaturity of both the hero and his teen-aged son, as well as their utter lack of intelligence. Luckily, the deus ex machina which partially propels the original is still available for this "modern" spin on the classic tale.

For all the special effects, I'd much rather read the book.

title: If you are looking for a good movie, please keep searching because this one does not qualify as such.
review:
Steven Spielberg's War of the Worlds is about a New York City dad with almost no time for his kids and their battle against evil alien invaders. Tom Cruise plays the father with Dakota Fanning and Justin Chatwin as his two, distant and resentful children. The little family must put aside their differences in order to survive the invasion. The aliens appear and wreak havoc on the city, and most of the United States, very efficiently with no concern for the humans that get in their way.

I thought this movie was awful; there were many plot inconsistencies, scenes with disgustingly bad acting, and things that weren't even in H. G. Wells' novel, on which this movie is based. I think Tom Cruise was a terrible choice for the narrator, especially since his emotional scenes came off extremely cheesy and badly played. Dakota Fanning is incredibly irritating in the beginning where all she does is scream and complain about dumb, random things that don't relate to or add anything to the plot at all. As for being a film based on Wells' classic, I really don't think the War of the Worlds movie version did the novel any justice at all. In fact, the only thing this movie had going for it was its use of special effects which, I will admit, were pretty sweet. This movie is a complete waste of time. Instead of watching this movie, take up juggling, ventriloquism, bird watching, or even spoon collecting instead, because at least then you'll have something to show for the two hours you would have otherwise wasted.

title: Great entertainment
review:
I've heard a lot of griping about this movie and I think people are just taking this medium, a movie, way too seriously. It is probably not a word for word remake of the 1898 novel by H.G. Wells. It has been reset without aliens from Mars. Fine. People have picked apart the way the plot moves along, finding flaws everywhere; for example, parts of major cities have little damage, other parts look like Hiroshima. I think we've taken this just a bit too far; this is not an English 201 course, where we dissect Spielberg's adaptation of the Wells novel, looking for strengths and weaknesses. This is nothing more than visceral entertainment, end of story.

This is my first viewing of the film and I found myself totally engrossed from beginning to end, with my nerves all tied up in knots. That the film ends abruptly is nothing new to movies and there will always be those who had mentally calculated a "better" way to end it. I think we'd be better off just looking at the story as it is. It is science fiction, not a glimpse of a possible reality, anymore than "Independance Day" was (and that is one of the silliest Sci Fi films I've ever seen). I think that our comments should be much more on how the action moves along rather than the gaps in reality. As soon as we catch ourselves measuring what is real or how things don't make sense I think we've lost the film and we should walk away. This being said, I didn't feel that there were so many obvious gaps in script continuity that made me laugh or scowl. It's a super fast paced adventure of survival with no certain outcome and that's about all we need to factor in. The way it unravels is irrelevant because it is not supposed to be within the realm of the possible everyday world.

Cruise, as usual, delivers an outstanding performance. His ridiculous commitment's to Scientology aside, he's a terrific actor and I've yet to see him fall on his face with a role. Dakota does scream quite a bit and act hysterical in the film. Don't blame her: Spielberg pulls all the strings and that is the way he formatted her character. On the other hand, did we expect a little girl of her age to be unmoved by monstrous aliens torching the world? I mean really, give the kid some slack. I'm sorry: I love her. And Tim Robbins' character is slimy, off-centered and just delicious in adding more creepiness and tension.

The special effects were totally outstanding. Look, if you're going to use CGI, you want the effects to look realistic and Spielberg knows how to deliver. You spend the big bucks and ILM and their computer droids deliver. The music was John Williams at his best. All in all, come on people: lighten up. It's fun, fast, furious, violent (heh, what year are we living in?) and fluff. Enjoy it for what it is.

title: War Of The Worlds ***
review: Although this may not have turned out to be the ultimate alien invasion movie everyone was expecting, it is still a spectacular, exciting and, at times, frightening version of H. G. Wells' famous sci-fi classic. I don't think that comparisons should really be made between this and the 1953 original (which, in itself, possesses a nostalgic charm totally absent from Spielberg's film) because of the enormous technological advances made in the special effects field but, in retrospect, it¡¦s interesting to note that both film versions of the novel can be seen as a Hollywood riposte to a recent catastrophic event which had hit the U.S. - the Cold War in the original and the attack on the Twin Towers in the remake; as a result - and thankfully so, I might add - Spielberg's approach to the material is refreshingly sober and intelligent, closer to that seen in SIGNS (2002) than the more jingoistic one adopted for INDEPENDENCE DAY (1996). Unfortunately, the anti-climactic "happy ending" seems more suggestive that if you are Tom Cruise nothing bad can really happen to you, rather than the more truthful message that if the family unit stays together under times of great emotional stress, it will eventually pull through despite the hardships and the losses. That said, Tom Cruise is ideally cast as the not-so-ideal father figure and delivers the goods in that respect; however, while Dakota Fanning steals some of his limelight, her character - and especially that of her brother - were something of a liability, coming off as rather annoying and one-dimensional. Also, it was a nice touch on Spielberg's part to give bit parts to the 1953 version's original stars, Gene Barry and Ann Robinson, at the very end of the film but, as I said before, the ending was misjudged, in my opinion, if not necessarily a fatal mistake.

title: Perfection
review:
I have read a large number of reviews for this movie, and I must say that I was surprised with the comments that I read. Firstly, just before its release the Australian movie programs "At The Movies" and "The Movie Show" saw reviews of (out of 5) 5, 4.5, 5, 5, and 5. 4/5 gave a perfect score. I saw the movie with my family, and we all later agreed with each other. 10 out of 10. Every single review or comment I read in the paper or saw on TV in Australia gave it a near perfect score. But what I've later seen is that this movie was loved by critics but considered rubbish by the public. I cannot see why this is so.

Tom Cruise puts in another of his excellent performances, and I believe that he is one of the better actors of his age in Hollywood. His character is believable as the caring father and protector for his children, who is going through a rough time with the break up with his wife/girlfriend Mirando Otto (can't remember which). Cruise and Spielberg had teamed up once before for the film Minority Report, and this movie indicates that this won't be the last time they will be both be involved in the same movie. Cruise has put in what I believe to be one of his best performances, along with Collateral and Top Gun. But the real star of the show is Dakota Fanning. This was the first time that I had seen her in something before, but since seeing the movie I have now watched Taken, I Am Sam and Man On Fire, and now know why she is one of the most sought after child actors in Hollywood. She is incredible, and is an extremely talented young actress. I only hope that she won't fade away as she reaches adulthood as so many child stars do.

Spielberg's direction is out of this world. He places us right into this family, and see the events unfold front Cruise's point of view (as well as Dakota's in a few scenes). Spielberg cleverly doesn't show us what is happening away from the family in order to place more focus on the family, allowing us to become emotionally attached to them, much as we would our own family members. But it is the special effects that raise this movie to new heights. Not the actual special effects (which, however, are earth-shattering) but how Spielberg takes the camera away from the special effects, away from the action. If this was real, you would not sit back and go Wow, that explosion was incredible. You'd be running. And that is what Spielberg does, he has the camera running from the explosions, trying to get to safety.

This movie will always be remembered as one of the best movies that I have ever seen, and that will not change, despite what other people may say about it.

title: Excellent Drama, but lacked a lovable hero.
review: I found "War of the Worlds" to be great drama. The acting and the directing were superb as well as the special effects. The reason I could not give it a ten was that the story lacked a truly lovable hero. Dakota Fanning and Tom Cruise gave great performances. Tom Cruises character, however, never seemed to rise above the average person in regards to me. he did grow from the character he was at the beginning, but that was something we expected. I think that Spielberg was excellent at catching the nature of panicked mobs. I believe that Spielberg was primarily focused in showing us a more realistic view of what might happen to people in such a situation than selling out seats, which is something a great director can take the leisure of doing.

title: W.o.W.
review:
This movie left us speechless -- literally. As we left the theater, we ran into friends, and simply could not come up with anything to say -- we were still in such shock from this movie. We see a lot of movies, and I am rarely as drawn into a movie as I was on this one. Frankly, the last Sci-Fi movie that affected me so was The Matrix (the first one!). I was on the edge of my seat the whole time -- even though I knew exactly how it would end. Spielberg really knows how to pull an audience in.

The special effects were incredible. The characters were developed adequate to the story (which wasn't really about the people, after all). And the bad guys were really scary! The ending might have been a bit too "pat" for me, except that it was so brief, it was hardly noticeable except as a chance to catch my breath after the hell we had all just been through.

title: Love it or hate it---this is a Masterpiece
review:
I felt initially: Where's the big scope? I want to see more destruction! Where's the rival to Independence Day?

Then I realized Spielberg made a conscious choice. (From a Cinematography standpoint, he cemented that statement with the *very* clever moving van shot as the family is making their escape.) Spielberg's statement: You and Iare sticking with Cruise's character. The focus is never going to leave him. Which is exactly what Spielberg did. We were in the dark because Cruise's character was in the dark. We were guessing just as much as he was. Half the time we/he really couldn't tell for sure what was going on: which is exactly how we'd be in a state of war like that.

(Which, on another side note, is almost exactly how the original novel reads!)

Spielberg opted to make a human experience War movie instead of a flash-bang sci-fi crowd-pleaser. The is art and drama...the CGI wasn't there to wow us (though it was well done)...it was there only when necessary to tell the story. The aliens were secondary to the Story, which is really about our deepest fears and how different people respond when pushed to the edge. For me, the creepiest scenes weren't with the aliens, they were with the mobs of people and with Tim Robbins' character.

(One more book note: Robbins' character is a combination of two major players in Wells' novel.) It's a Spielberg classic, conjuring up his best directing alongside Jaws, Close Encounters of the Third Kind, and Schindler's List. Interestingly, this movie plays out almost like a culmination of all three: the raw panic & fear of Jaws, the "one man's story" of Close Encounters, and the horrors and dehumanizing effects of war in Schindler.

Spielberg didn't make this movie to play to the crowd or please the masses. He simply told the story the way he wanted it told.

Again, just my opinion ... Love it or hate it: it's still a masterpiece.

title: Best Movie of the Year (Screen)
review:
At least ! A big catastrophe movie WITHOUT the President of United States... It is a good change, for us, the ordinary people.

And as it is Spielberg at the helm, the movie is a wonderful moment. He leaves all his colleagues far behind, because he is THE master of storytelling.

By sticking to this "private" perspective, he wins! The audience only knows what the characters know, and the situations have more weight. It's like a Reality movie, or a docu-drama: shoulder-camera, brilliant transition sequences. Beyond the story, it looks like melting-pot of a lot of his past success: "Jaws", "Close encounters", "Schindler's list", "Hook", "Jurassic" and it is always enjoyable to see how a great director still dig into his thematic after 20 and more movies: kids, family, individual or mass terror, space,....

But, as the movie deals with an invasion of Martians, it is frightening. I literally fall down in this "war of the worlds" as if it was for real. Feeling real emotions in front of a fake, fictitious world is the ultimate proof of talent.I was tensed, anxious in front of this never ending drama. Psychologically, I got the same reaction as on the "9.11": the world is reduced, the liberty of movement is more and more smaller. You never know what happens next and then, you start to appreciate your life minute after minute.

OK, the character of Tim Robbins is maybe not perfect, the Martians are far-fetched, but i got my more memorable movie experience since a long time.

In conclusion, a Classic story turns now into a Classic movie.....
