title: Watchable
review:
Spielberg attempts to hoodwink us out of our 10 dollars in this movie. This movie is not a movie about an alien invasion. It is a movie about one man and his kids living through a disaster. Or at least that's what the book is. The movie tries to mix that idea with poorly developed characters and superfluous sub-plots. Spielberg introduces two new characters in his adaptation a daughter and son who live with their mother, but are staying with Ray (Cruise) for the weekend. They are obviously only their to give Ray a reason to keep going and to make him more likable. But the movie fails on both counts. The kid's characters are never devolved enough. They feel like useless appendages.

We see Cruise running from one disaster to another; in the end it just seems tired. You might as well be watching volcano with aliens inserted instead of a volcano. Spielberg does deserve credit for keeping the characters (all of them even the extras) actions seem realistic and prudent.

This movie is in the end merely watchable. My advice: save your money for a better movie.

title: A movie that mixes terror, gore and aliens with a lack of substance
review:
You would usually expect a Spielberg movie to be more exciting and to have a very intriguing and growing plot. I found myself at first amazed, then started to see how the movie went from shallow to extreme and then just to go out being overly simplistic.

You would want to know how the Martians (they are Martians as the novel reads) came to be and how they would go about their business. You begin getting questions which some are answered but some are left for your own conclusions.

There are too many similarities with other movies that I think should have been avoided. I also think the scenes tend to be repetitive at times. I really disliked the little girl in the movie, she doesn't quite fit in. I for one prefer Independence Day, its more animated and has far much more substance.

title: Comments on Ending (Spoiler ONLY if you're familiar w/ original)
review:
My only hesitancy in going to see this movie is that I hated the way the original WOTW ended and assumed this would similarly disappoint. If you've seen/heard the radio version from the 30's or the movie version from the 50's, then you know what I'm talking about. The ending--including the voice-over my Morgan Freeman, who has the same timbre as Orson Welles--is very true to original story. After all, this is based on an H.G. Wells novel and don't you just hate it when a movie changes key plot elements? If you don't like the ending, blame H.G. Wells and not Spielberg.

That being said, I went to see this newest iteration and absolutely loved it. And surprisingly, I found myself not minding the ending as much as I have in the past, maybe because it was what I expected or maybe because that real life endings are also a little askew of expectations or wants..

Thought the story, the acting, and the special effects were absolutely A+. Yeah, there were a few inconsistencies and some nit-picky things I didn't care for, but this is in my top 3 for the year so far (Cinderella Man is #1 by far)... A nice holiday weekend escape.

title: A good film
review:
The film was fine and for the most part was a logical picture. The only part that was illogical was the fact that the alien machines were reanimated from their storage underground.

Why would that be? Perhaps it was trying to handle the idea that you can't travel faster than the speed of light to get somewhere and so a space invasion would have to be planned over a vast amount of time. Then one asks the question: how did the pilots of said vehicles get here? The movie shows how they got here but not exactly how. The buried vehicles made no sense.

It would have to be assumed that the aliens came in ships to our planet and then transferred to the hidden craft. That would mean that there were more of them waiting in space.

If that were the case, then the element that defeats them could be solved via the creation of a space suit! Their invasion would then be unstoppable.

It would have made more sense to have the creatures arrive on Earth in crafts that they use to invade the Earth. That would mean that they were using everything that they had on their campaign and had no backup. The underground thing was a strange concept.

Anyway, the movie was not about that. It was about life being an "emergency" and realizing what is really important. I felt sad seeing people die and happy that the irresponsible dad main character was waking up to what was important. That's what I enjoyed about the film.

title: Good good.
review:
Compared to the book, there were a few major differences. The biggest one was definitely the time. The movie was set in the 21st century, the book in the 19th. In ways this is both beneficial and disappointing. It would've been interesting to see humans who haven't even dreamed of powered flight to be fighting aliens with heat rays and the like. A second, in the book, people saw flashes of the pods being launched from Mars, then the pods landed every 24 hours and the aliens built the robots on earth (at least this is what I got from the book). The aliens also could barely walk on Earth due to our heavier gravity. There were a few other more minor differences, but it was still a pretty awesome movie when not bringing the book into it. The book was, of course, better, but that doesn't stop the movie from being good.

In other words, if you liked the book or just love alien movies, I'd strongly suggest this movie.

title: No one would have believed . . .
review:
From the perspective of someone who loved the original book, I was first in line to see Spielberg's adaptation, and I tried to watch it with an open mind. It was inevitable that any modern retelling would be subject to a large dose of poetic licence, but I was left with the impression that someone really didn't think things through.

The whole idea behind how the invaders got here in the first place seemed to be dreadfully hashed together. Gone was the suspense of the original story; one minute they weren't here, then suddenly they appeared in all their destructive glory without any satisfactorily explored reason (bar a few mumbled possibilities involving them being buried ages ago, and not one underground survey, rock slide, tectonic shift or quarry blasting team has come across one since). The whole premise behind the invaders 'riding the lightning' was novel, but I couldn't help feel it was just an excuse for some nifty special effects to help speed the story along.

The ending was a disappointment. In the original story, the hero confronts the invaders in order to end his life from his intolerable sense of loneliness and alienation (excuse the pun). Not once did I feel this was adequately explored or portrayed. I was left feeling somewhat cheated, half expecting someone to turn to camera and say, "well, now everything's back to normal then". There was no personal loss (quite the contrary!) and no sense of horror to the terrible events that had just happened. Too rushed, too schmaltzy and far too convenient.

The characterisation, I felt, was fairly weak. Tim Robbins as Ogilvy was a gestalt of three major characters; the parson, the artilleryman and the astronomer, but didn't really end up being any of them. No fault of Robbins Â– an excellent actor but victim to a considerably flaky script. Cruise's lead was, if anything, a pleasant surprise. Not really being a fan of his work, I was impressed by the level of credibility he transposed into Ray (the independent all-American blue collar worker facing adversity beyond his personal comprehension). The scene where his 'tough guy' mask fell away and he broke down in tears in the diner was especially poignant.

Don't get me wrong, this was not a bad movie and I would advise people to see it. It was very well acted, the direction easily equalled Spielberg's high bar and the special effects were outstanding. The tripods were exactly how I imagined H G Wells had envisaged them, right down to the grabbing tentacles and awesome heat ray. The whole ferry scene was excellently done (cobbling together the Weybridge battle and Thunderchild scenes from the book) as was the opening attack by the first tripod. I just couldn't help thinking that it was let down by a poorly developed screenplay. It may be interesting to see if there is an extended DVD version which may help to paper over the cracks.

Final score: 6/10

title: Anti-Climax? What's That All About?
review:
I saw this at an advance screening yesterday and whilst not expecting much (I never really liked the book, as well as the obvious Hollywood changes) I have to say that this movie blew me away.

In particular, the scenes of tension were spectacular, and really had me on the edge of my seat, after which the explosions of action would really work well, and not seem merely "put there for show".

As to the idea of the ending as an anti-climax, I can see why people would see it like this, but this was the genius of H. G. Wells. If the film had changed the ending, there would have been an outcry, as this would be ruining the image of one of the most well-known books of our time. Anti-climax? No way.

title: just an impression
review:
I saw the movie Tuesday evening. My comments--not to bad. The movie follows the line of the HG Well's book fairly well. There are only a few real departures from the novel: 1. How the Martians and their machines get to earth 2. A rip off from the 195? movie (two of them) 3. The lead not being a solitary individual 4. And how the Martians look 5. The crash of the 747--hmm---wonder how that went down and there was a convenient path for the three central characters to drive away???? 6. The capture and escape of tow of the leads

All in all--not to bad. The only real complaint I have is there is a rush to the end of the movie. Many of the scenes while being violent in nature are not gory. But with that said, it is pretty intense in places, esp. those where so many individuals are killed. The special effects are pretty good and the tripod fighting machine is well done.

I would have loved to have seen this movie set in Victorian England, as the book is and given a more faithful rendition of the novel.

Alas--while fairly well done, it is a Spielburg production and for better, or worse, it is ended in that neat and tidy fashion that only Spielburg seems to use.

title: Astonishing
review: Hands down, this is the best movie I've seen all year, and in the last few years, to be honest. I won't bother trying to convince people to see this because either you will or will not. It doesn't matter. The movie blew me away and surpassed all my expectations. In a time when most (almost all) movies really suck, this was a breath of fresh air! Those tripods are the most menacing antagonist in any film I've seen to date because they strike the right tone of being halfway between plausible, as though they could pop out of the ground any minute, and awe-inspiring, without being over-the-top like the city-destroyers in ID4. It truly is cinema at it's best.

title: Everything that you can expect from good sci-fi movie.
review: In a snap - it is everything that you can expect from a good sci-fi movie. Yes, Spielberg as a director, M. Freeman as a narrator and T. Cruise in the lead. Can you ask for more ? No, i doubt that. It is an eye candy. Yet it has even more - it manages to mess with your mind a little bit just like "Close encounters" or "Signs". The scenes of destructions are brilliantly constructed and totally believable. It delivers this magical touch of realism with first person view of tireless never-ending action and chaos. If you want to be pretentious to the extreme you can say that it could be a little bit better. There is a room for improvement. Story. Classical novel by H.G. Wells is just too classical for this kind of movie. Some insights of the author on how aliens and their "technology" should look like seems a little bit comical. The reason is - 50 years gap between scenario and movie. On the other hand, modern writers tend to push sci-fi props to the other extreme with over the top alien gadgets and often ruin the whole film. So Spielberg should have just improved same script a little bit more.

title: good/entertaining movie
review: i don't know where all the hostility came from for this movie. i think it was an 8 but gave it a 9 because of all the 1's it is getting from people who did not see it. although the effects and aliens were very hi tech, they were surprisingly realistic. the suspense was very well done as i was on the edge of my seat many times during this movie. i read a lot of reviews saying that dakota fanning was annoying... this is because she played an annoying 10 year old... and i think she did it very well. tom cruise was amazing. the ending got a lot of criticism and i would agree with that criticism, but that certainly did not take away from the two hours of great effects and suspense before that. the movie really reminded me of independence day... which i do not understand the low rating for... and i thoroughly enjoyed it. and by the way... i saw batman returns just days before this which i gave a 10 out of 10 so i was not going into war of the worlds with low movie expectations.

title: Dread reckoning
review:
Dread.A continuous sense of ever increasing dread is the driving force within War of the Worlds. Long before any invader is shown, you are gripping the arms of your seat, and slowly pushing back away from the attack you know is coming. And when the attacks begin, you find that you aren't quite ready for this type of film as a summer blockbuster.

But then again,director Spielberg has not been the same director once he finally directed the film he tried to avoid doing for years. Schindler's list could be the considered the A.D. period of the director's career,the initials standing for "always darker". Yes, he does insist still on the sugar coating at the end, but not before he has served you a heaping bowl of unfrosted shredded wheat covered with a heaping helping of wheat germ. But you know, the effects of his dish are very cinematic ally cleansing.

Dakota Fanning is as eerily excellent on screen as Cruise's daughter, and Cruise is in fine form. Tim Robbins was a welcome sight, though the basement sequence was a little windy. It's a good thing this film did not hit theaters until some time had passed from the events of 9/11. Even with the passing of time,this film strikes painfully close to the heart of our emotions of the unspoken dread of that time. When the children ask "Is it terrorist?", you can sense a dull ache of pain past brush your mind.

The effects are nearly perfect, existing only to serve the story. The van travel scene is impossibly brilliant, with the camera panning,zooming,assisting the tense narrative. This film is the anti-Close Encounters, and after seeing this film "We are not alone" will sound like some horrible threat.

title: Very unrewarding
review: This movie is simply a Jurassic Park style movie (great!), with an Independence Day scenario (lame), with an ending about as satisfying as that of Signs (terrible) and an ending about as well planned out, founded and explained as that of Vanilla Sky (absolutely horrendous). I think the most apt analogy is the train analogy. There's beautiful scenery on this train ride, the journey is great, but once you get to the station... you wish you would have just saved your 12 bucks and spent the night at home watching one of the new Star Wars movies, (shot against a blue screen) Ithink the acting was great for the most part. I maybe would have recast that kid who played the son, Robbie. The Morgan Freeman voice-over was a very lame introduction. The film itself was beautifully shot. Very well-directed and appealing to the eye, but there were so many holes in the telling of this story... There weren't holes in the story when I read H.G. Wells' version of it, but somewhere in the translation, many important parts of the story's telling just fell apart and got cut, I might wager a guess. I don't know if this next bit counts as a spoiler , but I've marked it anyway... Now, when the first city falls victim to the aliens... it sets off the EMP, right? and nothing electronic can work, right? so he changes the solenoid on the van and takes off (through very conveniently placed refuse). However, an issue arises when the van is involved in the second meeting with the aliens... The EMP just doesn't effect (affect?) it or something? The windows all stay intact. And the basement, where they hide in Boston... everything is destroyed. Entirely. Except for one little detail called STAIRS. Perfectly intact. still sporting what looks to be a brand new coat of paint. Completely untouched. Other than little things like this, and this movies complete utter failure to explain it's ending, or really establish how it ended and why, this movie is a pretty damn good thrill ride. Suspenseful and frightening at times. SOm beautiful social commentary at times. A beautiful story of one man who simply loves his kids, trying like Hell to keep them safe. Still not half as good as Batman though.

title: Ya Gotta Love Technology...
review:
I read reviewers reviews from all the big papers, I saw all of Tom Cruise and Dakota Fanning's press junkets -- but I still went to see this film.

I liked this film. Not love..but liked. Why? Well..it wasn't too far from the HG Wells original telling...and I think that is what is confusing folks. Sure, there was a few more CGI things added in...and a few twists and turns here and there for dramatic effect..but the story was still the story.

I wasn't expecting "mega" blow out of the martians...not with PG-13..and it was as PG-13 as it could be. With an "R" rating, I would have expected quite a whole lot more. But I am not the kind of movie goer that needs to see every detail of death and destruction -- and this film didn't do that.

Tom Cruise was okay in this film....Dakota Fanning was wonderful and Tim Robbins almost stole the show. 'Blockbuster' material in 2005 this is not -- but what it IS -- is a 'good' interpretation of a classic.

title: War of the Worlds...Just a basic post.
review:
The comments you are about to read are based upon acting, directing, and entertainment value only. I do not base my movie thoughts upon the actors or directors personal lives, however in the event that I do it will be because of a real good reason...

Cruise and Spielberg are back together again. Both parties gave a great performance in Minority Report and they do not fail in War Of The Worlds. The story line, of course, is completely different and treads the line of a basic story. Unlike such movies as The Matrix or Momento, War Of the Worlds is quite simple: Aliens want to kill humans, humans die and the rest try to survive.

Cruise plays Ray Ferrier. An average, divorced joe who makes a living working at the docks while having part time custody of his two children. As luck would have it, the War begins while Ferriers kids are at home with him.

The movie does a good job of getting to the point since we all know the plot of the movie. Industrial Light and Magic, again, puts on a great show and the length of the movie is perfect.

Besides the 2005 story line not matching that of the original, the only thing that got to me was the lungs on Dakota Fanning. After awhile I was like "SHUT UP ALREADY". All in all, I would see War of the Worlds again on the big screen.

title: Unpleasant and aimless
review:
War of the Worlds is an impressive movie on many levels. The technical aspects, first of all, everything from visuals to the sound design, are all amazing. Nothing less could be expected from Steven Spielberg. The alien tripods especially are very, very chilling as they walk across the crumpling town.

The problems all rise from the story and the characters. It's an unpleasant film to watch, mostly because it plays out more like a disaster film than an alien invasion popcorn film. And yes, it's clear that Spielberg intentionally meant it to be that way. Doesn't make it the right choice, though, at least in my books. Especially because even in a disaster movie you still usually finish on an uplifting note, all of humanity coming together to rebuild. Here the ending is, while not exactly dark, at least depressing. It's a message of meaningless suffering and the unpredictable cruelty of future and fate. I'm not surprised that so many people see terrorism allegories in this film, but the thing is, if you want to tell such a story, don't tell it in a way that makes us expect a popcorn film.

The actors and characters are also rather nondescript. You don't really end up rooting for any of them. The one that comes closest to resembling a sympathetic character is the little girl, played by Dakota Fanning, with her adorable hat fetish, but even she is rather boring and annoying most of the time. Tom Cruise is not bad, actually, but the script forces him to be something of a jerk, which has never worked out for him, mostly because it suits him just a bit too well.

War of the World fails as a movie because it's nowhere near entertaining enough to work as a popcorn film, but neither it has enough depth to make you think. You'll get something out of it for its production values, but they're not enough to justify its flaws. One of Spielberg's weakest, I'm afraid.

title: Science Fiction at it's worst
review:
I thought I would give this film a watch, but found it to be so boring, and also the plot to be stupid. The overacting, and obvious overtones of scientology philosophy puts me off. I was expecting to see Xenu come out and hydrobomb all the humans off the planet........ and yes, I have read about scientology, and it in itself is like a flesh eating virus sucking the blood out of it's practioners, and written by a science fiction author.

I think the supporting cast outshine Tom Cruise, but feel there could have been a larger cast to make this more believable instead of just focusing on tom and his family, as that part of the story was really very boring. I did enjoy Minority Report, which starred tom and was also directed by Spielberg, so had high hopes, and this film just lets you down, feels like a b movie you would expect students to make.

title: I expect rubbish from Spielberg, but this was shockingly bad
review:
I think it's only Americans who hold Steven Spielberg in any kind of regard - the rest of the world think he's an ego-tripping con-man who's good at pitch meetings and loves to spend studio money. He's kind of like an L Ron Hubbard of director-wannabes/producer-wannabes.

The last good film he made solo was Duel, when he was a fledgling. Even in Jaws you could see the formula taking shape - quick flurries to indicate mass activity of some kind; characters who suddenly get tearfully, chokingly serious; and his most annoying gimmick, characters who sit around talking themselves up - it's as though they are trying to get you to like them, and telling you what a good story you are in for.

The Indiana Jones films were made with Lucas keeping Steven on a very tight leash - a leash that was re-tightened after the disaster of Temple Of Doom.

Catch Me If You Can? - yes! I *will* grant that one! But I think it had an awful lot more to do with Leonardo and Tom working together well, and the fact it was a (more or less) true story, than any great captaincy in the directorial chair. Let's just say Mr. S didn't stuff it up, thank the gods.

Schindler's list? When you are Jewish and under the watchful eye of pretty much the entire world's Jewish population, with regard to the atrocities of the Nazi holocaust, you are going to tread very, very carefully lest you offend pretty much everyone. Even so, he managed to get some of his irritating trademarks into the film AND schmaltz up the ending.

And now, we come to War Of The Worlds.

With this embarrassing sci-fantasy... 'thing' that he has created, I really think the years of being praised by idiot sycophants has taken it's final toll.

There is nothing in this film to offer, nothing. Not one single thing. Dakota Fanning needs to die in the first few minutes. And I put up with the Tom Cruise character and his infinite ability to survive ANYTHING... until he started to sing.

The movie went under the Fast-Forward hammer from that point on - my gods I was so grateful I hadn't been forced to sit in a cinema for this giant, giant turkey. I really can't say - would I have stayed? There is a good chance not, that I would have left and gone to get on with my life. But, you know... train-wrecks and all that. The fascination with how badly a director/producer can get something wrong.

Heh, Spielberg saying "I have the power to make any movie I want." Really, Steven? There is an issue there - you don't have any talent, whatsoever. You're a hack who stumbled onto a moronic, sell-able formula a couple of decades ago, and all Warner Bros, Sony and the rest care about is money. Art? They release the flintlock on their Brownings at the mention of the 'A' word.

The alien machines underground. Really? You just wanted to get that in a film, didn't you? Come on Steven, fess up. What was it, a dream you had one night? Possibly it could have made a nice, weird film by itself - but it would need a real director and a real producer and ABOVE ALL... a writer. You need a writer, to write a story. That's what writers do, Steven.

The tentacle in the basement. I can hear you in the 3D editing suite now, Steven: "It doesn't go click enough! Add more clicky bits. More clicky bits! More more more! I need more clicky bits ADD MORE CLICKY BITS!!!". You did it with the aliens' eyes at the end too. It's all you know how to do, spend studio money and waste the time and lives of designers with talent, adding more clicky, more fall-off-cliff, more scream, and more more more unsubtle over-emphasis to your rubbish films.

Tom Cruise singing. In a film that was already one of these stupid "off-axis" genre w*nkfests that Hollywood has gone in for - so you didn't get to see anything interesting, really - that had already slowed down to the pace of a smacked-out snail... Tom starts singing. Yup, that's when the room collectively reached for the remote, and we skipped large chunks of the rest of this river of sewerage.

To those who haven't seen the 1953 original, please do - you'll enjoy it. For one thing, you'll be surprised at how good the FX were at the time. For another, you'll enjoy the presence of a story - to the extent that Wells' novel ever had one (its mainly people running screaming until the aliens die, but the military fights back, there is lots of discussion of what to do about these things, and the action doesn't stop to a dead-crawl so some fool can sing).

One day I'd like to see a proper brass-and-glass steam version of the original done, given that the 1953 one is already well updated from the novel.

Wells was decades ahead of his time. Spielberg is just a talentless idiot.

title: A satisfying adaptation, remake or re-imagining, whatever you choose
review:
This movie could be considered as an adaptation for the novel by H G Welles , as well as a remake for the original War of the Worlds movie or even of the Orson Wells radio dramatization, you could even call it a rip-off of Independence Day (or the other way around, I should say).

This is the first time Steven Spielberg gives the audience the hostile theory of the aliens. In Close Encounters and in ET we had the more friendly aliens, but here, they're mean spirited and with the sole purpose of wiping us out.

It's full of differences from the original novel, as I felt it was more faithful to the 50's movie, mainly the prologue and epilogue (this time narrated by the imposing voice of Morgan Freeman).

Still, the visual effects are stunningly great and, ironically, very realistic. There were scenes with one shot, no cuts, when all the mayhem is going on around, and it looked brilliant.

Tom Cruise is an overall good actor, and this is not an exception. The worst miscast I found was Dakota Fanning. The producers cast her just for her star power. The problem is, because she has grown so used to playing more mature and sometimes mentally disturbed parts, she just can't play a frightened baby girl, crying for mommy. Tim Robbins played an interesting character, though I didn't find much use for him.

The movie is sci-fi, still, it transforms very subtly into horror, and it works, although it can extend itself a little too much.

As for the score, well, it's John Williams, people. Yet, this one stands for it's Bernard Herrmann inspired end credits music, a brilliant fast paced intrigue cue.

Overall, it's very enjoying, fun and exciting, and pays tribute to all previous WotW adaptations and the source material itself.

Steven Spielberg has gone to a point where he doesn't need to try hard to make a very good movie. He just says the word, and the movie gets done. Although, I noticed that his movies are longer lately.

You can add War of the Worlds to Spieblerg's best movies list.

title: Why I liked this movie
review: I really don't know why people hate this movie so passionately when I thought it was pretty good. For one thing it is one of the most realistic alien movies that has yet to come out. Be real, if a ultra-powerful alien species came to Earth we would be in deep crap. We would have now idea what they wanted or what they were doing. Independence Day met its downfall when the president "saw" into the aliens minds. Not only is that a weak turn of events, but it is also a poor attempt to explain something that needs no explaining. If aliens show up destroying everyone in sight, it's pretty obvious that they don't like us for some reason. Rather War of the Worlds shows us what would happen if aliens really invaded. Confusion, hysteria, desperation, and not knowing the future to come. I rate this movie high because of the stunning visuals and because it was exciting to try to figure out what is happening while the main character does. It is a refreshing surprise to follow an average human being, unlike other movies where the character is omnipotent and whose knowledge and power is inhuman. I have also seen the original and I find the story of this movie's story better and the new visuals stunning.

title: Steven Spielberg is back with one of his darkest and frightening films yet!
review:
I have always admired the films of Steven Spielberg from the horror of Jaws, to the drama of Schindler's List, from the terror of Jurassic Park, to the onslaught of Saving Private Ryan, Spielberg is a director that rarely disappoints, and War of the Worlds has Spielberg back at the top of his game.

War of the Worlds is the latest of alien invasion films that once again has unkonwn entities from other worlds attacking our planet for reasons unknown.

Unlike the extremely insulting Independence Day, War of the Worlds does not insult or injure the audience with a stupid script. It's terrifying events will haunt audiences for years to come.

Tom Cruise is Ray Ferrier, a divorced New Jersey dockworker/crane operator whose two children visit him for the weekend.

In the middle of his weekend visit, lightning strikes occur all over his neighborhood, and all havoc breaks loose.

From that moment on, War of the Worlds has you in it's terrifying grip, and never lets go.

From a jaw dropping ferry sinking, to an all out battle between alien tripods and the U.S. military, to it's frightening conclusion, Spielberg carefully balances out all out science fiction battle sequences and scary moments perfectly.

The great thing about War of the Worlds is that the film focuses of Ray and his family, rather than stupid action sequences like those found in Independence Day. Ray isn't a hero, but rather a father trying to keep his children alive.

That is why Spielberg has become our modern day master filmmaker.

War of the Worlds is a terrific movie and gets a 10 on a scale of 1-10.

title: Terrific Sci-fi Hollywood Blockbuster Which Is Out Of This World!
review: 'War of the Worlds' was just as fantastic as I expected it to be! Obviously it's extremely different to the original 'War of the Worlds' because Special Effects and Technology has changed dramatically since UFO's were flying around on visible string. I think this film was clearly one of the best roles Tom Cruise has ever portrayed, because there is a clear absence of that cheeky infamous grin Mr Cruise uses frequently in his previous films. He isn't the stereotypical protagonist Action hero in this flick, instead I saw a helpless, everyday Father who truly loves his family. I hope his brilliant performance in this film widens his potential for future roles. One aspect I did notice was how fast the equilibrium was broken, because it seemed to go disastrous pretty quickly. The Special Effects were really good, but there weren't quite enough explosions or more Special effects for my liking, instead there seemed to be a lot more focus on the plot, and the relationship of the family. I think Steven Spielberg took quite a few risks with the appearance of the Aliens because of course no one knows what Aliens look like; Spielberg used the stereotypical look that has been produced in other films such as 'Alien'. I did enjoy the scenes with the Aliens creeping around the hut, and I found the way they moved quite creepy and very genuine. I don't like the people who think the film should copy the book, I mean I just saw it as a very successful Hollywood Sci-fi film which continues Spielberg's legacy.

title: Everything I had hoped it would be!
review:
The good news for me was that I had taken everything into consideration before I saw it. I had read the book and seen the original 1953 movie and heard an audio tape of the 1938 radio broadcast. So, naturally I knew how it would end. Also, I knew quite awhile ago that Spielberg was directing and Cruise was starring. Thus, I knew that everything would be wrapped up in a nice bow with the main characters being spared and the side characters being offed (just like in Jurassic Park or the Indiana Jones movies) and I would have to deal with Tom Cruise's standard intense style of acting. All these things I have learned to live with as Hollywood facts of life. Hollywood fact # 89: You can't have a hundred million dollar budget for a summer blockbuster and then kill children who are main characters. If the movie is about an alien invasion of Earth then we must except that this is a fantasy and thus other stretches of credibility should also be accepted.

I feel sorry for the people who can't just suspend disbelief and enjoy a well made movie. Like those people who watch space battle sequences and then complain that you can't hear sound in space.

But if you are not a jaded and cynical person and want to see an exceptionally well made remake of the classic tale then you are going to be thrilled to death.

I, myself was incredibly thrilled b/c this is the first time that H.G. Wells' original vision of a tripodal war machine (as opposed to the flying machines in the '53 version) has finally been realized on the big screen. And they look fantastic! Insect like. Totally Alien. Terrifying. The moment the first one finally erupts from the street, I felt a surge of cold dread run through my veins. The sound it makes is the sound of doom. You feel like you are there on the street watching as it happens and realize just how hopeless the situation would be. I love how, as the tripod attains its full height and surveys the situation, you get a sense that the alien inside is cracking its knuckles in anticipation. And then comes the heat ray annihilation and my heart just kept pounding throughout the rest of the movie.

The characters are very believable. This is not your happy, glowing cereal box family. This is a self-centered, unlikable jerk of a father coming to terms not only with the unfathomable annihilation threatening the world but also with the fact that he is so out of touch with his estranged children he doesn't even know that his eight year old daughter is allergic to peanuts.

One of the most frightening sequences in the movie, I'm happy to say, is lifted right out of the book where Ray and his daughter must hide in a basement with a ranting survivalist as the aliens puree humans all around them and then send in their spy tentacle to search for survivors.

The movie maintains a sense of gritty realism throughout with panicked mob scenes, bodies floating down a river and a sense of being completely cut off (no scenes of familiar landmarks like the Empire State Building or the Capitol Building being destroyed, only regular old buildings in regular old towns).

And for all those people griping about so called "plot holes" they should think first about whether it's an actual "plot inconsistency" or whether it just wasn't spelled out in detail b/c for the normal American family, they don't know everything, they only know what they observed.

Bottom line: If you go into this movie WANTING to be entertained, you will be. This is right up there with "Jurassic Park" and "Jaws". This movie is everything that "Independence Day" and "Signs" were not.

Along with "Batman Begins" this is the blockbuster movie event of the summer to see. Again and again.

title: A fantastic movie experience
review: I went into this not sure exactly what to expect. I didn't think it would be very true to the book, and it wasn't. I had read it about 4 weeks ago and loved it. There were VERY few similarities and I'm surprised they even attached the name to it. I also had low expectations of Spielberg after seeing Minority Report a couple of weeks prior. However I very much enjoyed this film. Very realistic and very disturbing in parts because of its realism. Some great performances from Tim Robbins and Dakota Fanning, and even Tom Cruise wasn't bad. Lovers of the book may be disappointed and I was too, which is mainly why I gave this a 9 not a 10. It is a wonderful film nonetheless even without staying true to the book. It shows genuine character development and some great suspense. In all, it was a very enthralling movie.

title: A Simply Spectacular Theater Experience
review:
If you're like me, you're puzzled and even annoyed at Tom Cruise's recent diatribes regarding psychiatry, postpartum depression, etc.. Clearly his judgment is more than a bit cloudy. However, don't let his outbursts and PDAs cheat you out of an incredible theater experience. See War of the Worlds not for Cruise but for Spielberg, Robbins, Fanning and the work of HG Wells. WOTW is a 2 hour cuticle-devouring ride that is the best bang for your movie buck in a very long time. (I'm not a sci-fi fan, don't like fantasy and have a low tolerance for violence. That having been said, this movie rocked. Plain and simple.)

The underlying theme "They're already here", resonates clearly as we still feel the aftermath of 9/11; references such as "is it the terrorists?" bring that home. The timing of this film's release feels right: brave armed men are seen marching into danger (and in all probability, death) when everyone else is running. Reminiscent of certain NY firefighters, yes? Or on a simpler basis, the US Army in Iraq. Only one little point made me go "huh?" - when Cruise takes on a mob and is the only one with a handgun. Come on! I don't recall HG Wells setting this story in Canada (my homeland). Seems to me everybody would be packing, wouldn't they? Isn't a situation like this exactly what the Constitution had in mind when the right to bear arms was written in? Hmmm.

At any rate, Dakota Fanning is fabulous, Cruise is solid and it's a movie that is well worth the exorbitant ticket price (and that's before the snacks, right?). But see it on the big screen; War of the Worlds should be experienced the good old fashioned way. Thank you Steven Spielberg.

I was very enthralled by the movie for the majority with great special effects and good banter between cruise and his kids which gives humor to lighten the film up slightly.This was the best i have ever seen cruise, i feel it is his best role and he like his kids in the film do an excellent job of portraying the situation realistically, the script is good with good lines but what i found bizarre was the fact there was very little plot, i mean aliens arrive and start eliminating earth and cruise figures hell take his kids to Boston which of course will be safer than new york, even more annoying was the fact that it was safer and in fact almost undamaged by the aliens, his ex-wife's street is in pristine condition. It was a very good movie and i would recommend it just because seeing it in the theater is the only way to do the film justice and see it properly, but its just death, destruction and then Morgan freeman telling us what happened.

title: This is War Movie. This is a War Movie on Steroids. Any Questions?
review:
After channeling Kubrick for awhile (with "A.I." and "Minority Report"), and delivering us two mildly entertaining larks ("Catch Me if You Can" and "The Terminal"), Steven Spielberg finally returns to what he does best: crafting thrilling big-budget Summer tent-pole movies. Of course, this being the older more mature Spielberg, "War of the Worlds" is far darker and more brooding than many of his past crowd pleasers, and it is also weighed down by the classically sentimental Spielberg cheese.

Spielberg expertly weaves in some timely immediacy to his tale of alien invasion that adds to the mounting suspense and terror. He hauntingly reminds us of the shock and awe of 9/11 with his images of crowds running for their lives and buildings toppling. There's also a very effective sense of the unknown, which mirrors the terror and fear of New York City in the early moments of the attacks on the World Trade Center. "Who is doing this do us, and is this the End of the World?" These are the same questions the citizens ask in the early moments of "War of the Worlds". Later in the movie, as the survivors are hiding in basements after the fall of civilization and the rise of the alien occupiers, we get a not-so-subtle but very meaningful reference to current geo-politics (pick your poison: the US involvement in Iraq, or the Israeli presence in Palestine). "Occupations never succeed," Tim Robbins' character reminds us all.

All of that makes for a nice modernization of H.G. Wells' classic tale. The strenuous attempts at character development, however, keep the movie from reaching for greatness. The fractured family at the center of our story was in crisis long before the aliens arrived, and using the end of the world as a way to bridge the gap between broken relationships (particularly between father and child) is a bit quaint and cheesy despite the best efforts from the cast. Tom Cruise acquits himself nicely as the deadbeat dad fighting to survive and protect his children. For most of the movie, the superstar actor makes you forget he is Tom Cruise (that loathsome Scientology-loving, psychology-bashing, Katie Holmes-cradle-rocking, media whore), which is a real testament to his innate talents and Spielberg's deft direction. And Dakota Fanning's unnaturally natural yet very powerful performance as his scared daughter would've been more of a revelation had this actress not already been so grotesquely over-exposed at such a young age. Also, the overtly happy ending after the anti-climactic albeit faithful to the original source material demise of the aliens, is a bit of a letdown.

In the end though, audiences should fear not, for Spielberg delivers those trademark long, lingering awe-inspiring money shots (alien tripods vaporizing towns from hilltops at night, a crowd in a frenzy to get on a ferry boat destined for doom foolishly thinking it is their only ticket to survival). For the excellent build-up of tension and those fantastic pay offs, this is Spielberg's best popcorn flick since "Jurassic Park."

title: A Must-See Scary Summer Movie
review:
Steven Spielberg has always been known for his outstanding use of special effects, whether it was the mechanical shark from Jaws or the subtly integrated futuristic scenery of Minority Report, so it comes to no surprise that all of the CG in War of the Worlds are beautiful. What is remarkable, is that from a director known for sentimentality, sometimes going overboard in that department, comes what is the most bleak summer movie ever.

War of the Worlds is a hard movie to sit through at times; the amount of tension and the atmosphere of constant dread are at times almost overwhelming, and I mean that as an accomplishment. This movie is scarier than most horror movies, but I don't recall jumping during any scene. The way the aliens exterminate their prey, the way the humans helplessly try to flee, all of it fills you with a sense of terror. Even when the invaders aren't on screen, the human paranoia around the protagonists comes into play. As Tom Cruise and his kids drive through a crowd of people while in one of the few working vehicles remaining, the results are just brutal. I don't want to give anything away, but when it's finally revealed just to what purpose the aliens intend to use our species for, I guarantee revelation will disturb you long after you leave the movie.

Acting in the movie is all around exceptional. The audience only has a limited time to get to know the characters of Ray, along with his kids Rob and Rachel, so it's quite an accomplishment that they are able to make you care about them their quest to reach Boston. Tom Cruise does a very good job of playing someone legitimately fearful for the safety of himself and his family, and for those reluctant to see the movie because of his off-screen behavior, you'll quickly forget such trivial issues once you watch his character for a minute or two. A few minor complaints have been made that towards the later portions of the movie, he acts unrealistically heroic, but I definitely disagree with this view (saying more would likely spoil some things). Dakota Fanning, who plays Tom's daughter, is convincing, especially for a child actor. Also, watch out for Tim Robbins; he plays a shell-shocked hermit that Ray and Rachel meet late in the movie, and he steals every moment he's on screen.

One thing keeps this movie from being a classic. This movie has arguably the most abrupt ending I've ever seen. I can't believe after constant building of tension throughout the entire movie, it takes such a steep dive after the long climb. The resolution isn't a bad one (water isn't the aliens' weakness, thankfully), but it isn't satisfying because it just seems to come out of nowhere. When you hear Morgan Freeman narrate the epilogue, the first thing that will enter your mind is, "That's it?!" Still, even with this minor flaw, this is the second best movie to come out this summer and worth every minute of your time.

title: They're here...
review:
I have recently commented on the 1953 movie "The War of the Worlds" - that it was a perfect examination of humans if Martian invaders came to our planet to wipe us out and then looked to call Earth their new home. I re-watched that movie three days ago and it is still effective in telling its story. That film is also a favorite of mine that scared me a lot when I was kid.

"The War of the Worlds" has shared a long and colorful history in the annals of American pop culture, since the story's origins began with the publishing of the 1898 novel written by H.G. Wells. Since then, it's been memorably retold in many formats, from Orson Welles' chilling 1938 radio broadcast (which surely enough caused a widespread panic), to Byron Haskin directing the aforementioned first film adaptation in '53, to a television series that ran during the 1980s, and finally to this big-budget action epic that's directed by Steven Spielberg and stars Tom Cruise.

If anything, "War of the Worlds" serves the purpose of returning Spielberg to form in the eyes of the public and a few select members of his fanbase. He really goes for the jugular with this picture in creating a scenario that in tone, is all-too realistic and brings back a mood of terror not evident in Spielberg's work since "Jaws" (1975). But of course Spielberg is no stranger to aliens, especially with "E.T." (1982) and "Close Encounters of the Third Kind" (1977) under his belt.

And "War of the Worlds" has a bankable film star - Tom Cruise, who is not on cruise control at all during this picture. Much has been made in recent weeks about Cruise's religious Scientology beliefs, which have since come to include the belief in the existence of aliens. Does this hype it up? Sure. Does this make me want to see it anymore? Yeah. Why? Because with Spielberg and Cruise together, it's a perfect match of two alien geeks, especially since they first teamed up in "Minority Report" (2002), and that movie was dazzling.

As for the movie, it doesn't disappoint in any respect. It features a master filmmaker back in the game of mastering his imaginative craft of storytelling in the most perfect fashion. Actually, though, "War of the Worlds" is quite literally terrifying. It's impossible to not overlook the real-world similarities present in this film's screenplay by Josh Friedman and David Koepp, as well as the many parallels to our own reality as human beings and the only species in this universe with brains and thoughts of planetary conquest.

In "War of the Worlds," after a grim opening narration by a gravely voiced Morgan Freeman, enormous and ominous EMP (electromagnetic pulse) storms have been zapping out electrical systems all over the world. I just love this particular segment of the movie, as the mood and tension begin mounting to unbearable levels and never lets up. But of course, we humans are oblivious that our actions on this planet have been monitored by an alien force that has patiently plotted our demise for eons.

Gone from this picture are brainy scientist-types and military personnel and it's the better for it; instead we focus in on blue-collar Everyman man-boy Ray Ferrier (Cruise), who has the kids for the weekend. In the tradition of Spielbergian fathers, Ray is irresponsible and not a good dad even though he tries his hardest. Ray's son Robbie (Justin Chatwin) openly despises him for being a bad father but his young daughter Rachel (the amazing Dakota Fanning) is a little more forgiving.

This next part is where Spielberg really shows off his skill of imagination, which is when the Martians invade. It turns out that the Martians' tripod war machines were already here, buried deep underground millions of years of ago and when they were ready to attack, the Martians were beamed to Earth in space capsules (through the EMP storms) and reactivated the machines.

The tripod war machines make an astonishing debut, rising up out of the ground and then vaporizing countless fleeing humans with their death rays. It soon becomes a race against time as Ray, Robbie, and Rachel try to make it to Boston from New Jersey as they escape the major cities that have fallen to the Martians, as well as the thousands of other desperate, terrified individuals.

From the beginning, "War of the Worlds" wraps you up in its grip and doesn't let go. Tom Cruise is more than adequate, giving one of his finest performances and providing a strong emotional center. The supporting players are great too, especially the delightful Ms. Fanning and a rather creepy cameo from Tim Robbins as Oglivy, a paranoid survivalist.

What's most impressive are the Martian invaders and their tripods. Spielberg took a gamble in showing us the Martians' direct confrontation with human beings by presenting the invaders to be vampires, apparently needing blood to survive. Humans are captured by the Martians and are then harvested; the creatures then eject the veinal remains (which are scattered about in areas where the invaders have already hit) and is quite nasty but is still effectively chilling in that it makes them that much more ruthless.

If there are any shortcomings, it's that the film's ending seems too abrupt (though it should be familiar to those who have followed the story in its past incarnations), and Spielberg seems to lose his grip on the story as it draws to a close. These are the only things I felt took away from the film.

"War of the Worlds" is a perfect summer movie that shows a master on top of his game once again. It's quite terrifying in its premise, as real-world events factor into the on-screen action. It's just too bad we humans won't ever learn from what annihilation will bring onto us if such a thing does occur.

8/10

title: Awe-inspiring
review: Spielberg exceeded expectations. This is simple-minded in it's depiction of menace the way that his early made-for-TV dazzler "Duel" was. The action is as scary and nail-biting as that in "Jaws", except here it is more disturbing and personal. The moral complexities of "A.I." and "Minority Report" are gone in favor of pure mind-bending special effects (some of the best ever glimpsed) and documentary-like realism. The tripods exist and annihilate in natural light and look utterly real. The actors (Cruise, Fanning, Roberts) are good but they really take a backseat to the dazzling horrorshow that Spielberg has put on display for us here. Remember the suspense and awe that "Close Encounters" created, only to be resolved with a sense of child-like wonder? Well, this is all of the suspense and wonder and creepiness of that film except the motivations of the aliens are strictly evil. I have to say that, despite some forgivable gaps in logic, this is Spielberg's most effective out-of-body-experience movie in years, probably since "Jurassic Park". And, similarly, it raises the bar for special effects. Unlike that film, little kids may be more terrified than elated by the action. Kudos to Spielberg for scaring the daylights out of us and giving us another masterful, truly other-worldly experience at the movies.

title: Spielberg shows us why he is king of his craft
review: I left this movie shaken and jumpy. Horrifying is the descriptive term that I thought best fits this film. I felt wrung out emotionally. The culprit is superb film-making/superior storytelling. Spielberg nailed this one. Because the story is told from the standpoint of one family, it seems that it is happening to us. I am a huge sci fi fan and the 53 version of this story is one of my favs. But I am intolerant of a lot of sci fi films because they insult your intelligence or are populated with characters that act unbelievably(see independence day). This war is probably the best sci-fi film I have seen in years. The special effects are tremendous but do not drive the story. The human drama, the horror of their plight is the thread that holds your attention throughout. I have seen some of the negative reviews of this film. I will not go into detail into specific plot points for fear of revealing spoilers but the so called logic gaffes that many have pointed out, reveal a lack of imagination on the part of the reviewers. I strongly recommend this film but don't bring the little ones this is the stuff of nightmares.

title: Get A Life!!!
review:
I cannot believe how much negativity there is out there for this film! OK - so there are some sizeable holes in the plot, there are some distinct changes to the story (naturally), there is Dakota Fanning's screaming and there is a sharp ending. So what? This movie takes the good decision to maintain the POV of Mr. Average Joe (Cruise) and his attempts to wrap his head around the fact that aliens are invading the Earth and everything he knows is exploding around him in big balls of fire. He is dazed and confused but recognises that his primary goal is the protection and survival of his children. This is a neat juxtaposition of the set up in which we learn that he is a crap father with little or no parenting skills whatsoever - in fact he is selfish and frankly a bit of a loser.

SS sticks with Cruise's POV and doesn't get lost in the need to have lots of war room scenes and failed fighter / tank / nuclear bomb attacks on the invading tri-pods / mother ships etc. I liked that fact that all we know as the audience is what we could realistically expect the central characters to know. Therefore, we don't know why the aliens are here - they just are and they're ripping the joint up! As far as the children are concerned. I'll admit that I wanted to punch out the son's lights a few times but hey, he's a teenage boy with raging hormones and a real chip on his shoulder about his ineffectual father. As for Dakota Fanning, well, all the whinging geeks out there who have decried her panicking and screaming clearly have no idea what it is like to have young children, especially frightened or hysterical young children. I do. I have two daughters who, when they were younger, could cry up a storm when they needed to.

This film has some startling special effects, especially in the sound department - which I haven't seen mentioned. The CGI is effortless and seamless. The Tripods are frightening and awesome. I do have a gripe about the aliens - they are stunningly like ID4's aliens which I found odd. But, hey, there is nothing to say that two people cannot have the same vision of what aliens may look like.

There are the appropriate nods in the direction of both the book and the original film but I think the updating works well and should be applauded. The acting is excellent - both from the POV of the bewildered and sometimes ineffectual Cruise character, to the kids, to the general despair of those periphery characters we meet along the way.

If I have one reservation, it is the final scene of reunion between the mother and children. I think she should of had a couple of sooty smudges on her cheeks and perhaps a small rip in her blouse (I have deducted a point appropriately). Other than that... a cracking popcorn munching blockbuster!

title: Blown away
review:
OK. First things first. Husband and I went to see this film today. TOTALLY blew me away. We loved this movie. It was tense, suspenseful, scary, it was...WOW. We debated not going because of Tom Cruise's very public ridiculousness, but ultimately decided his personal life wasn't going to keep us away from a Spielberg movie (whom we both admire).

Now I realize that opinion's are as different as the people who have them. And I realize that not everyone is going to agree with everyone else. BUT (ok, here we go) to those of you who are criticizing Dakota Fanning for her screaming and shrieking, I have to ask "WHAT THE HECK IS WRONG WITH YOU????" THE CHILD IS 11!!! She is witnessing the most terrifying thing in her life!!! She is seeing her neighborhood destroyed! Her father in a petrified stupor after seeing people vaporized! She is seeing man in his most animalistic behavior!!! WHAT DO YOU EXPECT HER TO DO??? "oh, look. Monsters are destroying everything I hold near and dear. Oh drat. Here come the aliens, coming after me again. Oh dear, someone is holding a gun to father's head so they can steal our car - blah, blah, blah. Shall we have tea?" You guys are insane if you think you wouldn't be needing to change your pants if this kind of thing went down in your neighborhood! Give me a break! Yes, Cruise's character is a butt. He's a blue collar man with emotional issues towards his re-married ex-wife and the kids he doesn't connect with. Yes, his son is a butt. He's a teenage boy with emotional issues towards his divorced parents and a dad he isn't quite sure he wants to associate with. And yes, the daughter, while not a butt, does have issues and a few emotional problems. Yes, there is a shot of someone taking digital pictures and using a camcorder after the lightening storm causes everything electrical or battery operated to stop. So what? Here's your chance to list it as a goof on IMDb. Your so eagle eyed, YOU go get a job as a film editor! You don't like how Spielberg tells a story or directs the characters or the direction he takes the movie in? SO WHAT! YOU go get a director's hat and bull horn and make your own movie!! Lord, love a duck people! It's a movie! It's escapism! We went to see this movie because we wanted to be entertained. And you know what? It entertained the heck out of us!! It sucked us in! We bought it! I'm a mom of a 10 year old daughter and when Rachel (Fanning) started losing it that first time, my eyes were full of tears for that child. When Robbie (Chatwin) was being a smart mouth toward his dad (Cruise) I wanted to smack him! When those stupid machines started rising from the earth and zapping whatever moved, I about crushed my husbands hand! When Rachel and Ray are in that basement and that thing comes looking for them?? Good Lord, I was holding my breath. (That darn Spielberg.) And I beg to differ with the "critics" out there who said Cruise's character couldn't care a less about his kids - were you watching the same movie? From moment one, once the invasion started, his only thought was to keep those kids from harm and get them to the only place he thought they would be safe - with their mother. When Robbie would not take no for an answer about watching the Army fight the machines and Ray is screaming at him to come back with him to where he left Rachel - oy. A father having to choose which child to save. The emotion on his face was about as real as you could imagine. Meryl Streep gets an Oscar nomination for playing that kind of role in "Sophie's Choice" - while Cruise gets his teeth kicked in about how unconcerned he acts towards his kids.

Oh well, as I said everyone has their own opinion. So do yourself a favor. See this movie and form your own opinion. Those who complain they spent full price to see it - boohoo. Ever hear of a matinÃ©e? Go see it. Love it or hate it - whatever. At least see it for yourself!

title: This Movies Is The Boyo (best movie ever) A Must See
review: This movie has to be the best Alien movie in history. The events in this movie could actually happen, and Spielberg shows what can happen, where as other films such as Signs is completely stupid, Aliens being scared of water, this film shoes what could really happen to the Aliens. The acting is immense in this film, especially from Dakota and Tom. The special effects really bring the movie to life, its pratically drags you into the movie and you feel what the actors feel and how terrible the onslaught is. I have to say although that this movie should be a 15 not a 12A as to be frank it could give kids nightmares for life. In the first 30 minutes people get cut up, blood is all over.

review: I feel compelled to try and answer some of the "gameboy", "play station" experts who have panned some of the storyline in this fine film. Okay so the machines were termed unstable by rule because they were tripods. Did you happen to notice that the aliens were also three limbed? That was their standard for stability. Silly of them not to check with us, eh? Secondly: So the aliens didn't have the "unknown virus" thingy checked out. How moronic of them! Who in the universe wouldn't plan on "post occupational hazards"? Hum...lemme see! Nope! No one we humans have seen lately.eeeeeeeRIGHT! Thirdly: So the "video game" crowd was disappointed that they didn't see the "BIG BATTLE OVER THE HILL" and instead had to endure the drama of Ray attempting to save his son from going to and dying in a futile conflict. Fourth: "Why would the aliens 'death-ray' the very people they plan to harvest, subjugate or maybe democratize?" What invading force would be stupid enough to unleash something like, oh let's call it "shock and awe" on it's intended victims in an attempt to subdue their will to fight? (Shrug!Got me!) Fifth: The machines were 'planted' a million years ago when no humans populated the planet? (Anticipation maybe? They got an advanced poof copy of Genisis maybe?) How silly of their military leaders not to set the stage for our annihilation while we watched! And the guys installing the sewers and such didn't bump into this cache of weapons of mass destruction. Could they have possibly been a mile deep? These guys...(It was easy to see this was not a multi-gendered invasion force. Oh, you missed THAT detail Einstein?)... knew how to dig BIG DEEP holes! Too many machines? Too much overkill? How 'bout a Haliburton style budget on their planet except that they get what they pay for? Sixth, Seventh, Eigth, Ninth and Tenth lumped together: What killed them? Why did their machines wobble and fall? What happened to their force field armor? Didn't like the lightning bolt arrival? Some loon reading "My Pet Goat" while the the nation is under attack? Be real! Now how serious could THAT have been?) Relax people! Now personally I would have liked to have seen some leadership moments coming from Washington but...I guess there was brush to be cleared in Texas.

title: Spray the Blood
review:
This was a good GROSS movie. The aliens were gross and made FOG HORN SOUNDS just before they would start zapping everybody in sight. I was grossed out and creep-ed out how sinister the tripods appeared to be. Miranda Otto was a great actress in this movie and proved herself to be way more versatile than the Miranda Otto of LORD OF THE RINGS.

title: Good Action Film
review: I rate this movie purely for what it is -- an action movie with alien invaders. Kind of like Independence Day. If you are looking for a movie that is entertaining, I highly recommend this. People have complained that this movie has no plot. My response is that getting attacked by aliens IS the plot. There's not supposed to be too much to the movie, therefore, making it a movie for nearly everyone. (I wouldn't recommend bringing young kids to it. They may be frightened.) Had there been an extensive plot we would be in that movie theater for hours. If I wanted to go see a drama then I would have gone to see Cinderella Man (also a very good movie) or some other movie. I wanted to see a good action film and that's exactly what I got.

title: A brilliant modern-day horror film
review:
I loved it in a way I haven't loved a movie in a long time. I loved it for truly disturbing me, for really keeping me unnerved. I don't scare easily, but the building of horror upon horror in this film really got under my skin. I walked in thinking I'd probably "like" it or enjoy it, but that there really wasn't much left to do with an alien invasion movie, especially in a story already done. I was wrong. Whatever was going on in my head and my heart during the events of 9/11, Spielberg managed to tap right into that part of me again.

Oh, and Oscars for Dakota Fanning, Michael Babcock (sound designer... BEST SOUND IN A MOVIE... EVER!!!!) and Dennis Muren.

I know some have faulted it for not showing us enough big SFX battles. That is like the son, Robbie. He had to see it. It's something inside of us that keeps us glued to the TV on days like 9/11, or when the US invaded Iraq. We have to see it. But in this movie, we are completely limited to what Ray sees and experiences, with few exceptions. I thought that was kind of brilliant, and by never taking us out of his shoes, that's what makes the horror work. It's immersive in a way similar (in effect) to Blair Witch Project, without having to rely on a video camera. So in the end, we're like Robbie. We want to see it all. When we go to movies, we're used to seeing it all, as if the audience is omniscient. When we don't see it, it gets under our skin. And when what happens does happen, it's all the more effective.

I loved the ending, especially for not taking the easy way out: to try to outdo everything that's been done before.

title: This movie is Crazy
review: I have to admit Tom Cruise was not quite as good in this movie as he normally is, but Dakota Fanning was an amazing actress and quite frankly did a better job than Cruise. If you go for nothing else, go to see her. The movie itself was lacking in some dialog areas and there were more than a few holes in the plot sequence, but the action was amazing, Steven Spielberg did a stunning job coordinating the action sequences. The movie contains elements of the cheesy movies from the 60s but it makes them seem more real with the higher budget! Sure, the entire time you're thinking, yeah right, but at the same time, there's an eerie element of realness to the whole thing. On the whole, I don't know if I would buy the DVD when it comes out, but it's worth the price of a movie ticket. It was pretty good. Though I have to agree with others, the ending was pretty lame.

title: Incredible special effects and great summer movie
review:
Man, I really liked this movie!!! I know part of it might be from all the hype and some of the reviews I read at Ain't It Cool News, but I've seen through the hype on most movies, so I think my opinion is real. My wife really liked it too, and she is very honest when it comes to movies, even if she knows I like them.

War of the Worlds is a screen adaptation of the novel written by H.G. Wells in which aliens from another planet come to destroy the inhabitants of earth. In the movie, we follow Ray Ferrier (Tom Cruise) and his son (Justin Chatwin) and daughter (Dakota Fanning) as they attempt to escape the terror and destruction of the aliens and go to Boston where Ray's ex-wife (Miranda Otto) is supposed to be. Ray is a terrible father to his children, who seem to barely know him, but he seems to get a new lease on their relationship by surviving this ordeal.

The special effects in this movie are the BEST I've ever seen, and I am predicting an Oscar for best visual effects. The movie, on the other hand, won't win an Oscar for much else, but I really enjoyed watching it for more than the special effects. This film is terrifying, real, grips you from the very first alien sequence and doesn't let go until the end. You are on the edge of your seat the entire time, wondering what is going to happen next. And speaking of the first alien sequence - watching the way the aliens kill people has to be seen to be believed. It is spectacular and horrifying at the same time. The ending is okay, and stays true to the book from what I hear, but I was expecting something more spectacular.

Besides some of the plot holes, this movie is just awesome. The acting is great, and the effects and meant to only be seen in a theater. Please go out and see this movie before you rent it, and you won't be sorry. I'm going to try and see it again soon!

title: Its GREAT
review: Every time I saw a commercial I would always say "Oh! I can't wait!" This movie was phenomenal!! I loved it! I'm not a big Sci-fi person, but this movie was great. I loved the plot and everything about it. There were a few sore spots in it but i didn't care. The action is great. It makes your heart beat way faster than usual. The entire cast put on a great performance. Special effects were heart pounding and this movie kept you on the edge of your seat from beginning to end. Well worth the time and money. my favorite actor in this movie was not Tom Cruise, but the new and upcoming star, Justin Chatwin. What a Hettie...

title: a great movie
review: in war of the worlds the first 3/4's of the movies is pure genius and old school Spielberg. The movie follows a dad (cruise) who is divorced and has two kids he barely knows.Cruises ex wife is going on a trip to Boston and gives cruise the kids for the weekend. Cruise a horrible parent try to learn more about his children until a violent lightning storm erupts next to his home. The ensuing events after this lead to a mass alien invasion and Tom cruise his daughter (fanning) and his son on a fight for survival from the alien invasion. This was a great movie..it frightened and excited with its amazing special effect. The aliens were very straight forward and the movie did not trail off and get to complicated or weird like most alien sci FYI movies. Cruise plays a great role probably his best since risky business and shows off great acting skills. This movies dose not disappoint except for a bad shallow character played by Tim robins. Robbins who has not intrigue or mystery seems to just be in the movie to make it longer. All in all with the terrible movies that have been coming out lately this was a delight.

title: Really worth seeing.
review:
If this were released in 1953 it would have given new meaning to the rating system, (G, PG13, etc). The acting was very good. Dakota, the girl that played the daughter, really stoled the show. I used to get nightmares as a kid from the aspects of movies like War of the Worlds, The Blob and Dr Who and the Daleks (1963, I hope they redo it), the whole aspect of the world being invaded by creatures from another planet really did not come to me as that unbelievable. Then life happened, I get night mares from it now. And now the same story this well done will be influencing my dreams with the same cast of characters (three legged creatures from another planet) coming to take over.

Suppliment

I notice that a lot of people have comment about how bad this movie is and the flat acting of Mr. Cruise. I have even read some people tell Mr. Spielberg to stick to the story line. For the situation, aside from sometimes thinking Dakota's screaming was a bit loud, everyone acted just fine. It was their character. I would like very much to know how a lot of other people would have handled themselves. The movie did have a few question mark items, like how the hell did they find a working vehicle so quickly. That and how some cameras worked while other things didn't. I firmly believe that the items that didn't work stopped working because they were on, the vehicles in the middle of the street, watches, etc, the SUV they found worked because it was parked and off when the attack happened. As for the story line I believe the original "War of the Worlds" like "Wizzard of Oz" appeared in newspapers as a story that people followed for kicks, sort of like a comic strip. There have been different versions of each book available for reading due to the editing differences of those that decided to join all the daily/weekly episodes together. The movie stuck to Mr. Wells' original thesis of a man running for his life, I read the book, it is sort of slow, really. But when it was originally written if the author was to be able to bring to words what was in the latest movie... But while everyone speaks vividly of the special effects and plot lines, no one has yet made a statement of the people being struck by the beams coming from the ship. That was a really cool effect, but probably already used in another movie.

title: a good improvement on the original
review:
If you want to be entertained then this is the movie for you!

Honestly there is nothing to complain about when it comes to the destructive action scenes. However the ending was too rushed.

In some ways its a pity they couldn't do a sequel and show how the rest of the world coped with it. As we only concentrate on 3 people all the way through.

haunting, genuinely scary at times and (for once) tom cruise was acting well.

A good movie. The aliens were also imaginatively designed as well.

a warning though. I don't know the rating of this movie (as I went to see it with the family) but DON'T bring small children to see it as some scenes WILL upset sensitive people.

title: Great special FX but only an average movie
review: I have to say that the first half of the movie had me grinning from ear to ear with the stunts and special effects!! The kids were gripping my arms with ever increasing intensity throughout the film. The sound mix is incredible and the acting of the cast is generally OK, without any stand-out performances, in my humble opinion! The problem I had with the movie is that there are some gigantic plot- holes!! And also I had the impression that there were large chunks of time missing from the movie, without any explanation. It's definitely worth seeing, especially on the big screen, just don't expect anything intellectually challenging.

title: surprise ending!
review: Here's another good movie by Spielburg. Everythings good about it; I wish it was longer! But, the ending, has a surprise in it, that probably only movie 'geeks' would like! The effects are great of course, and the suspense is greatly highlighted, because of the sound! Be sure to see the movie, in a properly constructed theatre. It is following closely, the original 1953 classic, also in great color. This original is also worth seeing, and it's shown on TV sometimes. The film has a proper rating, so mature teenagers, can handle it. Hopefully, no one will talk, or misbehave, or use a cellphone, in the theatre, when you view it. Since theatre management usually won't help, the best option is to find another seat. I'm sorry people, but the rude people of our world, rule it. Please pass the popcorn! John

title: Really a great movie!
review: Even knowing how the story ends, it was so well crafted I found myself worrying just how long the aliens would have the upper hand! The portrayal of the aliens cruelty and indifference to life was amazing. You could hear a pin drop in the packed theater! Tom Cruise did a very believable job of conveying the determination and despair of a father who is trying desperately to safeguard his children in a world gone crazy. Yes, the film it evoked memories of 9/11, but while many have suggested it was deliberate, I believe that any film from now until the next generation, depicting carnage on this scale, will always remind us of 9/11!

title: Did I see a different movie?
review:
I am wondering if I saw a different movie than some other.

I have to admit when I first heard Spielberg and Cruise were doing this movie I was very apprehensive. Although I have some issues with the film, but overall they pulled it off.

One of the most frequent complaints is the camcorder running after the aliens land. If you listened to the TV broadcast prior to the aliens appearing, it was stated the the EMP effects where temporary. Personally, I think temporary EMP effects are bull, but it gives a thin cover for the camcorder. Of course, this cover is bull when you consider that a car's electronics (which are probably more robust than a camcorders) do not recover from the effects of an EMP.

Same with the only running car. I think Spielberg's theory is if the solenoids are not in a car they would not be effected by the EMP and the mechanic tells Cruise that when he replaced them the car worked, so Cruise knew there was at least one working car.

There are many things that don't seem to work, but I have learned to try and shut off the analytical side of my brain for Spielberg movies.

But among those I wonder about: How these giant machines remained undiscovered under major metropolitan areas for so long.

How an unarmed Cruise killed a crazy Robbins who had a shovel in his hand and was looking at Cruise when he closed the door? I did find the fact that Cruise killed Robbins only on the pretext that he MAY give them away refreshing and unusual for a Spielberg movie. This was 1st degree murder.
