review: i loved the movie very entertaining but there were so many mistakes like when they were in the basement at there moms and every thing outside was destroyed THERE CAR WAS STILL THERE IN PERFECT CONDITION. and WHAT WAS killing the aliens? and when the first robots came the was a guy with a camera taking pictures and there was a guy with a video camera how could those have worked if there was no power? why were they spraying blood every where why did the aliens do that? and what were the birds doing? a lot of unanswered questions I have someone please answer me the movie was good and entertaining though. I really liked it the CGI was amazing

title: Wow. This year's Best
review:
You can pretty much rest assured that those placing poor reviews of this film, are simply 'following orders' from the "attack-Tom-Cruise- for-speaking-his-opinion-on-the-drug-industry" crowd.

It is a fantastic film. Chilling. Intense. Epic. Visually stunning, and I have not had this much fun at a theater in years. After having seen both originals (made in the 70's) - the European version, and the American version - you'd think, since I knew what was coming I wouldn't be on the edge of my seat. Well...I was on the edge of my seat many times thru-out this movie. Well directed, well acted, and true to the original story. Its great. Go see it.

title: Speilbergs latest work proves the old man still can surprise...
review:
Speilbergs latest blockbuster contains everything you would expect from a Hollywood production of such scale; explosions, sci-fi, based upon a successful book etc but i was impressed none the less. Spielberg has bought something new to the table it would seem by deifying Hollywood convention.

In H.G. Wells novel we follow the actions of a single male heroine, the book is set in Victorian England, of course Hollywood demands that much of the books charm be sacrificed for special effects and modern and easily identifiable setting but the film remains true to one of the most important aspects of the Narrative. In previous sci-fi - such as Armageddon & Independence Day there are multifaceted narratives, the audience is allowed to identify with a variety of characters with different perspectives giving the audience an omnipotent view of the film world i.e. the president, will smith and Jeff Goldblums characters in independence day. In this way we become spectators, voyeurs over the film world - an established convention in this genre. War of the Worlds stays true to the novel in that we follow the plight of Tom Cruises character and no others, I found that identifying with this character constantly was more involving and gripping than such films as Independence day, where the audience is so alienated from the film that it is hard to involve one's self emotionally with the characters.

Apart from this, the film is visually stimulating, the effects are beyond pretty much anything I have seen and a shot in such a way that you actually fell in the action. The Tri-pods look and move fantastically, the film actually scares me, which is unusual. I would suggest this film for anyone who is a lover of action/sci fi and special effects, in terms of dialogue and characterisation the film offers very little but it will appeal to the inner child in anyone - go to the cinema to watch this, it deserves a big screen despite Cruise's usual two dimensional acting.

title: War of the Worlds-Genius
review: Spielbergs war of the worlds is simply genius a combination of sci-fi, horror, suspense and action all packed into 2 hours making it one of the most thoroughly enjoying experiences u will ever find. some criticisms has been made of the ending but i loved the simple approach Spielberg made to the movie through the eyes of Cruises character Ray Ferrier. Visually this film cannot not be touched the tripod ships are menacing to look as are the creepy martians. John Williams musical score is simply brilliant and proves reliable to Spileberg as hes done in the past with film like Jaws and Schindlers List. Srong performances from everybody including Cruise and a brilliant Dakota Fanning. H.G. Wells would be proud of Spielbergs adaption as the intended horror and chills are maintained throughout. This proves why Spileberg is still the greatest director to ever grace the cinematic world.

title: Wow! A real ball-tearer of a movie
review: After the recent Tom Cruise and Katie shows I was quite prepared to be put off by Tom in this movie but I have to say that he really can act. The emotion he shows is really compelling and Spielberg has produced a movie to surpass all other horror movies. This movie is certainly not for the tiny tots or weak of stomach as this is realism of the first order. The metaphors in the movie stand out - Tom covered in a fine dust - What is it? It's the dust produced by evaporated people a la September 11. The extermination of the human race by a superior race - the holocaust again and the ultimate triumph of the human race over the exterminators. My only quibble is over the ending which was a real downer. Steven, surely Miranda Otto could have at least rushed up to Tom and hugged/kissed him for bringing her children back safely rather than Tom just standing there in the distance and getting just an appreciative glance from Miranda.

title: The Tripods looks spectacular
review:
From design, modelling, animation and final rendering, the Tripods are a paragon of Alien design.

Streamlined, aggressive and terrifying, I have never witnessed aliens like this on film. The head is a circular front light display capped off by a helmet. The legs are 3 taped tentacles. Two at the front, one at the back. They end in three pronged hands. The other smaller tentacles they have top off the look. The only humour in the film comes from the aliens. Sucking up people with a tentacled straw and later pissing them out as red weed fertiliser. The aliens in the cellar spinning a wheel was a good touch. So was the tripod reflections in car windows.

They rock man, they make the film.

title: Great suspense film
review: Having read a lot of the reviews, I find it amazing that people are trying to find the tiniest cracks in the movie to try and tear it down. This is about FANTASY and ESACPISM folks! My wife and I saw this movie tonight and we both agreed that it was one of the best films we've seen in a long while. As with any sci-fi film, you have to suspend your belief in a few things. Yes, there is a scene where a guy's cam-corder is working when all other electronic items have ceased working. But if that alone ruined what was happening at that particular moment in the movie, then you weren't going to be interested to begin with. The effects were brilliant, not to mention the sound. Hearing what was basically a horn coming from the alien ships, and to have it make your skin crawl after a few times of hearing it - well only a great director could do that. And you won't look at dust the same way ever again. Or a train crossing. Filming from the POV of Cruise's character and his family was awesome. You saw what they saw which was just enough to keep you unnerved. The acting was as good as you could hope for - after all, they were running for their lives for most of the movie. Personally, I think this was such a superior film to ID4. No huge famous landmarks to destroy - just everyday stuff, which makes it more personal. And we aren't a "fly on the wall" with the President or his Generals to find out what we're going to do to fight back. We just go along with Ray and his family and the rest of the ordinary folks, trying to find a place to hide - much more terrifying. The ending was appropriate. Again, we are seeing this as Cruise (Ray) and his family saw it. The general of the army isn't going to happen to be on that street to explain his battle plans to civilians passing by. It's also true to the book, which is that bacteria kills the aliens. End of story. Great movie - best of the year.

title: A note on the camcorder incident by the previous reader
review: I think he misunderstood one thing. The reason all electronic equipment stopped was due to the possible EM radiation possibly caused by the lightning, and not the tripods. If you noticed the tripods shot a heat ray, therefore no EM radiation, hence the camcorder and the van worked. Also, remember the reason the van worked? Manni? The only thing I also did not like was the sudden ending, but I guess by then I was too peaked out and just wanted more. I think H.G. Wells would be proud of Mr. Spielberg. Thanks Stephen, for another job well done. At our showing, the audience walked out exhausted and dazed. Tom is as always true to his career. He really submerges himself in his work. As for Dakota, well, what can you say? I remember her in "Trapped", "Man on Fire", etc. and thought she had a good career on her hands but I think she really showed what she's capable of doing at such a tender age. I have a question for Mr Spielberg...will the DVD contain extra footage? Something that maybe was left off due to time restraints? With the DVD at home, we can always pause to go to the restroom, get a bite to eat, etc. so time is not a restraint here. If you have additional footage, please bring it on. It'll just make the nerves get crazier, but at least we'll be home to take something to help us relax, during or after the movie.

title: a good IL' alien invasion movie
review:
War Of The Worlds is not one of Spielberg's best, but it's not his worst. Despite what some people say about the movie, it is a good sci-fi/action flick. The special effects in this movie is amazing. Some of the best since Lord Of The Rings and much more realistic then the effects in the Star Wars preqels.

Some people complain that Tom Cruise ruined the movie, but I thought he was pretty good. It really doesn't matter what people say because Tom Cruise is a good actor. I did find Dakota Fanning sometimes annoying... I just felt like throwing her out a window or something... maybe that's what Spielberg wanted, who knows? Anyways, I give this movie a 7/10.

title: Sci-fi for real
review:
Well. I liked this one. I'll give you three reasons.

1. It's dark. Actually, it's scary all the way through. I can't even remember hearing a single witty one liner. Much of the earth is destroyed and billions of people are killed, that shouldn't be funny. It should be dark.

2. In it's genre it felt real. Granted, aliens invading earth to drink our blood can never feel real. This one just about pulls it off, though. The focus on one family works wonders. They don't really know what's going on and don't have a lot of answers. They just try to survive. A focus on, say, the president or the military would have meant weapons, tactics and heroes. The feeling of presence and relating would be lost in such a big and formal perspective.

3. Visuals. Very impressive. The illusion didn't break once.

I'm sure a lot of people will have many objections and unanswered questions about this one. What did the aliens want? Wouldn't such a technologically advanced species be able to prevent what ends up killing them? But for me, that's what's good about it. The darkness, presence and sense of relating would have been somewhat lost if all questions were answered. Who could possibly have answers in the midst of annihilation and confusion? This was nothing like Independence Day. It was more like Alien, gritty and claustrophobic. This is sci-fi for grown ups.

title: Something New
review: Well I've been looking forward to War Of The Worlds since i new Spielberg and Cruise were again working together. I feel they pull it off, Tom Cruise plays a father of two very well. He shines in the role of the caring father throughout the film. Dakota Fanning is brilliant she continues to show off her skills of acting at such a young age, i find amazing. Justin Chatwin plays the arrogant son to perfection, he along with Dakota Fanning will be around a long time after seeing these performances. Spielberg again makes another good movie not great like Shindler's list but a good solid movie that many people will enjoy. He mixes his special effects in well and the storyline is very much original. Not saying too much on the movie don't want to give it away, but i feel many people who go to see this movie will enjoy it but i can see others not getting to grips with it. I however found this movie exciting and different 9 out of 10 for me!! Enjoy!!

title: This movie didn't quite cut it
review:
This movie was a real let down. It truly was. The trailers and commercials only show the good stuff, but when you watch the movie, it leaves you feeling disappointing and hollow.

The overall movie is really good, but Spielberg leaves out too much from the book. The son of Ray Ferrier is Robbie, and i really don't like him. I wanted him to die. And he probably should have. The last thing we see is Robbie walking over to watch the army fight the tripod, and a massive explosion occurs, and all we see is the robot on fire, and still alive.

The end really sucked, and all of a sudden they show Robbie is alive. There is enough suspense and acting to make it a good movie, but it just could have been better.

title: A new caliber for disaster movies * lite spoilers *
review: I can honestly say I can't remember a single disaster movie I've seen that I even marginally liked. Whether it be tornadoes and floods, or volcanoes and asteroids, there has just never been a movie that has done justice to the visual destruction of our civilization. Every ounce of destruction in this movie is awe-inspiring. Everything that falls, blows up or dies is witnessed through the characters in such a way that is shown not just for the special effects category at an award ceremony, but to put into perspective just how horrifying and intimidating these invaders are. And intimidating they are. This is bar-none the most brutal and efficient evil I've ever seen in a movie. It's as if humanity is nothing more than an infestation; being dealt with by an exterminator with a million magnifying glasses. For once, the world being brought to it's knees by it's destruction seems plausible. And humanity doesn't just rally together and fight the good fight, people do all they can to survive, often times at the expense of others, sometimes justified, sometimes selfishly. And it's all done so well, that when a question arises as to why something happens or how did this person survive, it doesn't even matter, because with all of the chaos and horror that has just ensued, anything seems possible. As benevolent as E.T. was, these aliens are malevolent. Truly intimidating, and more importantly, believable, this movie in it's affect is unique.

title: Dazzling effects give War of the Worlds an edge...
review: In Steven Spielberg's adaptation of the H.G. Wells novel War of the Worlds, Tom Cruise plays Ray Ferrier, a divorced father who has his kids Rachel and Robbie, played by Dakota Fanning and Justin Chatwin, over his home in New York. Suddenly the world is attacked by "tripods" as they are called and havoc breaks loose. The sheer terror in the faces of people give the movie realistic qualities, even though it seems like this could never happen. When these visitors attack, people run, like any other "When aliens attack" movie. What makes this movie so different from Independence Day and all others of this genre is the realism, the "What is..." factor. M. Nigght Shamylan's Signs is another film that comes to mind, a movie that shows what would happen if regular people are thrown into an extraordinary situation. If you are in the mood to be dazzled, scared, and entertained, go see War of the Worlds.

title: Partially satisfied, but very upset with the Hollywood ending.
review:
First of all, I don't know how closely this film follows the book and I can't watch dated SCI-FI movies, because the technology bugs me.

Pros - 1. The first 2/3 of the movie was intense and it hit the ground running within 10 minutes. 2. Tom Cruise did a decent job acting for the first at least 2/3 of the movie. 3. The Special Effects were awesome. 4. I was entertained, and this is important. The movie was not totally meaningless like "The Hulk" or "Darkness" (two movies that I've seen recently. 5. There were many intense scenes where I felt my self actually caring about what would happen next.

Some spoilers down here. Cons - There are probably more, but these are the ones that bothered me most. 1. Dakota Fanning! I am usually impressed with this little girl's acting ability, and even though her character was to play a girl with some obvious mental issues and phobias, the screaming was just too much. I wanted to scream out, "shut up!", on several occasions. 2. The entire neighborhood is wiped out by an airliner, but for some reason the minivan sitting in the middle of flaming debris, that the Ferrier family was driving, manages to stay completely in tact and there isn't a problem driving through all of the debris when they leave. 3. In the middle of the movie, the son decides that he must prove something to himself by running into a big ball of fire developed by the aliens. He obviously bought the farm here. The fact that one of the main characters "dies", actually brings some heart to the movie, but I just didn't get the kid's reasoning. Please dad, let me go commit suicide. I will do it bravely. 4. Although I actually enjoyed the character played by Tim Robbins, it seemed like he was playing the resurrected character that he played in "Mystic River". Hmmm, is he being type-casted? 5. I thought the aliens in the cellar scene was stupid (or at least the aliens seemed stupid), even though I understand it's purpose was to show the audience that they were breathing our air and drinking our water, which was important to understand the ending. 6. Now for the cheap "hollow"wood ending. After the aliens start to die off because they can't live in our environment, we see that somehow after going through hell, Ray Ferrier and his daughter manage to make it to their destination in Boston, where his pregnant ex-wife, her husband, and her parents look like they were living in an area that the aliens seemed to miss. It must have something to do with the lifting of the "Curse of the Bambino". The people all come to the door and they look all nice and clean, like they were living in there own private Idaho in downtown Boston. OK, so I'll let them go on this. Afterall, everyone likes a happy ending, right? Then, just when I thought the movie would be fine if they just ended it there, the son (yes the one that should have died) comes out of the house and hugs his dad. Now why would they do this? I felt betrayed. This wasn't a surprise. It was just stupid. It made me lose all emotion for the movie, and regret that I actually started to care for the other two characters.

Here are some other technical things that I questioned when I heard or saw them.

1. How stable would those tripod machines actually be? 2. If the machines were buried in the ground for who knows how long, wouldn't these aliens have produced something far more advanced over the years? 3. It seemed like the aliens were using the humans as a method of fuel, later in the movie. If this is the case, what were they using when they first appeared and starting wiping the humans out? 4. It cracked me up when the military guy in the basket says "get down", after he sees the grenade pins come out of Ray's mouth. Where was everyone supposed to get down to? 5. When the para-scope eye thing was roaming around in the cellar, I thought it should have been able to see the people running around. 6. Would fixing just the solenoid on a car make it suddenly operate after an EMP type situation? Did I miss something? Did the guy say that he replace the battery? I actually thought the engine block sitting in his house would play a bigger part. Do video cameras work without solenoids or something, since at least two of them remained operational during the attacks?

I gave this movie 6 out of 10, because I was entertained throughout and the special effects were awesome. Like Maximus said in Gladiator, "Are you not entertained". Though there were some obvious flaws throughout the movie, I still enjoyed most of it. If it wasn't for the stupid ending, I probably would have given it a 7 or 8. Because of the ending, I wanted to actually give it a 3 or less, but then I realized that with that one exception, it was still a decent show. I also gave it a 1 point bonus because of SCI-FI content.

For all of those people rating this movie at ones and twos, if you want to see a movie that is truly deserving of such a low rating, go rent House of the Dead or Alone in the Dark - These are some of the worst movies I have ever seen (ironically, these movies were both done by the same director).

title: Lacks Intensity
review: Well, I think that Wells would have liked the movie. It is technically well done, the aliens & their machines are depicted very much like they are in the book, the visuals are keeping viewers on the edge of their seats. Some scenes are quite intense, especially memorable is the scene, when a burning train is going past the crowd of scared people & of course the battle scenes are breathtaking. I also liked a moment, when the crowd, consumed by fear, is ready to do anything to get the car, showing that humans are just as cruel as aliens. The acting was very good, yet Dakota's part was rather irritating. Direction though is somewhat questionable. I got an impression, that the film is rushed. I think it should've been longer. It doesn't have tension slowly building up as in The Independence Day. The aliens are appearing way too abruptly. We don't see much of the consequences of the war to the humanity, cause the story basically rotates around the Ferrier family & the action mainly takes place in small towns. Needless to say, that scenes of destruction of The Capitol, Empire State Building & the city of Los Angeles in The Independence Day looked more intense, showing the scale of the tragedy. The other small flaw of the War of the Worlds is that we have too little characters introduced. And, boy, how the hell Robbie survives? Now, that's way too unrealistic, even for this genre. And what the hell with the aliens: the scenes with the mirror & bicycle were irrelevant. Spielberg tries with the help of humor to relieve the tension, which is not really there & thus ruins a bit a dark & despair atmosphere, which is only starting to build up. I don't know, but I think that this film has got it all right, except the direction, which is not quite matching the whole thing. A movie like this would be more successful, if James Cameron or at least Roland Emmerich was in the director's chair. The film lacks tragedy, drama, emotional intensity, pain & agony. It's too light. It does keep you focused, but more because of the special effects & music. Something's not there. It could've been better.

title: Death and destruction with present day parenting ability
review: For the films first 20 - 30 minutes the film really had my mind racing, but, for the rest of the movie we were stuck in a story line of Ray Ferrier's abilities as a father with a few injected alien attacks. Don't get me wrong I enjoy an emotional aspect to a movie such as this; all disaster movies need some drama so we'll embrace or hate the characters (for reference check out the 70's library of disaster movies). However, this movie had so much eye candy to offer I felt like it could have given the audience more fight so the movie would have more balance. I do feel it is a good movie and Spielberg did have his work cut out for him with the original already being a sci-fi masterpiece. He said it isn't a remake, which explains the character development being more explored than the original. The special effects are magnificent, the way the aliens exterminate us humans is a original concept. The tripods are crafted extremely well and the sounds they emanated made my deafness worthwhile. The aliens however seem a bit goofy looking. In the end, I do recommend the movie; it is worth the ticket price.

title: Good enough for an evening at the movies
review:
Simple plot, aliens, and Dakota fanning. I know what you're thinking, its a flop. Well I'm happy to report that it is quite the contrary. While its certainly not one of Spielberg's best works, it is certainly good enough to see at least once in the theater.

The plot goes something like this: Ray Ferrier is divorced. He lives in New Jersey and today happens to be his weekend to spend with his kids, Robby and Rachel. Unfortunately he's not that great a father and his kids don't really like him that much. Things start to go awry and before you know it alien tripods (activated by alien controlled lightning storms) start to rise from the ground and start attacking the city. While this happens all electronic devices stop working and Ray happens to get the only working car and takes his kids on a quest first to their mother and then just for survival. Thats about it. Its not exactly thought provoking, but since when has a Spielberg film have a great plot? (besides Minority Report of course) The movie can best be looked at in two ways. One way is as an alien movie, and the other is a movie where all the characters are hopeless and panicked trying to find any way to survive. When the movie sticks to the survival aspect it is quite successful. There is a scene where a group of people violently attack Ray and his kids because they are the only people with a car. I wont tell you how that scene ends but it is quite unnerving. Tons of scenes of human desperation make this movie quite interesting, and at some points very suspenseful and almost scary. The other parts where its simply the aliens attacking are less impressive. While the effects are quite good, spectacular at some points, it never is really too exciting. Once the machines start picking people off, the horror of whats happening seems to go down. The reason is that since we don't know these people so we don't care about them when they meet their demise. When the aliens are specifically attacking Ray and the kids, it becomes much better.

Now lets talk about the characters. Ray is completely unlikable for the first part of the film. He is ignorant and a horrible father. Its not Tom Cruise's fault, he does the best he can with what he's given, but nevertheless its not until the middle that we begin to like him. At this point, however, he's left to keep yelling orders and try to calm down his daughter for the rest of the film. Justin Chatwin's Robbie is a rebellious teenager who refuses to listen to his father. The part is well acted and I liked him even though he was a jerk. Dakota Fanning as Rachel is quite annoying. Her character is claustrophobic and constantly a cry baby. Even when the aliens aren't attacking she finds something to cry and scream (in terror) about. Needless to say of all the characters, I liked her the least.

The problems of the film are these. First we have no idea why the aliens are attacking us. I guess you could just say that they want to rule the planet but why? Do they want our resources, or do they just want to cause us trouble? The film doesn't make an attempt to answer this. As I said before I just wanted to shut Dakota Fanning up. Many questions about the plot are also left unanswered (those i will not go through because of spoilers) The movie does seem to last a little long, and along with that the ending seems rushed, Finally, speaking of the ending, its typical Spielberg, meaning its a happy ending meant to be uplifting. It would have been much more effective if it had a bitter-sweet ending instead.

All said, the movie is quite good. There are parts that are quite suspenseful and moving. Although the plot leaves something to be desired, this is a popcorn movie. Just sit back and enjoy. (Also if you have a girlfriend, bring her, you'll be in for some cuddling time when the "scary stuff" hits) Star rating: 3.5 out of 5

title: See it for the Effects, Enjoy the Ride
review:
I am always eager for Spielberg to 'wow' movie audiences again in creating big movie moments, last seen with "Jurassic Park" and "Saving Private Ryan". One thing that bothered me about the making of this film was the rush to production, and merely months to create a huge blockbuster that could normally take a year. My fear was that some special effects could look unfinished, or the film editing not quite refined. My guess is that every last hour was exhausted getting this film in the can, and some parts of the film are unbalanced.

But first the fantastic news, the special effects, which there are aplenty, are definitely up to snuff. Although, there were quite a few feathered matte lines associated with very active camera shots filled in with ominous clouds. There is a fun "circling the van" set piece that resembles a few CGI intensive car commercials. My guess is that the only really thing in that shot besides the actors were the seats they were sitting on, and the rest of the van was photo-real CGI. This film really is another feather in the cap for ILM, able to conjure clouds, fire, water, as well as creepy aliens. One thing for sure, this is the film I really wanted to see when I was lured into seeing Shylaman's "Signs" (see my review). We get a great revisit of ILM's great achievements. A recreation (or perhaps borrowed to save time) of the 'water tentacle' from "Abyss". The fearsome cloud effects seen originally in "Twister". Then the velociraptors that stalked in "Jurassic Park".

Spielberg also pushes the amusement park ride by defying logic and allowing our main characters to be literally inches away from every battle and massacre that occurs within driving distance. But the script and story seem to get lost. In the first half of the movie, we feel the terror quite effectively by witnessing very widespread death and destruction. But the second half lacks momentum, as Cruise and his kids lose focus and can't quite spell out their plans. The relentless fight for survival in the first half is replaced by darkness and depression, instead of hope and determination. The scattered second half is what I feel could've been tightened up with a little more time for refinement. I'm not spoiling too much by saying that the last part of the film takes place in a single basement, and loses it's earlier large scope. The expectation is for this dark creepy basement to give you the whillikers, but after a while I felt like I would rather take my chances and run away instead of hangout in some creep's cellar.

I also think a tighter script would have produced other poignant moments if they were fleshed out better. A few more side characters would've added depth. A few less family quarrels would've prevented being a turn-off for audiences. "Close Encounters" maintains that balance, again with the added depth of some side characters. In other words, Spielberg has his cake but does not get to eat it too. He gives us great eye candy, but it is hard to swallow the human side. But in this case, I don't care. Having spent a while to think about WOTW, weighing the good parts with the average parts, I feel about 80% satisfied. I rank it better than "Minority Report", but not as groundbreaking as "Jurassic Park".

As far as supplanting the 1950's version as the new classic? Of course not.

title: Very intense the whole time.
review:
This movie was very intense and sometimes downright scary. The realism and possibility of this actually happening alone is enough to make it viewable.

Cruise and the rest of the crew are as good as you can get when it comes to casting. And what a better actor to get than Tom Cruise, a person who follows a "religion" that believes we were attacked by aliens millions of years ago. The storyline again is realistic and very possible if there are actual aliens.

I was on the edge of my seat the whole time and downright close to anxiety attacks because of the way Spielberg brings you up and down, up and down. Genius, pure genius.

Believe it or not, it was quite humorous and got a lot of laughter from the audience and myself. Some parts were just breathtaking visually. Of course it had top notch graphics, and the sound effects were bar none the best I've heard in a theater.

It was so loud and "in your face" at times, the speakers in the theater were actually popping and crackling. The system was just on the edge of handling these sound effects.

Enough rambling, go see this and as always, don't get too hyped up. I've found that believing the hype always gives you a let down. So just keep an open mind and go into it like a 5 year old. Spielberg is a genius, know this !!

title: War of the Worlds could be described as a mix of The Day After Tomorrow, Signs, plus some good acting and a little originality.
review: War of the Worlds could be described as a mix of The Day After Tomorrow, Signs, plus some good acting and a little originality. The first forty minutes or so are very dark and scary as 'they' slowly show their presence on earth. We see clearly each member of the family's reactions to this invasion: Ray Ferrier (Tom Cruise) tries to act cool for his kids, especially Rachel (Dakota Fanning) but still panics as he tries to keep both himself and his kids alive; Robbie (Justin Chatwin) wants Ray to tell him what's going on, he wants to fight it and protect little sister; and Rachel is frightened as no one tells her what is happening. After this extremely tense opening, the rest of the movie is mainly just the three trying to survive. Although not as intense as the opening, this does provide some eyes-shut, ears-blocked moments as the Ferriers slowly realise what is happening, and what it means for them: in order to survive, they are going to have to sacrifice others. In some ways this film is reminiscent of Nazi Germany - homeless thousands (and perhaps millions, although not shown in the film) wandering across the country, looking for a non-existent sanctuary, the race for survival, and the chilling feeling of having nowhere to run, of being cornered by an all-powerful enemy. It definitely gets under your skin. The acting is strong: Cruise, Chatwin and Fanning are all good, and although Cruise is in almost every scene of the movie, his character is not over-developed in comparison to the other two. For example, in one scene Rachel is sitting with a blindfold, singing a nursery rhyme while in another room Ray is killing a man. Instead of seeing the act itself, we see the situation from Rachel's point of view and it is infinitely more effective. There are some weaknesses: somehow a camcorder survives in working order (towards the beginning of the film) as even Ray's watch stops working, the ending of the film is rather abrupt (although thanks to HG Wells, this isn't a typical macho alien-fighting ending) and how exactly did Robbie survive that explosion? With great special effects, a token soundtrack and some good acting, with the addition of some truly edgy scenes this film deserves nine out of ten.

title: The first downright scary movie I've seen in years!!
review: I've been waiting for this movie for months now. I'm a huge fan of the original, and couldn't wait to see what Spielberg did with the concept. He didn't disappoint. While the overall plot of the movie is the same (aliens try to take over planet Earth), the underlying plots are totally different. In this one, there's a divorced dad with his two kids for the weekend, and his cluelessness quickly becomes a fierce fight to protect them. While some WOTW fans may be put off by the basic changes Spielberg made to the original script, I think most fans will rather delight in the fact that there are now two WOTW films to adore! The special effects are nothing short of dazzling! Even the sounds made by the "tripods" are haunting! If you enjoy a good "scare me! scare me!" movie, don't miss this one!!!

title: the references to colonialism
review:
Probably everyone knows the plot: the evil aliens attack defenseless Earthlings. In this version, Ray Ferrier (Tom Cruise) is a divorced New Jersey longshoreman watching his son Robbie (Justin Chatwin) and daughter Rachel (Dakota Fanning) for the weekend. Then, a most unusual lightning storm knocks out all power and a giant machine crawls out of the ground and starts killing everyone in sight.

Needless to say, Ray, Robbie and Rachel flee. But no matter where they go, the aliens are everywhere. The movie's high point comes when Ray and Rachel hide out with Harlan Ogilvy (Tim Robbins), a paranoid loner ready to fight the aliens to the death.

Knowing that H.G. Wells' original novel was an allegory for colonialism, one can certainly see it in the movie. Not just the way that the aliens are running roughshod over everyone, but in what Ogilvy says: "This isn't a war...this is extermination." Whether or not that's an allusion to the Iraq War, I don't know, but we can certainly read it as such.

Some parts of the movie are pretty predictable, but overall, I liked it. Morgan Freeman's narration isn't quite as effective as his narration in "Million Dollar Baby", but he still does quite well.

title: Great Summer Film!
review:
When first going into "War of the Worlds," you might be going to see Tom Cruise, or you might be going for Steven Spielberg, or you could just be going along for the ride, but when you leave, you'll want to go back and see it again!

This movie is fantastic when wanting to see an action adventure movie, with touching scenes containing how far a father would go to protect his kids from aliens that are extremely hostile towards the earth, and everyone in it. Tom Cruise plays Ray Ferrier, a divorced man who's more of a kid than it seems at first glance. One weekend, he's forced to watch his kids, Robbie, played by Justin Chatwin, and Rachel, played by Dakota Fanning. Considering Ray is an extremely irresponsible adult, the kids are not thrilled.

After Robbie takes Ray's car without permission, (or a license) Ray walks out front to see neighbors staring straight up above his house to see a cloud with a huge hole in the center with flashing lights, that almost looks as if it's an opening to a different galaxy. He goes inside to have Rachel take a look. As he views from the backyard of his house, the dark cloud shoots off multiple strikes of lightning, in one single spot, not too far from his home. When the storm finally stops, Robbie returns, as Ray leaves to check the single spot out, advising Robbie to stay with Rachel. Unfortunately, he finds the lightning hit spot, where the beginning of the ultimate war lays beneath his feet.

Throughout the rest of the movie, Ray tries to find peace from these deadly invaders, in order to protect his kids, which can become difficult when he hardly knows them. Along the way he runs into difficult objects, such as angry crowds of desperate people, a man in a basement who seems to be mentally insane, and figuring out that running will not protect his children, no matter how determined he is.

This movie has a great story, and has fantastic acting, but at times pulls away from getting to know the characters.

this movie also stars also stars the Lord of the Rings, Miranda Otto, and Academy Award winner Tim Robbins.

Warning: Movie contains similar references to 9/11

title: a couple minutes of plot, a few good actors and an all around amazing movie
review: I saw this at the drive in's. The screen huge, as the tripods came out of the ground i held my breath. This movie no doubt has the greatest special effects i've ever seen in my whole life. Yes Tom Cruise even pulled off a decent performance and i hate the guy and most of his movies. A lot of people are mad that Steven Spielberg relied to much on the sfx and had the storyline as an afterthought, but Spielberg did this because the movie has been made like 10 times, each one focusing on the story, and Spielberg knew that to return to greatness he would have to do something that no one has done yet with this franchise, he made the best summer adventure anyone will see in their life. Next to this movie, star wars comes out looking like the telletubbies

title: Exciting summer blockbuster, intense action
review:
Spielberg is at it again shoving Michael Bay and Roland Emmerich's noses in the crap. He shows us how to truly produce an exciting summer hit. It has all the makings and then some. You have consistently great big-name actor(Tom Cruise), up and coming child actor(Dakota Fanning), intense special effects, and explosions all for a big Hollywood budget. I'm usually not a fan of blow-em-up action films, but this one turned my head. Spielberg focused on the characters, and their true persona's unfolded as the storyline progressed; this is hard to find in a July summer blockbuster.

Its opens as Cruise's kids are less than excited to be visiting their biological father for a few days. He attempts to connect with his kids, but fails miserably. Soon an eerie storm approaches their home in New York and as Cruise explores the town to understand this phenomenon he finds himself running from a giant tripod that is disintegrating people with lasers. from there he grabs his children and attempts to find his ex-wife and the rest of his family. They have a run-in with a terrible mob and down-trodden, but willing to fight Tim Robbins(who is remarkable, one of the best scenes in the movie).

The ending falls somewhat short of whats expected of Spielberg, but it's Spielberg; One of the greatest directors of any and all generations. Consistently great i might add. who are we as the general public who only watch a bunch of movies and act as though we are the film master to say Spielberg sucks. I give it an 8/10, only because the ending was lackluster. The movie is brilliant overall.

title: I would see this one twice..
review:
You'll have to suspend your belief system for this one (as you must do for 95% of all movies). Don't get caught up in the fact that certain things don't make "sense." If Aliens truly did invade us, trust me, many things would be Unexplained.. Therefore, just relax and imagine that this could really happen and then be prepared to see a scary movie.

However, here is a simple explanation as to why you think the outcome was the way it was: I think these aliens were arrogant and didn't respect us. Anyone know what arrogance will get you when you don't respect your opponent! In addition, perhaps microbiology isn't an issue from the planet they are from, therefore, the aliens wouldn't have any specialist in this particular field, or it just didn't occur to them that germs would be a problem on Earth since its not a problem on their planet. Or it could be that when they buried their equipment 1000s or millions of years ago, there was no germ problem and they didn't bother to check again before they returned. Again, these aliens are basically terrorist and didn't respect us just as we don't respect ants. In addition, one might wonder why they didn't come up with a more efficient way to destroy us, but the fact is that they needed to kill us one by one and basically use the rest of us as nourishment for the terroforming they were conducting. Maybe it will take them 3, 5, or maybe 10 years to kill everyone, but the result is for the use of the Earth for potentially 1000s of years to come.

The point of all of this is the fact that since the movie didn't explain any of this its fun to come up with your own ideas about why the aliens screwed up, why they are here, why there technology is flawed, why certain cameras work and others don't..etc etc If you're imaginative and don't need someone to explain everything for you, then you'll enjoy this.. this is the difference between those that like it and those that don't..

title: Worst Movie Ever
review: What in the world was that? OK, I understand the need to pay homage to HG Wells and everything, but let's not forget he was writing for a different audience. People actually thought Earth was getting attacked and freaked out. We are sitting in a movie theater. There's a big difference. One of the worst parts is the lack of a plot. The whole movie consists of them running. There is hardly anything that shows a bit of understanding of what is going on, why they came, why they attacked at that point, and why the aliens look exactly like the ones in Independence Day. Then, after all this running, it just ends. They never explain what happened to the son either. Sure, it was somewhat nice to have a movie without the natural progression where they come, they beat the crap out of us, we figure some crazy way to beat them that has a small chance of working, then we beat them, but geez, develop the plot somewhat, if not even that, develop the characters. They jump into the attack 5 minutes into the movie. I might have gotten over it had the ending not come without warning and had been so stupid.

title: Strongly plotted film about a man's growth as a father...
review: I loved this movie! Yes, there are the inconsistencies regarding the electro-magnetic pulse, but that's relatively minor overall. Despite what some posters have written, the plot revolves around the character Ray Ferrier's growth as a father caught up in an epochal catastrophe--THAT'S the story--the alien invasion is the background story. It is remarkable faithful to H.G. Wells's novel, updates notwithstanding. The heroics are kept to a minimum--there is one moment that does strain credibility. Otherwise, I found the reactions of the panicked crowds all too believable. The film is filled with breathtaking imagery--it's both otherworldly and reminiscent of illustrations from older editions of the novel. I found the suspense nearly unbearable in parts, which also make this one of the most frightening movies I've seen. The performances by Dakota Fanning and Tom Cruise also deserve mention. Fanning is preternaturally convincing. Cruise delivers a deeply searching performance as an overly self-involved man, a true lout, who is broken down by fear and confusion and is forced to come to grips with what is really important. It may sound hackneyed, but it is brilliantly rendered here. Bravo to him and all others involved with this film.

title: Special Effects Kicked Ass!
review:
Well I was quit surprised that the movie was more than just a digital graphics/special effects mile stone(meaning something new to the silver screen in my opinion), however the story of the family was pretty good as well, despite the shortness of this movie in comparison to other sci- fi thrillers.

Just a reminder for people in theaters who eat chips from a crinkly ass chip bags, it's damn rude. I missed a few areas of the dialog because some @#$% was eating chips from a loud chip bag, especially when the crap head squeezed the chip bag three freaking times in a row! But other than that, his wife snatched the things away from his and chucked them down the isle, I think a few people cheered when she chucked them down the isle!

The Movie itself was well put together, though the action started pretty quick and you could get a sense that it was already happening in other parts of the world before the actual action began in the general area where the movie was based. title: Excellent to be as simplistic as one can
review:
The first thing I must say is the negative because they are few (aside from the actual premise itself). The ending is able to be gotten, but you may be caught in in prior events to fully follow it. Not so much because it is difficult, but because with so much hopelessness and tension your mind is anything but clear. Second is the continuity error some caught, when the guy is taping the attacks right after an EMP kills all in the area. Yet slightly thereafter cars started working again, so it is possible.

Next I will go on a limb and say Tom Cruise deserves nothing less than an Oscar nomination. I spoke with a friend who thought Mel Gibson could pull the role off (when I asked who else might be able to play the part). It's certainly possible and other names could certainly surface; however, Cruise's conversion in natural, understanding, foreseen, yet never blunt: it is expected and it is brilliant. Next is Dakota Fanning, she is the best child actor since Haley Joel Osmont. Justin Chatwin in his short time in the movie and limited lines gives a more than credible performance, although there is a part in the movie that is sketchy (I will not reveal it). It's not impossible and the beauty is you are lost in the moment like he and all others.

This movie does not lose you in the action. You feel hopeless when the characters do. The hardest acting was from Tim Robbins. Making a smaller show - - essentially a cameo - - could have been undone by such a big name, but he is believable and the part "chilling" as most have been describing this movie. Even Rick Gonzalez is credible enough. People act as they do in this movie and I would absolutely expect the actions we see in this movie.

The special effects are award-worthy and Spielberg makes a nearly two hour movie taut, fraught with tension, and disturbing. Honestly, I think Robbins is the sickest dude in this movie and there are some sick, desperate people. Cruise, there, is phenomenal and Fanning may be even better.

The writing is excellent. I half expect to hear of major paranoia being prevalent the next time, well, you'll see. It is no secret now the movie's premise of invasion, nor even their method of travel as alluded to in the line before. God is the greatest, quietest star of this film. Spielberg doesn't blunt you with religion, but it is clear how he feels. Nature is God's truest creature and, we humans, the master of it, right? Overall this is an incredible movie that fulfills Tommy Lee Jones' proclamation that "a person is smart, but people are dumb, panicky animals and you know it."

title: Way Better then Expected!
review:
Spielberg has done a superb job making this movie which is highly original from the 1953 version. In it Tom Cruise is an irresponible divorced father who is given charge of his two children for the weekend. The movie is about how he has to cope with death all around him while keeping his children and himself from becoming mad.

There are some real touching and heart wrenching scenes especially when his young daughter is witnessing the horrors of people being vaporized and hungry mobs attacking their car.

The special effects are phenomenal and the story grips you from start to finish.

There were a few confusing things like what the aliens were actually doing to the humans. It seems like they were mixing the humans' blood with some sort of plant to create vines all over everything. I hope that Spielberg will explain this when the DVD comes out.

title: Unsurpassed effects overcomes fatal plot hole
review:
(POSSIBLE SPOILERS FOR ANYONE WHO HAS NOT READ THE BOOK) You won't be disappointed shelling out nine dollars for this one. Looks great, sounds great, hews to the spirit of Wells' book, does homage to every previous version, radio broadcast, Gorge Pal film, and LP with Riuchard Burton. All the elements of Wells story are there, the stranger in the farmhouse, the Thunder Child, and the red weed.

An obvious attempt to stand "CE3K" on its head, and equally obvious to use Dakota Fanning to make you think of Drew Barrymore in "E.T." A very good addition not found in any other version to the original story comes late in the movie.

(DEFINITE SPOILER) But a warning for hardcore science fiction fans: Spielberg adds an element to the Martian invasion that renders the movie what Roger Ebert has called the Idiot Plot. We learn that the Martians prepared for their invasion by burying their Tripods on earth long ago. If that's the case, then WHY INVADE NOW? And why didn't earth's germs get them while they were burying the machines? (Never mind the guy at ground zero with the working video camera.)

It would appear that, due to the characteristics of the medium and the anti-visual bias of science fiction storytelling, Spielberg has proved again that it is impossible to make a good science fiction film. Two points off for the gigantic plot hole.

title: If you are currently looking for a movie that has plenty to say about the current state of political affairs - then this is it!
review:
On the surface this is your standard Spielberg manipulative movie, told brilliantly, pulling the right emotional cords and full of spectacular actions scenes. But if you look deep down into the bowels, there is an ugly side, most of it dug up from the USA's backyard.

Representing the USA is Ray Ferrier, a blue collar worker with a failed marriage and children he cannot seem to connect with. Sounds like another single parent in a screwed-up dysfunctional world.

From underneath him the Earth opens up and out come the menacing alien giant tripods, ready to destroy the world. These machines have been right under civilization's noses for millions of years, and I'm sure it was the crazed Ogilvy (Tim Robbins) who pointed it out. That's when the penny dropped for me.

The enemy is right under our noses! But who are our enemies? The terrorists? No, Ray crossed them off the list. How about the politicians? They create fear within us, planting the seed of paranoia, which then flowers into panic and then mayhem within our own minds. That's what happens to our protagonist, Ray Ferrier, as he attempts to get away from this mysteries alien invasion. He can't make sense of it, but his first instinct is to get his children away from it. And on this journey of survival, he packs a hand gun, like all good citizens should do when being invaded.

Ray and his children manage to get away in the only mobile vehicle. Along the way they come across a convoy of army vehicles that are headed towards the disaster. Ray's teenage angst ridden son wants to join them and fight the unbeatable war. But Ray won't have none of that because he knows what the consequences will be - the same consequences as sending our young naïve troops to Iraq.

Somewhere amongst all this carnage there is a scene of an airplane scattered over a suburban street. Ray finds a TV cameraman and a journalist scavenging through this disaster, pulling out food and filling up there bags with the supplies. (The same way Journalists find stories) But the journalist does show Ray something of interest that they have captured on camera, and that is the lightning that hit the Earth before the tripods came alive. Hidden in the rods of lightning are these creatures that penetrate the Earth to get to the tripods underground. Is this how a few politicians with hidden agendas are penetrating our society? And then raising the evil empire to conquer all? Maybe I'm going right off track but I'm enjoying this a little too much to stop right now. Anyway, back to the story where the journalist's aim is to get the hell out of there since they can't get a good story out of Ray. It says a lot about today's journalism. (I couldn't help myself again.) Now, while the politicians are  sorry, I meant to say Aliens - are sending our citizens into a mad frenzy, Ray and his children drive right into one. A fight ensures over the vehicle but Ray has his trusty gun that takes control over proceedings. But someone else comes out one better and points a gun at Ray's head. He's not ready to die for a silly cause as he realises that his intention is to save the family. The man with the gun manages to take control of the vehicle and only drives a few metres before being shot down. Ray and children can only watch the madness as everyone fights for the car. (A nice little piece for the anti-gun lobby movement.) Ray and family seem to be getting into more deep s**t. This time the army comes to the rescue and Ray's teenage boy wants to fight the good cause. Ray tries to talk him out of it but the foolish young boy has an urge to take on evil. Ray knows he has to let his son go sooner or later, as other parents did when they sent their children off to Iraq, fearing for the worse.

The only safe place for Ray and his daughter is in the basement of a crazed man, Ogilvy. This man must surely represent the mid-west American. All this man wants to do is to take on the aliens with a shotgun and an axe. It's what a lot of American's wanted to do after 9/11, find an enemy and seek vengeance. Maybe too haste a move was made and Ray feels the same. He knows that is not a wise move since it will only stir up trouble and jeopardise his daughter's life (who I might add represents the innocence of a nation). The only way Ray can convince this nut Ogilvy is by eliminating him in a very fine cinematic moment.

An interesting piece occurs when Ray and daughter are now captives in the tripod's cage. The alien tripod randomly picks out a human and sprays their blood over the land. (Obviously a reference to the blood of soldiers being sprayed over foreign soil) Ray is up next and it's only the reaction of a soldier who knows the evil intentions of the alien tripod and the parting of father and daughter. How about we link this to soldiers who are losing faith in their government's decision making and have to now take their own action? And it pays off as they manage to escape.

The ending is very simple as the alien tripods die. Not because of the intelligent weapons created by Humans, but because of bacteria that only humans are immune to. Now, what does this say about our politicians? Are they immune to our votes? Now, maybe I'm right off track but it was fun to watch this movie in that perspective. But then again, this movie could be about the unfair treatment of divorced fathers and the raw deal they get. But that's another thesis in itself.

title: A very well done thriller
review: I'd have to say that this film is certainly the most powerful alien thriller I have ever seen. Steven Speilburg truly proves that he is one of the greatest directors of our time without so much as a flop on his record. Not only was the movie clever, but ultimately touching. Many say the movie was actually not well done but in fact a total wast of time. I would not listen to these negative critics who have clearly lost their sense of what a good movie actually is. title: this was a great movie (spoilers maybe)
review:
the people complaining about war of the worlds minor problems, such as the video camera working after the electromagnetic pulse are, in my mind, totally missing the point. yes, there were a few out of whack details (wouldn't any culture capable of attacking us in the way that these aliens do have a firm understanding of the microbiology of earth?), but those pale in comparison to the emotional intensity of this film. as much as i might not like tom cruise the guy, tom cruise the actor came through with a very believable performance, and no amount of op rah couch jumping can change that.

title: Great movie that no one will like.
review:
This is a very good movie that nobody will like and probably be a bust at the box office, and it's a shame because Spielberg did a nice job recreating H.G Wells classic story. This movie should stand on its on feet and unfortunately has been out shined by the ass that Tom Cruise has become off camera. Maybe he should worry more about his on screen performance then his off screen tirades about Scientology or Katie Holmes.

The movie is based on the H.G. Wells story about how aliens come to the planet and kick some major butt, but in the end, they die because of something that on our planet that we humans have grown used too.

The main reason why people won't like this movie is because we get our butts kicked in the movie. Unlike Independence Day, the aliens do come down and destroy and kill us, but, this time we can do nothing to stop them, i.e. we are helpless. Not a fun movie for the movie crowd on a patriotic weekend such as July 4th. Since we humans win by default, there was not a lot of cheering in the theater when I watched. Spielberg continues to be a great story teller and one of the best directors ever. No scene was too long, he was able to control the over-acting impulses that Cruise can have, and he brings out the talents of the adorably wonderful young actress Dakota Fanning (Man on Fire) who plays Cruise's daughter Rachel Ferrier. I just hope that she is going to school because she is appearing in every movie that requires a young girl to act. Hey, casting directors, let her go to school will ya? Tom Cruise (Minority Report), as Ray Ferrier, does a steady but not spectacular job as the deadbeat dad trying to deal with what is going on. I did find that his reactions to events around him are probably closer to reality then the courageous hero's we normally find in these kind of movie. To give an indication of how dark this movie is, the final act begins by having Cruise's character kill another man who has lost his mind after watching the aliens use humans as fertilizer. There is no happy ending in the movie, and yes the children and Tom survive, but there are no rah-rah scenes here, so don't go expecting it.

I tell you all to go see it, but like I said, I don't think people will like it and it will be a disappointment at the box office, the blame of which can be put on the story itself, because it is so good, and so depressing all at once. Give it a shot.

title: Probably the best blockbuster this summer
review:
I've just got home after watching War of the Worlds and I have to say that i thoroughly enjoyed it. When I first saw the trailers I was sceptical like most thinking it would be no more than a cheesy disaster movie like Independence Day but having seen it I know that it offers so much more.

Firstly, the acting performances are great. Tom Cruise is solid in the lead role and manages to realistically convey true terror throughout (he is especially effective during the appearance of the first 'tripod'). Dakota Fanning is brilliant as Cruise's daughter, a young girl fraught with panic and bewilderment at the events that transpire around her. In one memorable scene where dead bodies are floating down the river in front of her she conveys these emotions without uttering a word. The rest of the cast all deliver solid enough performances and I felt this helped it to avoid any cheesy or cringe worthy moments which so often taint disaster movies.

The special effects in this film are absolutely stunning and are definitely some of the finest I have ever seen. The 'tripods' are truly terrifying and my adrenaline was pumping whenever they loomed into view and emitted their chilling war cry. Without believable special effects the movie wouldn't have been able to properly create believable terror, which I think is perhaps this movies strongest emotion.

However, I did feel that it did end a bit suddenly and without any prior indication of why the 'tripods' start to falter and the shields fail. It is explained in a small piece of narration by Morgan Freeman at the end but some earlier explanation would have been nice and helped to build up to a more satisfying climax.

Also, if you have a general dislike for this type of movie then this probably won't do much to sway you. You will also dislike this movie if you are the type of person who insists on knitpicking every tiny detail throughout such as how Tom Cruise manages to avoid death rays or how his car manages to avoid being blown up when most of the house whose driveway it is parked in is destroyed (the answer is simple, the story follows this character BECAUSE he doesn't get zapped at the start and the fact his car survives is believable and irrelevant as the story would simply have gone off in a different direction if it had been).

I would definitely recommend this movie as it is superior to practically every other movie in this genre thanks to believable performances a solid script, great casting and special effects which enhance the story rather than overwhelm it.

8 out of 10

title: A truly chilling and frightening tale
review:
Have just seen this at previews here in the UK this afternoon and have come away very unnerved - and thats from a 35 year old sci-fi fan! Ever since reading the original story and hearing Richard Burton narrate the musical version this story has - unlike any other story of alien invasion - unnerved me and I don't know why, it reads/plays in a very chilling and realistic manner. I liked the 1950's film version, it did not come over in the same way and was a fairly stock sci-fi tale from the time.

Onto the new film and I expected a fairly good alien invasion story with good effects but in setting it in the present day it would lack the menace apparent in the original story - thankfully. I was totally wrong - it's scary, chilling and has real menace, Independence Day it certainly is not. How on earth this got a 12A ticket is beyond me, it may not be very graphic - it doesn't need to be - yet it skillfully generates a real and powerful terror amongst it's cast. There's little in the way of false and all knowing heroics here, the cast act with real fear which combined with the strictly limited viewpoint we see gives a very unusual take on the alien invasion genre.

This Cruise/Spielberg version is also, surprisingly quite faithful to the original story. If this film was rushed, I can't see it on the screen.

Is it recommended? Yes, it's a superb piece of work and Cruise/Spielberg ought to be recognized for this. Yet I can't say I liked it because of how disturbing it was. Have had to watch something very lighthearted for the rest of the day.

review:
The movie started out with the tag line "With envious eyes they watched and slowly drew their plans against us." Earlier this week I heard Tim Robbins who played the mysterious man in the basement (Ogilvy). Nature finally rewards the residents of earth, those who have lived with nature through millenniums of evolution. Nature destroys those who slowly drew their plans against us. Wow! Thank you Steven Spielberg.

title: Great movie
review:
Steven Spielberg's War of the Worlds is one of the best movies I've seen this year. The performances, the story and the special effects are really great.

The film explores parenthood, and its not just about action and aliens attacking. It explores Ray Ferrier's (Tom Cruise) growth as a father as tripod alien machines destroy our world.

The actions scenes are very well managed and extremely taken care of by a real master, Mr. Spielberg. Although the film only portrays a family struggling to survive the attacks, Spielberg made it as big as he could. The situations in which the characters are involved make it hard for someone to not have fun and at the same time feel scared at moments, it's really cool.

The idea of aliens coming out of the ground is really great, and it makes us really wonder if that is, in fact possible.

The character of Ogilvy, played smartly by Tim Robbins, is great too, although I would've asked for more scenes involving the character, because it was very secondary.

Bottom line is, "War of the Worlds" is the best we'll come across this summer and makes us remember the days in which Jurassic Park scared us to death. If you want to see a big action movie, this is definitely for you.
