title: Decent but no more
review: This film, a remake of a Hollywood classic, could have been so much better. The film has all the right ingredients, save one. It has the actors and actresses...Tom Cruise, Dakota Fanning, and the Director, Spielberg. What it lacks is a decent script. And much of the script is good (not great, but good). But the ending of the film is a complete failure. The action and suspense very abruptly end. There's no indication previous to the very end that the invaders are being affected by Earth's germs and viruses until, all of a sudden, they're falling over. One would think that, as sickness began to take the invaders, that their behavior might become a bit erratic, but there's no sign of that. Also, all of a sudden, Cruise and Fanning find themselves on a street full of nice, neat, untouched little brownstone houses. There's no indication that the city around them is completely devastated. There are no survivors clamoring to get under the shelter in one or more of these surviving homes. And the son surviving the fireball on the other side of the hill is implausible. Then, of course, we must have the requisite and sickening reconciliation between father and son. ACK! 6 out of 10 only for the first 3/4 of the film. The last quarter is a 1 out of 10; it simply becomes too laughable to take seriously. A wasted opportunity to remake an old favorite.

title: What was the story?
review:
I just saw War of the Worlds on Pay Pre View, last night. I had heard a couple of comments from friends who had seen it. But I wanted to watch and make my own decision. So my mate and I watched it.

Where was Steven doing? I had read the trivia and goofs for the movie. And I did find some of them after thinking about them. And why was everyone yelling? Ray and the kids need to take some chill pills. I wanted to tell them to shut up. The gun shot gave a brief moment of silence, but didn't last long. During the whole movie, I could barely hear what was going on. The machines were the only thing I could figure out that wasn't yelling. I sat there wondering where the connections with the original movie came in. I have seen original movie when I have was younger and it was scary. But looking at the new one, I noticed it wasn't scary. The only connections I noticed was the during the farmhouse with the probing eye. The character that Tim Robbins played needed major doses of Prozac. Schizophrentic characters can be fun to play, but when combined from three different ones made Olgivy someone who had escaped the Psycho ward. The only other connection that I thought was cool was who the grandparents were. I recognized Gene, but I didn't Ann.

The visual effects were fantastic. The machines made the first look like toys found in an old thrift store. The probing eye was nicely done. The look was very close to the original. But didn't work out when it came to the chopping. The creatures were very nicely done. Almost the kind I might find in MIB. They didn't look like aliens that came to take over the planet.

Over all, the movie was a personal dud for me. The yelling and chasing for close to 2 hours made me tired and unfulfilled. Their dying left an unanswered question of what did kill them. For those who don't remember, it was the common cold that killed them. I didn't pay much to view it, but found out that it wasn't worth it.

title: This is an intense movie.
review:
War of the Worlds is a chilling take on what would happen if an alien invasion were actually to happen. It focuses on a father trying to safely take his two children away from the danger.

The overall mood and the feel of the movie are good. It's really dark and intense, and it captures the feelings and reactions that people might have in a situation like this pretty well. Tom Cruise's performance as a man just trying to save his kids is good. When he first sees the alien tripod, he actually looks terrified. The special effects are really good, and the alien tripods were actually as scary as they should be, especially when they sound off before firing a death ray.

There are a few flaws in the film. The worst part was the ending. It had no logic with what happened earlier in the movie, and it left a few plot holes. Also, I think that the movie should have shown what was happening on a world scale, instead of just focusing on one character.

All in all, it was a really enjoyable movie, though not one of Spielberg's best. 7/10

title: Views on the 2005 and 1953 original War of the Worlds
review:
I was thrilled to know that Stephen Spielberg was remaking the War of the Worlds which came out last July, 2005. Having seen the original and owning it on DVD I was eager to compare the two. HG Wells' classic story is timeless and can be adapted for different concerns of different generations. The 1953 version was made at time of the post-war atomic age where for the first time we were reliving in fear of being wiped out by the newly-found super-science eg: the atomic bomb. The cold war put forward the idea of being attacked by other nations and remember, the UFO phenomenon had taken hold. The film saw the earth being attacked by these invaders from Mars with mankind fighting for survival until the invaders were destroyed by the unlikely slaying of a virus which killed them. The very real threat of being attacked by something or someone with superior technology somehow seemed possible. In the original 1953 film, flying swan shaped machines replaced the heavy lumbering tripod conception of Well's original. The special effects department thought this a good idea and indeed it worked for the time. The overhead wire technique was used to propel the machine along and you can just about make this out in some scenes in the movie. The message of fear of invasion had been established.

The remake, although modelled on the original, concerned our very real threat of being attacked by terrorists. Spielberg himself said that the film was inspired my the events of 9/11 and showcased a very vivid story of what could happen if we were attacked and showed Tom Cruise desperately trying to protect his family from the onslaught of these enemies. The effects in both films were brilliant. The 1953 original was good for the time it was made and I still have shivers when watching it: the hissing of the invaders, the the heat ray, the scene where the three men come to greet the Martians etc. The tripods in the re-make were really brilliant and the alien design so real. Just listen to the sound of those wars machines out side the bunker where Tom Cruise, Dakota Fanning and Tim Robbins were. Could we perhaps learn a lesson from the story today? It gives food for though as to our own time where the threat of attack is still ugly and real.Plot wise, I would have to agree with other user's comments that Spielberg could have added more scenes in the way of the military fighting the aliens and remember in the first film the deadly heat ray vaporising the tanks and combat units. What is different though in the remake is of course our not being told of where the invaders come from, which adds to our tension. My advice is to watch the original first and then the remake and you will get a better overview of the story line. Result I would give 7 out of 10.

title: An above-average blockbuster with great special effects, but suffers from a poor ending
review:
Steven Spielberg's version of War of the Worlds is above-average, but it is just a tad over-hyped. There are some awesome action scenes, but it is not very tense or scary like the original was and the aliens are unthreatening, subsiding when Cruise confronts them (Battlefield Earth?). The ending is also rushed and inadequate. Then again, War of the Worlds is little more than a blockbuster. Blockbusters are meant to entertain (which is why Godzilla sucks) and War of the Worlds does this.

The plot revolves around a father (Ray) who gets the chance to meet his kids who treat him with little respect. This changes quickly when a light-and-sound show occurs and aliens invade the Earth, causing havoc wherever they go. Eventually, Ray meets up with this paranoid gun-toting hack (Tim Robbins) and plans to defeat the aliens.

The acting, as per normal in every Tom Cruise movie I see, is a mixed bag. Cruise and Robbins are OK, but the children are so annoying you almost want to leave them to the aliens.

The ending is the worst part of this film and as I said before, it feels a little like the ending in Battlefield Earth (that's not a compliment). These aliens can wipe out a whole battalion yet fall at the hands of one man? Also, the climax of the film, that is to say the final confrontation, is disappointing - the alien leader dies just like that, without so much as a whimper. And guess what from? The common cold! I knew this was coming, but it's still lame. As for the family reunion, it just feels tacked on.

Fortunately, the special effects and the action scenes here are awesome and almost carry the film by themselves. The best of these scenes would be when Cruise is running down the street and houses are being demolished and trucks exploding behind him. The light-and-sound show scenes are also great to watch.

In the end, War of the Worlds is not much more than your typical blockbuster, but it is always entertaining, which makes it worth recommending.

3.5/5 stars

title: Just not that great
review: With the epic status that this movie was advertised with, it was a supreme disappointment. Tom Cruise did an alright job with his one character, and it's a pretty good character, but we've just seen it to much. For a Spielberg film it lacked in characterization and ending. For example, I really didn't care if Robbie died or not. Overall I think Dakota Fanning's performance was fairly decent, even if her scream got pretty ear shattering. And I wish Miranda Otto had a larger part!Hurray for LOTR! I'm also not anxious for MI 3. Hmmm, I wonder what Tom Cruise's character will be like? Anyways, the original version is fine as is, and for its time it was epic. Go check that out. I think it's well worth the rental fee.

title: Well done, scary, but ends with a whimper
review:
War of the Worlds is at this point practically an archetype. It is "the" alien invasion premise, and Spielberg does it proud in this updated version of the tale. The acting, the effects, the pacing ... all very good. Yes, the allusions to the Holocaust and 9/11 are a bit too much, but not annoyingly so. They just stand out when they happen. There is one twist regarding how the aliens grow their "red vine" that is so macabre as to be disturbing. I thought it was a nice touch for a scary movie.

The oddest thing about this movie is its ending, or more specifically, how it is handled. If you have read the book, or know anything about any incarnation of War of the Worlds, than you basically know what happens at the end. Spielberg chooses to create a thrilling movie for the first hour and a half, and then it essentially ends off camera. We literally go from thrill ride to safety in a few seconds and we are not sure why. Viewers are brought up to speed quickly, but there is no real emotional impact or sense of relief. There is mostly a lot of, "Huh?" Of course, in all of the War of the Worlds versions, the ending is somewhat silly. It is even more so in Spielberg's movie, which at several points has characters talking about the fact that the aliens must have been planning this invasion for thousands of years. If so, how did they overlook their Achilles heal? Unless that is an allusion to the Bush administration's "planning" of the Iraq war, it makes no sense. These aliens made a major boo-boo.

I enjoyed the first 80 percent of War of the Worlds. If the final 20 percent had been better, it might have earned a 9. As it was, I gave it a 7.

title: Damn Beautiful....but lacking in story
review: First off let me say that I've read the book and no I'm not gonna compare it truth is i don't remember the book that well anyway ,I went to see this film in the theaters and was looking forward to a great sci-fi film, I was however disappointed , it wasn't the special effects those were probably the most superb special effects I've ever seen...it wasn't the actors I love Tom Cruise and Tim Robbins it was in short the story , it felt as if it were just made to get to the next special effect ,it tried to be emotional and I just saw no chemistry between Cruise and his 'Family' , all in all it was just disappointing after all the hype ,it was a major let down,but I still recommend renting it for the special effects. oh and p.s.Viva La Kathy Griffin Dakota Fanning is the worst childhood actor I've ever seen and she has that bug-eyed crackhead stare ....creepy

title: Wow
review:
Wow! I just watched War Of the Worlds and all I can say is wow... Wow did that suck. That movie was horrible. It started off okay, can't go wrong with Morgan freeman (or so I thought).

It all went stupid when the invasion began. First they take out all of the electronics, the cell phones don't work, the watches, but camcorders still work sop a man can film his destruction. Next you realize that the machines came from underground and they were probably there for a very long time. So why didn't they conquer earth when they put these machines underground! And second how did they know were to f***ing put them? "Oh well lets put 50 of them here cause in one million years new York City will be here..."

Next they get in a car that has a new starter so now it works just fine. well if it is that simple how come they are they only ones in the damn movie with a car!

Well, the next annoying bit is the family in general. Okay we get that it is a dysfunctional family... We don't need to spend half the movie dealing with it. I know the characters have to develop (which was just way to obvious).

Now why did the birds fly towards the destruction every time? Birds are not that dumb! They know to run away when everything is dieing! And so many random unexplained things. Why was that train on fire? Why does laundry constantly fall from the sky? And the scene in the basement. A twenty minute game of hide and go seek. I was not on the edge of my seat.

Then we get to the end. The only thing in the movie they got from the book and they still f***ed it up! The aliens died do to spores in the atmosphere that we are immune to now. Was that that hard to say? Morgan Freeman said something, but I don't know what! And what was the deal with the family at the end. A billion people are dead. that is one in five people dead. Except for everyone Tom Cruise has ever met. They are all fine! The son is still alive even though he should be dead, and the Mom, and her family managed to hide in the only part of all of Boston that was not destroyed. They're house was just fine! The only redeeming part of the whole movie is Dakota Fanning's performance. She did a really good job.

Let me give you some advise if you didn't have the misfortune of seeing this movie... Don't!!! It was two hours and $15 I will never get back! H. G. Wells is spinning in his grave!

title: Good AND Bad?
review:
I commend H.G. Wells, and Stephen Spielburg as well, because the story is very creative, and the adaptation of it to the present day was done very well. Yet still, as much as I loved this movie, I feel the need to question Mr. Spielburg... Or Mr. Wells (whichever one wrote the ridiculous part where the ENTIRE FAMILY reunites in the end). Beyond this, and a couple other flaws, I was so damn impressed with the imagery Spielburg and/or Wells used (i.e. the burning train), that I am giving it a 9 - just because it is so worthwhile to see. There is maybe one other movie I've seen that has actually legitimately scared me. And not just as in shocking or gruesome, but it's scary in the way a nightmare might scare you. This alone makes WOTW worth seeing. In addition to a few other outstanding pieces of the movie such as the character development.

I really didn't know whether to give this a 5 or a 10, because it has a few really crappy parts and some major flaws, but if you ignore those things, it is an incredible movie. So it gets a 9.

title: Visually Spectacular
review:
With the rush of re-makes that have developed this summer, the old favorite would be just the kind of thing Spielberg would go for. With the massive fan-base that Steven built for those visually wonderful films such as Terminator 2 and Jarrasic Park, how could he possibly resist this futuristic tale of the outside world? With obvious time and money spent by the visual department and the CG techs, Spielburg has created a masterpiece that is timeless. With the terrifyingly realistic effects and plot, along with the best of performers, the highlight of which being Dakota Fanning and her charming father-daughter love for Tom Cruise.

Gripping, edge-of-your-seat action that's one white-knuckle ride no one could possibly resist. Intese dialogue and themes, extensive research on effects, and a well-written plot makes "War of the Worlds" a well-made timeless thrill ride that won't stop until the final scene.

title: For aliens that are supposedly thousands of years ahead of us, they sure are stupid!
review: There is a fundamental flaw with any movie that tries to depict an alien invasion.... the humans win! Look, indigenous tribes in the Americas didn't do well against their more advanced European invaders, and humans sure as heck don't have a chance against a species that has no problem whatsoever travelling the speed of light. I'm almost offended that Steven Spielberg expected me to take this stuff serious. At least in "Independence Day," I never once get the impression that the director expects me to find his film symbolic or realistic. Instead of the bad parent anti-hero in Tom Cruise who lucks himself into survival, we get the President of the United States yelling "Booyah!" as he fires missiles off his jet. Maybe "War of the Worlds" made sense fifty years ago when it was first transferred to the big screen, but now, it's one of those movies that makes you say to yourself, "Yeah... sure.... mkay." For sophisticated beings, aliens sure do pick the biggest clunkiest invasion tools such as the giant tripods that they use to storm through cities picking off humans one by one, and apparently, they have yet to perfect heat sensors, x-rays or anything that would allow them to hunt humans through a method other than visual and audio detection. Since the movie admits that they have been planning this invasion for a looooong time, you would think aliens would invent an attack plan far more lethal and easier, like say... a mutated virus? Oh wait, I forgot, that's how they die... again! Lucky for us, these aliens spent so much time on quantum physics, that never had a chance to sit in a basic biology class and discover the tiny world of germs. If you want to watch a classic Spielberg alien flick, then grab "Close Encounters of the 3rd Kind" as soon as possible, if you want an alien invasion cheese fest that at least pumps you up, rent "Independence Day." Spielberg is too talented to waste his time on this "War of the Worlds" fluff.

title: A wild thrill ride best viewed in theaters
review:
Spielberg's version of H.G. Wells classic is another shocker from Spielberg. Just like some of his other creations such as Jaws and Jurassic Park, War of the Worlds is a genuine thrill ride.

Ray Ferrier is an ordinary citizen living in an ordinary world. That is, until his peace is disturbed when a giant lightning storm hits. The storm isn't ordinary, though. For example, lighting seems to hit repetitively in one spot, and the wind seems to be going in the opposite direction it usually does. If that wasn't enough shock a giant alien ship rises from the ground, and starts to kill people, lots and lots of people.

The thrills are at their highest, when giant machines start consuming humans by the minute. If you really want to know how big they are, compare the size of the people to the size of the ships. Now, THAT is scary. The "war" (Ray running from aliens) is undoubtedly thrilling! However, the noise isn't balanced out. The beginning contains almost inaudible dialogue. The film then becomes unbearably loud when the aliens start attacking. Plot holes may also be the demise of many.

But, the film makes a good thriller, and moments of drama ---small spoiler! --- (such as when Ray kills Tim Robbins) make the film very fun.

7/10

Good: Thrills, drama, some twists and fabulous narration by Morgan Freeman

Bad: Noise is unbalanced, plot holes and definitely isn't better the second time

title: excellent!
review:
Everyone's always complaining about how Hollywood's been infected with the remake syndrome as of late, and yes, it does in many ways represent a lack of creativity in filmmakers and an unwillingness to take risks on the part of movie bigwigs. But there's something else that drives a heck of a lot of remakes nowadays. Directors that remember the movies that had an effect on them growing up, and want to pay tribute to them, bring them to a new generation of moviegoers, or simply do them justice by today's standards. Such is the case with Steven Spielberg's take on H.G. Wells' War of the Worlds.

Steven Spielberg knows how to handle big stories and he knows how to ground them in human moments. But the truth is, I don't think it matters how you feel about Steven Spielberg or Tom Cruise because this version of War of the Worlds will still kick your ass halfway into next week. Within the first 10 minutes, it pulls you in and never lets go. The movie is kinetic and intense and gripping in every sense. At times the camera-work is erratic and hand-held, other times it swoops and rotates around at impossible angles. The camera stays close to the ground, hovering near the main characters at all times, keeping us at their level and focused on their emotions. We are trapped inside this family's story of survival and tugged along at a breakneck pace.

The decision to add the 2 children to the story is a Spielberg-ism that is likely to have some purists up in arms. However, American family values aside, it just makes the main character even more desperate to survive and adds to the tension. Sometimes child actors can be annoying, but both Dakota Fanning and Justin Chatwin did a decent job. The son, Robbie (Chatwin), comes off at first as the typical Gen-X teenager who hates his divorced father, but he doesn't go too far overboard with the angst and still makes us identify with him. Dakota Fanning on the other hand is endearing, and although she seems like she's going to be that annoying kid who is wiser han anyone her age should ever be, she ends up simply "reacting" more than acting.

Tom Cruise's hammy tendencies, on the other hand, might make you crack a smile a few times, but it never gets out of hand. He does a surprisingly good job of playing the average joe as opposed to the all-American hero for once.

War of the Worlds combines the post-apocalyptic awe of 28 Days Later, and some of the taut nail-biting moments of M. Night Shyamalan's own alien terror flick, Signs. One thing people seem to forget about War of the Worlds (perhaps a result of the now dated 1953 movie), is that Orson Welles once caused mass pandemonium when he did a radio broadcast based on the book. It was scary stuff. The concept of invaders from outer space is indeed a frightening one, and one that Spielberg proves can still be chilling even today if we are given the proper cues. There are some disturbing images in this movie (okay, only PG-13 disturbing), and yet at the same time it is often what we don't see (or can't see clearly) that gets under our skin the most.

This is a movie that could have crumbled under the sheer weight of computer generated effects. However, nothing looked awkward or obviously fake. I loved the look of the tripods in this film, as they maintained their old 50's-style design without seeming cheesy or out of place. The aliens themselves were creepy and menacing and yes, a thousand times cooler looking than those skinny future robot thingies in A.I.

The thing that floors me the most about this movie is that it was shot on such a tight schedule. Every scene seems to have been executed with such forethought and precision, and the effects integrated flawlessly, and yet the entire production was finished in less than 10 months. Maybe the ending seemed a little abrupt, but still, if that isn't proof of Spielberg's mastery of cinema, I don't know what is.

Some people are going to say that Steven Spielberg is offering a commentary on 9/11, but I don't know about that. He's just grounding it in realism, in the here and now. You can interpret it any way you like, but I think all Spielberg has done is taken a classic story, modernized it, upped the intensity, and injected some depth into the characters. Unlike similar disaster-type movies you might see by Roland Emmerich, this one will stay with you long after the credits have rolled because you feel like you actually lived it. It's blockbusters like these that remind you why you love going to the movies in the first place.

title: Spielberg takes a "dark" approach.
review:
"War of the worlds" is a Steven Spielberg adaptation of H.G. Wells' story. It is a dark disaster movie, that follows the family of divorced dock worker Ray Ferrier, and his two children. We see them struggling to stay one step ahead of an alien invasion, which we are told has been in planning for more than a million years. This invasion starts when a barrage of lighting comes down and uncovers a stash of alien tripods that have been hidden under the earth's surface since before man existed.

Tom Cruise plays Ray Ferrier, and does a decent job portraying the "bad" dad, but struggles at times to convince as the working class dock worker. However when the action begins, the panic and desperation he shows adds to the films suspense. The acting highlight would be Tim Robbins as a crazy survivor who shelters the family in his basement. Spielberg returns to the tried and tested formula of a summer disaster movie, after recent films like "The Terminal", and as he often does involves a family story at the centre. He does a great job cranking up the suspense, and the special are brilliant, with the devastation of homes etc. by the tripods very realistic, making the film quite scary. As said the film is very dark, with little comedy, or joy, and thankfully the ending is not cheesy or particularly happy.

Memorable scenes include a section where we see crowds of people fighting over a working car, and it shows the human desperation often shown in times of disaster. Post 9/11 fears are also conveyed when Ray's son asks, "Is it terrorists?"

In conclusion i would say "War of the Worlds" is an excellent movie, with it dark and gritty, and i am thankful that Spielberg did not allow Tom Cruise did not take on the alien invasion single handedly, as in some blockbusters, rather showing him as an "average Joe". The tension is built up, the acting decent and the special effects scary.

8/10

title: Pointless
review: I only call it awful because at the very end the only thing that came to mind was "pointless." It was full of suspense, action, great acting and over the top special effects - but in the end there was just no point to the movie whatsoever. I felt completely cheated out of the two hours I'd spent watching by a lame, cop out of an ending. (And I realize it's based on a book, so I suppose the fault lies w/ H.G. Wells rather than Speilburg, but... yeah. If I - or any other contemporary author - wrote an ending like that, my editor would laugh me out of his office.) Wow, I just got told by the automated thingy that I have to say more bad things about the movie... OK, I guess I'll try to balance this out by saying that Dakota Fanning is a young actress we should be watching because she was spectacular in this. Given her age - I think she out acted Cruise (not a slam on him, just that she's just a kid and she is really, really good. She reminds me of Kirsten Duntst when she was that age.)

title: Effective telling of the old story,but oh,those CGI's!
review: This is a story that if told well,could be a very effective hide under the covers type of movie.After all,let's not forget that Orson Welles' radio telling of this same story scared a young nation nearly to death in 1938.This time,it is put in another pair of more than capable hands, Steven Spielberg.We can rest assured that he will stop at nothing to tell this familiar story to us as good as we know he can.He succeeds, throwing in a credible combo of father and daughter,Tom Cruise and Dakota Fanning.There are alterations to the original story,but you won't mind.In fact,you may end up going,"Hey,that's a good idea,why didn't they do that before?".All in all,this is,as I stated before,a very good hide under the covers flick.There's just one problem that I have with it, personally.Until they come up with computer graphics(or CGI's,as I hear they are called),that are a little more realistic looking,I am afraid I am going to be nothing but bothered by them.That being said,it is still an excellent film otherwise.

title: Great Entertainment- Ignore Poor Reviews
review: I really cant see what peoples problem with this is. I didn't go to the cinema to see it, but when I bought it on DVD I wish I had. The film is superb entertainment from start to finish. There's nothing noticeable about any bad performances from any actors or actress's. People are moaning about Cruise, Robbins and Fanning (being the main characters) but they put in great performances. If you just sit back and enjoy the action it really is a great film. I love the little adjustments Spielberg has made to the original story (like the lightning entries). They really seem to fit in. One small problem, like, how the hell did the son survive the heat ray. Ah well. Anything can happen in a movie (like the plane crashing into the house, but not touching the car). However, this movie is highly underrated and being a fan of HG Wells' WOTW, this is a great movie.

title: What's worse? This or A.I.?
review:
Why is it that when Spielberg is great, he's really great but when he does something horrible like this, it's REALLY HORRIBLE? This is the worst movie I have seen seen A.I. - his other really horrible movie.

Tom Cruise was totally unbelievable in this character. Tim Robbins - what WAS his character supposed to be doing? Dakota Fanning? She's usually great but only tolerable in this role. Did Spielberg phone the entire thing in? Was he even there while they were trying to act this out? You have three normally BRILLIANT actors doing the wost jobs of their careers - almost like they had NO direction but because of their experience, that really couldn't be the case.

The movie started out with a BIG bang and promised to be exciting. But then it just made no sense. Nothing flowed and there were horrible plot flaws throughout. They all run into the one room of the basement that had a window shedding light into it. Then they closed the door and it was dark. WHY? What happened to the window? The end was pure schlock. HOW were the people in the one neighborhood in Boston completely unaffected by it all? And HOW did the son beat them there? I'm SO glad we only rented this.

title: Very Intense Action Show
review: It's long time ago I haven't seen such a spectacular action movie. It begins slow but only some minutes later it starts without a break with action, great special effects, suspense and edge-of-your-seat. I really didn't expect an intense action blockbuster but this successful remake did it. Well worth for the 3 Oscar nominations for best sound editing, sound mixing and visual effects. Normally I don't watch sci-fi films because I like more realistic stories but the critics here and the casting of Tom Cruise / Dakota Fanning pushed me finally to buy the DVD. The story hits some problems of nowadays that is the terrorism for example. My wife didn't like it and gives a rating of 4/10. I vote 8/10 and the final average score is therefore 6/10. If you enjoyed it then don't miss TERMINATOR 3.

title: I'm sick of people overreacting
review: I am very sick of people saying that War of the Worlds is an awful film. Have you ever known Spielberg to make an awful film? The short answer is no, hes never even made a bad one, some aren't masterpieces, but some are, see Minority Report, Saving Private Ryan, Jaws, Schindler's List, E.T., Indiana Jones, etc. War of the Worlds is truly a great piece of cinema with a few missteps. I'm not sure what Spielberg was thinking with the ending, but aside from the last twenty minutes or so, and the boring first ten or fifteen, it is an excellent film with excellent acting. Tom Cruise does shine in the role as well as Dakota Fanning. Spielberg gave depth to the film as well, such as the various 9/11 references, but I guess some people just ignore them because of the ending. Ignore them and form your own opinion. Well worth a look! 8/10

title: No nothing, nada, zip, zilch here
review:
No point (or joy) in this one. And, next time a movie begins with those cold-bluish print overtones on the film, I'm turning it off right away (had enough of that in "Minority Report."). There aren't really any spoilers in this review, but because this movie IS such a spoiler, I checked the box anyway.

To begin with, the only reasons I'm even giving "War of the Worlds" two stars: 1. Excellent musical score. 2. Great special effects. Both or these, however, were inherently wasted on the movie itself. There are just too many "but, why(s) or why not(s)", "but how(s)" but, but, but AND NO ONE to answer any of the questions except for Harlan, an apparent Ed Gein wannabe character played quite creepily by Tim Robbins, who somehow knew in his infinite psychotic wisdom that "they" (the aliens) had been planning this (attack) for a million years. But, why? Hey blockbuster-making-movie guy (yes, I'm talking to you SS), you really should care somewhat about the main characters as you're telling the story. I didn't. Tom Cruise plays Ray Ferrier, a hotshot heavy equipment operator who is extremely selfish, full of himself, and a (goes without saying) lousy dad. Robbie Ferrier, played by Justin Chatwin, is the whining-chip (on the shoulder) off-the-old-block teenage-mutant-ninja-son who chooses this time of Armageddon to tell dad just how lousy he really is (natch). And then there is Rachel (Ferrier), played by the much heralded Dakota Fanning, the wise-old ten-something kid who is much more annoying (remember Lloyd's "most annoying sound in the world" from Dumb and Dumber) than she is likable. And what happened to Ms. Fanning's little girl looks? I mean she looks like someone took a twenty year old head and stuck it on a ten-year- old's body. It must be those awkward years.

Not much else to say. So there you have it, three characters, with which you really don't care what happens to any of them, yet whom all somehow triumph in a few days time over aliens vampires, dysfunctional family relations, hordes of armed and dangerous zealot survivalists, and one psycho. (Now that I've seen the film, I kind of wish the aliensor Harlan would have won)

P.S. Is it PC now not to call a Martian a Martian? I mean, really!

j.braun

title: Not too good a review I am sorry
review:
After waiting for this film come out I found it to be a great anti climax. There was more suspense in the older version which at least kept you gripped. This film was so predicable and boring than it may have been better to have made it an all out animation for what the contribution of the actors was worth.

It was more about animation than a credible story line.

It went from an ever deminitive Tom Cruise whom I like normally to antiquated graphics which were bettered in previous films.

Is this now the decline and swansong of Spielberg and Cruise?

I know this is a contrary view but its honest and I give it a big thumbs down

title: Utterly Terrifying
review:
SPOILERS!

It has been a good long while since I've watched a movie that was as tense and terrifying as 'War of the Worlds.' Watching it was like being in one of those dreams where something huge and terrifying is after you, and you are running but you can't get away.

I suppose those who are critical of the lack of logic in having the tripods come out of the ground have a valid point, but so what? If you are willing to suspend disbelief and enjoy the movie, it's a minor issue. The scene where the tripod emerges from the middle of an intersection was absolutely terrifying; it rises to a staggering height, towering over the buildings, and then a whine begins and reaches a crescendo before the aliens begin to vaporize people into puffs of gray dust. I could completely relate to Ray (and I think the decision to tell the story from his perspectiveas a parent, trying to protect a child, was the best choice) as he dashes down the street, zigging and zagging, trying to avoid instant annihilation. He dodges into a store, thinking a building might offer some shelterand then the people to his left and right inside the store get it, like someone blowing dandelions away, followed by a car being thrown through the front wall like a child's toy. After that it was the tops of houses and buildings, and increasingly larger structures (bridges and an entire neighborhood) get blown away.

Spielberg and his CGI team got everything right with the appearance, movement, and sound of the tripods. Utterly alien in appearance and in their gait, the machines seem organic and alive  from the weird tentacles, the jettisoning of fluid from ports on the sides, the lights which look like eyes, the low frequency blatting noise, the weird feet, to the obscene, puckered orifice which slurps up humans. The tripods are "malevolence" writ large, particularly when their role in the aliens' plan for the human race is revealed as the movie progresses. I speak here of the unfortunate victim who Ray watches get skewered and drained dry of blood, which is then blown out from the rear of the tripod. Ugh!

For this kind of movie, I thought the character development was good, particularly of Ray, the divorced parent who loves his kids, but hasn't spent enough time and effort with them to earn the title 'Dad' when the movie begins. By the end of the movie, he is certainly their father, through and through. The scene where he has to let his son go was particularly poignant.

All in all, a thumbs up for this film. I will definitely be buying the DVD.

title: A remake work making.
review:
The War of the Worlds has been told, and retold in many ways, and all but one variation was very successful. Steven Spielberg's version is one of many that was successful.

The variations of War of the Worlds has had an impact on the society that had watched or listened to it. The 1938 radio broadcast for the fear of the rise of the Nazis in Germany. 1953, the fear of communism. Independence Day, using the story as a blueprint society's view of alien visitations, abductions, the Roswell incident, and Area 51. And now 2005 living in the post 9/11 world.

Unlike the 1953 version, this version hits us closer to home, where we can relate to the characters much more easily. It isn't a brilliant scientist who tries to save us this time, it's where we see a man trying to save his children from the invaders, as we all would try to do. The incredible acting and character development helps to build the intensity and the drama of the movie, and even several comical moments.

The invaders themselves are just as intriguing. Where as all the other versions of the War of the Worlds has us technically know where they came from, like from Mars or outer space in general, the origin of the invaders in this movie is still unknown to us. The primary assumption is that they too are from outer space, but as far as we know, they are from another dimension, or another time. That lack of knowledge and not knowing their motives makes them even scarier and more mysterious.

The scene where our heroes are first fleeing from the invaders in the van is incredible. The tripods, excellent. Both mechanical and yet living.

A classical story remade by a man who usually knows how to make movies. Once again, Spielberg at his best.

title: How come they did such a lame movie?
review: Honestly, this big budget movie has so many incredible flaws it becomes a joke. This is why many purists do not like Hollywood movies. They push all kind of bad stuff in our throat with lots of advertising. The part in the basement is way too long and lacks any credibility, based on the rest of the movie. The two kids makes you want to get a vasectomy, in case you ever father something like them. After you see all electronic device stop, even a wristwatch, you have people making movies of the machines! Spielberg should read the book GROUPTHINK or what happen to groups whey they are following their leader too blindly. What I like the most about this film is that I rented it for a mere 1$. I am sorry for all those who paid big money to see such a movie.

title: ET is back and boy is he pis*ed off!!!
review:
Ray Ferrier (Cruise) is a simple, divorced, builder living a modest life in New Jersey. His two kids are staying for the weekend, this is however a much different weekend as lightning storms strike all over the world making giant alien machines arise from the ground and killing thousands of lives. In an attempt to bring the kids back to their mom Ray and his family embark on a nightmarish journey where they have to deal not only with mortality caused by the aliens but also with all the desperate humans willing to do anything to survive.

A Long time ago a certain film director contradicted the generalized idea of aliens coming to conquer earth with heart warming tales such as "Close Encounters of the Third Kind" and "E.T.". Although in 2005 Spielberg completely reversed his vision of aliens to bring us a very dark Sci-Fi story.

Highly influenced by the actual atmosphere of paranoia in which the USA have been living since September 11th , the old H.G. Wells classic finds here a new interpretation. It's still follows its storyline but there are some deep connections to nowadays terrorism reality.

Unfortunately the screenplay is far from brilliant and Spielberg does make the huge mistake of following the box office friendly happy ending formula.

However, the movie does go way beyond the screenplay's limitations and that is due to the fact that Spielberg is a genius behind the camera who is able to create an emotional roller-coaster which keeps us at the edge of our seats all throughout the movie in a series of breathtaking scenes of pure anxiety and terror with astonishing special effects.

Tom Cruise is good at the characterization of an imperfect man who goes beyond his flaws becoming a heroic man who will do everything to protect his family. Dakota Fanning is amazing has the scared kid and it's no wonder why Hollywood cant get enough of her. Tim Robbins is however the scene stealer with his scarier than the aliens ideas.

Despite not being a masterpiece, War of the Worlds manages to be a mixture of family drama and pure sci-fi horror which, highly because it reflects the actual spirit of an America drawn in fear, will remain as one of the biggest and best movies of the year.

7 out of 10 (Sci-Fi Thriller - 2005)

title: Very Disappointing and ANNOYING!
review:
I disliked this film so much it compelled me to come and vote and write about it, which I do not often do.

1. Why do people have to remake films - AND they choose classic films to remake, it's an insult to the original.

2. Firstly the end was very very poor, like a quick-fix rushed ending, executed with no respect for the intelligence or emotions of the viewer who had been unlucky enough to have invested a while sat watching the film. I'm not complaining at the story, but at the way it was presented to the viwer by the director. Rubbish, I left the cinema feeling robbed of my ticket fee.

3. Isn't this film more of TV standard, it just seemed to me it was a little tale, and would be better on the little screen at 1am.

title: Almost - but not quite...
review:
Although I enjoyed this film, I felt that it was somewhat overshadowed by the film "Independance Day" of a few years earlier. It lacks the entertainment value of that earlier film, perhaps because it tries to be too serious and lacks humour.

The first part of the film, with the invasion coming, and the panic that ensues as people try to escape, is scary and extremely well done. Excellent special effects, of course, which are now a required standard in a movie of this calibre. The rest of the movie is OK, although the action scenes with Tom Cruise go overboard, and the scene in the cellar was better done in the earlier 1950's version. Just why there had to be a lunatic down their who Tom Cruise had to kill, I don't know. It added nothing to the movie.

Apart from being updated to the 21st Century, the film sticks pretty closely to H.G. Wells' classic 19th Century Novel "The War of the Worlds". And therein lies the problem with the plot. The idea of aliens invading earth, and then getting destroyed by bacteria which we humans have become immune to, but which the aliens overlooked, may have been acceptable and new back for the audeinces of 1897, but for a 2005 audience it doesn't wash. We know aliens are cleverer thatn that!

In the original 1897 book, we humans have no power to stop the invasion - and so it is in this film. No Wil Smith or Bruce Willis to save the world. Plots like this aren't good for the popcorn market, so I guess that's why Hollywood threw in the Tom Cruise heroics.

For me, the movie is a curious mixture of 19th Century visionary science fiction and 21st century Hollywood action, and doesn't quite come off.

title: Worst Ending Ever
review:
Tom Cruise's performance in this movie is actually very good and the FX are great. Unfortunately both are eclipsed by an unforgivably awful ending. Also the kids are annoying and their defiance ceases to be character development and becomes a hindrance to the story.

The aliens' fate is fine but the happy family reunion absolutely made me ill. Sometimes a movie deserves a dark ending; even summer blockbusters.

The ending felt like it had been filmed first and then didn't work with all of the death and destruction that was shot afterwards. Possibly. But regardless, the movie deserved better.

Better than ID4. Signs is a better invasion movie.

title: Spielberg can never stick with the story
review:
Spielberg's movie is alright but right at the heart of it is a family film (just like nearly all of Spielberg's movies) the effects are astounding but Dakota Fanning cant stop screaming! Tom Cruise is good at trying to be the perfect father who tries to keep his promise and in a miracle through all of the near death experiences his son who runs straight at one of the tripods with the army and the crazy man, they all end up happily ever after.

Spielberg was good at showing how the aliens died of viruses but didn't stick stick to the plot of H.G Wells original story, showing how the aliens would have destroyed the planet and how superior they were to humans, but in Spielberg's case he took the story chucked it in the bin and wrote another story about family struggling through hard times.for example E.t was about family struggling through hard times as was Jurrasic Park really.

title: Better the Second Time Around
review:
We watched this on DVD tonight, and I enjoyed it even more than I did when I saw it the opening weekend.

The sound and special effects are awesome. Too often what looks great on the screen at the theatre doesn't look as good when you see it on video. The special effects in THE DAY AFTER TOMORROW suffered on the small screen and it was all too obvious when miniatures were cut in.

This looked REAL every minute.

The analogy with 9/11 is clear: Tom Cruise coming into the house covered with white dust after running for his life through the streets, the walls of buildings plastered with pictures of missing people, the desperate attempts of people to locate their loved ones.

Sure, the first half is way better than the second and the whole basement scene could have been cut, and Dakota way overacted. But it was a thrill ride, and a darned good one. If I want serious drama the video store has a whole section of it. The scene in the car is amazing. I'm pretty literate about film making, but throughout this all I could think was Wow! How in the world did they do that? I'm sure that they didn't destroy a whole neighborhood in New Jersey and an elevated highway. Well, I guess they didn't. But, boy, it looked like the real thing.

There was a lot I admired about this movie, but the biggest thing is that Tom Cruise did not save the world singlehandedly. He takes out exactly one of the however many thousand warships the aliens have. The character is an average Joe trying to keep himself and his family alive against rough odds. Way to go, Tom. I'm sure the suits who run the studio suggested that the script be rewritten so that the high dollar leading man could wipe out the aliens himself. Mr. Spielberg, thank you.

If this had been about twenty-five minutes shorter, it would have gotten those other two stars.

title: Strip away the impressive CGI and you have... quite a good movie
review:
Boasting some of the most memorable special effects to grace cinema screens in recent times - this Hollywood blockbuster has more substance than your usual CGI saturated film. This is partly due to its Orwellian roots, and also the fact that Spielberg does the novel justice with this excellent appropriation.

Whilst it boasts Tom Cruise as the star of this titanic struggle between worlds, the real talent in this film is Dakota Fanning - her acting is simply superb, further cementing her position as the best child-actor currently going around.

If you are into the science-fiction genre this is a must see, and even if you're not - War of the Worlds is worth a look.

title: 70% Spielberg
review:
It seems like SPielberg's being waiting till the advances in digital technology have let him make "War the worlds" in the way he needed to do it. So, there's no doubt: the movie is technically perfect, amazing. But when it's about S.S. we all know what we're gonna have, and there are no surprises (except for the expected ones). So in this massive extraterrestrial invasion we got the best Spielberg (the one that's expert on terrify people, the master in suspense), and the worst side of the Jewish director: the demagogue, the one with a dubious morality, the happy endings...

As for the actors, Dakota Fanning keeps on amazing me; she's one of the best child-actors ever. And Tom Curise... well, let's say he's passed this test.

*My rate 6.5/10

title: bad bad baaaaaaaaaaaaaaad in a bad way.
review:
well well well....i thk Spielberg is highly overrated. i mean...ET wasn't that wow anyway..and anyone could have done Jurassic park and even made it better.

WOTW shouldn't have made the amount of money it did...in fact it should have suffered the loss that water world made back in the day. i totally agree with each and every one who gave this movie a bad review. in fact after watchin the movie...i wasn't sure if i watched it well cos i there were so many plot holes and i didn't feel like watchin it again to see if i could watch it well. so i rather decided to check in IMDb..and boy oo boy was i relieved to know that so many of u shared my view as well. i checked the spoiler box just in case i may end up saying something about this stupid film. well i must say..i like sci.fi. films and invasion films..but this i think is the worst, the ending was rushed, tom cruise i think was OK, the small girl was aiight..but that boy was so annoying..and he miraculously survived...yeesh(from sin city)....go watch sin city instead...cos i burrowed this movie along side sin city, which i agree is a very good movie..and like one reviewer said..batman begins is a pretty decent movie..don't waste ur money on this movie.
