title: rubbish aliens but OK film.
review: War of the worlds No one will forget the arrival of the first tri-pod. It is one of the most amazing set pieces I have ever seen. From a small hole in the road made by freak lightning all hell breaks loose and my god what an impressive hell. Fifteen minutes of pure unstoppable chaos, I was sat open-mouthed. Sticking much to the original but with dashes of Spielberg's flair for action and adventure the story is quite a simple one. What would happen to earth were we invaded, threatened and seemingly helpless? Is it everyman for himself or each other? Well as it turns out both, people go crazy prepared to do anything to escape or people like tom cruises character holding it together for the sake of his family. This is Spielberg so you get the slightly hammy family value motifs loosely woven into the plot, but it doesn't really matter or get in the way. Most impressive though are the tri-pods and their gadgets and gizmos. Rising like a football stadium sized iron with an eyeball and lasers, when the culling of humans begins you start to wonder how Spielberg got it to be a 12a (he has done this trick before, see Jaws: swallows man alive, Jurassic park: two t-rex's rip man in half, A.I.: flaming heads flying through the air towards children etc) The red weed is after all human blood. So in a flurry of disintegrated locals tom flees with his kids to nowhere in particular but just not there. In this respect the film is similar to signs, told from the view of one family's struggle against a greater evil, a sort of futuristic road movie. We get an idea of what is happening in the rest of the world from TV reports and radio bulletins. Spielberg's direction makes it so that by the time you reach the Hudson ferry scenes you've almost forgotten the amazing storms that started the whole thing. Ultimately there is a start to this story but not really an end and in this way it is true to the original and the way it's done means the film doesn't really need one. Best of all was the couple that sat behind me who were gushing at the prospect of wotw 2 & 3 because of this. There is bound to be three he said to his wife just like star wars. Oh how I laughed. A bold piece of summer eye-candy. A little too dark for the under twelve's but alien-tastic fun for everyone else.

title: Nice planet... we'll take it!
review:
Before I get started, I just want to say that the 'War of the Worlds' story, in whatever shape or form, is the only thing that has ever scared me so much that I couldn't sleep at night. After suffering insomnia from both the book and the musical, I (foolishly) went to see the movie.

I'll only tell you the beginning bit because I don't want to spoil the story. (Though, chances are, you already know what happens.)

The movie takes place in America (Big Surprise!). After a monologue by Morgan Freeman, we are introduced to the movies antagonist, Ray Farrell (Tom Cruise). Ray is your average schmo who lives in New Jersey. It just so happens that his ex-wife is dropping off their two kids to stay with him for the weekend, while she visits her parents in Boston. They are the teenage son, Robbie (who clearly holds no respect for his father) and the ten-year-old daughter,Rachael (who, when told to order take-out, orders healthy food?!)

Ray's ex seems worried about leaving the kids with our, less than responsible, hero, but he waves her off with a smile and the words, "There's nothing to worry about!" (Irony, anyone?)

Now the fun starts. First of all, there's this freak thunder storm where lightning strikes the same spot twenty-something times in a row! As if that isn't bizarre enough, EVERY machine (cars, watches, pace-makers, you name it) stops all over town.

Ray ventures outside to see what all the hoo-hah is. He winds up (along with a group of expendable extras) gathered around a crater that is quickly growing in size, until finally it coughs up a giant alien tripod! The towering machine gets straight down to business. It whips out two heat rays and fires them at the gawking crowd. (Sucks to be them!)

Ray narrowly escapes instant cremation, dashes home, grabs his freaked-out offspring, manages to get to the only working car in New Jersey and floors it in the direction of Boston.

That's enough for the story, time for the special effects. What can I say; the tripods look very realistic and even scarier than they look on the musical cover, so no complaints there. I was a little disappointed with how the aliens themselves looked,but you can make up your own mind on that. The overall visual effects, combined with the sound, caused me to jump, gasp and cower at many a point in this film. The music is very creepy too, though I would have premiered it if they'd included the signature tune from the musical. (The martian battle-cry would've been awesome too.)

Overall. 'War of the Worlds' may be far from perfect, (there are plenty of plot holes and parts that just make you go "huh?") but it gave me a thrill and deprived me of sleep for three weeks after seeing it, which makes it as good as the book and musical in my mind.

If you haven't seen it, give it a try. (As a reminder not to shack up with deranged ambulance drivers, if nothing else!)

title: Special effects in comparison to 1953
review: The original 1953 version for its time set a new standard for graphics and FX entertainment. 52 years later while the use of PC generated imagery and enhancement make for an entertaining experience, the movie was worth my 2 visits. Cruise in most of his previous movies being somewhat of a hero in each, was belittled by the obviously superior technologically advanced aliens. Making his character more believable. The FX environment seemed to dwindle when cruise and several other captives in one of the alien probes/death machines as the containment area compared to a scene out of the Road Warrior... Overall I rated the movie an 7 for FX, acting and dialog. This is a generous rating mostly due to my interest in the category of sci-fi and digital effects. I think if we can recreate both an emotional and visually stunning movie like Gladiator (one of my top favs)the creators of this movie could have used a little more imagination like the original film makers. I will however ad this flick to my collection.

title: Great Beginning
review:
The build up to the first appearance of the tripods is really pure Spielberg magic. It's cleverly shot and the timing is great. Then hell breaks loose and the first attack is happening in front of your eyes. These 20 minutes are simply the most intense scenes I've seen in a long time in cinema.

After that it's a pure escape movie which is sometimes really boring (the cellar scene should have been completely deleted). The plot is missing dramatic moments here. The attacks are still exciting but they seem to be chained together without glue.

The FX are absolutely stunning and "realistic". The camera is always moving and shaking, but the CGI elements are integrated seamlessly. So, ILM, good job.

In the whole WotW is an interesting movie but could have been much better by building a detailed story around the invasion. Nevertheless it has a great intro and the rest is great eye candy with state-of-the-art effects.

I would have liked them to hold to the original version, but this was still a fantastic job (thus the 9 out of 10 score). Loved it all the way. This often happens when you get too used to an actors style (in general), and they do a major departure from what you expect, or when you get used to special effects fitting a certain set of parameters, and the work is "out side the box".

title: This is why we go to the movies!!
review:
I knew that when reading other reviews that people would be harsh against this. Any time this many people sees a movie there is bound to be difference in opinion. Nonetheless after seeing the amazing spine tingling trailers I sat in awe of one of the greatest theatrical films ever. First off you've got an amazing blockbuster combination. DirectorSteven Spielberg, this guy can't do much wrong. He's hands down the greatest director in the history of film impressing movie goers for decades and even taking some critical acclaim along the way. The guy knows how to make a blockbuster. Superstar Tom Cruisesay what you will about his personal life right now the guy is a great actor and Minority Report, the outstanding Collateral, the Mission Impossible serieshe makes a great movie star. Supporting castDakota Fanning who is becoming an incredible actress can hold her own against any star. Tim Robbins brief role was also well done and well cast.

War Of The Worlds is based on H.G. Wells classic sci fi story. A father who doesn't really know how to be a father, Ray Ferrier, is left to care for his two children for the weekend while their mother and stepfather are visiting her parents. His son is a rebellious bitter teenager who is becoming a man slowly without his father. His daughter isn't quite old enough to resent him for not being around and she still needs a lot of protecting from anyone willing to provide. Suddenly everything changes when a freak storm sends Aliens from another world down to Earth and uncovers killing machines (tri-pods) that they may have buried centuries earlier. Not as much of a war as it is an extermination, the Aliens begin to destroy everything and everyone in sight. Ray barely makes it out of New York with his two children as they desperately try to make their way across the war torn, devastated country side to Boston to find the children's mother. As they make the trek Ray begins to realize that the love he has for his children will keep them all alive.

First off, no other film has had special effects like thisperiod. It was amazing, astonishing, justwow!! I am sure the film was rampant with CGI but you'd never know it, it is so cleverly used and disguised. The explosions, the storms, the actual aliensjust brilliantly done. This film really is less of a sci fi action film and more of a film about human nature. You get to see so many sides, some of the horribly disturbing of the human condition. There are many, many disturbing scenes in the film that just make your stomach turn and you forget you're watching this fantasy story and you feel like you're right there with them being attacked by these aliens. One of the most disturbing scenes in the film is when Rachel Ferrier played by Dakota Fanning comes across a literal river of bodies. Even watching the Aliens destroy the human beings into dust is disturbing. There is non stop action and it just has you on the edge of your seat until the very last moment. And there we come in to the big problem of the filmthe ending. It's very tacked on and yes it's the proper ending and perfectly feasible but never properly set up. It just sort of happens and everything stops and it's over. It's a huge let down after being so built up for two hours. Nonetheless if you want the best movie of the year to see in the theateryou need to see War Of The Worlds. It's the reason movies were made, it's fun, it makes you emotional, cry out, sucks you in it's just amazing. Go see it!! 9/10

title: Spielberg and Cruise -- mixed bag, this one...
review:
I completely agree with what one reviewer stated -- that Spielberg is THE master of the big budget Hollywood SFX movie, and certainly outclasses the lesser competition offered by comparative amateurs Bay and Emmerich. Spieberg's SFX, while impressive and unrivaled, still play a close second to character definition and development. You care about his characters and their progress through the film. Yeah okay, I thought Tom Cruise's character was an *ssh*le too, but you came to a reluctant understanding and respect for his love for his kids.

I certainly didn't feel any of this character empathy from "Day After Tomorrow" or "The Island." I was almost happy NYC froze over in DAT, if only to shut up those whiny New York nomads and put an end to all their belly-aching. Lady Liberty destroyed? Give me a break -- why not add a final shout of "Damn you! Damn you all the hell!" Sure, the plot suffered somewhat and I too groaned at the abrupt and convenient ending typical of many Hollywood films, but you have to admit some of the scenes in the film were the most intense and exciting you watched in a long time.

title: Whoooosh! With our de-clothing ray!
review:
See, the problem with films these days is too much of a good thing. Too much CGI, too much violence and, in this case, too much sickly sweet goody-goodness for its, errr own good.

It started off weakly, with Morgan Freeman's rendition of the now famous opening narration. Morgan Freeman is a great actor, don't get me wrong, but he sounded bored whilst reading this. Hardly the commanding voice of Richard Burton.

Dakota Fanning.... Not since Ernie Reyes Jr in Conan the Destroyer have I wanted to see a child torn limb from limb so badly. All she does is scream and dispense child-prodigy pearls of wisdom between breaths. Then she screams some more. All this, and losing the use of her legs constantly so that Daddy Cruise has to lug her around like a suitcase, left me beyond irritated with her. In fact, my partner remarked that the movie should be retitled "Carry the Daughter".

The son was equally annoying, but made bearable because you actually thought he might have died at one point. How naive of me to assume that any central character might die in a Spielberg production. Magically he teleports from the jaws of certain death to happy safety in Boston. Or so it seems.

The movie, for all its technical prowess, is woeful in many departments. Spielberg seemed to be attempting to "do a Titanic", in that he set a drama against the backdrop of a tragedy, which was almost incidental to the film. Cameron got it right in Titanic. Spielberg doesn't here. The unfolding family drama is just downright aggravating and just gets in the way.

The plot is just so full of holes that it is embarrassing and insulting to think such a cinematic giant as Spielberg couldn't have even bothered attempting to patch them up. Are we really to swallow that aliens as curious and active as these ones are portrayed can plan a million years ahead? That they would plant machines on our world that long ago "just in case" or as some kind of "lay away" plan? C'mon! The whole thing is so woolly. I mean, woolly story, woolly physics, so much wool that you could knit an entire cardigan whilst watching it! But, on the plus side I learned these unassailable truths from watching this production:

1. Aliens can hide thousands upon thousands of death machines beneath the Earth's surface which, over the course of a million years, are not once damaged or unearthed by seismic activity.

2. Alien weaponry can silently vaporise people but mysteriously leave their clothing unharmed.

3. Aliens are smart enough to make their death machines waterproof but don't think to include an air filtration unit as basic equipment.

4. Electromagnetic Pulses (EMP) will knock out all electrical and electronic equipment and devices, unless said devices are integral to the laughable plot.

5. A jet passenger liner can crash on your house but you will be unharmed if you stay in the basement. What's more, your car will also suffer no ill effects, even though your house and neighbourhood are completely demolished and a convenient, rubble-free path will allow you to drive away afterwards.

6. Newspaper people will scavenge amongst the dead for provisions after even as short a time as one day without food or water.

7. Alien death machines get sick just like their occupants, losing the ability to stand motionless or even operate their defensive shields, thus allowing hapless humans to take them out with simple anti-tank weaponry.

8. After sending machines to Earth millennia ago, the aliens are happy to use these million year old relics again, apparently not having developed their technology any further in the intervening epochs.

9. When planning a sight-seeing trip to an abandoned farmstead, aliens will never bother to put on any kind of protective suit, instead relying on their natural immunity to protect them from any bugs.

If I seem flippant with the above, well....it's the only way I can find to get across the scorn with which I regard this movie. A great opportunity was wasted here. The 1953 version still stands as the undisputed champion of these movies. But, if you must watch an alien invasion movie, rent Independence Day. At least that had no pretensions about what it was. This is just painful.

And to think, Spielberg was worried that Cruise's off-screen antics might negatively affect the movie's revenue. Frankly, the movie would have been a whole lot more entertaining if Tombo had saved the day with a bottle of vitamins. At least we could all have had a good laugh then.

title: Solid entertainment
review:
Stephen Spielberg is a legendary director, no question about that. While i don't see him as the one making the most enjoyable movies in the world there is a certain quality to his work that usually makes it worth at least the two hours you spend watching it. "War of the worlds" is no exception.

Lately it feels like overblown special effects and huge scenes of destruction have been showing up in almost every movie. What was previously something almost unreal and astounding to watch has become commonplace and nothing at all spectacular. When stepping into the movie theater today, watching a big-budget movie, you know that the effects will be good. It's simply not that hard anymore to make it look very nice. So a movie relying more or less exclusively on it's effects is not very likely to appeal to me. "War of the worlds" is more or less a movie like that, but still i found it quite enjoyable.

First of all Tom Cruise is not a bad actor. He's not worth the insane wages he pulls in but he hardly ever gives a bad performance. Here he's as solid as Spielbergs directing. Dakota Fanning is suitably annoying as his odd and twitchy daughter, Justin Chatwin rather lame as his "rebellious" son. The effects are, as can be expected, very good. Rating among the better i've seen as a matter of fact. Adding quite considerably to the enjoyment of the film. Also i like the way that the film-makers kept the look of the original 1950's movie. A nice touch.

So, what's the verdict? Well it's not a bad movie, actually it exceeded my expectations (that were not very high i willingly admit). It's entertaining enough while it lasts. In the end though it's just too bland to really stay with you. The day after i watched it i remember being asked if it was any good and even that close to watching it i could hardly remember it. So it's not likely to ever become a classic or a movie that i would like to own. But it's good entertainment for the moment, saved mostly by it's fast pace and solid directing from Spielberg. I rate it 6/10.

title: Was expecting the worst
review: I'd read a lot of bad things about this film when it came out, so I thought I'd wait until the hoopla died down, that way I could see it at a theater near me that shows movies well after their normal run ... and admission is only $4. Turns out, it was not a total waste. I ended up enjoying the movie DESPITE the sentimental, family-reuniting plot used to tie the action together. It almost felt as though Spielberg was toying with some of his own conventions from movies like ET (ie: the scene where a Spongebob cartoon is playing on the TV, commenting on the ongoing action and a lot of the family's dialog throughout). It was like watching the evil, flip-side of ET. After awhile, I almost ignored this aspect of the movie because it became so overwhelmed by the Martian invasion itself. The tripods were easily the coolest  and scariest  sci-fi devices I've seen in awhile. Their first appearance is nothing short of stunning. The on-the-ground visual approach to the film worked extremely well; which seems like the whole point of showing it from one family's point-of-view. All of the atrocities committed by the invaders  the harvesting of blood, the disintegrations  were palpable from this angle. The scenes of mass migration from major cities, and especially the shot of scores of bodies floating downstream really disturbed me, especially considering the recent situation in New Orleans. And when people began rioting and shooting at each other over a car that ran, the whole invasion situation seemed eerily real. If only the family's story didn't get in the way in certain places (ie: the son appearing at the end... it would have been more believable had he died), this could have been a far better movie.

title: Skirmish of the Worlds.
review: Intense theme, huge CGI effects, but the movie just felt empty on the whole. Maybe it was the fact that the running story followed a tired, typical family group and never really had any other focus. Maybe the said story moves along a bit too quickly, leaving some holes behind. Who knows? Still, as a summer movie, it makes with the eye-candy and provides us with some astonishing scenes of hostile alien chaos. Tom Cruise was pretty much his normal self but I'm sort of getting tired of seeing Dakota Fanning, what with her ringed, droopy eyes. Tim Robbins makes an appearance too, in a role that doesn't seem to suit him. Ah, what can you do?

title: Great special effects, try not to analyse it, just enjoy it!
review:
The special effects for this movie is awesome, but the technology concept is not as convincing. The sound of the alien ship is exactly that of a ship's horn, that made it a bit funny than scary. The aliens are quite similar in shape to that in "Independence Day." The storyline is not smooth enough. Without knowing the story ahead of time, it's hard to understand who actually killed the aliens, is it the virus or the birds.

However, Tom Cruise's performance is excellent in presenting a father's most original intention. Not to save the world, but just a daughter. Parallel to the son's interest to save the world, it further emphasized basic human characteristics in troubled time.

The scene at the harbour, where they were forced to give up their car is relatively realistic- basic survival instinct.

If your intention is just to enjoy a good sci-fi special effect movie, and not too picky about the logic or what does and doesn't make sense, this is it.

title: Surprisingly faithful to Wells; surprisingly, a paean to family life
review:
I admit to a great deal of apprehension about the news that this science fiction classic would be retold by Spielberg with Cruise; but once in the theater, almost all of my fears quickly faded away.

With one major exception, Spielberg has hewn closely to H.G. Wells' original story. (That exception concerns when and how the tripods first reach their destination.) This in itself was a pleasant surprise; but when I saw how the story unfolded at the micro, family level, I truly appreciated Spielberg's vision in trying to connect a modern audience with what is by now almost a parody of a First Contact story between alien cultures. By keeping the focus tightly on Cruise and his highly dysfunctional family, Spielberg tells the story inside-out, in a way that keeps the viewer glued to the plot.

Highly recommended, although young children are certain to be frightened by the dark, claustrophobic scenes of panicked flight and one-sided combat that characterize much of the film.

title: this kicked butt
review:
okay. when i first saw the 1953 version of this movie i fell asleep in class. but i saw the preview for this is theaters and i thought, "thats how it should be!" One major plus of this movie was the main characters. Tom Cruise and Dakota Fanning gave excellent performances. At the beginning, there is a 10 to 20 min background of the family situation then almost as soon as that ends the main purpose of the movie beings. The special effects were very well done, presenting it to be very real. The sounds, the visuals, and the heart-breaking story of this family keep you on the edge of your seat. Ray Ferrier (Cruise) is a father who cant be relied on as his son, Robby (Justin Chatwick)puts it. Rachel (Fanning) puts on a great performance of sympathizing with her father and teaching him lessons without meaning to.

The movie length however was long yes and some of the plot story was redundant. The basement scene for one.

I suggest seeing this movie.

title: If i was an alien bent on the extermination of the human race.. i'd be armed with more then a death ray and shield
review:
I quite liked this movie In the UK it was rated 12A.. luckily I didn't take my boyfriend's little brother to see it as the killing was a bit detailed. The killing of the humans I thought was great though. I don't recall seeing many movies with scenes like this one. I remember coming out of the cinema thinking "woah".

I admit that there were bits i didn't like about the movie.. The Americanisation of the story and the bad father plot annoyed me a bit. I also thought, as mentioned before, the basement scene was too long. I felt that the ending was a bit rushed. The aliens planed this for years and years yet one alien pod goes down and all the others fall with it as they now have a weakness... *yawn* If you're going to spend all this time and money on a movie you could at least make the ending better/match up to the better parts of the movie. But anyways I thought it was a good movie. I shall be buying it when it comes out on DVD.

title: Excellent!!
review:
I'm yet to see the original of this film, but after seeing this remake definitely makes me want to go out and buy it.

To begin with, I'm NOT a fan of Tom Cruise at all. Upon leaving the cinema I decided to go out and buy Minority Report, and Vanilla Sky just because of the respect I'd gained for Cruise after seeing that film.

The special effects are mind blowing, but definitely not over the top and have you sitting on the edge of your seat throughout the entire film. The first time that you get to see one of the machines had me sitting with my jaw hanging open going "Holy Sh*t!!" The film definitely makes an impact on you, and it's fantastic to see a film with a GOOD alien plot.

Dakota Fanning is, as always, fantastic in this film - Very natural and believable acting. Will never stop going to see her films! Tim Robbins plays an interesting part, but a good one. Kutos to him too.

title: Total escapism through a thrilling adventure
review: I took four 11 year olds to see this as a birthday treat and really didn't want to see this movie at all as I'm totally fed up with Hollywood blockbusters and stars. What a surprise, I was literally sat on the edge of my seat in the cinema as thrilling special effects spilled out one after another. Didn't really need a good story line as the movie moved so fast from one nerve wracking moment to the next. There is the tiniest typical Hollywood movie moment at the end but besides that - great. Dakota Fanning was criticised for annoying screaming, I would have screamed faced with the same situations. As for the 11 year olds, they got out of their seats and hid they were so scared - at last something that fazes the oh so cool kids of today.

title: outstanding
review: oh my god this film was the most awesome film i av ever seen it was fantastic from start to finish i recommend any1 who thinks the old one is good then they watch this and you will be blown away watch it if u dare !!! my dad was a bit weary about watching it because we watched the new charlie and the chocolate factory and it was a load of rubbish and he didn't think this film would be any good compared to the original but he was amazed and that was my 57 year old dad and he doesn't say anything is betta that what he as already said was awesome the first time round ... .............. .......... .......... ........... so just watch it and see what you think of it !!

title: Speilbergs finest?
review:
I saw this movie with high expectations, I wasn't too badly disappointed either. But as a fan of the original, I think it strayed from the plot, of which the idea was "stolen".

A lot of people I talked to, said they thought it was rubbish, based mostly on the ending, which I had to educate them, by telling them the opening Morgan Freeman speech told us of our allies and its true to the original. I think most of these people expected an Independence day style ending.

title: realism beyond belief in this fantastic Spielberg remake!
review:
i have never actually read the H.G. Wells masterpiece The War Of The Worlds but i've heard that this film doesn't follow the storyline properly. i'm actually all for following the original book when a film based on one is released, and it annoys me when a film doesn't follow on properly. if i'd read the book this comment may have been more negative.

this film really impressed me! it starts straight into the action with amazing realism and got me hooked from the very beginning. i thought the tripods were very cool, and they looked fantastically real. the heat ray was great as well. Cruise is very good as a father on the edge but what really impressed me was the amazing performance from Dakota Fanning. i don't know very many good child actors but Dakota was the star of this film i think. one of my favourite parts of this film was undoubtedly the time spent in the mad dudes lair. it added a very creepy edge to the film and when the aliens were crawling through the house i could feel the tension in the cinema. the slow conflict build between cruise and the mad dude is portrayed very well. i watched in awe when the ferry capsized, that part was very well done, and as i've already mentioned, Spielberg made realism a very important factor in this film. here's a bit of ridiculous trivia: Spielberg bought a whole jumbo jet just so he could blow it up in the film! worked well though. overall i thought this film was excellent, good performances, ultimate realism, and very atmospheric. however, i think that Spielberg should not have strayed from the actual storyline. my advice: watch the film before you read the book! a great piece of cinematography: 8/10

title: Might be scary for some people
review:
I was looking forward to seeing this film for months and it was better than I expected. In this film, divorced Tom Cruise is not seen as THE hero he has always been, but an everyday person fighting for his life just like everyone else. He has to protect his two children. His daughter gets annoying after a while with the screams but this adds to the love shown between brother and sister, and Tom Cruise as the dad is perfect as trying hard to become a part of their life and a good dad.

This is an excellent film. the visual effects are fantastic and it looks so real. I thought it was quite scary in places but my sister was quite literally shaking and she's 14! Yet, she isn't used to this sort of film as I am. Far better, in my opinion, than the original. More up to date and it shows what a father has to do to protect his children. Watch and enjoy!

title: Spielbergs best since "Brothers"
review: Not a bad alien/action movie. Spielbergs movies have been a bit darker this past decade (ie: "AI") and "War" is no different. That does not mean its bad. Its a sort of combination of Close Encounters, ET and Band of Brothers. There's also this cliché in a lot of near future/distant future movies that portray military troops as mindless automatons itching to violate ALL civil liberties as soon as the first wave of attacks begin. Not necessarily so with "War". The enemy IS the enemy. There's also a certain "classic flavor" about "War". Death and dying are not shown unless they NEED to be shown to hold the story together, this becomes very obvious in a scene involving Cruise, Fanning, and Robbins. And last, for its realism, I give War a ten out of ten. There are no knock out punches (re: Will Smith in ID4 punching out an alien pilot), the situations appear about as real as they can appear given the hellish situation the characters find themselves in. Try to see this one before it exits theaters, if not, put it at the top of your rental list.

title: Great Ride
review: Wow...this film was a pretty cool ride from near the beginning. The special effects were fantastic but the actors did a fine job with their roles as well. Despite all media frenzy surrounding Tom Cruise these days, it's easy for people to forget that he is talented and gifted actor who's pulled off a wide variety of characters in his acting history; everything from silly (Risky Business) to serious (Born On The Fourth Of July) to surreal (Minority Report,etc.). He does a bang-up job as part-time dad with some serious self-issues, and it's nice to see this character evolve in to a better human being (even it's forced on him by alien invasion). Spielberg certainly knows how to make a movie that entertains the masses and keeps those of us with relatively short attention spans on the edges of our seats. The two kids get a little whiny in the beginning but their characters come along nicely too. This flick certainly has it's jump-out-of-your-seat moments so be prepared. Worth the price of the ticket while it's still in the theatres. Go see it!

title: Spielberg blinks again...
review:
War of the Worlds is a film that is easily recommendable, but simply fails to achieve greatness. The opening half hour shows that Steven Spielberg still knows how to scare people. The revelation of the tripod alien machines is without a doubt one of the most frightening scenes I have witnessed on the big screen and alone makes the film worth seeing. In terms of technical achievement and suspense, War of the Worlds hits its mark.

Unfortunately, War of the Worlds is yet another example of Steven Spielberg approaching greatness in a science-fiction film, only to blink in the game of chicken that is being an unapologetic artist. Like Minority Report and A.I., Spielberg shows great potential to not wimp out with a dark subject matter... and then wimps out. As seen in those two films, he seems to feel it is necessary to wrap up a film with absolute, perfect happiness, thus negating any sense of reality to the situation whatsoever. While we see such an apocalyptic nightmare as the alien invasion is presented, in the end the main character suffers no loss: both his children survive even when we are almost assured of one's death.

Spielberg is one of the few filmmakers alive today that could afford to take his name for a spin and risk making a film that does not conform to the Hollywood rule of making everything work out in the end. I will never understand why he feels it necessary to ensure that the main character suffers no loss or that the horrors of the situation are always resolved in such a way as to let the audience breathe a complete sigh of relief.

Even Frank Capra knew that this was unnecessary. Did Mr Potter ever pay for his actions in It's A Wonderful Life? No. However, Spielberg doesn't seem able to accept the fact that life doesn't work out perfectly. Until he does, he will continue to make films like War of the Worlds that are very entertaining throughout, but ultimately disappoint in the end.

title: Special f/x marathon!
review:
This movie is best viewed on the big screen. It is worth seeing, but just make sure you do it while it is still in theaters, or only on video/DVD if you are able to watch it with a really nice home theater system. If not, the movie will just not sit well with you.

Cruise puts in his usual decent performance. Nothing to write home about, but definitely performs the action movie role well. Dakota Fanning is amazing. She is easily the best child actor out of Hollywood since Tatum O'Neal. She will win an Oscar before the age of 18 (she just won't win it for this action-packed blockbuster.) If you like sci-fi, action, and special f/x you will like this movie. If you're looking for revelation and great drama go see something else.

title: Great movie, great ending.
review:
Now, I realize that many people didn't like this movie because of the ending. I agree, partly. The inclusion of Ray ending up with his family was somewhat trite, but that's what you get for a Hollywood movie and Spielberg in general. Remember, this is the dude who managed to ruin AI with that happy ending he tacked on.

Anyway, for those who didn't like the sudden "look the Martians are dead because of bacteria and virii" ending, read the book. See the original movie. Listen to the Orson Welles radio play. This is the original ending and the proper ending. I, for one, love the ending as it takes the power out of our hands and puts it into the hands of the random, making us watch in futility as people die for 2 hours without any way to fight back.

And I laughed my ass off.

title: Creepy but clever
review: Tom Cruise and Steven Spielberg are made for each other. Their last pairing on 'Minority Report' was a match made in heaven, a gripping and engaging film. This is no different. Tom is pushed into the shadows by the truly talented Dakota Fanning (Hide and Seek)and he never quite convinces us that hes a careless layabout. Spielbergs directing is a sensation, with plenty of choppy editing and explosive special effects, but at many times the plot line is lacking and you are left feeling you might have missed something. The soundtrack isn't anywhere near as gripping as the original, but the narration, by none other than Morgan Freeman, pulls you right into the action. For those who haven't read thebook, the ending is a revelation leaving you in awe that something so simple can have sure dire consequences, and you will laugh that it had such a massive impact. Overall, the CGI is spectacular, the acting is only average, the plot is a little gappy, but this is a film for any action addict.

title: "Gripping"
review: War of the worlds is a brilliantly but together piece of cinema. It has a gripping atmosphere with a strong performance from Tom Cruise and equally sensitive performances from his caricatures' off springs. I have to say that I thought the 12 rating was a bit of a surprise, this film had enough suggestive material to send the creative minded into frenzy. I have to admit that I didn't know that much about the whole war of the world's concept. I'd heard the odd snippet of Richard Burton doing the voice over for the musical piece. Nice to here Morgan Freeman adding his unmistakable tone to the beginning of this roller-coaster. The one thing in particular that stood out for me was that the story was based solely around Tom Cruise and his family. There was none of this Independence Day rubbish about America battling the alien invaders and showing the rest of the world how it's done. This film is brilliant and had me on the edge of my seat for the duration. So much so that when the end came I was slightly disappointed. The film just ends with very little explanation. That is, I have to say, the only criticism I have. A truly enjoyable film, with a great performance from Tom Cruise and Spielberg back to his best.

title: Flawed but fantastic
review:
There are really 2 movies here, both are vignettes, and one is much better than the other. One story is a surprisingly believable update of HG Wells classic novel, shown as a 'road movie' thru the eyes of Tom Cruise. He does panic well, although Dakota Fanning steals the entire movie from under him. It really works on your nerves the first time you see it. A small note here because I haven't seen it mentioned... John Williams score for this film is his best in a long while. It's wallpaper, and it's perfect. What doesn't work is the character sketch of Cruise's family. Ray is forced to choose between his children during a military strike scene that looks like the CGI guys rushed and it all falls apart right there. This a sci-fi/horror movie- not 'Sophie's choice'. Then the concentration-camp like 'basement' sequence. The inevitable 'give me back my child' action sequence. From here on out it's all CGI, actors and sets and oh, well.

But damn that first hour is good. Those tripods are beautiful and belong to that realm of solid, imposing, realistic looking CGIs.

title: Better than the Original Movie
review:
So, this is an alien invasion movie. If you don't have expectations of what this could bring, I don't know how helpful my review will be. On the flip-side, since you're considering this movie, I'll assume you've seen some of these. The genre really dates at least back to the days of "Them," which isn't about aliens at all, but giant ants, but the idea is the same.

The basic formula is malevolent creatures wreak havoc on earth. You can also make a good case for many other sub-genres essentially sharing the same formula. Whether it's disaster films, or a mutant virus in "Outbreak," the asteroid in "Deep Impact," Godzilla in those films, or even zombie movies, like "Dawn of the Dead," we're dealing with Good v. Evil, where humans are always wear the white hat. I would argue these movies should be distinguished from the entirely psychological dramas that rely on similar threats, as in "The Day the Earth Stood Still," "Failsafe," or "War Games," but where humanity doesn't actually deal with the disaster occurring.

Movies traditional to this genre, "The Puppet Masters," is another example, the disasters do occur, and movie then focuses on dealing with the consequences (inevitably humanity wins). In all these cases, as in War of the Worlds, the evil is not understandable, it isn't reasonable, you aren't expected to sympathize with the bad guys. Really these films are about two things.

1. How would humans react to potential annihilation or destruction. Basically the human element.

2. Special Effects. How convincing is the destruction, i.e., how suspenseful is the movie.

Assuming you've seen a few of these kinds of movies, call them dystopian, you know most are truly terrible, take Dolph Lundgren's, "I Come in Peace," (so poor it becomes a comedy) or the "Critters" sequels as examples. Most in this genre are simply so bad you're sorry to have sat through them. War of the Worlds is not one of these. Instead, it is a nearly flawlessly executed.

The film goes beyond the typical disaster epic, personalizing the destruction metaphorically with Tom Cruise's character's own family disaster--divorce and alienated children. Cruise does a fine job as the typically flawed hero, who creates all his own problems but is able to shine when real danger threatens. The role doesn't require much of Cruise, but his performance is certainly better than run of the mill.

The special effects are incredible. Simply the best FX yet to come out of Hollywood yet. Some have complained about the whether the alien craft are menacing enough, they were for me.

The psychological aspects presented by potential human extinction are well done, but limited due to Spielberg's choice of using Cruise's family as symbolic of the greater world. There are the mob scenes and mass hysteria, obligatory, but well executed.

Without giving away the ending, I would say the movie's only flaw is its ending. The pacing of the story changes too abruptly and the close of the film isn't all it could be. But the movie was/is a blockbuster with millions of dollars of investment at stake...the general public wants, and gets, its focus-group tested ending. Some of you will be disturbed by this, others of you will understand, and still more will enjoy it. I'm in the camp of those that understand the practicalities, so the ending doesn't dissuade me from giving a 10 out of 10 rating.

Simply the best alien invasion movie ever made.

title: Very very very good!
review: I loved this movie! The ending was awesome! The plot was awesome, and Tom Cruise (Looks and acting) and Dakota Fanning were at their best. This movie ROCKED. I liked the quiet/loud moments, they made me jump. And how happy the ending was...(That's a bit of a spoiler...isn't it?). It was my favorite summer movie. He did the character really well. And I like how they took the old movie (and Radio show) and put new characters and a new family plot too.

title: War of the not so logical events
review:
when i first heard that war of the worlds is being filmed and above all that Steven Spielberg,the man who gave us such movies as "E.T" and of course "Close Encounters of the Third Kind" is going to direct it ! i was watching the movie and the first question that came up to my head was "why ?",and i don't mean,why did the aliens come to earth;but why,after i was under the impression that the EMP strike of the Aliens killed all electrical power around it for miles,i saw a man taking pictures with what looked like a good new camera,and them i saw another guy with a digital video cam taking snap shots at the Tri-Walker,should i go on ? from the fact that they didn't have to stop for one moment cause of a block in the road,or that in the whole movie you could see only three people who are not police or army that have guns (and this is America we are talking about here !). a lot of things didn't make sense,and it takes more than a lot of (very nice) visual effects to distract a movie buff as myself from.

over all,i gave this movie a Passing score of 6,sorry,but i really wanted this movie to be more than just another flashy war/judgment day/Si-Fi movie,but that's what it was...Too Bad !

title: It could have been better....
review:
OK it was a great movie but it could have been better.

First of all when a director makes the audience think someone is dead but really alive is quite stupid.

Everyone thought Robbie was dead but he appears at the end,( how can he survive the machines when he was right in front of them )? Miranda Otto's character also survives when her whole city was destroyed and her house wasn't even touched.

What was the point of storing humans in pods when the aliens main mission was to completely annihilate the human race? Last but not least wouldn't the tripods be covered in bacteria if they were buried for so long? I'm not criticising the film I'm just seeing how it could improve.

Henry

title: The weakest, most unsatisfying movie ending I've ever seen.
review: Despite some cool visual effects... this movie is ultimately a miserable flop. Reaching its high-point about 15 minutes in, the story then sputters along for awhile before nose-diving into a utterly pathetic, brainless ending that leaves the viewer feeling cheapened and cheated. The characters are not believable, and with the exception of Dakota Fanning, not even likable. But even Fanning's predictable cuteness doesn't work in this film. The story is highly melodramatic with little real substance or depth, and the plot never takes clear shape. The whole film is further handicapped by the fact that it takes itself much too seriously. What was Spielberg thinking on this one? Definitely his worst piece to date.

title: Dynamite! Explosive! Don't miss it! A must-see!
review:
War of the Worlds does exactly what it says on the tin and it does not disappoint. Expecting a summer blockbuster aimed at kids and therefore not expecting to be particularly impressed, I found myself surprised and absolutely riveted, with a pounding heart for most of the movie. The effects are phenomenal, worth discussion at length in themselves. I am looking foreword to the DVD bonus material for some explanation. There are no clever but clichéd aerial shots, zooms or views from the tripod's perspective; the storytelling is done from the viewpoint of Cruise's character only and this makes it compelling, utterly absorbing and very real as a result.

In an age where natural disasters, heart-stopping news stories and eyewitness accounts of appalling tragedy are unfortunately becoming more and more commonplace, Spielberg harnesses the power of the personal to great effect. We see only the desperate run for the protagonist's life throughout the first two thirds of the movie, without any silly Bruce Willis heroics. This is neatly backed up by Cruise's reliably strong and underplayed acting as Joe Average, plonked in a workaday domestic situation, failing miserably at restoring a broken relationship with his resentful children.

Like AI - Artificial Intelligence, E.T. Close Encounters and even Jaws, Spielberg has always lavished attention on the scene-setting, making the squabbles between siblings, corny jokes, flawed parenting and suppressed emotion compelling viewing in itself. This, contrasted with the extraordinary, whether it's sharks, aliens or robots make the subsequent action all the more powerful.

As a result you can see evidence of all these previous successes reflected in War Of The Worlds, along with some hefty borrowing from M Night Shayalman's Signs, Falling Down and his own work as producer in Twister. Nevertheless, you can justifiably add here that Spielberg was at the forefront of all these and where does the pastiche begin and end with a genre such as this? Probably with Spielberg himself.

Thank God Spielberg was first tackling such a project and Michael Bay or Jerry Bruckheimer didn't get a look in - mercifully and very tastefully, considering the naturally high body count in a film of this nature, the audience is spared flying body parts and dying people gasping their last. While hapless citizens are exterminated over and over these are almost wholly filmed in the distance. Again in these troubled times there is no need to glorify this kind of gratuitous gore: we see enough of it on TV. While this may have been made to gain the 12A certificate the UK and the equivalent domestically, it also makes much more palatable viewing and reflects the intelligence and sensitivity of the director.

Finally a word about that ending. Yes it's weak, yes Cruise does take on a bit of Bruce "Welcome to the party pal" Willis's characteristics (the book had a completely different and violent ending as it's set in a village in southeast England at the end of the c19th) and everyone - in a comfortable suburb of Boston at least - lives happily ever after. It doesn't sit particularly well after the shocking pace of the previous 90 minutes, and it was greeted with a few groans in the cinema where I saw it.

But let's put this in context: as long as we have conservative, probably Republican, white American men at the helm of the the studios involved in financing movies and more than enough evidence that happy endings put bums on seats, I don't see things changing in my lifetime. It's disappointing but that's life. I was just glad to get home to my own humdrum domestic situation and put the kettle on, happy not to have bloodsucking monsters tearing down my door.

title: Good action movie
review:
I went to see this one in the movies, where I hadn't gone for a while and I have to admit this was a good experience. One has to see it on big screen. It is definitely a Spielberg movie - massive, impressive and well-built episodes with the army, aliens and the fighting. An atmosphere of mystery was added. I didn't feel bored or annoyed even once.

Regarding this, I had to give 10 points. Even the jokes at the beginning sounded very funny to me. Intenseness of the situation grew gradually.

"War of the Worlds" clearly achieved excellently this sense of catastrophe, that could engage people and offer them excitement while sitting safely in their chairs. So I definitely recommend watching this film.

title: Go rent Signs. Much better science fiction alien attack
review: I always thought Signs with Mel Gibson was OK, but not anything to write home about. Until I saw War of the Worlds. Now Signs looks like a top notch drama/suspense/science fiction. Both movies are the same as far as the main characters running from an unknown. At least in Signs there is some small bit of "discovery" by the main characters. Not so in War of the Worlds. Also, the suspense was much greater in Signs. On top of tjhe story being a bummer, the acting is terrible. The special effects were very "small screen". The best special effect was an alien head/neck trying to find the main characters in a basement. It looked no better than a vacuum cleaner hose.

title: Not As Great As Expectations, But Still Good
review:
Construction man Ray Ferrier (Tom Cruise) is having a busy weekend: He's late to meet his ex-wife, odd strikes of thunder are occurring, and he has to babysit his ex's two kids for the weekend: Distant teen Robbie (Justin Chatwin) and little girl Rachel (Dakota Fanning), both of which dislike him intensely. But as the thunder gets worse, giant alien tripods come out of the ground and start blasting everyone to dust! So, the family fights for survival as they wander throughout the state.

Don't be fooled by the marketing campaign for War of the Worlds: This is not a war film about aliens and other planets, including our own: This is simply a movie where Tom Cruise and Dakota Fanning wander the state of Massachusetts for two hours, and we occasionally get ear-splitting action scenes or brief glimpses of the alien tripods. War of the Worlds should have been titled "Ferrier." But still, War of the Worlds is a fast-paced, loud and interesting action movie with great production values and impressive performances from everybody. The film is massively entertaining although there isn't much substance, and there are intense dark themes that help the movie become a legitimately scary movie.

The film moves along at a killer pace, and there are moments of genuine suspensesomething I haven't felt in a theater for a long time. For that reason, War of the Worlds is a unique and rewarding theatrical experience, and it therefore pays off repeatedly. The special effects are awesome, and the way the tripods blow people to bits is actually very disturbing and, perhaps, more effective than director Steven Spielberg and company were expecting. Hey, the more the merrier, right? Spielberg gives a fabulous direction job, and supporting actor Tim Robbins gives the film's most interesting performance, however short it is. The rest of the cast shines as the movie moves along with disturbing action sequences and hardcore suspense, which means that those expecting a harmless action film along the lines of The Day After Tomorrow will be a bit disturbed: War of the Worlds is intense stuff.

But, since we've come to expect a movie about a war and worlds, when the film finally ends, we can't help but feel the "That's it?" factor. But, if you enter the film knowing that the film will go as I say, then you will find War of the Worlds to be a grand pleasurewhich is how I feel, too, although I can't say I wasn't just a little bit disappointed.

title: A personal survival story
review:
I thought this was a much better story than a lot of the other alien invasion stories of the past several years. You're not overburdened with a lot of technical jargon and scenes of generals and Presidents in situation rooms planning strategies. It's also not about jet fighter pilots or other military men taking these aliens out. It's simply the story of a father (Cruise) heavily focused on the survival of his two kids. His kids are the overriding concern here, not how to fight these aliens, finding out who they are, and why they're doing this, etc. He's a father that will do everything in his power to make sure nothing happens to his kids, and he'll go to great lengths to make sure nothing happens to them.

Kudos to Spielberg for resisting the urge to turn this into a grand heroic adventure (like Independence Day), and keeping it on a personal level. In a way it was similar to M. Knight Shymalon's Signs, but Signs was not nearly as scary as this.

Tim Robbins shows up to make a cameo as a creepy survivor, which Tom Cruise and family meet up with halfway through the movie. Morgan Freeman also shows up as the narrator of the movie.

title: another Spielberg fantasy
review:
War of the Worlds is a modern retelling of the novel written by H.G. Wells. In this remake, a family faces alien attacks and finds a way to survive this huge mess.

I enjoyed all the action, explosions, and the actors. Tom Cruise did an outstanding job with his role as a divorced man, Ray Ferrier. Dakota Fanning, gee, a child like her can sure act! Justin Chatwin-great new appearance from him. Both Justin and Dakota play Ray's children and together, all three of them find a way to survive the alien attacks. Finally, Tim Robbins, he did a great job portraying a frightened psycho.

Overall, I enjoyed the whole movie. This sci-fi fantasy is not for everyone, especially for people who don't like sci-fi and fantasies. A 8 out of 10 and a solid B won't hurt a bit.

title: Not Spielberg's best alien movie, but still good
review: After watching the brilliant Minority Report, I couldn't wait to see the next collaboration by Spielberg & Cruise, hoping for an even better film. War of the Worlds is good, but nowhere near Minority Report. The premise is pretty simple, Cruise plays a divorced dad who gets his kids for a couple of days while his ex-wife visits her parents. Couldn't have picked a worse time, as this is when the martians decide to attack us and take over the world, and plumage our resources. Cruise, who is not a very responsible dad, must grow up and protect his kids while they try to make their way to Boston, to their Mother. This film is not really about aliens and their takeover, but about family. The film which is masked to really resemble the 9/11 attacks a couple years ago. This film is more about family relationships then sci-fi action pix. But the flick does contain some the greatest special effects ever witnessed on film. A must see!

title: Closer to the Book
review: I have a very fond place in my heart for George Pal's The War of the Worlds made during the golden age of science fiction. I was somewhat apprehensive upon hearing a remake was in the works, but many of my fears were allayed hearing the film would be directed by none other than Stevin Spielberg. Well, overall, this remake was a quality film yet I have some ambivalent feelings toward it. Spielberg does what he does best: lots of great suspense and solid storytelling, awesome, state-of-the-art special effects, wonderful music by John Williams, and an outwardly satisfying film...for the most part. Actually, this film was somewhat of a letdown for me. Now before you misunderstand, I did think it was a decent film. It was definitely much closer to the spirit of the book. The special effects...WOW! When you see the spaceships and the Martians, they look stunning and horrifying. I also like the way that Spielberg stays in touch with the common man rather than, say the president ala Independence Day(a film I ultimately enjoyed more). What I didn't take to was the kids as protagonists again...a typical Spielberg device but one that really doesn't work nearly as well in this film. Dakota Fanning as Rachel does a serviceable job in a rather stereotypical role as the frightened out of her wits pre-adolescent. Justin Chatwin; however, as the obnoxious, rebellious teen at odds with a father he feels antipathy for is far less satisfying. I didn't like the kid at all. Tom Cruise is acceptable at best...and really that is rather generous. Spielberg might have added a bit more depth to these characters. And I really am puzzled at Spielberg's use of the two stars from the original Pal film: Gene Barry and Ann Robinson. If you blink, you will miss them. They are not even on screen three seconds. C'mon Steve. Couldn't you give them just a bit more screen time? With what they have, you might have well not used them at all.But these acting concerns aside for a film effects oriented, this remake is a quality film but definitely not one of its director's best.

title: Sorry, Spielberg, this is not anywhere close to being your best.
review: There are disappointments, and then there are mega disappointments, and this movie rates close to being a mega disappointment. Some effects were very cool, but hey, where's the plot? Is it taking kids to Mommy? I tried desperately to look for some similarities to the creation of H. G. Wells and I came up with a strained brain. And by the way, if all the other cars had their juice drained out of them by the tripods, what about Tom Cruise's wagon? Cruise, it seems, has become an aimless 'cruise missile' - pardon the pun an'all. Went to see it on the strength of Spielberg's reputation and came out regretting the time spent. I hate to give a bad review, but there's no escaping this one. Sorry, Spielberg, but this effort is not even close to being your best.

title: Fresh out of the theater
review:
First let me start by saying that I have not seen the other version of the film nor have I read the book. Now before some of you get discard my opinions altogether let me say that this movie was what it was. A major summer action film. Lets put Spielberg, Cruise, Fanning, Robbins for a half cup of tea and the voice of Freeman together to make a remake. And as much as Mr. Cruise annoys me in interviews and what not he delivers another solid performance. Sure there was a lot of explosions and screaming but a big summer action movie would be incomplete without it much less an invasion/they are trying to take over the world movie.

To me the part I really enjoyed was that it took a shot at how powerless we really are as human beings. Aliens attack earth and start exterminating and harvesting us and we cannot stop them. And then the viruses of the earth that we have cursed for so long becomes our salvation. Viruses - one of the things we can't beat - we only become immune. So we cant beat bacteria and we can't beat aliens, however luckily we have developed an immunity based relationship with the bacteria and the aliens, as much studying as they did, did not account for this. Too bad eh? The only part I did not really like at all was the fact that Robbie lived. I mean what are the chances then again the chances of a lot of that movie actually happening are pretty slim so I guess it fits the theme. Overall it was a good theater experience but I will not be renting or buying, not unless I get surround sound or something.

title: Spielbergs alian invasion film is solid but not great
review: Spielberg's end of the world invasion film is decent. The acting was not great, special effects were amazing, Spielberg's direction was truly brilliant, spielberg is a master of his craft. However the film did not end in a believable manner, chatwin was horrible and cruise was only decent. I thought this film could have been better, but nonetheless, was entertaining. I would have liked maybe for their to be more characters involved, Spielberg instead showed us only one family and didn't give much depth to them, although Cruise's character was well-written. The script wasn't bad, the film had a good style but could have been better. About as good as A.I., not as good as Minority report 8/10

title: A great epic, but a bit too much ET and hidden meaning
review:
I came to this movie with some preconceptions, my image was clouded by two names. Spielbergs tendency to be very off form of late and Cruise who has been bigger than any character he's played, and my fear was that seeing him on screen would bring thoughts of his antics offscreen rather than of the character he's playing.

I wasn't prepared for the movie that I saw, and some excellent screen moments from both Cruise and Spielberg. Here they both prove that they are on better than ever form and that when needed to they can deliver the best in Hollywood.

Let's start with Cruise. His performance begins like the Cruise we think we know, it's almost as if Spielberg knew that the audience would need to be guided along to this character rather than just dropped in front of him. The first moment I saw him I thought of the actor, the name.

Then Spielberg pulls you down to ground level and there he is, grinning his hugely perfect and confident grin, stepping proudly to a big mustang and speeding through the corners parking at his house. Suddenly there's a change, you see him step down the performance, there's still some swagger and confidence, and you can still see the personality Cruise, but as the seconds move on and the characters are introduced, so does the personality Cruise disappear. Until the moment the kids have left the car and you're staring at a defensive, embittered and distant father.

Early on he's firing with all cylinders playing the angry father trying to find some way to get to his kids without letting real emotion come through. His kids don't accept him as his father, and the daughter is taking a mothering role while the son is rebelling and lashing out.

This protective exterior comes crashing down quite early on in the movie, as the invasion begins its initial stages. The scene that marks the turn most effectively is when her returns to his family and they begin to ask what has happened. From this point onwards I didn't even think of the personality or even the name of Cruise again, he was just a superb actor.

Throughout the movie he's called upon to display some really strong moments of emotion, particularly of the paternal kind, and I just can't begin to say how convincing and utterly compelling he is during these scenes. It just goes to show what a truly great actor really can do.

The supporting actors are good in the movie, with Dakota Fanning giving an excellent performance as a confused and panicked young child. There's no doubt that she is one of the strongest child actors there is in Hollywood just now, and if she is nurtured well and does not fall for the trappings of Hollywood, she just might become a superb actress. However, her character is called upon to whine, cry, scream, and generally be difficult, and this does get quite grating by the latter half of the movie, although it is fair to say that in such circumstances that's probably how a child would act.

I think this is probably the only time I'd say this about Tim Robbins but his character seemed out of place, and didn't seem to serve any other dramatic purpose than to show that the father wanted to protect his children, yet we knew this already. The character appears out of nowhere, waves over two people amongst the masses running from the battle. I just couldn't fathom that and it seemed merely a need to recreate a section of the original story, whereas the film might have carried better either without it, or a much toned down set of scenes.

The action sequences and effects are stunning. The the tripods walking around the cities firing their rays; people exploding and being vaporised; cars, buildings and roadways being blasted and thrown across the screen with amazing realism, and the action sequence with the boat crossing, all are just stunningly created on screen. I actually couldn't distinguish CGI from model from fullsize, and in the end from reality. It's superbly created and crafted and shows that Spielberg is most definitely back on form.

I found that throughout this telling of War of the Worlds I was thinking of Shymalans Signs again and again. There are many comparisons, and Spielberg is telling the Worlds story from the family viewpoint, yet taking them out of the house.

There are flaws in the story, and it's obviously here to serve a more current purpose with all the terrorism links throughout, yet it is done in that huge epic style and a very impressive one at that. Cruise is stunning in this role, more than I've seen him in a long time, and I totally forgot his personality and who he is off screen and was lost in his performance.

The best thing throughout this movie that I haven't yet mentioned is the overriding feeling of dread that comes out of the movie. I sat through the film with an unease of what was, or could, happen, despite knowing the entire story. That feeling shows a good movie, it drew you in and took you along for the ride making you as anxious as the characters you were watching. This was utterly compelling on screen, yet, in the end, Spielberg wins.

After all this suspense and edge of your seat excitement, we're treated to a typically Spielberg ending, and I have to say that we were surprised beyond words at the twee-ness of it all. To be quite frank it was a complete cop out, designed to give you that nice pat on the head and say "look, everything will be okay" and I hated it. With the message that was being given out throughout the movie we expected an ending that was based more in reality than the world of E.T..

title: Best Sci-fi film yet
review:
HG Wells classic novel has been made a radio broadcast and also made into a film in the 1950s but the best time to remake it would be now, especially as computers help create stunning visual effects. The original film made in the 1950s starred Gene Barry and the film won an Oscar for best special effects. The Steven Spielberg remake deserves an Oscar for the same reason.

War of the Worlds follows ray Ferrier with his son and daughter fighting to survive devastating alien attacks. The only main thing that was changed in this film compared to the original film was the time in which it was set. It is set in present day America, as director Steven Spielberg wanted to give the disaster a realistic view and how a family would fight to survive it. Overall the film is very good, it has a great story, and if you are a fan of Steven Spielberg you must see this film, and when it is given a DVD release, it is worth a purchase.

title: The Good Dad
review:
Finally got around to seeing Steven Spielberg's "War of the Worlds" starring Tom Cruise. Spielberg and Cruise had collaborated before on the very novel and ambitious "Minority Report". A couple years ago when both announced that they were re-teaming on the big budget remake of H.G. Wells's "War of the Worlds", I was both excited and puzzled. The original "War of the Worlds" movie (not the Orson Wells radio broadcast), was for it's time a great science fiction flick, but void of a compelling human story. In keeping with the novel, Spielberg's "War of the Worlds" is still essentially an allegory for natural selection. However, I can now see what drew Spielberg and Cruise to this story which focuses on father, Ray Ferrier (Cruise) and his two kids, Rachel (the awesome Dakota Fanning), and Robbie (talented newcomer Justin Chatwin) in the midst of the devastating alien attack. Cruise's Ray is a divorced crane operator. He is an arrogant and selfish father, who is looking after his kids for the weekend while his ex-wife Mary Ann (a strong Miranda Otto) and her current husband are on a trip up state. Then the world literally comes to a stand still.

The story by Josh Friedman and David Koepp has some great expository touches. For instance we learn through news clips and mostly through survivalist Harlan Ogilvy (the perfectly deranged Tim Robbins) that this war or attempted genocide had been planned for perhaps a million years. The alien weapons of mass destruction were planted underground at various sites around the world, awaiting a predetermined alien mobilization command. The special effects and CGI are cutting edge amazing. "War of the Worlds" is visually stunning.

Given all that, the alien threat is more background, and Spielberg directs our attention to the Ferrier family. In the very beginning, he establishes Ray (Tom Cruise) as a bad Dad. Cruise is effective and believable in portraying Ray's transformation to good Dad. There is a powerful scene where Ray must separate from his son Robbie (Chatwin). The scene is unexpectedly poignant. Justin Chatwin is a powerful young actor. Dakota Fanning is a true talent, becoming more accomplished with each role. Here as Rachel she is truly terrified, but always has her wits about her. She is always natural with a radiant presence. Ultimately, what distinguishes Steven Spielberg's "War of the Worlds" is not the stunning visually effects, but it's story of family. It's the journey of a man learning to become a good father. That is compelling. So are the performances by Cruise, Danning, and Chatwin. Acknowledge too, Spielberg's inspired and deeply personal direction.

title: Not too bad...
review:
I suppose this is the most eagerly awaited blockbuster of the summer? Well, for me it was an overall success; not in the same league of excellence as Close Encounters or Jaws, but better than the Lost World and Hook! The Spielberg hallmarks are there; the gradual build up of tension through little signs, barely noticeable at first, that something is up (or down); the ordinary Joe going about his humdrum life before being interrupted by something big; the cutesy kid.

The plot direction is pretty faithful to the book, given that it's been updated from the 19th Century to present day, and moved from Woking to New Jersey! The invasion, the Martians, the 'war', the eventual demise of the aliens all follow the book. Interestingly, the main protagonist in the book is a philosopher; in the film a dockworker! How times change; the idea that a hero in such a film could be a philosopher would be too outrageous to contemplate. I'm beginning to find Tom Cruise a problem in such roles, just because it's Tom Cruise. He's certainly a good enough actor and plays his part well, but he's now a prisoner of his massive persona, and I find it difficult to get away from that to just accept him as Ray Ferrier. This is my problem really, but if it affects how we all see him it becomes his problem.

Obviously subsidiary characters are conflated or eliminated in the film; the Tim Robbins character is most like the curate in the book; at least, that character had to be killed by the protagonist. Wells seems to use this character to attack religion, or, at least, religious types. No such analysis required in the film; it's just a romping adventure yarn and as such is a little one dimensional, unfortunately. The pace, special effects, excitement, tension and drama cannot be faulted, however, and it's a thoroughly entertaining ride.

The theme of a cataclysmic event is popular at the moment, and reflects the post 9/11, 7/7 zeitgeist (ooo, too many stupid words there). We all seem to be living with the feeling that anything could happen today, a little like during wartime, so this movie is released at the right time to capture this unease. Mankind are now perceived to be losing control of our destiny; we're under attack from within (terrorist attacks) and without (climate change), and this story shows us how things could be if we were to lose control completely.

title: Plot less disaster
review:
Tom Cruise's character was poorly thought out. After reminiscing about his comments when he tried to fiddle with the characters that made up Mission Impossible, I think I understand him a little. He must make the story unique. Otherwise he feels that the story is just more of the same. Unfortunately, Cruise seems to influence every script he's in to the detriment of common sense. In this case it was a disaster of Biblical proportions.

Why does Cruise ruin nearly everything he's done since Top Gun? The script was so idiotic I was rooting for the aliens to zap him! The two kids were actually out-acting the star. When child actors have more sense written into their characters than the star, something's very wrong. Now, if Tom Cruise's character died, then maybe the 2 kids could go and do something that made sense. Running toward populated areas when he knew there were going to be more aliens there was beyond dumb. Idiot plot. Idiot acting! Score of 1. (and that's being generous).

review:
I had been waiting to see this film for ages, i saw a trailer months ago and knew it was a must see!!!
