title: Brilliantly Terrifying
review:
Spielberg's version of WAR OF THE WORLDS is a rather dark vision and utterly terrifying at times. It does what it is supposed to do: scare the living daylights out of you. In an age of terrorism, the film shows us how totally horrifying terrorism is. One can interpret WAR OF THE WORLDS as analogous to our own times. Indiscriminate death, wholesale, delivered with fear tactics and absolutely scary.

The story of the protagonist father, played by Tom Cruise, is wholly predictable, yet in keeping with the tradition of a hometown hero who saves his children and himself from a horrifying fate. Cruise is great as is Dakota Fanning, both deserve awards for their performance.

However, I believe there exists a major flaw in the film that truly bothers me: The demise of the aliens is not dramatically realized. It just happens and is explained to us by the narrator, Morgan Freeman.

Destruction and annihilation are considerably realistic, thus absolutely terrifying. The aliens and their technology are very foreign and exceptionally well done, yet I was on the edge of my seat throughout. Gorgeously edited, John Williams' unique score at times frightened me to death, or should I say, to attention.

This is not entertainment, it's really serious stuff and might agitate some viewers. Not recommended for small children or sensitive types.

title: A brilliantly made film
review:
No, this won't go down in my books as Spielberg's greatest movie. He has a couple of films from my childhood that are in close competition for that slot. However, this is solid entertainment and one of the better movies I've seen in a while. I truly can't remember the last time I sat so rigidly in my seat with an awestruck sensation. The action came precisely when needed - just when your senses are starting to calm down and the flow hints at dragging.

I sat here for about an hour this morning reading the reviews. As I read them, I began to get a very good idea of what to expect from the film. It was clear that most of the people that wrote a negative review got hung up on the little details that seem to detract from the plot upon first thought. For instance - how did the one camcorder work when everything else was dead and how did the van start when all the other cars wouldn't. A question probably asked a lot is, "How could a veteran filmmaker such as Steven Spielberg miss such a blatant plot hole?" Well, the answer is probably this - HE DIDN'T MISS IT! In order to accept such a thing happening, you have to understand how electro-magnetic pulses function. The pulse fries any electric circuitry that is close enough to the area to be affected and is NOT SHIELDED. It is feasible that the camcorder in question was in a carrying case that protects from electro-magnetic interference. They do exist. For the van, what the harsh reviewers failed to mention is that the van is at a car repair shop and the damaged part had been replaced. There are no lingering effects of an electro-magnetic pulse. Once a damaged part has been replaced, the product should work again. The other camera that was seen being used was a wind-up camera (not digital) with no electronic circuitry.

OK, moving on. Dakota Fanning's character doesn't scream that much and the only part that she does that might be construed as annoying is when she has the panic attack in the back seat of the van. People, she is an 11 year old girl. My 7 year old daughter is a lot more annoying with her outbursts than Dakota Fanning was with hers. It wasn't that bad and I'd like to see how you would react in similar circumstances.

The ending of the film wasn't really that abrupt either. They do have a nice little final confrontation between one of the affected tripods and the Army soldiers firing Avenger missiles at it. By the way, the soldier that checks on the dying alien that pokes out of the downed tripod is a co-worker of mine here at Fort Irwin. I have to mention the military role in this as well. I really appreciated the fact that Mr. Spielberg showed the soldiers as they truly are - men and women who are just as scared as everyone else, but have a mission to perform. There is one part that I felt was unbelievable and that was at the ferry scene. There is no way that a single line of soldiers was going to keep a terrorized crowd from stampeding them to get aboard that ferry. They would have been knocked senseless and trampled.

The people that did not enjoy this film most likely were expecting a film where everything is laid out before them in explicit detail. That doesn't happen here and I personally think that is what made this such a unique film. This is nothing more than a trip down terror lane with a side helping of spectacular ILM handy-work.

title: Not one of Speilbergs best.
review:
!!!!!POSSIBLE SPOILER ALERT!!!!! As the saying goes, "If it ain't broke, don't fix it". It can easily be said about this. War of the Worlds sticks to the basic premise of the original but it also has the traditional Spielberg trademark stamped all over it. This being the essence of a broken family or strained relationships that occur within a family and the struggle to bring them together. The common day everyman that becomes a hero from saving the moment from unfamiliar or more powerful obstacles.

This is what differs the most from the original. In the original, now there is only a vague explanation in the new one, the aliens come from Mars because there planet has become uninhabitable and an explanation as to why they have chosen our planet and not the others in our solar system. The remake doesn't explore this to any extent and only gives the explanation that they placed machines under ground before humans inhabited the Earth, and when the time was right they arrived in bolts of lightning and started to claim the Earth for their own. There is no real explanation as to where they came from and why. It doesn't concentrate on the threat, it becomes second hand to what is happening with Tom Cruise's family.

War of the Worlds, as with numerous Spielberg films, it is divided into two halves. It is similar to A.I. in the sense the first half is quite bright and sets up the film, while the second half is dark and focuses on the threats and a lot of the dangers that the family has to face, as with Haley Joel Osment's character in A.I.

This is bit of a disappointment as the movie seems to be aimed more at the popcorn crowd and it doesn't do the original justice which is a shame because Spielberg is one of the greatest, if not THE greatest, storyteller of our time and has brought us some the greatest films ever. It's not a bad film as it is well put together, it's just you're typical summer movie blockbuster. The film does have its moments but fans of the original might feel let down as that is one of the true great sci-fi classics and will stand the test of time and be remembered for a long time. Unfortunately, this one won't be and will not be remembered as one of Speilbergs greatest efforts either.

title: Despite claims to the contrary this is a remake of the '53 film.
review:
As with Spielberg I have been a huge fan of this story for many years now. Anyone who has read my posts on the boards will know that I have been critical of the choice to move the story both in space and time. What I was expecting going into the movie was to see a good movie that was a poor retelling of the original story.

On the whole I think I was wrong on both counts. I'll start with the good. More of the book has survived in the story than I expected although much of it has been handled in a clumsy and confused manner. This film is quite scary in places but it is not a consistent "horror movie" and doesn't have the same fluidity of mood as a film like Signs. The acting is pretty good, Dakota Fanning especially is excellent as she has been in quite a few films recently. Defintately one to watch out for in the future. The special effects are adequate but don't do anything you haven't seen before.

On the negative front however... The actual characters aren't particularly likable, at no point in the movie did I particularly care what happened to them over the extras. There are plot holes you could drive an articulated lorry through, most of which have come from the clumsy transition of the story to modern day. The movie is very short and yet has a whole subsection of the original story cut out. The transplantation to modern day hasn't actually added anything to the movie or made it easier to identify with the main characters, and has in fact made many major story problems which have not been well explained. I don't want this review to contain spoilers so I will provide no detail but most of the technical points of the story are provided by characters wildly speculating (unrealisticly in my opinion) or with a particularly poor scene with a news crew.

Over all this movie isn't terrible but has far too much lacking both as a straight up event movie and as a telling of the story. I have seen interviews with both Spielberg and Cruise where they have said straight up that this is not a remake of the '53 George Pal movie, but I'm afraid that is just not true. There is at least one scene lifted straight from it and the intro and outro are very similar. The overall spirit of the movie is identical as is the general B-Movie feel.

If you are a movie fan then go and see Batman Begins, it has none of the clumsiness of WoW.

If you are a fan of the story then go and see Batman Begins, it'll just be better for your blood pressure.

I really expected much much more from Spielberg. I'm not the kind of idiot that makes silly claims of movie boycotts etc but Spielberg has seriously fallen in my estimation.

As a movie I would rate this: 6/10

As a War of the Worlds Story: 3/10

Over all I was generous and gave: 5/10

I think this movie would have been better served by a different title and that would have left Spielberg free to handle some of the story problems better.

title: good start, but it seemed the movie went on auto-pilot half way through
review:
It might be because I had such high expectations and hopes for this film. I generally like a broad range of movies from art-house to pure Hollywood escapism / adventure. I went in with a fairly open mind, and at first it was really excellent! The build up with just hints of what was going on was engrossing. I like the perspective of the average personin the dark, afraid, not knowing at all whats going onEurope obliterated, Europe OK etc. Even cinemagraphically, Spielberg flerts with grainy / out of focus camera shots, or views of what the people see in their car mirrors, instead of spelling it all out. Also, not too much heavy handed foreshadowingthe "Dad, I got a sliver. But its OK, as my body will just push it out on its own" metaphor early on in the movie I thought was just enough of a nod and a wink to the audience.

But after that, it seemed to go on auto-pilot to "lets please everyone in the audience island." As a demographic who no longer gets excited about "oooh, will the hero die half way through the film", I just don't get into scenes like that anymore. I think I was 7 or 8, when I figured out that Cptn Kirk was not going to die in each episode. Then again, if you are 7 or 8, this is definitely for you! Especially being a Spielberg film, you just know none of the principle good characters will get killed (especially the chilled!), no matter how grim it looks. So on its own, it just isn't a great suspense vehicle, as there needs to be more e.g advance the plot in an interesting way, add another dimension to the character by revealing who they are through testing and dangerous conditions. The movie at times tried to show this, but it seems it just could not decide how much time and effort doing it. Should it be the purely amazing F/X film ? maybe a little. Should it be a study on how people respond at the end of the world (e.g. Last Night, or the new BattleStar Galactica ?) Yeah, some of that too. The problem is, that many littles does not add up to a lot. And that Tim Robbins scene ? WTF ? That's a minus sadly. He is a great actor, but this was a poorly written part.

Pluses ? The alien tripods. Although nothing new (flinging cars, huge explosions, bridges falling like wooden blocks), its well done.

The ending ? No where near as bad as AI. But then again, that's a hard one to top /bottom out on. Still, when the scene switches to the outskirts of Boston, I had this sense that there was an editing error. I never read the book, but it does seem like a tough nut to sell from a climax perspectivehow do you properly build up to an ending where tiny germs off camera kill the aliens, without making it look like the "Deus ex machina" that frankly, the ending is. The 50's B movie version of it kind of pulled it off in a cheesy self aware way, and I figured he would use Morgan Freeman's great voice to do the same. But alas, it didn't really work.

I saw 6 out of 10 and my partner says 5

title: Good atmosphere, many logical errors: Average
review:
If you...

...want to see a movie with superior Special Effects, wonderfully oppressing atmosphere and pulse-driving action... SEE IT!

...expect a logical, good-scripted and conclusive movie with distinctive characters, profundity, character integrity and development, a movie that touches you for more than shocking with too loud special effects, DO YOURSELF A FAVOR, Don't SEE IT!

Most common NEGATIVE Arguments * The script isn't very professional as for many logical errors, most have already been mentioned. Simply explaining the errors with "the original was like that, so Spielberg had no choice", well, if sticking to the original that close, why even make a remake? I think Spielberg was too much under time pressure to work out the details enough. Please, the argument "it's just a movie, not everything has to be explained, i just want to get entertained", thats okay with me, but please accept that there are people who like to think about details in movies, as I do, and then, such script errors are annoying. And War of the Worlds really has many such errors.

* The image of the actual aliens did not support the fact (given from the narrator's prologue) that the aliens were greatly intelligent. I found them rather giving the picture of dull, uncautious and reckless idiots, playing with the old bicycle. Knowing that intelligence and wisdom are two independent things (a Nobel-prized doctor can still be clumsy) makes it possible to unite their picture with their told intellect (with much good will and complicated explaining), but on the whole, it's rather unsuiting. Just like most (all?!) other things we see and learn about the aliens in the movie. Just my opinion, don't kill me.

* The character consistency/development is unsteady and irritating in my opinion. Sometimes character traits are formed for the audience but they have no effect to the plot or the later behavior of the same character. nearly all character builds in that movie suffer that problem. E.g. the son, first he seems rather reasonable, soothing his sister in the car and agreeing that "driving to Boston to mom" is the right thing to do, then when the army band drives by, he neither wants to see his mom, nor save his sister anymore, he wants to join the soldiers (i wonder if a boy his age, he isn't even 16 as he has no license, would really be that stupidly brave in such an extreme situation, no matter what his character is like) and "fight the tripods". then he sees how useless it is, he takes his sister in his arms and promises her to take care of her. nice, but later he wants to stay with the Abrams tanks (!) that obviously don't touch the tripods and try fight?! lol no comment. that in the end he's still there made me laugh sourly in the cinema. all that leaves me with the feeling like having eating a gallon of cotton candy when i was really hungry and needed a steak.

* While being an entertaining movie, the end is somewhat hilarious i think. it's a superficial stereotype Hollywood on-schedule blockbuster happy ending. still i accept that some people like it, happy endings are sooo nice, aren't they? tear. myself, i hate non-happy-endings in the first place, but in the long term they usually are more valuable for a movie experience, don't you all think? uhm probably not, i get that.

Most common POSITIVE Arguments * Spielberg succeeds in creating a mind-blowingly oppressive atmosphere all over the film, except for the ending perhaps. Especially the first 20 minutes are extremely well done. I was caught by the movie just as I was caught by the atmospheres that "official masterpiece" movies like 2001, Alien or Se7en create, and that gives the movie 90% of all credit i give it. That is not to be underestimated because many people who do not care about every detail in a movie, who do not even want to analyze it, are simply caught by the movie like they haven't often before, I see that, and that's probably the reason why it is by many considered "the best movie ever". Makes sense to me, although its not my opinion.

* The special effects are very impressing and I really don't think they are either exaggerated nor inappropriate. Combined with the nice done camera setup, they massively add to the atmosphere. Often, special effects are evaluated as story/dialog/complexity/integrity substitute, for a reason. But its wrong to make generalizations here. Probably you will all agree that the weaknesses of this movie have at least nothing to do with the good CGI, yes? * Personally i found the general acting not that bad. It wasn't extremely good either, but its not a great point of criticism. Simply given the script and the plain dialogs, the actors make a good job out of it and add to the atmosphere. Although I found Rachel, the role of Fanning, rather annoying, she did a good job out of what she was told.

Result: After all an entertaining summer blockbuster with great special effects and atmosphere but lacking consistency and many logical errors.

title: Although somewhat lackuster at times, 'War of the Worlds' still remains a technical knockout with a chilling atmosphere
review:
War of The Worlds Dock-worker Ray(Cruise) has never had a close relationship with either of his kids. They are at his house for the weekend when a sudden storm erupts, then large alien-infested tri-pods begin to emerge from the ground after lightening strikes there numerous times, killing many people. Ray runs with his children. But he soon realizes they're under attack... and if they want to survive, they'll have to fight...

War of the Worlds... directed by Steven Spielberg.

All the "summer movie qualifications" are present in the newest look at the world under attack by aliens. In this film, these qualifications are pumped up to a maximum level, with some of the best effects to hit the screen in a while. Director Steven Spielberg is at the top of his game here, bringing us a variety of explosive stunts and interesting camera angles. The actors are also at the top of their game here as well, Cruise handling his part well, Fanning showing off her emotions once again here quite well.

You might be wondering the part in my summary that says "lackuster". What did I mean by that? Well, by the end, we've seen what these tri-pods can do, and we know the humans will win. The aliens attacking every place Ray appears at becomes a stretch by the finale.

These negative points aside, 'War of the Worlds' a chilling look at the world under attack, with spectacular effects, a well-visualized atmosphere, and edge-of-your-seat fun throughout. A perfect example of a summer movie. 3 from 4 PG13: intense sequences of sci-fi action/violence, disturbing images and language.

If there's one thing that'll stand out in this movie, is the annoyance. I just returned after watching the movie(not even 10 minutes have passed), and all I can say is that, the annoying little girl(Dakota Fanning) and her elder brother(Justin Chatwin) will surely irritate anyone to hell.

Tom Cruise does a good job of being the divorced father, and his affection for both of his children is very apparent, but like most divorcées, his children thinks otherwise. They dislike him, because they feel that he feels too much about himself. The young girl of 10 years must surely know when there is a crisis and when to keep calm and shut up and when to listen to her father. Even more goes for her brother, who is old enough to be in college, and yet acts so immature and childish.

Saying all these, you once again have to praise Spielberg for pulling off an extraordinary action sequences, and incredible camera work. You have to appreciate the pace of the movie. It started of very fast, then it mellowed down, and then fast again, only to mellow down for am incredibly long slow sequence where, the humans stealthily escape from the clutches of the aliens, then finally fast again till the end.

Tom Cruise, as Ray Ferrier, gives a reasonably good performance. Tim Robbins plays a small but nice role as the eccentric Ogilvy, who is bent upon destroying th aliens. Dakota Fanning, although was extremely irritating as the young Rachel Ferrier, is commendable.

Overall, this is yet again an Independence Day remake, with great computer graphics, and a sci-fi plot. The animation, recreated during the sequence where, the aliens are seen extracting the blood of humans, and planting their pods is awesome.

But even after watching this much acclaimed movie, I have to say, that something is still nagging in the back of my mind. It really didn't satisfy me greatly.

An ordinary 6/10!!!!

title: Fairly entertaining with many flaws and a poor-rushed ending
review:
(contains minor spoilers) The movie is called War of the Worlds. But it is more like Invasion of Earth as you only see destruction and mayhem caused by one side..not really a war between two worlds..

With that aside, the movie is quite good. It has some of the best special effects. Tom Cruise gave a good performance. The direction was pretty good.

What disappointed me, was that half way through the movie i realized that this is just a 'chase movie' where Cruise and his two kids just run out from one situation to another..The first few situations are suspenseful and done well. Then it started getting tiresome and predictable..

The ending to me was just rushed. The explanation that was given in the end of the movie was poorly done as though the crew did not know how to end the movie and came up with something at the end just for the sake of ending the movie. Some people might remember Shyamalan's 'The Signs' where the aliens are threaten by water..Whether people like Signs or not, Shyamalan was trying to prove a point that sometimes things happen for a reason. And he was able to build that up from the beginning of the movie to his conclusion. But don't expect any themes that can spark any level of intellectual discussions in the War of the Worlds.

I am sure people can enjoy the movie despite its flaws and its ending. But i am sure some people may find it disappointing that this movie is just 2 hours of running and just to show off new special effect technologies.

title: Unimpressive
review:
I agree with some of the previous reviewers saying that the cinematography in this movie was excellent. In particular, I was impressed by the camera movement accompanying Tom Cruise as he escapes crumbling New Jersey in a van with his kids. Amazing how the "lens" weaved in and out of traffic as the car rode down the turnpike. Great job overall.

The storyline was intense but had a questionable integrity. Here we have beings who have effectively fried our electronic circuits, yet conveniently some TV crews and random pedestrians are still filming, not to mention the fully operational army combat vehicles and the Hudson ferry. Perhaps the EMP has a narrow radius, but if the aliens could thrust Earth back into the Stone Age, why stop with a few blocks of New Jersey? Why not EMP the entire planet if you had the capacity? That would put any resistance to rest, and make for an interesting story.

My biggest concern; however, is for Ray Ferrier. As a father, Tom Cruise's character goes through a positive transformation from a selfish, uncaring individual into a tender, protective parent. Why then does he coldly kill the slightly paranoid Oglivy (played by Tim Robbins)? I thought it was an evil and unnecessary twist in Ferrier's character development. There are other ways of keeping someone "quiet" to avoid being detected by blood-thirsty invaders. I'm sorry but that Heart of Darkness/everyone for himself attitude may fit a faceless mob but not the main character who is supposedly undergoing a positive change.

I give the movie 6/10.

title: First Rate Except...
review: My daughter and I just saw the Spielberg edition of "War of the Worlds." The cast is all first rate and Dakota Fanning is dynamite. I am not a Tom Cruise fan but I do love Spielberg and that is why I went to view the movie. The music is adequate and does not get in the way of the plot or dialogue. When I don't notice the score, it is a good thing--except in "Cape Fear" and "Mystic River" for which the score becomes an extra character. The intensity level is maximum and I love a good scare! The special FX are pretty good--under created rather than overdone. Morgan Freeman does the prologue and epilogue which serves to tie the movie together with a bow. My only criticism of this first rate film is the abominable conclusion--NO I WON'T SPOIL the movie, but like Spielberg's "AI" the movie should have ended 5 minutes from when Spielberg did. This lack of knowing when to stop the movie is now officially a problem with the director who I worship and adore for his responsible movie making. This could've have been a perfect movie, but because of the sloppy ending, it is regrettably NOT!

title: Clearly Not a Feel-Good Action Movie
review:
I left the theater with a real bad taste in my mouth after seeing War of the Worlds. Not so much because of the suggestions of gore towards the end of the film, but because the film impresses upon you a real sense of futility.

Unlike other disaster films, this film has no positive emotional thread to carry you through the tension and horror. The main character, played by Tom Cruise, is such an incredible loser in life and does virtually nothing heroic or redeeming (except tossing one grenade). He, and his dysfunctional family, are basically tossed about by events instead of influencing them.

Without either a positive emotional core, or characters that actually make a difference to the plot, this film ends up being an exercise in how to destroy others with great efficiency. And the ending, although faithful to H.G. Wells' original novel, doesn't play to a contemporary audience. Instead of redemption from divine design (Wells' original intent), the ending suggests that man doesn't really matter. And based on the uninteresting, lackluster characters, that suits mankind just fine.

5 out of 10. An action/disaster movie without an emotional core falls pessimistically flat.

Barky

title: I expected a little more
review: I have been looking forward to WOTW for quite some time and I did find it to be a very entertaining popcorn movie. My disappointment lies in the movies ending. After all these people have been through they walk right up to a row of untouched houses with a nice neat untouched family waiting for them. Come on Steven, what were you thinking. How could you let this happen to your movie? It's just plain lazy. This could have been one of those rare action films that is actually good. What we get instead is a fun thrill ride that fizzles out in the end. If your expecting ET or Close Encounters quality then your out of luck. If you just want to get out of the sun enjoy some popcorn and a coke then this is the movie for you

title: Disappointing! - Could have done a lot better!
review:
If you're going to the cinema to see a remake of the 1953 classic film then forget it. This NEW version isn't a version at all. It's totally NEW. The story revolves around 3-main characters. Ray Farrier, (Tom Cruise) his son Robbie (Justin Chatwin) and his daughter Rachel (Dakota Fanning).

Having seen the trailers and watched the interviews with the cast members I was really excited about seeing this movie. Sadly though, on this occasion it's all hype and not enough substance. I was really disappointed with Spielberg's latest effort.

The characters are dull and boring, the storyline is weak and the special effects are not that special at all. By the end f the movie I couldn't care less if they lived or died.

After beginning brightly the storyline seemed to lose its way. Meaningless dialogue between the characters and very little action means you're sitting there desperately waiting for something to happen. "War of the Worlds" is a hugely disappointing film and not even the introduction of Tim Robbins can save it from being just an average movie.

More character development, a more serious storyline and better visual effects were needed to make this film a summer blockbuster. Still, the trailers for "The Island" and the Harry Potter" new film looked good.

We also have the Chronicles of Narnia and King Kong to look forward to.

Marks out of 10  A disappointing 6/10

title: good scary moments, lack of battles scenes
review: Dakota Fanning was incredible as usual as was Justin Chatwin, Tom Cruise was OK. There were some great scares but too much emphasis on gore and death and alien machines. Not enough plot, final battle scene or sufficient explanation of ending. Tim Robbins underused and weird interaction with Tom Cruise's character. Too much special effects not enough good dialogue or storyline. Loved interaction between Dakota and Justin. Mirando Otto played great part as mom dealing with family issues. Great fan of Spielberg however thought this one belonged with "A.I" as lacking in his usual fabulous story, plot, dialogue and ingenuity. Overall, thought this was good for DVD watching but not up paying money for theater watching.

title: Giant killer robots from space...what's not to love?
review:
I admit, I have never seen the original War of the Worlds. I am slowly compiling a list of all the classic sci-fi movies I have never seen, and it's currently embarrassingly long. That confession made, I can at least say that I'm reviewing this movie with a fresh perspective.

The first and most obvious thing to be said is that visually, the movie is stunning. The beginning of the invasion, when the Tripods climb out of the craters in the asphalt, surrounded by buildings that are imploding, crumbling, and being split down the middle, is an incredible image and one of the best uses of CGI I've seen in a long time. The machinery, the destruction, the aliens themselves are rendered beautifully and terrifyingly.

Stephen Spielberg does something else incredible, beyond the sheer impressiveness of the visuals--he keeps the tension pulsing throughout the entire movie. There is an honest question of who will make it out alive, of how we will prevail, when we will prevail, even if we will prevail at all (though honestly, if this question had been answered unsatisfyingly, no one would have liked this movie at all). Tom Cruise, as a dead-beat dad, is suddenly forced to figure out a way to bring his two children to safety. His daughter Rachel (played by the unbearably cute Dakota Fanning) in particular adds to the sense of urgency, both through her young age and her frequent panic attacks due to a bad case of claustrophobia.

I do have two criticisms, though. The first is Tim Robbins' bizarre sequence. Despite the fact that he is unquestionably an amazingly talented actor, I had trouble feeling that his role as an obsessive would-be leader of the (literally) "underground resistance" added much to the movie at all. The second would be the sticking point that many other viewers have complained about--the fairly ending. The audience is asked to swallow a weak explanation and a tie-up-loose-ends approach that rarely seems credible in film and literature. Still, my attitude is that by the time you reach the end, who cares? It's been a satisfying ride.

Whole-heartedly recommended to lovers of thrillers, action, and sci-fi alike.

title: By Jingo!!
review:
Aside from all the bloopers (shame on you , Spielberg!!),this movie also galled most non-Americans with several snide asides.

At one stage, Cruise's son asks where the alien machines are from, and when Cruise replies "not from here", his newly gung-ho offspring asks "from Europe?". Funny in a way, bur revealing about how many Americans feel about their ancestral lands.

In another scene, Robbins says that in Japan apparently a way has been found to defeat the machines, and the immediate reaction is "well we should be able to do it, too". We should all know the USA holds the monopoly on military technology, no-one else comes close, and Werner von Braun still turns in his grave.

Most private motor vehicles stop running, but the all-American Humvee carries on? I'm surprised the downed airliner wasn't identified as an Airbus.

Baloney, and barely disguised pro-American propaganda.

title: Disappointing
review:
What went wrong? From a purely technical standpoint War of the Worlds is fine--the special effects are first rate and this is the type of material Steven Spielberg can direct in his sleep. His film-making is taut and he stages some of the finest action/suspense sequences that audiences are likely to see this summer. War of the Worlds could have been a classic--so why did it leave me feeling indifferent and cold and why does everyone I talk to seem to leave the movie kind of underwhelmed? I think the problem is the script. Spielberg and writer David Koepp decided to focus entirely on three characters--Tom Cruise's deadbeat dad Ray and his two children. The whole movie follows them from one calamitous event after another as they try not to get zapped by the aliens. There aren't even really any other actors that are on screen long enough to really qualify as characters.

There are a couple of problems with this. First, it makes the story unnecessarily narrow. This is a movie about the destruction of the planet and we spend all of our time following 3 characters. The other problem is that we're pretty sure Spielberg isn't going to kill Tom Cruise or his kids. That creates basically a feature length version of the raptor chasing the kids scene from Jurassic Park--how do you generate suspense when you know the characters who are being threatened with death are never going to get killed? After a while watching the same 2 or 3 characters narrowly escape from the aliens gets to be monotonous and that's pretty much all that War of the Worlds has to offer--one special effects oriented action scene after another after another. There's no plot, too few characters and no soul, just a lot of action and special effects.

There's also a really lame happy ending, which seems to be Spielberg's Achilles heel these days, that unfortunate need to please. He doesn't completely betray the material like he did with Minority Report, but only because there isn't nearly as much to betray. The ending here is ludicrous and stupid but I didn't mind because at least the movie was over.

title: Decent flick with too much hype
review:
Even though I read the glowing reviews many critics made of WoW, I wasn't really expecting much. It wasn't a movie i was looking forward to, like for example Batman Begins, but nevertheless i decided to give it a try. For the most part the movie was surprisingly entertaining. I'll start with the good parts:

-I enjoyed the scene of which Tom and his son were playing catch living in New England I could appreciate it.

-The Scenes of high-tense action, which seemed to happen scene after scene. That was one thing about it, it never slowed down at all, which i liked. it almost seemed to blur into one big action sequence.

-I also enjoyed the scene in which tom had to let his son go. It was probably the best scene in the movie.

-I think it portrayed how people would act perfectly if something like this would happen. with the scene where everyone is fighting over the car and all.

Now onto the bad parts, stop reading if you don't want to know the ending:

-The Ending. period. i mean i understand how the aliens died and all, but it sucks at the same time. I left the theater thinking i wanted to go back to my house and create a weapon to kill the aliens before the Earth gets to them first. I wanted the people to kick some ass or at least some battle of which people find out their weakness. it sucks that they just died eventually. and what was up with tom going to his ex wife's parents house? How did they survive when there are no people out on the streets, and none of them had a scratch on them? I don't understand how any of them survived when there was a toll of 1 billion dead. it left me with a sour taste in my mouth, but then i realized how i didn't really want to kill myself during the movie as a whole, so i forgave it

overall i thought it was an entertaining movie and worth a rental and a purchase if you can deal with the ending.

title: What was Stephen thinking?
review: Outside of making a ton of money, he passed on Indiana Jones IV for this unsatisfying ET invades earth movie. As bad as "Signs" was, that was a superior movie to this. I suppose if you like spectacular special effects, and things blowing up every 3 seconds; and don't care much for character development you will be more tolerant than me towards this movie. I saw "War of the Worlds" yesterday. This morning TBS ran "Aliens" (1987). The interplay between Ripley & Newt was so much better than between Ray & Rachel. Lastly moving to a spoiler. The scene where the 4 little aliens stalk Ray & Rachel in the basement is nearly identical to Spielberg's "Jurassic Park" scene where the raptors stalk the children in the kitchen. Oh well, at least the new Batman wasn't a bust, and George Romero's latest zombie fest will take the bad taste of this movie out of your mouth.

title: Ho Hum -- Inavsion By A Well Oiled Spielberg Machine
review:
This movie is getting great reviews. I know that. I also know that it did nothing for me.

I wasn't scared. I wasn't thrilled. I felt I'd seen the movie before. I looked at my watch again and again. I was bored.

Steven Spielberg's careful touches are on view, but after seeing so many Spielberg movies, and three Spielberg movies about alien-human contact, I just felt like I was watching the standard issue, well oiled, Spielberg machine.

You have the collision of very average, working class people, with heavy Joisy accents, and exotic aliens.

You have the erasure of women, and the focus on the average guy hero, who has been abandoned by his significant woman, in this case, his wife, who left him and got knocked up by a richer, kinder, more handsome man.

You have fast moving action.

You have plenty of quotes from other movies. There is an alien-bicycle encounter, a quote from "ET," there are rampaging, numbed humans, acting like Zombies, a reference to George Romero movies. There are scenes that, in their lighting and composition, reference 1950s sci fi and film noir.

The new touch is the constant reference to 9-11. As with 9-11, attackers strike from the sky, causing large structures to tumble, but these attackers have really been "buried" among us all along, without our knowledge.

As with 9-11, the attackers and their reasoning are pretty foreign to us.

As with 9-11, crowds run through city streets, shredded office papers rain from the sky, survivors are coated in ash, and family members hang up signs asking for info about lost relatives.

As with 9-11, families that had previously seemed casual are suddenly drawn in more tightly together, and love is expressed.

It's all very, very well done, and I can't really tell you why I was so bored, so not scared, so not moved. Maybe because, at this point, it was just all too recognizable, even with the 9-11 touches, as a patented Spielberg product.

title: Not nearly as good as it should have been
review: Oh how the mighty have fallen. There was a time when the names Spielberg and Cruise guaranteed something out of the ordinary. No longer. Which is not to say that this is a bad movie. It's just that there is NOTHING special about. There is none of the wonder and inspiration that Spielberg is LEGENDARY for in his movies. While Cruise goes a bit against type by playing a real jerk, there is nothing original in his performance. What does separate this movie from the other end of the world disaster epics is the fact that it follows one family's struggle to stay alive. In fact, during scenes of either mass destruction or epic battles, Spielberg focuses on his characters' reactions to the situation. After all if you were in the middle of this, would you be standing there watching the whole thing, or would you be making dust trails for the horizon? So in fact the movie does have a strong "you are there" feel to it. But what works against this approach is the fact that there is not ONE likable character in this movie. Cruise is a jerk, his son is a punk, and Dakota Fanning as his daughter may very well be the most annoying child character in recent history. Not only does she not stop screaming for 2 hours, but she screams in an air raid siren type of way. Now a little girl probably would in fact do that in real life, but as an audience member watching the movie, you wish she'd get zapped. Which brings me to my next point. What is the point of the alien invasion? What are they here for? Their machines have been buried for a million years, so they've been planning this for a while. But for what? When the machines erupt, their ray beams turn whole cities of humans to dust. But later in the movie they capture people, cage them, suck their blood, and spray it like fertilizer. Why? Are they here to kill us or use us? Make up your minds! Maybe that plays into Spielbergs whole approach of being in the middle of it all and not really knowing what's going on. After all in a situation like this, the common man is not privy to all the answers. But as a moviegoer it's very unsatisfying. Finally this movie contains what may very well be the worst ending EVER!!!!!! The final 5 minutes of this movie, which I assume was meant to be the big emotional release, was laughable. It follows the standard movie rule that kids never die. But it's done so ham-handedly, I had to groan. Like Cruise's character, I am a divorced father. I see my children primarily on weekends. So at the end, when Cruise drops his kids off at his wife's front door, I laughed and thought "Well that was a helluva weekend." All this may make it sound like I didn't like the movie. But I did. I did like it. But if I had waited for video, I don't think I would've been missing anything. I am a movie FANATIC. I go to the movies at least 20 times a year, and have over 1000 movies in my collection. I go see just about anything. This is the first movie directed by Spielberg that I have seen in theaters since the original Jurassic Park. The last Cruise movie I saw in theaters was the first Mission Impossible. And that's a pretty sad statement considering that Spielberg and Cruise used to make movies that deserved and demanded to be seen on the big screen.

title: war of the worlds is worth seeing in theater
review: the weird sounds and dark aesthetic mysterious things capture the imagination with the anticipation of the unknown, cuz i haven't seen any other war of the worlds, the family conflict dialog was irritation, character development was embarrassing and it was like the blair which project where ear muffs would have been nice, a lot of useless scenes to kill time spoiled the cool stuff, the resolution wasn't a brain teaser so more creative energy could have been used in the mauling, i think Spielberg owed Tim Roberts a favor cuz his entire mystic river scene was lame, the sound effects get a solid ten, i still recommend the movie even to people who barely go because its spooky and stimulating on the big screen, as a DVD, i would use that as a Frisbee, it seems like star wars the new older ones recently put out shows the directors are getting weak and old and the young strong animation and special effects generation is dominating, hopefully balance will come there, I'm going to bed

title: Jurassic Park, except with alien tripods instead of dinosaurs
review: No one wanted to love this movie more than me. War of the Worlds is a visual and technical masterpiece to be sure, but everything else pretty much fell flat. Instead of being drawn in by the story and its characters' plight, as I was with such films as Close Encounters of the Third Kind and Signs, I found myself completely uninterested in what was happening and who it was happening to. I thoroughly enjoyed the first CGI attack sequence that got the film off to a running start, but it wasn't long after that I began to realize that this wasn't going to be anything more than a Jurassic Park-type experience, except with alien tripods instead of dinosaurs. Spielberg did use some restraint by only showing the actual aliens twice in the film and by limiting what we saw to what Tom Cruise's character saw, but M. Night Shyamalan already perfected the technique of "understated horror" in the film, Signs. I won't even get into the forced "Party of Five" family drama that Spielberg unsuccessfully tried to kick-start several times during the film, with some intended dramatic moments that were just plain laughable. I'm still confused as to why the Ferrier trio complained about having nothing to eat other than peanut butter and condiments while they were standing in the ex-wife's kitchen, right next to a huge refrigerator. I guess I'll let that one slide. War of the Worlds is not a bad film by any means, it's just simply not as good as it could have been.

title: Worth seeing but don't get your hopes up for a great plot.
review: Great interesting beginning, all the character building that I was expecting with a the great cast they had, but as the movie progressed it really fell flat for me. The chase consuming most of the movie was very well done and the animation and special effects deserve an 'A', but that was the movie. The fact that the ending dropped on you in the last 5 minutes draws away from the good points. The fact that the summery was just narrated over by some voice that sounded like Morgan Freeman though, was more than disappointing. If I knew what to expect before going I would definitely see it once, but having the choice I would have chosen to see Bateman again. Saying this the friend I went with loved it even though she admitted that the ending could have used a little work.

title: Not bad but not great either...
review: Let me start off by saying I'm not a huge fan of Steven Spielberg. But I like most of his movies and I like the War of the Worlds story, so I was really optimistic going into this, but not expecting too much from Spielberg. It delivered some pretty stunning visuals but a lot of the story was a bit hard to swallow. *possible spoilers to follow* For example there is one scene where all of the electrical equipment stops working, even Tom Cruise's character's watch. But then, later in the same scene, people are tape recording what's going on with digital hand-held camcorders! That was ridiculous and there were other ridiculous plot holes. Like when Tom Cruise at the end of the film finds his family/friends in Boston and they are all completely clean! After this huge invasion of the entire planet where almost everybody is killed we're I guess supposed to believe that these people are all clean enough and dressed nicely enough to go to church? Plot holes galore and the writing on this movie wasn't superb, you can see everything coming, but it's shot pretty well and without giving too much away I can just say that a lot of the scenes look fantastic. If you're into great effects that are done right without necessarily caring too much about plot holes you should probably see this on the big screen. I give it 5.5/10

title: Suspenseful, but seriously flawed
review: Had a good feeling about this movie until something like half an hour remained. The effects were nice, and the savage nature of man, when he is backed into a corner, was brilliantly portrayed through the battle-for-the-car scene. But the boy was beyond obnoxious, not to mention incredibly stupid (literally, hard to imagine anybody being this dumb). Seriously, the world is in deep pooh-pooh, and now you decide to stage a teenage rebellion?!? And what the hell did he think he would accomplish by taking on the aliens kamikaze style? And how the hell did he survive that? And why, in name of all that is logical, did the aliens who supposedly was vastly superior in intelligence not come up with some sort of vaccine to counter the bacteria on a planet they supposedly had planned to conquer for a million years? Ridiculous.

title: What's the problem with this ?
review:
First, it is a well made film! Second, it is not what we usually expect.

Spilberg made a new point of view in this movie. You will not know more throughout the movie, then an ordinary man would know in this situation. You will get really little information about "who are they, why did they come, whats that red thing, what made them ill exactly" ? In a typical Hollywood movie you always get these answers. Nor from this film. The only "hollywoodian answer" is that "how did aliens get into tripods".

The working video camera is really a miss. The best thing in the movie if you see it in a good theaters, the sound will press you into your seat. There are really great noises, and sounds.

At the end you will feel some emptiness , because of the unanswered questions.

That's my opinion.

title: The 1953 version is better.
review: The acting is superb, the best asset of the film. Ms. Fanning's abilities are far ahead of her age. She is amazing. It's her film. We should definitely see more of Jason Chatwin. Cruise and Robbins are, as always, engrossing two watch. This film certainly is not up to the director's standards. Nor is the music up to the standards of the composer. At times it is intrusive. The special effects were OK, but nothing new. The film drags in places and the ending is so predictable and so unsatisfying. It is worth renting the DVD, which will probably be out soon, but it isn't worth $8-$10 since nothing requires that you see it on a big screen. If the 1953 version is available on DVD I think you will enjoy it more.

title: The greatest Sci-Fi movie of all time!!!!!
review: Steven Spielberg has made many great movies, and most of them have a less serious tone than this extremely well done remake of the H.G. Wells classic "War of the Worlds". I had been hoping to see at least one really good movie this summer, and after a very disappointing Star Wars finale my hopes were not very high for this one. We went to the rush hour show on opening day at my favorite theater with stadium seating, and the best sound system around. Our timing was perfect, as the coming attractions were just starting as we got our popcorn and soda, and perfect seats. I won't spoil it for anyone who has not seen this movie, but this is truly Mr. Spielberg's masterpiece. Although this is a remake and stays close to the original, it adds enough new surprises to truly stun the viewer. The special effects are second to none, and raise the bar ten notches over anything done before. The real beauty of this movie is that the special effects do not overpower the movie, as the story and actors shine through them with great intensity. The acting is first rate, and Tom Cruise comes through as a very believable blue collar worker with none of his usual "I am totally in control of the situation" attitude. Dakota Fanning has been great in past movies, but she has really grown as an actress to help this movie achieve perfection. She leaves you gasping for air on the edge of your seat in some intense scenes. I would have liked to see a bigger cameo role for Gene Berry, but at his age it is truly amazing he was able to make an appearance. For those who compared this movie with that Mel Gibson flop "Signs", I can only have pity on them for not being able to appreciate a film that towers over some of the best Sci-Fi movies ever made. These people simply don't like science fiction, and should not bother going to these movies. As someone who loved the original, War of the Worlds 2005 is a breath of Sci-Fi fresh air. It reminds me of the clear superiority, and effect the original movie Alien had when it came out. This is a MUST SEE movie, and will define quality in Sci-Fi movies for years to come. It easily deserves best movie of 2005. Steven Spielberg take a bow, you have outdone yourself.

title: Thrilling, Breathtaking, left me speechless...
review:
I went to see this movie with pretty low expectations. I only really wanted to go because fo the brilliant Dakota Fanning. So I took a friend and bought plenty of candy to keep me busy. Well I only three pieces of chocolate covered raisins while watching the movie.

This movie was brilliant, the beginning was perfect, the middle was so exciting and thrilling and then ending was simple and precise. Dakota Fanning I believe is the greatest actress. She was unbelievable in this movie along with every other movie she had been in. I truly respect and admire her.

The cg was brilliant, there were probably only 2 times that I actually even noticed it! Wonderful, wonderful, wonderful! I juts didn't understand one part, in the beginning after the storm, all the cars, lights, phones, watches and tons of others stopped. But the video cameras and cameras were still working!! I didn't understand that...

but still: I LOVED THAT MOVIE!!!! please go see it!!!!!!

title: possible screw-up
review:
It looked to me like the Martians blasted an arched span of freeway behind Tom Cruise, then blasted it again a few minutes later when they blew up the whole elevated span.

Howcome the Department of "San" or some other agency didn't dig one of these up giant walking machines up every now and again? I mean, they're buried everywhere!

The plot line of this WOTW is the same one in the late and very unlamented TV show Battlestar Galactica: "Ragtags running from the Cylon terror!"

title: Faithful to the Book
review:
I wasn't going to write out a review for this movie, (too lazy...) but after reading all of the negative reviews here on IMDb I had to put in a good word for this wonderful flick.

Most of the bad reviews seem to stem from the ending of the movie. This ending consisted of two things: 1) The son survived. 2) The aliens were killed by germs.

What many of these reviewers don't seem to know is that these endings are completely faithful to the spirit of the book. H.G.Wells *wanted* a happy ending for the main character.

Also, the entire point of War of the Worlds is to show that if aliens came and tried to kill us we wouldn't have a chance of beating them on our own. It also points out that we shouldn't underestimate the beings that we consider to be the least of everything because there is power in everything.

I went into the movie *hoping and praying* that SS would stick to the Book for the ending and was relieved when the ending came. Maybe if more people these days read classic literature there would have been less grumpiness and more relief at the end of the movie.

Please open your minds and give this movie a chance.

title: 9/11 meets evil E.T.
review:
When 9/11 passed, Spielberg argued that no movies about it should be made, because the events were too horrific and commercial exploitation would be distasteful. Some years on, I was very surprised to see him just do that. It's not direct, but rather indirect that the comparison is drawn: dwindling papers, photos of missing loved ones, debris and dust, enemy already among us, etc. All reactions are passing also: From denial (Rachel), saving your own soul (Ray) to combative (Robbie). Ogilvy (Tim Robbins) is probably the most interesting character in this sense: he combines all these reactions but ultimately turns insane. If you draw the comparison further it doesn't hold up well because it tries to combine 9/11 with the original War of the Worlds. So it ends up more like an evil E.T. (with again a strong emphasis here on a broken family)

Tension building is very well done. Time is taken to set up the situation, many shots are distant to get the wide panorama. Especially the hazy and over-lit shots in the beginning are interesting, suggesting something is out there. It's also a very dark film with a limited uplifting end. The scene with people fighting for a car or a place on the ferry are almost in another category. Note also that the church is the first building to be demolished by the invaders.

To bring it up once again: The PG-13 is what Spielberg is usually aiming for (murder on Ogilvy and feeding of tripods with humans not shown), but there remains much to be seen where the rating is debatable (people blown to pieces, bodies in the river). A lesser known director would not have come away with this.

Compared to the recent Kingdom of Heaven however, there is no ultimate political statement, no vision on the whole project shining through. This has always been Spielberg's weakness. And while he is almost as competent technically as his late friend Kubrick, that's the main reason why their movies are on different levels.

title: Not terrible, but not as amazing as I thought
review: Taking into account that I usually enjoy sci-fi films, however, i've never read the book and so may not really appreciate this film like some may. I didn't find the film a disaster, but wasn't really grabbed by it either. The special effects were pretty good as one would expect. And the acting was pretty reasonable. I'm not a huge Tom Cruise fan, but he played his role pretty well here. Tim Robbins wasn't at his usual brilliance but was adequate in his supporting role. Unfortuneatly, Miranda Otto wasn't used nearly enough and this was quite disappointing. The only actor who really shines, as she always does was Dakotta Fanning. It's not her best, but it really does cement her as the best child actress around. The letdown for me was the story. Granted it was good to see something different from the usual aliens 'indepence day' type story (not that i dislike ID4), the story seemed drawn out and in parts slow. It doesn't have the heroic feel that blockbusters like Independence Day have, it's more of the 'one man and his family's struggle against invasion and almost certain doom' feel that Signs had. Yet it's nowhere near as chilling or I believe, as effective as Signs. So granted the great effects it's probably worth seeing it on the big screen, but don't do in with the hope it will be a Spielberg classic, i doubt it'll be one of those 'i'll always remember the time i went and saw war of the worlds' experiences.
